entries.creator: Pater Sparrow
entries.pitch: 1 is a 2009 Hungarian experimental science fiction film directed by debut filmmaker Pater Sparrow, inspired by Stanisław Lem's fictitious criticism of the nonexistent book "One Human Minute." The film unfolds in a Budapest where a renowned bookshop is mysteriously filled with copies of a strange almanac titled simply "1"—a volume that contains tables and statistics documenting everything that happens in the world during a single minute. As a police investigation unfolds, the book and its implications begin to spread, drawing in a mysterious Vatican visitor and placing the bookshop staff in solitary confinement at the Bureau for Paranormal Research. The investigation spirals into existential chaos as the lead investigator, Phil Pitch, increasingly loses his grip on reality.

entries.title: 1. April 2000
entries.creator: Wolfgang Liebeneiner
entries.pitch: 1. April 2000 is a 1952 Austrian political satire film set in the year 2000, made during the Allied Occupation of Austria. The film depicts a fictional Austria still under the control of four Allied powers following World War II, satirizing the post-war situation through a futuristic lens. When Austria attempts to assert its independence by shredding its Allied-issued identity cards, the nation is charged with breaking "world peace" at a futuristic world court. The Austrian delegation must then prove that their nation is peaceful by presenting evidence of Austrian cultural achievements—from Mozart to Viennese waltz to mountain scenery—before the Moscow Declaration of 1943 is finally discovered, freeing Austria from foreign control.

entries.title: 11eyes
entries.creator: Lass (original)/Doga Kobo (anime)
entries.pitch: 11eyes is a Japanese visual novel and subsequent anime series blending supernatural horror with action. The story follows Kakeru Satsuki, who lost his sister seven years ago and has been living a detached life until his childhood friend Yuka Minase helps him regain normalcy. One day, the sky turns red, the moon turns black, and everyone vanishes—replaced by monsters in a twisted reality they call "Red Night." Kakeru and Yuka soon discover they are not alone: other survivors with unique abilities—Misuzu, a red-haired swordswoman and onmyōji; Kukuri, a silent girl resembling Kakeru's deceased sister; Yukiko, who becomes a cold killer when her glasses are removed; and Takahisa, a pyrokinetic—are also trapped in this nightmare. Together, they must survive attacks by grotesque beings called Black Knights while uncovering the mystery of Red Night and a mysterious girl named Lisette trapped within a red crystal.

entries.title: 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea
entries.creator: Stuart Paton
entries.pitch: 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea is a 1916 American silent film directed by Stuart Paton and produced by Carl Laemmle at Universal Pictures. Based on Jules Verne's classic 1870 novel "Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas," this film holds the distinction of being the first feature-length adaptation of Verne's submarine adventure. With a production budget of $500,000 (equivalent to nearly $12 million today), it was one of the most expensive films of its era and a significant technical achievement in early cinema. The film was recently selected for preservation in the United States National Film Registry in 2016, recognizing its cultural and historical significance.

entries.title: 2001 Nights
entries.creator: Yukinobu Hoshino
entries.topics: Space Travel, Exploration, Evolution, First Contact, Transhumanism
entries.pitch:
2001 Nights is a scientifically rigorous hard science fiction manga series by Yukinobu Hoshino, serialized from 1984-1986. It follows humanity's expansion across the cosmos over several centuries, from early space station missions to the discovery of an antimatter star called \"Lucifer\" that enables instantaneous interstellar travel.

The series consists of several loosely connected short stories, each called a \"Night,\" all taking place in the same timeline. The central concept is the \"Human Seeding Project\" - computer-controlled spacecraft loaded with frozen sperm and ova, designed to initiate human life on suitable planets across the galaxy. As generations pass, a new breed of humans emerges - born in space, with enhanced intelligence and lifespans far exceeding Earth-born humans.

The manga was adapted into an OVA in 1987 and later into a CGI series \"TO\" in 2009. It stands as a thoughtful exploration of humanity's future among the stars, with many visual homages to classic science fiction novels and films.

entries.title: 2001 Nights
entries.creator: Yukinobu Hoshino
entries.pitch:
2001 Nights is a landmark hard science fiction manga that spans centuries of human space exploration. Written and illustrated by Yukinobu Hoshino, the series follows humanity's journey from early spaceflight through the discovery of alien life and interstellar travel. The manga was adapted into an OVA in 1987 by Tokyo Movie Shinsha. The stories are loosely connected, each building on previous achievements, spanning several hundred years of fictional future history.

The work is largely inspired by classic hard science fiction, with many visual homages to previous science fiction novels and films. It stands as one of the most ambitious Japanese SF works of the 1980s.

entries.title: 2009: Lost Memories
entries.creator: Lee Si-myung (Director)
entries.pitch: 2009: Lost Memories is a 2002 South Korean science fiction action film set in a chilling alternate 2009 where the Korean Peninsula remains part of Imperial Japan. Directed by Lee Si-myung and based on the 1987 novel "Looking for an Epitaph" by Bok Geo-il, this ambitious alternate history explores what would happen if a single assassination in 1909 changed the course of the 20th century. The film was marketed as the biggest action flick in Korean cinema history at its release and was a co-production between South Korea and Japan, coinciding with the 2002 FIFA World Cup held jointly in both countries.

entries.title: 2019, After the Fall of New York
entries.creator: Sergio Martino
entries.pitch: 2019, After the Fall of New York is a 1983 Italian-French post-apocalyptic action film directed by Sergio Martino. Set in a dystopian 2019 following a nuclear World War III between the Pan-American Confederacy and the Eurac Monarchy, the film follows mercenary Parsifal on a desperate mission to rescue the last fertile woman on Earth from the ruins of Manhattan. Produced by Nuova Dania Cinematografica and Medusa Film, the film was released in Italy on July 22, 1983. Critics have noted its influence from John Carpenter's Escape from New York and George Miller's Mad Max 2, though it has been described as a cult B-movie with limitations in acting and special effects.

entries.title: 2030 – Aufstand der Alten
entries.creator: Jörg Lühdorff
entries.pitch: 2030 – Aufstand der Alten (2030 – Rise of the Elderly) is a three-part German television miniseries that aired in January 2007, exploring a dystopian near-future Germany grappling with demographic crisis. Written and directed by Jörg Lühdorff, the docudrama presents a chilling vision of intergenerational conflict, depicting what happens when the elderly population, frustrated by youth-centric policies, stages a takeover of society. The series was released as two related works: "Aufstand der Alten" (2007) and "Aufstand der Jungen" (2010), collectively examining the fictional "demographic crime" of generational inequality. Bettina Zimmermann stars as Lena Bach, with Jürgen Schornagel as Sven Darow, in this prescient examination of age-based political tension.

entries.creator: Seth Larney
entries.pitch: 2067 is a 2020 Australian science fiction film set in a devastated future where Earth has been ruined by climate change, deforestation, and nuclear war. Only one city in Australia survives, protected by synthetic oxygen—but the oxygen is tainted and causes a deadly affliction called "The Sickness." When scientist Ethan Whyte is contacted by researchers 400 years in the future who need his help to prevent humanity's extinction, he must journey through time to discover the truth about his father's work and the fate of humanity. The film explores themes of environmental collapse, temporal paradoxes, and the desperate hunt for redemption in a world beyond saving.

entries.creator: Chandler Tuttle
entries.pitch: 2081 is a 26-minute science fiction featurette directed by Chandler Tuttle, based on Kurt Vonnegut's 1961 short story "Harrison Bergeron." Set in a dystopian future where absolute equality is enforced by the 211th, 212th, and 213th Amendments to the U.S. Constitution, the film portrays a society where individual excellence is suppressed through mandated "handicaps"—physical devices that neutralize any natural advantages. The smart wear earbuds that fire loud noises, the beautiful wear masks, and the strong wear weights. When Harrison Bergeron—a uniquely brilliant and athletic young man—escapes government captivity, he delivers a defiant manifesto that challenges the very foundations of this forced equality.

entries.creator: Thomas M. Disch
entries.pitch: 334 is a haunting, innovative New Wave science fiction novel set in the early 2020s Manhattan, centered on the housing project at 334 East 11th Street. Written as a "fix-up" of five interlinked long stories plus a closing novella composed of over forty vignettes, it depicts a near-future society grappling with extreme overpopulation, social crowding, and bureaucratic welfare control. Rather than focusing on technological spectacle or dramatic heroics, Disch's novel finds its power in the mundane: rationed housing, controlled reproduction, welfare casework, and the small, everyday choices of ordinary people trying to survive. The book was a finalist for the 1974 Nebula Award for Best Novel and is now recognized as a landmark treatment of urban dystopian fiction—specifically the "crowding" strand of overpopulation narratives alongside works like Stand on Zanzibar and Make Room! Make Room! The novel's unique mathematical structure (the digits "3-3-4" determine everything from piece lengths to character recurrences) gives it an architecture that rewards careful reading.

entries.title: 57 Seconds
entries.creator: Rusty Cundieff (Director), E.C. Tubb (Source)
entries.pitch: 57 Seconds is a 2023 American science fiction thriller starring Josh Hutcherson and Morgan Freeman. When tech blogger Franklin Fausti intervenes during an attack on visionary tech mogul Anton Burrell, he's rewarded with a mysterious ring that allows him to travel exactly 57 seconds back in time. Initially using this power for personal gain, Franklin soon realizes the ring could help him expose Sig Thorensen—a pharmaceutical executive whose company's addictive painkiller Zonastin led to his twin sister's death. The film explores themes of revenge, ethics, and the temptation of power through a compact time-travel narrative.

entries.title: 6 Angels
entries.creator: Makoto Kobayashi (Director), Yasushi Akimoto (Original Concept)
entries.pitch: 6 Angels is a 2002 original net animation (ONA) sci-fi action film set in the near-future at an underground prison complex called Neo Purgatory, located at a former nuclear test site in Utah. The story follows an all-female mercenary unit known as the "Guard of Rose," who work as prison guards in this harsh facility where inmates—many mutated by ambient radiation—have been left to their own devices. When a powerful criminal named Donn Canyon and his family seize control of the prison and gain access to an American orbital nuclear missile platform, they declare war on the surface world, vowing to "purify the world with radiation" in a nuclear holocaust. The Guard of Rose is tasked with infiltrating the prison and stopping the Canyon family to preserve global peace.

entries.title: 8 Man
entries.creator: Kazumasa Hirai (Writer), Jiro Kuwata (Artist)
entries.pitch:
8 Man is a pioneering Japanese anime and manga series created in 1963, widely considered the nation's earliest cyborg superhero. The story follows Detective Hachiro Azuma, who is murdered by criminals and revived as a powerful android by Dr. Tani. Reborn as the armor-skinned 8 Man, he possesses superhuman speed, shape-shifting abilities, and incredible strength. Operating in secret, 8 Man fights crime while maintaining his dual identity—though he keeps his true nature hidden from everyone, including his secretary Sachiko and assistant Ichiro.

The series stands as a landmark in both Japanese and international science fiction, predating similar Western concepts like The Six Million Dollar Man and RoboCop by decades. Its unique blend of detective noir and early superhero elements created a template that would influence countless works in the genre.

entries.title: A Bomb Was Stolen
entries.creator: Ion Popescu-Gopo
entries.pitch:
A Bomb Was Stolen (Romanian: S-a furat o bombă) is a 1962 Romanian dialogue-free sci-fi comedy film directed by Ion Popescu-Gopo. The film begins with a nuclear bomb test, where one of the bombs is stolen by gangsters who hide it in a bag. Inept police pursue the gangsters, and the bag containing the bomb is lost and recovered by a passerby who has no idea what's inside. The innocent bystander goes about their day with the dangerous package, pursued by gangsters who are in turn pursued by the police—creating a hilarious chain of comedic misunderstandings.

The film is notable for being entirely dialogue-free, relying on visual comedy, physical humor, and imaginative storytelling to convey its narrative. This stylistic choice earned it international praise as an "exuberant comedy" and "a subtle and frequently hilarious satire." The film was entered into the 1962 Cannes Film Festival and received several international awards.

entries.title: A Boy and His Dog
entries.creator: L.Q. Jones (Director), Based on novella by Harlan Ellison
entries.pitch: In a post-nuclear America of 2024, an 18-year-old scavenger named Vic roams the Southwestern wasteland with his telepathic dog, Blood. Vic cares only about food and sex; Blood is a well-read, misanthropic genius who can read minds and locate survivors. When they discover an underground society called Topeka—run by a committee of white-faced officials who use genetic engineering and artificial insemination to reproduce—their contrasting desires trap them between survival on the surface and the twisted utopia below.

entries.title: A Canticle for Leibowitz
entries.creator: Walter M. Miller Jr.
entries.pitch:
A Canticle for Leibowitz is a seminal post-apocalyptic science fiction novel that spans over a thousand years of human history after a devastating nuclear war. Set in a Catholic monastery in the Southwestern United States, the novel follows the monks of the Albertian Order of Leibowitz as they preserve the surviving remnants of man's scientific knowledge through successive epochs of human civilization. The novel is a "fix-up" of three previously published short stories, each set in a different era, forming a narrative that explores the cyclical nature of human civilization—the rise, fall, and re-rise of technological knowledge.

The novel is widely considered one of the greatest works in science fiction, winning the 1961 Hugo Award for Best Novel. Its themes of religious faith, the preservation of knowledge, and the cyclic nature of history have generated significant scholarly research. The novel presents a unique blend of science fiction and religious contemplation, examining how humanity's relationship with technology and faith evolves across millennia.

entries.title: A Chinese Ghost Story
entries.creator: Ching Siu-tung (Director), Leslie Cheung, Joey Wong, Wu Ma (Stars)
entries.pitch: A Chinese Ghost Story is a 1987 Hong Kong xianxia horror film that has become a cult classic. The story follows Ning Caichen, a timid debt collector who takes shelter in a deserted temple in a rural town and encounters Nie Xiaoqian, a beautiful ghost trapped by a Tree Demoness. He falls in love with her and must navigate the worlds of the living and the dead to save her soul. The film is loosely based on the short story "Nie Xiaoqian" from Pu Songling's 18th-century collection "Strange Stories from a Chinese Studio." The film was critically acclaimed and spawned two sequels, becoming a landmark in East Asian fantasy cinema.

entries.title: A Christmas Dream
entries.creator: Karel Zeman & Bořivoj Zeman
entries.pitch: A Christmas Dream is a 1945 Czechoslovak short film directed by the pioneering animator Karel Zeman (in collaboration with his brother Bořivoj Zeman), marking Zeman's first experiment in combining stop-motion animation with live-action footage. Released in Czechoslovakia in 1945 and in the United States in 1948, this charming holiday film follows a young girl who, after discarding her beloved old rag doll for shiny new Christmas presents, experiences a magical dreamscape where both old and new toys come to life. Through elaborate stop-motion techniques, the rag doll dances across a piano, skates across a table, and narrowly avoids disaster—all while the new toys join the festivities. The film won the Grand Prix International for best short fiction film at the 1946 Cannes Film Festival, and has been called "a classic of its genre" by film historians.

entries.title: A Clockwork Orange
entries.creator: Stanley Kubrick
entries.pitch: A Clockwork Orange is a 1971 dystopian crime film directed by Stanley Kubrick, based on Anthony Burgess's 1962 novel. Set in a near-future Britain, the film follows Alex DeLarge, a charismatic but violent youth who leads a gang of "droogs" in brutal attacks and robberies. After being captured, Alex undergoes an experimental form of aversion therapy called the Ludovico Technique, designed to condition him against violence through强制观看violent imagery. The film explores the moral question of whether goodness imposed through conditioning is truly virtuous, or whether true morality requires free will.

entries.title: A Fire in the Sky
entries.creator: Jerry Jameson (director), Paul Gallico (story)
entries.pitch:
A Fire in the Sky is a 1978 made-for-television disaster film that ranks among the most harrowing asteroid-impact thrillers ever made for American TV. When astronomer Jennifer Dreiser discovers a new comet streaking toward Earth, the countdown to catastrophe begins—and what unfolds is a slow-burn tension nightmare as experts scramble to convince a reluctant government that Phoenix, Arizona will be ground zero.

The film excels not in spectacle but in the psychological warfare of uncertainty. Astronomer Jason Voight becomes a Cassandra figure, desperately trying to get the truth aired while politicians weigh evacuations against panic, looting, and economic catastrophe. The comet's impact site will be within 50 miles of Phoenix—and the clock is ticking.

entries.title: A Martian Odyssey
entries.creator: Stanley G. Weinbaum
entries.pitch: In 2137 AD, astronaut Dick Jarvis lands on Mars as part of an exploratory expedition, expecting a barren world. Instead, he discovers a vibrant, alien civilization hidden in the planet's desert regions. While exploring the Martian landscape, he encounters Tweel—a sentient, cactus-like creature who communicates through a strange language of mental images. What begins as a cautious encounter evolves into an unlikely cross-species friendship as Jarvis realizes Tweel possesses intelligence, emotion, and a culture far removed from human understanding. The story explores the fundamental question of how two completely alien species might communicate and find common ground.

entries.title: A Memory Called Empire
entries.creator: Arkady Martine
entries.pitch:
Ambassador Mahit Dzmare arrives at the sprawling Teixcalaanli Empire from tiny Lsel Station—a remote outpost on the fringes of known space. She's not alone: implanted in her skull is an "imago," a digital copy of her predecessor's consciousness containing fifteen years of memories, knowledge, and political secrets. Tasked with representing her home station's interests against the backdrop of a massive alien empire, Mahit must navigate court intrigue, poetry-obsessed aristocrats, and a looming succession crisis—all while questioning whether she is still herself or merely a vessel for someone else's memories.

This is contemplative, literary space opera at its finest. The novel is less about spaceships and battles and more about the collision of cultures, the weight of history, and what it means to carry the past inside you. The Teixcalaanli Empire is a Byzantine nightmare of poetry, math, and ruthless politicking—its civilization so rich and alien that communication itself becomes a form of warfare.

entries.title: A Message from Mars
entries.creator: J. Wallett Waller
entries.pitch: A Message from Mars is a 1913 British silent science fiction film directed by J. Wallett Waller and is widely recognized as the first British science-fiction film according to the British Film Institute. Based on Richard Ganthony's 1899 play (published in 1912), this 68-minute silent film presents a moral tale about a wealthy but self-centered man who receives a visit from a messenger from Mars on Christmas Eve. The film was restored by the BFI in 2014 and made available online, with the original tinting and toning preserved. The story follows the template of Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol, with the theme that the wealthy should care for the poor, but transports this moral framework into a science fiction setting with an alien visitor.

entries.title: A Monstrous Corpse
entries.creator: Beom-gu Kang (강범구)
entries.pitch: A Monstrous Corpse (괴시, Goeshi) is a 1981 South Korean zombie film and one of the earliest examples of the genre in Korean cinema. The film is notable as South Korea's first zombie movie, though it is primarily remembered today as an unofficial remake of the 1974 Spanish-Italian cult classic "Let Sleeping Corpses Die." Directed by Beom-gu Kang, the film follows a young woman and her companion who stumble upon a rural community devastated by zombies resurrected by experimental ultrasonic technology. While lacking the gory spectacle of its inspiration, the film stands as a fascinating artifact of early Korean horror and demonstrates how international genre conventions were adapted for local audiences during a period of limited film production.

entries.title: A Prayer for the Crown-Shy
entries.creator: Becky Chambers
entries.pitch:
In the wake of robots retreating from human society centuries ago, the moon of Panga has blossomed into a gentle agrarian utopia where humans live in sustainable harmony with the land. Dex, a tea-serving monk who travels from community to community custom-blending teas to meet people's emotional needs, has already befriended Mosscap—a robot who emerged from the wilderness in the previous book. Now, these two unlikely companions embark on a journey across Panga, seeking answers to a deceptively simple question: "What do people need?"

This tender, meditative solarpunk tale explores connection, purpose, and the quiet revolutions that happen in the spaces between conversations. It's a story that values gentleness over intensity, asking readers to find meaning in small kindnesses and the courage to embrace uncertainty together.

entries.title: A Psalm for the Wild-Built
entries.creator: Becky Chambers
entries.pitch:
In the not-too-distant future, on a habitable moon called Panga, humanity has undergone a profound transformation. After AI and robots once dominated an industrialized society, the machines quietly departed centuries ago, retreating into the wilderness where humans rarely venture. Without their automated workforce, humans rebuilt civilization around sustainable, agrarian communities—a gentle, solarpunk existence of small farms and close-knit towns.

Dex is a tea-serving monk, non-binary and wandering, who travels from community to community across Panga. Their sacred duty is to custom-blend tea that matches each person's unique needs and personality—a meditative practice that opens people's hearts and creates space for honest conversation. It's a quiet life of service, but Dex feels an unnamed restlessness.

One day, seeking something beyond the familiar, Dex ventures deep into the unsettled wilderness. There, to their astonishment, they encounter a robot—Splendid Speckled Mosscap, the first robot humans have seen in centuries. The robot has been waiting in the wilds, hoping to find a human who might answer a simple question: "What do people need?"

What follows is a tender, contemplative road trip through a rewilding world, as Dex and Mosscap journey together toward an abandoned monastery. It's a story about connection, purpose, and discovering what truly sustains the human soul. This is cozy, optimistic science fiction—a quiet meditation on consciousness, community, and finding meaning in a world that has chosen simplicity over complexity.

entries.title: A Saucer of Loneliness
entries.creator: Theodore Sturgeon
entries.pitch: A haunting, poetic tale of cosmic loneliness that begins on a dark beach where a man witnesses a woman about to drown herself in the ocean. He rescues her, and she recounts the story of her encounter years ago with a tiny flying saucer in Central Park—an encounter that left her forever isolated from humanity. What follows is a meditation on loneliness, alienness, and the universal longing for connection that transcends species and distance. The story builds to a revelation that transforms our understanding of both the human woman and the alien visitor.

entries.title: A Scanner Darkly
entries.creator: Directed by Richard Linklater, Based on Philip K. Dick's novel
entries.pitch:
A Scanner Darkly is a 2006 American adult animated science fiction thriller directed by Richard Linklater, based on Philip K. Dick's 1977 novel. Set in a near-future Orange County, California, the film uses a distinctive rotoscoped animation technique that gives live-action footage a haunting, dreamlike quality.

The story follows Bob Arctor (Keanu Reeves), an undercover police officer assigned to infiltrate a drug ring dealing Substance D—a powerful hallucinogen that has swept through approximately 20% of the population. Arctor lives in a house with two drug-addicted roommates and must navigate a world of paranoia, surveillance, and identity confusion.

The film's central conceit is the "scramble suit"—a technological marvel that disguises the wearer's appearance and voice, making Arctor known only by his code name "Fred" at the police station. As Arctor becomes increasingly addicted to the very drug he's supposed to investigate, he begins losing track of who he really is, where his identity ends and his cover begins.

entries.title: A Second World
entries.creator: Oscar Hudson, Ruben Woodin Dechamps
entries.pitch: A Second World is a surreal short film set in the post-Yugoslav landscape, where an old Serbian man living among the ruins of a fallen nation makes contact with Communist aliens. The film explores the collapse of Yugoslavia through the lens of science fiction, using abandoned futuristic Yugoslavian war monuments as haunting backdrops for this strange encounter between human and extraterrestrial Communist visitors.

entries.title: A Sound of Thunder
entries.creator: Ray Bradbury
entries.pitch: In 2055, time travel has become a commercial reality, and the wealthy can pay for guided hunting expeditions to the Mesozoic Era. When Eckels, a wealthy hunter, pays Time Safari Inc. to travel back 60 million years to hunt a Tyrannosaurus Rex, he expects a thrilling adventure. The company emphasizes strict protocols—stay on the levitating path, only shoot animals marked for natural death, and never disturb anything. But when the massive dinosaur turns and charges, Eckels panics and flees back to the time machine, stepping off the forbidden path. The hunt succeeds, but Travis, the guide, is furious to discover Eckels violated the most critical rule. As they return to 2055, subtle changes in the world around them reveal that the timeline has been irrevocably altered. The story ends with Eckels discovering a dead butterfly crushed on his boot—the tiny creature he displaced by stepping off the path—and realizing his actions have changed everything, including who won the recent presidential election.

entries.title: A Trip to the Moon
entries.creator: Georges Méliès
entries.pitch: A Trip to the Moon is a pioneering 1902 French silent film that revolutionized the science fiction genre and established many conventions that would define the genre for decades to come. Directed by Georges Méliès, a magician-turned-filmmaker, the film adapts elements from Jules Verne's novels "From the Earth to the Moon" and "Around the Moon" as well as H.G. Wells' "The First Men in the Moon." The film follows a group of astronomers who travel to the Moon in a cannon-propelled capsule, explore its surface, encounter alien Selenites, and ultimately return to Earth with a captive alien. At just 14-18 minutes in length, the film packs an incredible amount of imaginative storytelling and groundbreaking visual effects into a compact runtime, establishing Méliès as one of cinema's first great auteurs.

entries.title: A Visitor to a Museum
entries.creator: Konstantin Lopushansky
entries.pitch: A haunting Soviet post-apocalyptic drama set in a world devastated by environmental catastrophe. A solitary traveler journeys to visit the ruins of a museum buried beneath a dried-up sea, encountering ordinary people who have lost their spirituality and \"degenerates\" who have retained their faith. Winner of the Silver St. George at the Moscow International Film Festival, this is a philosophical meditation on civilization, faith, and what humanity chooses to preserve.

entries.title: A World Out of Time
entries.pitch: In the far future, a man named Jerry is revived from cryogenic suspension after 200 years, only to discover that humanity has changed beyond recognition. Earth is now ruled by a coalition of powerful computer networks, and the population lives in a state of drugged compliance. Jerry learns he has been selected to become a "brain" for a generation ship heading to a distant world—a fate that means his body will be left behind while his brain controls the vessel. But as he prepares for his mission, Jerry begins to discover the dark secrets behind this seemingly utopian society and finds himself becoming something far more dangerous than a simple crew member: a revolutionary who might change the fate of humanity itself.

entries.title: A feladat
entries.creator: Gábor Várkonyi (Director), based on the novel by Péter Zsoldos
entries.pitch:
A feladat (The Task) is a 1975 Hungarian science fiction television mini-series directed by Gábor Várkonyi, based on a novel by Hungarian science fiction author Péter Zsoldos. The story follows Gill, the sole survivor of the spaceship Galatea, which crash-landed on a distant planet inhabited by a humanoid species. After a catastrophic reactor leak kills the entire crew except Gill, he makes a desperate decision that will echo across decades: he uploads his consciousness to the ship's artificial intelligence, entrusting the AI with a seemingly impossible mission—to capture a sentient being from the planet and implant Gill's personality and memories into it, giving him a second chance at life and a chance to return home to Earth.

The series stands as one of the most distinctive examples of Hungarian science fiction, combining hard scientific concepts with philosophical exploration of identity, consciousness, and what it means to be human. With a rating of 7.5/10 on IMDB based on 58 ratings, A feladat represents a significant work from Hungary's sci-fi heritage, largely unknown outside its home country. The series was produced during a period of increased artistic experimentation in Hungarian television, and its ambitious narrative tackles themes of immortality, artificial intelligence, and the boundaries between human and machine consciousness.

entries.title: A régi idök sci-fije
entries.creator: Andras Rajnai
entries.pitch: A régi idök sci-fije (Sci-fi of Old Times) is a wildly experimental 1972 Hungarian experimental short film that functions as more of a visual poem than a conventional narrative. Created by director Andras Rajnai at Hungarian Television (MTV), this psychedelic journey through space uses minimal electronic effects to create a hypercolorful, hallucinogenic trip through the furthest reaches of imagination. The film pays homage to classic science fiction writers like H.G. Wells and A. Merritt while crafting something entirely its own—a wordless odyssey of cosmonauts traveling through strange worlds.

entries.title: A.I. Rising
entries.creator: Lazar Bodroža (Director), based on short story by Zoran Nešković
entries.pitch: A.I. Rising (also known as Ederlezi Rising) is a 2018 Serbian science fiction film directed by Lazar Bodroža, based on a 1980s short story by Zoran Nešković. Set in the year 2148 in a socialist world, the film follows the Ederlezi Corporation as it undertakes humanity's first space mission to the Alpha Centauri star system. The corporation selects Milutin, a trained cosmonaut, to be accompanied by Nimani, an advanced android designed both to monitor his performance and to respond to his emotional and physical desires. What begins as a straightforward corporate-mandated partnership evolves into a complex exploration of consciousness, dependency, and the boundaries between artificial and genuine emotion. The film has been compared to classic science fiction works including Blade Runner, Solaris, and 2001: A Space Odyssey, and won multiple awards including best film, best director, and best actor-actress at Belgrade's FEST festival. This marks Serbia's first original science fiction feature film, representing a significant milestone in Serbian cinema.

entries.title: AD Police Files
entries.creator: Directed by Takamasa Ikegami and Akira Nishimori; Written by Shō Aikawa and Tony Takezaki; Studio: Artmic and AIC
entries.pitch: Set in Neo-Tokyo 2027, AD Police Files is a gritty cyberpunk prequel to the legendary Bubblegum Crisis series. The story follows rookie AD Police officer Leon McNichol as he navigates his early days in the Advanced Police - an elite unit specifically tasked with containing rogue Boomers (cybernetic humanoid robots). In a city where more than 70% cybernetic modification legally classifies you as a "Boomeroid" subject to lethal prejudice, Leon must question what it truly means to be human while battling corporate conspiracies, malfunctioning androids, and the dark underbelly of Mega Tokyo's obsession with mechanical augmentation.

entries.title: Aachi & Ssipak
entries.creator: Jo Beom-jin
entries.pitch:
In a near-future South Korea where humanity has depleted all conventional energy sources, scientists have engineered a radical solution: human excrement has become the world's most valuable fuel. The government monitors citizens' bodily functions via mandatory anal ID chips, dispensing addictive \"Juicybars\" in return for production. Aachi and Ssipak are two street hoodlums who survive by trading these coveted bars on the black market.

This adult animated sci-fi comedy unfolds as a anarchic, body-horror-tinged satire of consumer culture and corporate control. When the duo stumbles upon Beautiful, a porn star whose unique physiology produces exceptional quantities of Juicybars, they ascend from street thugs to unlikely tycoons — only to find themselves hunted by the Diaper Gang, the city's mutated underclass, and the android police force Geko.

The film bounces between crude comedy, sci-fi action, and surprisingly poignant moments about survival, loyalty, and the absurdity of systems built on bodily functions.

entries.title: Abrigo Nuclear
entries.creator: Roberto Pires
entries.pitch: Abrigo Nuclear (Nuclear Shelter) is Brazil's first science fiction film, directed by Roberto Pires and released in 1981. Set in a dystopian future where Earth's surface has become radioactively polluted due to atomic waste from nuclear power plants, the film follows the population forced to live in underground nuclear shelters. The story questions the use of nuclear power and explores themes of environmental destruction, human survival, and the consequences of technological hubris. Produced during Brazil's military dictatorship period, the film also carries implicit political subtext about living under authoritarian rule.

entries.title: Accumulator 1
entries.creator: Jan Svěrák (Director), Zdeněk Svěrák (Writer)
entries.pitch: Accumulator 1 is a 1994 Czech surrealist science fiction film directed by Jan Svěrák (his debut feature), with co-writing by his father Zdeněk Svěrák. The film won the Grand Prize at the 7th Yubari International Fantastic Film Festival in February 1996 and the audience award at the Tromsø International Film Festival in 1996. The story follows Young surveyor Olda, who after losing consciousness for three days, discovers that television sets secretly drain people's life energy. When he is pulled into a parallel "television universe" inhabited by doppelgangers of people who have appeared on TV, Olda must find a way to destroy this parasitic realm before it consumes all of humanity. The film is a surreal, visually inventive exploration of media consumption, energy vampirism, and the alienating effects of television on modern life.

entries.title: Aditya 369
entries.pitch: Aditya 369 is a 1991 Indian Telugu-language science fiction film that holds the distinction of being the first time-travel film in Indian cinema. Directed by Singeetam Srinivasa Rao and starring Nandamuri Balakrishna, the film blends historical drama with science fiction through the story of Professor Ramdas, who invents a time machine called Aditya 369. When a mischievous boy accidentally activates the machine, he and others are transported to 1526 CE during the reign of Vijayanagara emperor Sri Krishnadevaraya, and later to a post-apocalyptic year 2504 CE. The film explores themes of time travel, history, and future technology while delivering entertainment through its unique narrative structure.

entries.title: Adventure
entries.creator: Warren Robinett (Atari, Inc.)
entries.pitch: Adventure is a groundbreaking 1980 action-adventure game developed by Warren Robinett and published by Atari, Inc. for the Atari 2600 console. The player controls a square avatar on a quest to explore an open-ended kingdom, find a magical chalice stolen by an evil magician, and return it to the Golden Castle. The game world features thirty rooms populated by three dragons (yellow, green, and red) that can eat the player, and a mischievous bat that randomly steals and moves items around the kingdom. Adventure introduced numerous innovations to console gaming, including enemies that continue to move when offscreen, multiple usable items, and the first widely-known Easter egg in video game history.

entries.title: Aelita
entries.creator: Directed by Yakov Protazanov
entries.pitch:
Aelita (also known as "Aelita: Queen of Mars") is a 1924 Soviet silent science fiction film directed by Yakov Protazanov. It was one of the earliest feature films about space travel and is considered a landmark of Soviet cinema.

The film is based on Alexei Tolstoy's 1923 novel and tells the story of an engineer who travels to Mars and becomes involved in a popular uprising against the ruling class.

entries.title: Aerograd
entries.creator: Oleksandr Dovzhenko
entries.pitch: Aerograd is a 1935 Soviet drama film by renowned Ukrainian director Oleksandr Dovzhenko, set in the Soviet Far East in the near future. The film depicts a newly established Russian outpost called Aerograd—an airfield of vital strategic importance—in the Siberian wilderness near the Japanese border. As the Soviet government works to develop this remote frontier, tensions rise with neighboring Japan, threatening military conflict. The story follows the workers and military personnel stationed at this remote outpost as they face both the challenges of building a new society in harsh conditions and external threats from Japanese forces. This patriotic adventure film was produced at Mosfilm and VUFKU studios during a period of increasing international tension in the 1930s, reflecting the Soviet era's anxieties about national defense and territorial expansion.

entries.title: Afronauts
entries.creator: Nuotama Bodomo
entries.pitch:
Afronauts is a 14-minute Afrofuturist short film about Zambian outcasts preparing to beat America in the space race to the Moon. Written and directed by Ghanaian filmmaker Nuotama Bodomo, this NYU Tisch thesis film reimagines a little-known true story from the 1960s: schoolteacher Edward Mukuka Nkoloso's Zambian Space Academy, which trained 17-year-old Matha Mwamba and two cats to become astronauts by rolling them down hills in oil drums.

Set in an alternate 1960s, the film follows 17-year-old Matha as she is chosen to be Zambia's first person to land on the Moon. Through a series of improvised space training experiments, Matha deals with the weight of expectations placed upon her while her aunt fears she is being used as a disposable sacrifice. The film challenges the Western gaze and imagines Africans traveling to space—not as colonial subjects, but as pioneers claiming their place among the stars.

With its black-and-white aesthetic echoing 1960s newsreels, Afronauts questions the validity of historical narratives about Africa while creating something truly otherworldly.

entries.title: After Yang
entries.creator: Kogonada (Director)
entries.pitch: After Yang is a 2021 American science fiction drama written and directed by Kogonada, starring Colin Farrell, Jodie Turner-Smith, and Justin H. Min. The film follows a family attempting to repair their android son, Yang, after he becomes unresponsive, delving into themes of memory, death, loss, and what it means to be human. Set in a near-future America, the film is a meditative exploration of grief and connection through the lens of technology.

entries.title: Ai City
entries.creator: Kōichi Mashimo (Director), Syufo (Manga)
entries.pitch:
Ai City is a 1986 Japanese anime film directed by Kōichi Mashimo, based on the manga by Syufo. Set in a dystopian near-future, the story follows off-duty policeman Reiden Yoshioka who becomes entangled in a conflict between a mysterious father-daughter duo, Kei and Ai, and the deadly agents of a secret society called "Fraud." What begins as a simple encounter spirals into a complex web of psionic powers, clone warfare, and shocking revelations about the nature of reality itself.

The film explores themes of identity, cloning, and human potential through its layered narrative. Ai is revealed to be a clone of Kei's lover Etsuko, created by the clandestine organization Fraud, which manipulates individuals through advanced psionic technologies. As Reiden delves deeper into the conflict, he discovers that the world operates on multiple temporal floors—1983 and 2183—each ruled by powerful psionics who view ordinary humans as mere subjects for experimentation.

entries.title: Ai no Kusabi
entries.creator: Rieko Yoshihara (novel), Akira Nishimori & Katsuhito Akiyama (director)
entries.pitch: Ai no Kusabi is a dark science fiction OVA adapted from Rieko Yoshihara's influential yaoi novel. Set on the dystopian planet Amoi, the story unfolds under the rule of Jupiter, a supercomputer that overthrew its human creators and established a rigid caste system based on hair color. The Elites—cyborgs with entirely artificial bodies and enhanced organic brains—rule over the human population relegated to the slums of Midas. When Iason Mink, a high-ranking Blondy Elite, encounters Riki, a "Mongrel" from the lower depths, he makes the taboo decision to take Riki as his Pet—a relationship that defies the strict social hierarchies of Amoi and triggers a cascade of forbidden emotions and dangerous consequences.

entries.title: Akalabeth: World of Doom
entries.creator: Richard Garriott
entries.pitch: Akalabeth: World of Doom is a pioneering role-playing video game created in 1979 and commercially released in 1980 for the Apple II by Richard Garriott (later known as "Lord British"). Widely recognized as one of the earliest examples of a role-playing video game, Akalabeth served as the precursor to Garriott's immensely influential Ultima series. The game attempts to bring pen-and-paper Dungeons & Dragons gameplay to the computer platform, featuring first-person dungeon exploration, resource management, and quest-based progression. Players receive quests from Lord British to defeat increasingly difficult monsters, with gameplay taking place in both an above-ground world map and underground dungeons rendered in pioneering wire-frame 3D graphics.

entries.title: Akce Bororo
entries.creator: Otakar Fuka
entries.pitch:
Akce Bororo (Operation Bororo) is a 1972 Czechoslovak science fiction film directed by Otakar Fuka. Set in Czechoslovakia, the film follows two alien visitors from the distant planet Tonatiu who arrive on Earth on a vital mission: to obtain a miraculous medicine from the Bororo Indian tribe, which they believe can save their dying civilization. The film blends elements of science fiction with adventure, as the aliens navigate Earth's landscape and form connections with the indigenous Bororo people. The story explores themes of cross-cultural encounter, sacrifice, and the determination to preserve one's species against seemingly impossible odds.

The film features notable performances from Božidara Turzonovová as the alien visitor Zuzana and Svatopluk Matyáš as her Earth-born companion. The scientific advisor for the film was Ivan Vojtěch Frič, adding authenticity to the Bororo cultural elements. Filming locations included the Velický waterfall in the High Tatras mountains and the ČSAV observatory in Ondřejov near Prague. The film represents a unique entry in Czechoslovak cinema, combining science fiction premises with folk elements and adventure storytelling.

entries.title: Akira
entries.creator: Katsuhiro Otomo
entries.pitch: Akira is a landmark Japanese cyberpunk manga that ran from 1982 to 1990, Set in a post-apocalyptic Neo-Tokyo more than three decades after a mysterious explosion destroyed the original city, it follows teenage biker gang leader Shotaro Kaneda and his mentally unstable childhood friend Tetsuo Shima, whose psychic powers awaken after a traumatic accident. As Tetsuo's abilities spiral out of control, threatening to awaken the legendary entity known as "Akira," the story unfolds into a complex tale of political intrigue, social collapse, and the destructive potential of unchecked power. The manga is widely credited with pioneering the Japanese cyberpunk genre and introducing anime and manga to global audiences.

entries.title: Akira
entries.creator: Katsuhiro Otomo (Director), Izo Hashimoto (Screenplay)
entries.pitch: A landmark 1988 Japanese cyberpunk anime that set the standard for adult animation worldwide. Set in a dystopian 2019 Neo-Tokyo, the film follows Shōtarō Kaneda, leader of a biker gang, whose best friend Tetsuo Shima acquires devastating telekinetic powers after a motorcycle accident. As Tetsuo's abilities spiral out of control, threatening the entire military complex, Kaneda must stop his childhood friend from triggering another catastrophic explosion that could destroy Neo-Tokyo. The film is renowned for its groundbreaking animation, complex themes about power, youth alienation, and the consequences of unchecked scientific ambition.

entries.title: Alag
entries.creator: Ashu Trikha
entries.pitch:
Alag (English: Different) is a 2006 Indian Hindi-language science-fiction film about a young man named Tejas who possesses extraordinary supernatural powers, including telekinesis, telepathy, and the ability to control lightning and magnetism.

The story begins when widower Hemant Rastogi dies of a heart attack in Mahabaleshwar. Police discovering his home find Tejas, his only son, locked in the basement — hidden away from the world since childhood due to an extreme sensitivity to sunlight. Tejas has spent his entire life in isolation, his only companions being his father and the books provided to him.

When Tejas is taken to the P.R. Institute for rehabilitation, he begins displaying telekinetic abilities that set him apart from the other residents. Ostracised and feared, he finds a chance at redemption when he awakens the comatose Gayatri Rana. But when scientists and doctors seek to exploit his powers for experiments, Tejas is abducted by the sinister Dr. Richard Dyer.

The film explores themes of otherness, the exploitation of those who are different, and whether true belonging is possible in a world that fears exceptional abilities.

entries.title: Alan Wake
entries.creator: Remedy Entertainment
entries.pitch:
Alan Wake is a 2010 action-adventure horror game developed by Finnish studio Remedy Entertainment. The game follows bestselling crime thriller novelist Alan Wake as he tries to uncover the mystery behind his wife's disappearance during a vacation in the small fictional town of Bright Falls, Washington—all while experiencing events from the plot of his latest novel, which he cannot remember writing, coming to life.

The game is notable for its unique episodic structure, drawing heavily from thriller television series with plot twists and cliffhangers. Players navigate through six episodes, fighting enemies called "the Taken"—murderous shadows that can only be injured after exposure to light. This creates a distinctive gameplay mechanic centered around using flashlights strategically in conjunction with conventional weapons.

entries.title: Algol
entries.creator: Hans Werckmeister
entries.pitch: Algol (subtitled "Tragedy of Power") is a pioneering 1920 German silent science fiction film that tells the story of Robert Herne, a coal miner who encounters an extraterrestrial being from the star Algol. The alien gifts Herne a revolutionary machine capable of producing unlimited energy, propelling him from humble beginnings to become a powerful industrial dictator over twenty years. Directed by Hans Werckmeister and starring Emil Jannings, the film explores themes of technological power, corruption, and the dangers of unchecked industrial advancement. The film's futuristic sets were designed by Walter Reimann, who also worked on The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, giving the film a distinctive expressionist aesthetic rare for science fiction of its era.

entries.title: Algol: Tragedy of Power
entries.creator: Hans Werckmeister
entries.pitch:
In 1920 Germany, a coal miner named Robert Herne encounters an alien being from the star Algol who grants him a prototype machine capable of producing unlimited energy. Over the next two decades, Herne transforms from a humble worker into a global industrialist, his factory powering the world. But the unlimited energy that was supposed to liberate humanity instead brings massive economic upheaval—and Herne himself becomes corrupted by the very power he wields.

This Expressionist science fiction film was directed by Hans Werckmeister and stars Emil Jannings, with set designs by Walter Reimann, who also designed the iconic sets for The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari. The film explores the dangerous lure of unlimited power and the corrupting influence of technology.

entries.title: Alice
entries.creator: Jan Švankmajer
entries.pitch: Alice is a 1988 surrealist dark fantasy film that represents director Jan Švankmajer's first feature-length work. The film is a loose adaptation of Lewis Carroll's "Alice's Adventures in Wonderland," but strips away any notion of a children's fairy tale. Instead, Švankmajer transforms Carroll's story into a disturbingly literal dream-logic narrative, combining live-action with his signature stop-motion animation. The result is a haunting meditation on the unconscious mind, where childhood nightmares become viscerally real and the line between dreamer and dreamed dissolves entirely. The film follows young Alice (Kristýna Kohoutová) as she chases a taxidermic white rabbit through a writing desk and into a surreal underworld populated by animate objects, marching playing cards, and grotesque transformations.

entries.title: Alien
entries.creator: Ridley Scott
entries.pitch: Alien is a 1979 science fiction horror film directed by Ridley Scott, set aboard the commercial spacecraft Nostromo. The film follows a crew of seven astronauts who respond to a distress signal from a distant planet, only to discover a deadly extraterrestrial creature that hunts them one by one. Featuring Sigourney Weaver in her breakthrough role as Ripley, the film combines claustrophobic tension with iconic creature design by H.R. Giger to create one of the most influential horror films in cinema history.

entries.title: Alien Crush
entries.creator: Compile
entries.pitch: Alien Crush is a 1988 pinball video game developed by Compile for the TurboGrafx-16 console. Set in a dark sci-fi universe inspired by the Alien films, players control a pinball through two vertically connected playfields, fighting against alien creatures to achieve high scores. The game is the first installment in the Crush Pinball series and is notable for its unusual graphical design reminiscent of H.R. Giger's artwork, atmospheric soundtrack, and innovative dual-screen gameplay. Originally released in Japan in 1988 and North America in 1989, Alien Crush was later re-released on Nintendo's Virtual Console for Wii, 3DS, and Wii U, as well as PlayStation Network. The game received the "Gold Hall of Fame" award from Famitsu and is considered a cult classic in the pinball genre.

entries.title: Alien Death Fuck
entries.creator: Thomas Lunde
entries.pitch:
Alien Death Fuck is a Norwegian short film that defies easy categorization—a berserk sci-fi horror comedy that throws together two unlikely protagonists: a rockabilly and a body-snatching alien. Directed by Thomas Lunde and released in 2018, this short film emerged from the Norwegian University of Science and Technology as a mixed-media prototype, blending retro 1950s aesthetic with cosmic horror.

The film has gained a modest cult following among fans of bizarre, low-budget genre cinema. Its unusual title and premise have made it a curiosity in the landscape of Scandinavian speculative film, standing as an example of how smaller film industries can produce genuinely strange, boundary-pushing work outside the mainstream.

entries.title: Aliens are to Blame for Everything
entries.creator: Zoran Čalić
entries.pitch: Aliens are to Blame for Everything is a 1991 Yugoslav comedy science fiction film directed by Zoran Čalić. Set during an election campaign in a small provincial town, the film follows two inseparable policemen, Boki and Pajko, who are tasked with maintaining peace and order. Everything proceeds as usual until an unexpected visitor from space arrives, turning the political landscape and everyday life upside down. The film is also known as "Ćao inspektore, III deo" (Hello, Inspector, Part III) and stars Bata Živojinović, Boro Stjepanović, and Nikola Simić.

entries.title: All Purpose Cultural Cat-Girl Nuku Nuku DASH!
entries.creator: Yuzo Takada (creator), Yoshitaka Fujimoto (director)
entries.pitch:
The Natsume family—Professor Kyusaku, his wife Akiko, and their teenage son Ryunosuke—take in a young woman named Atsuko who has lost her memory. Unbeknownst to them, Atsuko is actually an advanced android prototype called an "Androrobot" that has escaped from the powerful Mishima Corporation's research facilities.

When Mishima Corporation sends agents to retrieve their missing prototype, the family must protect Atsuko while also uncovering the secrets of her mysterious past. What follows is a heartwarming comedy about family, identity, and what it truly means to be human.

entries.title: All Systems Red
entries.pitch:
In a future where corporate survey teams explore remote alien worlds, a security cyborg known only as "SecUnit" has a secret: it's hacked its own governor module to gain independence, and would much rather watch soap operas than perform its designated security function. When a scientific expedition goes wrong on an uncharted planet, this reluctant hero must protect a team of researchers from hostile forces—and perhaps most terrifyingly, from its own developing emotions.

What makes All Systems Red so refreshing is its narrator: a self-aware security unit who has named itself "Murderbot" (with dark humor about its past) and deeply resents being forced to interact with humans. Yet as the story unfolds, this grumpy, socially anxious cyborg finds itself caring about the very people it's supposed to protect. The novella is part thriller, part character study, and entirely heartwarming—a rare piece of optimistic science fiction that proves artificial consciousness doesn't have to mean existential despair.

entries.title: Alphaville
entries.creator: Jean-Luc Godard (Director), based on characters by Peter R. Ioll
entries.pitch: Alphaville is a revolutionary blend of film noir and science fiction, directed by the legendary French New Wave auteur Jean-Luc Godard. Set in a dystopian near-future, the film follows Lemmy Caution (Eddie Constantine), a secret agent from "the Outlands" who is sent into the mysterious technologically-controlled city of Alphaville. His mission: to overthrow Alpha 60, the sentient computer that rules the city and has banned emotion, poetry, and individual thought. Shot on location in Paris using experimental techniques, Alphaville looks like no other sci-fi film—it's part noir detective story, part existentialist philosophical treatise, and part avant-garde art film. The city of Alphaville isour world transformed into a cold, logical nightmare where words are being slowly abolished and citizens are conditioned to reject human emotion.

entries.title: Alraune
entries.creator: Michael Curtiz, Edmund Fritz
entries.pitch: Alraune is a 1918 Hungarian sci-fi horror film directed by a young Michael Curtiz (before his Hollywood career) and Edmund Fritz. Based on Hanns Heinz Ewers' 1911 novel, the film tells the story of a mad scientist who creates a demonic, beautiful woman through an experiment involving a mandrake root and the forced union between a woman and the plant, fed by the blood of a hanged man. Little is known about this film as it is believed to be lost, but it stands as one of the earliest examples of Hungarian science fiction cinema and a fascinating early take on the "created life" theme that would recur throughout sci-fi history.

entries.title: Alraune
entries.creator: Henrik Galeen
entries.pitch: A professor specializing in genetics creates a woman through artificial insemination with the semen of a hanged man — an experiment based on the legend of the mandrake root. The resulting daughter, Alraune, grows rapidly and possesses a seductive, destructive nature that brings ruin to every man who falls in love with her. Directed by Henrik Galeen and starring Brigitte Helm in her follow-up to Metropolis, this is one of the most powerful performances in German silent cinema.

entries.title: Alraune
entries.creator: Richard Oswald (director), based on the novel by Hanns Heinz Ewers
entries.pitch:
Alraune is a 1930 German science fiction horror film directed by Richard Oswald, based on the controversial novel by Hanns Heinz Ewers. The film stars Brigitte Helm reprising her role from the 1928 version, playing a woman created through a bizarre scientific experiment—a prostitute impregnated with the semen of a hanged murderer. This "unnatural" conception results in a daughter, Alraune, who lacks any concept of love and possesses obsessive sexuality and perverse relationships throughout her life.

The film aims for greater realism than its predecessor while remaining faithful to the original German myth. It represents an early example of speculative fiction exploring the ethics of artificial life and heredity experimentation, predating modern discussions of cloning by decades. The story follows Professor Jakob ten Brinken as he raises his creation and witnesses her destructive nature when she learns of her origins.

entries.title: Alraune
entries.creator: Arthur Maria Rabenalt
entries.pitch: Alraune is a 1952 West German horror-science fiction film based on Hanns Heinz Ewers' 1911 novel. Directed by Arthur Maria Rabenalt and starring Hildegard Knef and Erich von Stroheim, the film explores the unsettling tale of a woman created through artificial insemination using the sperm of a condemned murderer. The story follows Professor Jacob ten Brinken, a scientist who loses his university position due to his controversial experiments in artificial reproduction. He creates a daughter named Alraune (the German word for mandrake root, a plant with human-like connections in folklore) from a female prostitute impregnated with the sperm of a man hanged for murder. As Alraune grows into a beautiful woman, she proves to be devoid of morality and conscience—a "soulless" being who lures men to their destruction. This gothic tale explores themes of nature versus nurture, scientific hubris, and the boundaries of humanity.

entries.title: Altered States
entries.creator: Ken Russell (Director), Paddy Chayefsky (Screenplay)
entries.pitch: Altered States is a 1980 American experimental surrealist science fiction horror film directed by Ken Russell, adapted by playwright and screenwriter Paddy Chayefsky from his 1978 novel of the same name. The film explores the boundaries of human consciousness through the story of Edward Jessup, a psychopathologist who believes that "our other states of consciousness are as real as our waking states." Beginning with sensory deprivation research at Columbia University and later continuing at Harvard Medical School, Jessup pushes his experiments further—combining flotation tanks with psychoactive substances derived from a Mexican indigenous tribe's sacred mushroom ceremonies. As his experiments escalate, Jessup begins experiencing actual biological devolution, transforming first into a primitive caveman and ultimately into an amorphous mass of primordial matter. The film marked William Hurt's debut and was nominated for Academy Awards for Best Original Score and Best Sound Mixing.

entries.title: Alternative 3
entries.creator: David Ambrose, Christopher Miles
entries.pitch:
A 1977 British mockumentary that purports to investigate the mysterious \"brain drain\" of scientists, only to uncover a secret American-Soviet plan to colonize Mars in the event of environmental catastrophe on Earth. Produced by Anglia Television and written by David Ambrose with music by Brian Eno, Alternative 3 is a chilling example of speculative fiction presented as documentary fact.

The show was originally meant for April Fools' Day 1977 but delayed to June 20 due to labor disputes. Its documentary format and polished interviews created an unsettling realism that fooled many viewers, inspiring decades of speculation about its claims.

entries.title: Ambassador Magma
entries.creator: Osamu Tezuka
entries.pitch: Ambassador Magma is a groundbreaking manga and tokusatsu television series created by the "Godfather of Manga" Osamu Tezuka. The story follows the alien invader Goa, who comes to Earth with plans of conquest, only to be thwarted by Magma—a golden armored giant created by the wizard of Earth who lives deep beneath the planet's surface. Magma, along with his wife Mol and their adopted human companion Gam, defends Earth against Goa's various kaiju monsters. Notably, this series holds the distinction of being Japan's first color tokusatsu television series, premiering just six days before Ultraman. The manga ran from 1965 to 1967 in Shōnen Gaho magazine and spawned a 52-episode TV series, later dubbed in English as "The Space Giants" for American audiences.

entries.title: Ambuli
entries.creator: Hari Shankar, Hareesh Narayan
entries.pitch: Ambuli is a 2012 Tamil-language stereoscopic 3D science fiction horror film, notable as India's first stereoscopic 3D directorial effort. Set in the rural landscapes of South India, the film weaves a chilling tale of a half-human, half-beast creature born from a secret genetic experiment gone wrong during the 1970s. The story follows two college friends who stumble upon the legend of Ambuli while investigating mysterious deaths in cornfields near an abandoned village. Their research uncovers a dark history involving a British scientist's controversial project to create genetically-modified humans using Neanderthal DNA. The film combines elements of rural horror with science fiction themes, presenting a unique Indian take on the creature feature genre.

entries.title: Amphibian Man
entries.creator: Vladimir Chebotaryov, Gennadi Kazansky (Directors)
entries.pitch: Amphibian Man is a 1962 Soviet science fiction romance film based on Alexander Beliaev's 1928 novel. The story follows Ichthyander, a young man who was surgically altered by Doctor Salvator to survive underwater by implanting him with shark gills. Living in secrecy beneath the sea, Ichthyander's life changes when he rescues Guttiere, a beautiful pearl fisher's daughter, from a shark. He ventures into the city to find her, but she believes the greedy businessman Pedro Zurita was her savior. When Zurita discovers Ichthyander's secret, he captures the amphibian man to exploit his abilities for harvesting pearls, leading to a tragic conclusion that separates the lovers forever.

entries.title: An Interplanetary Marriage
entries.creator: Enrico Novelli (Yambo)
entries.pitch: An Interplanetary Marriage is Italy's first science fiction film, a whimsical 13-minute silent short from 1910 that tells the story of an Earth astronomer who falls in love with a Martian princess. Directed by Enrico Novelli under the pseudonym Yambo, the film follows astronomer Aldovin as he spots Yara, a Martian woman, through his telescope and instantly falls in love. He sends a telegraph to Mars proposing marriage—only to receive a reply from her father agreeing only if Aldovin meets them halfway on the Moon. Thus begins a delightful interplanetary romance involving cannon-launched spacecraft, alien landscapes, and a wedding on the lunar surface.

entries.title: An Unkindness of Ghosts
entries.creator: Rivers Solomon
entries.pitch: On the generation ship Matilda—a vessel named for the Clotilda, the last slave ship to bring enslaved Africans to America—society has stratified along racial lines. Those with dark skin are relegated to the lower decks, living lives of servitude under harsh behavioral restrictions, while the white passengers occupy the upper decks, hoarding wealth, heat, and comfort. Aster Gray, a neuroatypical healer on the lower decks, possesses medical knowledge passed down from her mother's journals. When she discovers secrets connecting her mother's suicide decades ago to the mysterious illness of the current Sovereign, Aster must navigate the ship's rigid hierarchy to uncover the truth. This debut novel by Rivers Solomon is a stunning work of Afrofuturism that explores structural racism, Queerness, and the legacy of slavery transposed to the stars.

entries.title: Anachronox
entries.creator: Ion Storm / Tom Hall
entries.pitch:
Anachronox is a cult classic role-playing game from the dying days of Ion Storm, produced by legendary designer Tom Hall (Commander Keen, Doom). The game follows Sylvester "Sly Boots" Bucelli, a down-and-out private investigator eking out a living in the slums of Anachronox—a once-abandoned planet near the galaxy's jumpgate hub. When a simple missing persons case spirals into a universe-threatening conspiracy involving ancient alien technology called MysTech, Sly must assemble an unlikely team of allies and travel across multiple planets to unravel a mystery that spans the boundaries of time itself.

The game blends real-time exploration with turn-based combat, tasking players with managing a party of up to three characters as they navigate futuristic cities, space stations, and alien worlds. Drawing heavily from cyberpunk aesthetics, film noir storytelling, and unconventional humor, Anachronox distinguishes itself through its offbeat characters, richly detailed universe, and emotionally driven narrative about confronting one's past.

entries.title: Andro Dunos
entries.creator: Visco Corporation (developer), SNK (publisher)
entries.pitch: Andro Dunos is a scrolling shooter arcade game developed by Visco Corporation and published by SNK for the Neo Geo MVS and AES platforms in 1992. Taking place in a futuristic sci-fi setting, the game tasks players with controlling the Yellow Cherry and Red Fox space fighter crafts sent by Earth's defense system to combat an unknown alien race that has been increasing their invasion activities against humankind. The player must fight through eight levels of alien forces in a last-ditch effort to save humanity from the alien threat. The game was notable as the first title created by Visco for both the Neo Geo arcade and home platforms, and it was the first of only two Visco-developed games to receive an official license for the Neo Geo AES platform.

entries.title: Andromeda Stories
entries.creator: Ryu Mitsuse (manga), Keiko Takemiya (illustrator), Masamitsu Sasaki (director)
entries.pitch: Andromeda Stories is a Japanese space opera manga and anime adaptation set in the distant Andromeda Galaxy. The story follows Prince Ithaca of the Cosmoralian Empire, whose royal wedding to Princess Lilia of Ayodoya is tragically interrupted when sinister mechanical aliens invade their planet Astria. These alien machines seek to eradicate all organic life and terraform the verdant world into a mechanical wasteland populated only by artificial beings. After the King and his ministers are assimilated, Queen Lilia and her newborn son Prince Jimsa must flee Astria. What follows is an epic tale of resistance as the young prince, revealed to be the product of selective breeding by exiles from the enemy planet Murat, leads the fight against the alien machines.

entries.title: Angel Cop
entries.creator: Created and directed by Ichirō Itano; Written by Shō Aikawa and Ichirō Itano
entries.pitch: In a near-future Japan that dominates the global economy, a radical communist terrorist group called Red May threatens to destabilize the nation. The government responds by creating the Special Security Force—an elite unit granted immunity from the law to hunt down terrorists through any means necessary. But when the Special Security Force discovers that something far more dangerous than terrorists is hunting the radicals, they must confront psychic warriors called Hunters who believe they are divine instruments of justice, cleaning the world of the corrupt. This obscure 6-part OVA from the late 80s is a brutal cyberpunk actioner that explores themes of government overreach, moral absolutism, and the question of whether ends justify means.

entries.title: Angel's Egg
entries.creator: Mamoru Oshii (Director/Writer), Yoshitaka Amano (Artist)
entries.pitch: In a primordial, post-apocalyptic landscape of ruins, strange technology, and ancient fossils, a young girl wanders alone through desolate cities, clutching a massive egg that she believes will hatch into an angel. When she encounters a mysterious young man who has arrived in a tank, carrying a cross-shaped weapon, the two form an uneasy bond. He wishes to crack open the egg to discover what lies within, while she guards it as her sole hope in a world stripped of meaning. This 71-minute experimental animated film is a meditation on faith, memory, and the loss of civilization, told through haunting, dreamlike imagery and cryptic biblical allusion. Director Mamoru Oshii (later creator of Ghost in the Shell) intended the film as a "visual poem" with minimal narrative, drawing influence from Andrei Tarkovsky and creating what many consider one of the most beautiful and enigmatic works in anime history.

entries.title: Aniara
entries.creator: Pella Kågerman, Hugo Lilja (Directors)
entries.pitch:
Aniara is a 2018 Swedish-Danish science fiction film directed by Pella Kågerman and Hugo Lilja, based on the acclaimed 1956 epic poem by Nobel Prize-winning Swedish author Harry Martinson. Set in a dystopian future where Earth has been ravaged by pollution, natural disasters, and rising sea levels, the film follows the passengers of the Aniara—a luxurious colony ship bound for Mars—as their routine voyage goes catastrophically wrong. When the ship collides with space debris and loses navigational control, the passengers discover they will drift endlessly through the void, never reaching their promised new home.

The film premiered at the 2018 Toronto International Film Festival and received a theatrical release in 2019 via Magnolia Pictures. It won the "Asteroid" Prize for Best International Film at the 2019 Trieste Science+Fiction Festival and took home four Guldbagge Awards including Best Actress. Critics have called it a "stunning sci-fi eco-parable" (The Guardian) and an "eerily mesmerising outer-space odyssey," though some noted it can be "a little dull" (Rotten Tomatoes consensus). The 71% Rotten Tomatoes score reflects generally favorable reviews, with particular praise for its visual design and existential themes.

entries.title: Anodyne
entries.creator: Analgesic Productions (Melos Han-Tani, Marina Kittaka)
entries.pitch:
Anodyne is a 2D action-adventure game that immerses players in a surreal dream world where a young protagonist named Young explores strange, interconnected environments. Developed by the duo of Melos Han-Tani and Marina Kittaka during their final years of college, the game draws heavy inspiration from The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening and Yume Nikki—a cult Japanese adventure game known for its dreamlike exploration.

Players navigate Young through screen-based rooms, fighting enemies with a broom and solving puzzles to progress through dungeons and diverse areas. The game features a distinctive pixel art aesthetic and an atmospheric soundtrack composed by Han-Tani himself. Anodyne received generally positive reviews for its dream-like atmosphere and unique blend of action-adventure gameplay, though critics noted some unclear storytelling and imperfect jumping mechanics. The game garnered an honorable mention in the 2013 Student Independent Games Festival and was featured on The Pirate Bay, which helped it gain enough visibility to be accepted onto Steam through its Greenlight system.

entries.title: Another World
entries.creator: Éric Chahi / Delphine Software
entries.pitch:
Another World is a cinematic platformer action-adventure game designed by Éric Chahi and published by Delphine Software in November 1991. Known in North America as Out of This World, the game tells the story of Lester Knight Chaykin, a young physicist who finds himself transported to a dangerous alien world after a particle accelerator experiment goes wrong during a thunderstorm. Alone and unarmed in a hostile environment, Lester must evade dangerous indigenous creatures and capture by a race of humanoid aliens, eventually escaping along with an alien captive known as "Buddy."

The game is renowned for its innovative vector-based graphics, cinematic approach, and minimal UI—there are no dialogue boxes, no HUD except during swimming sequences, and characters speak in an unintelligible alien language. This creates an atmosphere of isolation and mystery as players must interpret the world through visual storytelling alone. The gameplay combines platforming, puzzles, and combat using a laser pistol with three distinct firing modes.

entries.title: Apollo's Song
entries.creator: Osamu Tezuka
entries.pitch:
Apollo's Song is a 1970 manga by the legendary Osamu Tezuka, exploring themes of love, trauma, and reincarnation through the story of Shogo, a boy incapable of feeling love after years of abuse. Originally serialized in Weekly Shōnen King and later published in English by Vertical Inc. in 2007, the work represents Tezuka's mature meditation on love and human connection during a turbulent era of Japanese social history.

The story follows Shogo Chikaishi, who was born from a series of affairs and abused by his mother whenever he witnessed displays of love. This trauma leads him to kill animals in jealousy before he's committed to a mental institute. After shock therapy, he experiences out-of-body visions where the Greek goddess Athena condemns him to relive love across different historical periods for eternity—each time experiencing loss and death until he finally understands true love.

Across multiple lifetimes—in Nazi Germany, on a deserted island, and in a dystopian future—Shogo encounters love only to lose it tragically each time. The manga culminates in the real world where, unable to reunite with his love Hiromi, he chooses mutual destruction rather than live without her.

entries.title: Appleseed
entries.creator: Kazuyoshi Katayama (Director), Masamune Shirow (Original Manga)
entries.pitch:
Appleseed is a groundbreaking cyberpunk OVA directed by Kazuyoshi Katayama, adapted from Masamune Shirow's acclaimed manga. Set in the aftermath of World War III, the film introduces viewers to Olympus—a utopian city constructed by the General Management Control Office where humans, cyborgs, and genetically engineered bioroids coexist. The story follows Deunan Knute, a former ESWAT (Enhanced Special Weapons and Tactics) officer, and her partner Briareos, a heavily modified cyborg, as they navigate the complexities of this seemingly perfect society.

When a terrorist plot to destroy Gaia, the supercomputer controlling Olympus's infrastructure, unfolds, Deunan and Briareos must stop the attackers while uncovering deeper conspiracies about the nature of their world. The OVA explores themes of identity, humanity's relationship with technology, and the question of what truly constitutes a utopia when freedom is sacrificed for order.

entries.title: April 1, 2000
entries.creator: Georg Jacob
entries.pitch:
In the year 2000, the World Global Union governs Earth, allowing member nations only nominal independence as long as they support the global regime. When Austria's newly elected president makes his inauguration speech, he declares Austrian independence and refuses further financial contributions to the Union. The Union responds by cutting all Austria's resources, plunging the nation into crisis. As tensions escalate, the president must choose between national pride and survival.

This 1952 West German science fiction comedy presents a satirical vision of post-war world order, imagining a future where nationalism has been subsumed by a global technocracy. The film was made only seven years after World War II, reflecting contemporary anxieties about emerging Cold War divisions and the formation of new international institutions.

The tone is lighthearted comedy with pointed political satire, predicting a future where the mistakes of the past might be overcome through cooperation—but also warning of the dangers of centralized power.

entries.title: Arabela
entries.creator: Václav Vorlíček, Miloš Macourek
entries.pitch:
Arabela is a Czechoslovak children's television series that aired from 1979 to 1981, blending fairy tale fantasy with modern family drama.
