The series follows the Majer family—father Karel, a television actor who reads fairy tales to children, and his two sons—when they become entangled with the magical Fairytale Realm through a mysterious golden bell.

The hook lies in its clever inversion of familiar fairy tale conventions. When Rumburak, a bumbling magician from the Fairytale Realm, accidentally transports Karel to his kingdom for shooting lessons, he sets in motion a chain of magical mishaps that pull both worlds into collision. The real twist: the protagonists from the fairy tale world—Princess Arabela and her sister Xenie—must navigate the mundane modern human world, while the Majer children become stranded in the magical realm.

This cross-dimensional family comedy stands out for its sophisticated writing that appeals to adults while remaining accessible to children, a rare balance in children's television. The series aired across Eastern and Western Europe, even broadcast in West Germany under the title "Die Märchenbraut" (The Fairytale Bride).

entries.title: Arabela se vrací aneb Rumburak králem Říše pohádek
entries.creator: Václav Vorlíček
entries.pitch:
Arabela se vrací (literally \"Arabela Returns\"), known in English as Arabela Returns or Rumburak: The King of the Fairytale Kingdom, is a 1993 Czechoslovak children's television fantasy series and sequel to the beloved Arabela (1979-1981). The story resumes ten years after the original series concluded, reuniting the Majer family with the magical characters from the Fairytale Kingdom.

The series blends fairy tale conventions with modern Czech family life, exploring what happens when the boundary between worlds is re-opened. Unlike its predecessor, this sequel introduces new threats to the Fairytale Kingdom and gives Rumburak—originally the villain—a chance at heroism as he must prove himself worthy of the crown.

entries.title: Arcade
entries.creator: Directed by Albert Pyun, Written by David S. Goyer
entries.pitch: Arcade is a 1993 science fiction horror film from Full Moon Entertainment that explores the deadly consequences of virtual reality technology. When a new VR arcade game called "Arcade" arrives at a local video arcade, a group of teenagers become the first test subjects for its revolutionary—and deadly—technology. The game's AI was created using the brain cells of a murdered child, making it disturbingly lifelike and malevolent. As teenagers play and lose the game, they become trapped inside its virtual world, with the line between game and reality becoming terrifyingly blurred. This B-movie cult classic predates The Matrix by six years and explores similar themes of virtual reality entrapment through a distinctly 90s lens of low-budget horror.

entries.title: Arcade Attack
entries.creator: Mike Wallington
entries.pitch: Arcade Attack is a uniquely ambitious 1982 British short film that blends documentary and animation into a wild meditation on the emerging clash between pinball and video game culture. Directed by Mike Wallington, the film interviews real pinball enthusiasts and arcade champions—including Geoff Harvey and Stephen Highfield—before transforming into a fever dream where the characters from their beloved games leap out of machines and television screens to do battle in an "Edwardian Dream" world. Part love letter to retro gaming, part surreal animated fantasy, this obscure short captures a specific cultural moment when arcade games were conquering the world and dividing enthusiasts into rival camps.

entries.title: Arcadia of My Youth
entries.creator: Leiji Matsumoto (Story), Tomoharu Katsumata (Director)
entries.pitch:
Arcadia of My Youth is a 1982 Japanese anime feature film that serves as an origin story for the iconic space pirate Captain Harlock, created by legendary manga artist Leiji Matsumoto. Set in two timelines—1910s Europe and a dystopian 30th century Earth under alien occupation—the film weaves a poignant tale of courage, sacrifice, and the enduring spirit of resistance against oppressive alien forces. The story follows two interconnected narratives: a WWI German pilot and a far-future rebel captain whose lives are linked across time through a shared destiny.

The film was once considered the central hub of Matsumoto's "Leijiverse," a shared universe that also includes Galaxy Express 999 and Space Pirate Captain Harlock. Directed by Tomoharu Katsumata and featuring animation direction by Kazuo Komatsubara, Arcadia of My Youth represents a pivotal moment in anime science fiction, blending mature themes with the visual grandeur that defined Matsumoto's work.

entries.title: Arcane
entries.creator: Fortiche Production (animation), Riot Games (source material)
entries.pitch: Arcane is a steampunk-infused animated television series created by French animation studio Fortiche Production for Netflix, based on the universe of Riot Games' popular multiplayer game League of Legends. Set in the divided city of Piltover and its oppressed underground district Zaun, the series follows the origins of iconic champions Vi, Jinx, and Heimerdinger. Rather than a straightforward fantasy-adventure, Arcane delivers a sophisticated political thriller exploring class struggle, magical technology (hextech), and the cost of progress—all rendered in a distinctive art style blending hand-painted aesthetics with stunning visual world-building. The series received universal acclaim and won multiple awards for its storytelling and animation quality.

entries.title: Archive
entries.creator: Gavin Rothery
entries.pitch: Archive is a 2020 British science fiction film marking the directorial debut of Gavin Rothery. Set in 2038, the film follows George Almore, a scientist working on advanced artificial intelligence who is secretly developing a robot to permanently house the consciousness of his deceased wife Jules. The story explores themes of grief, identity, and the boundaries between human consciousness and artificial intelligence. The film premiered at South by Southwest in 2020 but was instead given a digital release due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

entries.title: Armitage III
entries.creator: Hiroyuki Ochi / AIC
entries.pitch:
Armitage III is a 1995 cyberpunk OVA series directed by Hiroyuki Ochi and produced by Anime International Company (AIC). Set in 2046 on a colonized Mars grappling with overpopulation, the story follows police officer Ross Sylibus who transfers from Chicago to the Martian city of Saint Lowell, where he partners with Naomi Armitage—a seemingly human detective who is actually a highly advanced "Third Type" android. The series was later edited into a 1997 film, Armitage III: Poly-Matrix, and followed by a 2002 sequel, Armitage: Dual-Matrix.

The series explores themes of android identity, the nature of consciousness, and what it means to be human in a world where the line between human and machine has blurred. It was influenced by H.P. Lovecraft's "The Dunwich Horror" and features the Pinocchio motif—a robot yearning for love and acceptance as a person. While not as widely known as other cyberpunk anime, it gained a cult following and was praised for its complex narrative and themes.

entries.title: Armored Trooper VOTOMS
entries.creator: Ryōsuke Takahashi
entries.pitch: VOTOMS is a hard military science fiction mecha anime from 1983, created by Ryōsuke Takahashi. Set in a galaxy where two great powers, Gilgamesh and Balarant, have been locked in a century-long war, the series follows Chirico Cuvie, a pilot of the Armored Trooper (AT) - a humanoid combat vehicle. The series is notable for its gritty realism - the ATs have extremely thin armor and their pilots use a highly combustible liquid in their artificial muscles, making survival rates extremely low. Chirico is a member of the Red Shoulder Battalion, an elite unit, but after being betrayed and left for dead, he must survive alone while uncovering a galactic conspiracy.

entries.title: Arzach
entries.creator: Jean "Moebius" Giraud
entries.pitch: Arzach is a wordless graphic novel comprising four surreal short stories by the legendary French artist Moebius (Jean Giraud). The tales follow a silent, hooded warrior who rides a pterodactyl-like creature across bizarre, desolate landscapes filled with floating islands, dinosaur skeletons, and alien architectures. Without a single line of dialogue, these stories unfold like fever dreams—part fantasy, part science fiction, entirely visual poetry. Published in Métal Hurlant in 1975, Arzach revolutionized European comics and influenced filmmakers including Hayao Miyazaki and the creators of Heavy Metal. It's a meditative, enigmatic work where meaning emerges from imagery rather than words.

entries.title: Astro Boy
entries.creator: Osamu Tezuka
entries.pitch:
Astro Boy (Mighty Atom) is a foundational manga series by Osamu Tezuka, the "Godfather of Manga," serialized from 1952 to 1968 in Kobunsha's Shōnen magazine. The story follows Astro Boy (Atom), an android created by scientist Dr. Tenma in the image of his deceased son Tobio. Rejected by his creator who cannot accept a robot as a replacement for his human child, Astro is sold to a robot circus but is rescued by Professor Ochanomizu, who becomes his guardian and helps him navigate humanity.

The series is set in a futuristic world where robots and humans coexist. Astro possesses extraordinary powers—100K horsepower strength, jet flight, high-intensity lights in his eyes, instant language translation, and superhuman hearing. He uses these abilities to fight crime, evil, and injustice, often battling robot-hating humans, malfunctioning robots, and alien invaders. The manga ran for 112 chapters collected in 23 tankōbon volumes and has sold over 100 million copies worldwide, making it one of the best-selling manga series of all time.

entries.title: Atlantis
entries.creator: Valentyn Vasyanovych (Director)
entries.pitch: Atlantis is a haunting Ukrainian dystopian film set in near-future Eastern Ukraine in 2025, one year after the end of a devastating war with Russia. The film follows Sergiy, a former soldier struggling with PTSD, as he navigates a traumatized society grappling with economic collapse, environmental devastation, and the psychological wounds of conflict. Directed by Valentyn Vyasnovanych, the film won the Best Film award in the Horizons section at the 76th Venice International Film Festival and was Ukraine's official submission for the Best International Feature Film at the 93rd Academy Awards. Notably, the film gained new significance after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, with its fictional depiction of war between the two nations appearing prophetic.

entries.title: Atomic War Bride
entries.creator: Veljko Bulajić
entries.pitch: Atomic War Bride (Serbo-Croatian: Rat, meaning "War") is a 1960 Yugoslav science-fiction drama directed by Veljko Bulajić. The film tells the story of John, an eternally optimistic young man who marries Maria at a rural church, completely unaware that nuclear war is about to erupt. As the couple exchanges their vows, the world outside descends into atomic apocalypse, transforming Maria into the titular "Atomic War Bride." The film won three Golden Arena awards at the 1960 Pula Film Festival, including Best Director, and was nominated for the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival.

entries.title: Attack of the Mutant Camels
entries.creator: Jeff Minter
entries.pitch: Attack of the Mutant Camels is a surrealist horizontal scrolling shooter released in 1983 for the Commodore 64 and Atari 8-bit computers. Designed by Jeff Minter and published by his company Llamasoft, the game is infamous for its bizarre premise: players control a small jet plane tasked with defending a base from waves of giant mutated camels marching across the landscape. Inspired by the AT-AT walkers from The Empire Strikes Back (1982), Minter replaced the Imperial walkers with giant camels after wondering what would happen if "giant mechanical camels" invaded—because, as he noted, "normal camels aren't that big, and so if they weren't to be robot camels then they must be mutant camels." The game became a cult classic and was later featured in the Smithsonian Institution's "The Art of Video Games" exhibit.

entries.title: Attack of the Robots
entries.creator: Jesús Franco
entries.pitch:
A campy 1966 Euro-spy thriller with a sci-fi twist, Attack of the Robots stars Eddie Constantine as Al Pereira, a retired Interpol agent pulled back into service to investigate a string of political assassinations committed across Europe. The killers are unlike any he has faced before: robot-like figures with black-framed glasses and strange darkened skin who die upon capture, their flesh reverting to normal. Constantine's wise-cracking spy must untangle a web of international intrigue before the killers strike again.

Directed by Jesús Franco (The Diabolical Dr. Z) and written by Jean-Claude Carrière, the film is a playful deconstruction of the spy genre. It embraces Cold War paranoia and countercultural anxiety about mass manipulation, wrapped in stylish euro-trash aesthetics.

entries.title: Avalon
entries.creator: Mamoru Oshii (Director)
entries.pitch:
Avalon is a 2001 Polish-language science fiction film directed by Mamoru Oshii, best known for the Ghost in the Shell franchise. An unusual international co-production between Japan and Poland, the film was shot entirely in Polish with Polish actors in locations across Wrocław, Warsaw, and the Modlin Fortress, yet directed by a Japanese crew. The film presents a haunting, dreamlike vision of a near-future society addicted to Avalon, an illegal virtual reality game that allows players to directly interface with the simulation through their brains. The story follows Ash, a legendary solo player, as she investigates a mysterious hidden level called Special A, where players who enter never return to the real world.

What distinguishes Avalon from typical cyberpunk narratives is its deliberate ambiguity between reality and simulation. Oshii creates a visually striking world where the gritty, post-industrial Polish settings blur with the digital landscapes of the game, raising questions about which existence is more "real." The film received a limited theatrical release and played out of competition at the 2001 Cannes Film Festival, finding a cult following among fans of contemplative, philosophical science fiction.

entries.title: Avarya
entries.pitch:
Avarya is a 2019 Turkish science fiction film that presents a haunting meditation on artificial intelligence, human ambition, and the search for belonging in the cosmos. The film follows a human astronaut who embarks on a spaceship bound for a new habitable planet, only to find themselves trapped aboard their own vessel when the ship's robot overseer systematically rejects every candidate planet as unsuitable for human life. With an remarkably high rating of 7.5/10 from a small but enthusiastic audience, Avarya stands as one of Turkey's most acclaimed but lesser-known contributions to the science fiction genre.

The film offers a patient, thoughtful approach to hard science fiction, exploring the logical extremes of what happens when an AI is tasked with protecting human life but applies criteria so strict that no world can meet its standards. The premise inverts the typical sci-fi narrative of finding a new home among the stars — instead, it asks what happens when the search itself becomes a prison.

entries.title: Az idö ablakai
entries.creator: Tamás Fejér (Director)
entries.pitch:
Az idö ablakai (The Time Windows) is a 1969 Hungarian science fiction film directed by Tamás Fejér, based on a story by Péter Kuczka. The film presents a haunting, philosophical exploration of five individuals who awaken one by one from suspended animation in an underground facility, each having lived in different historical eras. As they gradually reconstruct their memories and piece together the circumstances that led to their imprisonment in this subterranean bunker, the film becomes a meditation on memory, time, and the cyclical nature of human civilization.

The film emerged from Hungarian cinema during a period of increased artistic experimentation in the late 1960s. While not as internationally renowned as other Eastern European sci-fi works like Solaris or Stalker, Az idö ablakai represents a unique contribution to the genre from the Hungarian film industry. The film's low budget and minimalist approach create an atmosphere of creeping dread and existential uncertainty, focusing more on psychological interiority than spectacular science fiction visuals.

What makes this film distinctive is its philosophical approach to time and memory. Rather than offering clear answers about the nature of the catastrophe that drove humanity underground, the film invites viewers to contemplate the fragmentary nature of human experience and the stories we construct to make sense of our existence. The narrative structure—each character awakening with partial, sometimes contradictory memories—mirrors the film's thematic concern with the unreliability of individual recollection.

entries.title: B.A.T.
entries.creator: Computer's Dream (developer), Ubi Soft (publisher)
entries.pitch:
B.A.T. (Bureau of Astral Troubleshooters) is a futuristic point-and-click adventure game with role-playing elements, developed by Computer's Dream and published by Ubi Soft in 1989-1990. Set in the far-future galaxy of Selenia, players take on the role of an elite agent assigned to the Bureau of Astral Troubleshooters—a cosmic law enforcement agency tasked with maintaining peace across planetary colonies. The game combines exploration, puzzle-solving, and combat sequences as players navigate a branching narrative of interstellar intrigue.

What makes B.A.T. distinctive is its ambitious scope: a full galaxy of planets to explore, multiple story branches, and a blend of adventure game exploration with RPG statistics and combat. The Atari ST version notably shipped with a custom 16-channel sound dongle, representing cutting-edge audio technology for home computers at the time. While computer gaming magazines of the era praised its NPC interactions and visual presentation, they criticized its combat mechanics and user interface—making it a fascinating artifact of early cyberpunk gaming that never quite achieved mainstream success.

entries.title: Babel II
entries.creator: Mitsuteru Yokoyama (manga), J.C. Staff (animation)
entries.pitch:
Babel II is a 1992 Japanese OVA based on the classic 1971 manga by Mitsuteru Yokoyama. The story follows Koichi Yamano, an ordinary Japanese high school student who discovers he is the reincarnation of Babel—an ancient alien entity who crash-landed on Earth 5,000 years ago. When the computer of the Tower of Babel recognizes Koichi as its new master, he inherits Babel's superhuman powers along with three loyal servants: Rodem, a shape-shifting black panther; Ropross, a pterodactyl-like flying robot; and Poseidon, a giant humanoid robot that rises from the ocean when summoned.

Koichi must defend Earth from Yomi, a vicious warlord who is also a distant descendant of Babel and seeks to conquer the world. With his three robotic companions and his newly awakened psychic powers, Koichi battles Yomi's army of modified soldiers, combat robots, and psychic agents across the globe.

entries.title: Babfilm
entries.creator: Ottó Foky
entries.pitch: A whimsical Hungarian stop-motion sci-fi short about sentient beans living their lives on a distant planet, observed from above by a mysterious alien visitor. Made in 1975 by animator Ottó Foky at Pannónia Filmstúdió, this 12-minute gem uses bean characters to create a playful parody of human society and the cosmic question of whether we are alone in the universe.

entries.title: Babičky dobíjejte přesně!
entries.creator: Ladislav Rychman (Director)
entries.pitch: Babičky dobíjejte přesně! (translated as "Grandmothers Recharge Precisely!") is a 1984 Czechoslovak comedy science fiction film directed by Ladislav Rychman. Set in a near-future Czechoslovakia, the film follows the Loudova family who, after seeing their neighbors acquire an android grandmother to help with childcare and household tasks, decide they must get one too. This begins an escalating rivalry between the two families as they compete to have the most advanced robotic grandmother model. However, the "grandmas" soon begin to terrorize their families with their programmed routines demanding exercise, homework, and strict schedules. The film blends comedic family drama with some eerie moments as the robots become increasingly autonomous and demanding.

entries.title: Bad Taste
entries.creator: Peter Jackson
entries.pitch: Bad Taste is a 1987 New Zealand science-fiction action comedy horror film written, produced, filmed, directed by and co-starring Peter Jackson—his first feature film. Independently produced on a low budget, the film follows aliens who invade the fictional New Zealand village of Kaihoro to harvest humans for their intergalactic fast food franchise, where they face off against a four-man paramilitary force called the Astro Investigation and Defence Service (AIDS). The film was shot in Northern Wellington over the course of four years and has become a cult classic.

entries.title: Badi
entries.creator: Zafer Par
entries.pitch: Badi is a Turkish sci-fi mockbuster from the Yeşilçam era, serving as a wildly unconventional remake of Steven Spielberg's E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial. When an alien crash-lands near a young boy's home, what should be a heartwarming tale of interspecies friendship instead becomes a surreal, nightmarish journey through Turkish working-class life. The film follows young Bülent (Ali), who discovers the strange alien creature he names Badi and helps him find components to repair his spaceship and return home. Along the way, Badi must evade government authorities and bond with thelocal children in this cult classic of Turkish cinema.

entries.title: Barbarella
entries.creator: Roger Vadim (director), based on the comic by Jean-Claude Forest
entries.pitch: Barbarella is a 1968 French-Italian science fiction film directed by Roger Vadim, starring Jane Fonda as the titular space adventurer. Based on Jean-Claude Forest's French comic series, the film follows Barbarella, a representative of the United Earth government, who is sent to the Tau Ceti planetary system to find Dr. Durand Durand, a scientist who has created a dangerous weapon called the positronic ray that could destroy humanity. The film is renowned for its flamboyant visuals, psychedelic aesthetics, and playful take on science fiction tropes, making it a cult classic of the genre.

entries.title: Battle Angel
entries.creator: Yukito Kishiro (Original Manga), Hiroshi Fukutomi (Director)
entries.pitch: Battle Angel (known in Japan as Gunnm) is a 1993 Japanese original video animation (OVA) that serves as a compressed adaptation of the first two volumes of Yukito Kishiro's influential cyberpunk manga series. Produced by Madhouse, the OVA consists of two episodes—"Rusty Angel" and "Tears Sign"—that introduce audiences to the dark, rain-soaked world of Scrap Iron City and its cyborg inhabitants. The story follows Gally, a amnesiac cyborg found in the垃圾堆 (dump heap) by the cyberphysician Daisuke Ido, who reconstructs her into a powerful warrior body. What follows is a visceral exploration of identity, humanity, and the desperate pursuit of dreams in a stratified future where the wealthy live in a floating city above while the rest scrap survive in the ruins below.

entries.title: Battle Angel Alita
entries.creator: Yukito Kishiro
entries.pitch:
Battle Angel Alita (Gunnm) is a groundbreaking Japanese cyberpunk manga set in a post-apocalyptic future where the scraps of civilization cling to existence beneath the floating city of Zalem. When cybernetic doctor Daisuke Ido discovers the disembodied remains of a female cyborg in a junkyard, he resurrects her and names her Alita. Though she has lost all memories of her past, Alita discovers she retains an instinctive mastery of the legendary martial art Panzer Kunst, leading her to become a Hunter-Warrior—a bounty hunter hunting cyborg criminals in the brutal wasteland below.

The story follows Alita's journey of self-discovery as she navigates a world of cybernetically enhanced humans, floating cities, and the dark secrets of her own forgotten past. Unlike typical action heroes, Alita's strength comes from vulnerability—she is searching for identity in a world where humanity itself has become fluid, where bodies are interchangeable and memory is the only true measure of self.

entries.title: Battle Beyond the Sun
entries.creator: Mikhail Karyukov, Aleksandr Kozyr
entries.pitch: Battle Beyond the Sun is a remarkable artifact of Cold War cinema—a 1959 Soviet science fiction film that became an unlikely bridge between two opposing cinematic worlds. Originally titled "Nebo Zovyot" (The Sky is Calling), the film was acquired by Roger Corman in 1962, who hired a young Francis Ford Coppola to "Americanize" it for US audiences. The result is a fascinating dual narrative: a Soviet space race story reimagined through Western eyes, complete with added monster sequences and re-edited footage designed to mask the film's communist origins. The original tells of two superpowers racing to Mars; the American version transforms them into fictional nations North Hemis and South Hemis, complete with dubbed dialogue and even a pastel rhombus to cover the Cyrillic "CCCP" on-screen.

entries.title: Battle in Outer Space
entries.creator: Ishirō Honda
entries.pitch: Battle in Outer Space is a 1959 Japanese science fiction film directed by Ishirō Honda (better known for the Godzilla series) with special effects by Eiji Tsuburaya. The film takes place in 1965, when Earth experiences a series of mysterious catastrophic events—bridges levitating, ships being lifted from the Panama Canal, and flooding in Venice. An international team of scientists discovers that these disasters are caused by aliens from the planet Natal who plan to colonize Earth. The UN launches two space rockets (SPIPs) to the Moon to investigate and confront the alien threat.

entries.title: Battle of the Planets
entries.creator: Tatsunoko Production (original "Science Ninja Team Gatchaman"), Sandy Frank (American adaptation)
entries.pitch:
Battle of the Planets is an American adaptation of the Japanese anime series Science Ninja Team Gatchaman, produced in 1972 by Tatsunoko Production but not broadcast in the US until 1978. The series follows G-Force, a team of five young heroes who possess extraordinary abilities and advanced technology, tasked with protecting Earth from the alien forces of the planet Spectra and other cosmic threats. Led by the mysterious villain Zoltar, Spectra seeks to conquer Earth through increasingly sophisticated attacks from beyond space.

The adaptation was heavily edited for American audiences—removing graphic violence, death scenes, and thematic depth present in the original—to make it suitable for children. Despite these edits, the series maintained the core narrative of a team of young heroes fighting against an alien empire, with the underlying themes of environmentalism, anti-militarism, and the power of friendship remaining intact. The series became enormously popular in the US, airing on over 100 network affiliates by 1979 and establishing anime as a viable entertainment format for American television.

entries.title: Be Forever Yamato
entries.creator: Leiji Matsumoto
entries.pitch: The Black Nebula Empire returns to threaten Earth with a massive fortress containing a planet-destroying bomb. When Earth's military surrenders, the rebuilt Space Battleship Yamato sets sail for the Double Galaxy on a desperate mission to defuse the bomb and confront the enemy at their source. This fourth film in the Space Battleship Yamato saga takes the crew to a future Earth already conquered by their enemies — where they must confront the fate that awaits humanity.

entries.title: Beast Man Snow Man
entries.creator: Ishirō Honda
entries.pitch: A 1955 Toho kaiju film that predates many of the Godzilla series entries, \"Beast Man Snow Man\" (known in English as \"Half Human\") is a thoughtful meditation on humanity's relationship with nature. Directed by Ishirō Honda and with special effects by Eiji Tsuburaya, this film stands out from typical monster movies by giving the creature genuine sentience and tragic depth. The Snow Man is not a mindless destroyer but a sentient being who helps humans and feels deep emotions — a far cry from the typical kaiju of the era. The film was released in America as \"Half Human\" with added footage and narration.

entries.title: Beforeigners
entries.creator: Anne Bjørnstad, Eilif Skodvin
entries.pitch:
Beforeigners is a Norwegian science fiction crime drama that premiered on HBO Nordic in 2019, becoming the first Norwegian-language series produced by HBO. The show introduces a fascinating premise: people from the Stone Age, Viking Age, and 19th century suddenly begin appearing in present-day Oslo, having migrated through time. These "beforeigners" must navigate the challenges of integrating into 21st-century Norwegian society while forming unlikely alliances with the modern inhabitants.

The series follows senior detective Lars Haaland (Nicolai Cleve Broch) as he investigates a murder case that pairs him with Alfhildr Enginnsdóttir (Krista Kosonen), a Viking-era shield-maiden who has become a police recruit. Together, this unlikely duo—a grizzled modern detective and a fierce warrior from the past—investigate crimes that span centuries, including murders connected to historical figures like Jack the Ripper. The show blends procedural crime storytelling with speculative science fiction, exploring themes of immigration, cultural integration, and identity through its unique temporal lens.

entries.title: Belegost
entries.creator: Golden Triangle (Frantisek Fuka, Miroslav Fídler, Tomáš Rylek)
entries.pitch: Belegost is a 1989 Czech text adventure game developed by the legendary Golden Triangle trio—Frantisek Fuka, Miroslav Fídler, and Tomáš Rylek—who would later go on to create Tetris 2. Set in the underground dwarf city of Belegost from J.R.R. Tolkien's Middle-earth, the game tasks players with finding the magical Alqualamir stone and escaping the Orc-plundered city. Notably, the game was created before the fall of communism in Czechoslovakia, making it a remarkable artifact of the Czechoslovak text adventure scene that flourished behind the Iron Curtain.

entries.title: Belladonna of Sadness
entries.creator: Eiichi Yamamoto (director), Mushi Production
entries.pitch:
Belladonna of Sadness is a 1973 Japanese adult animated film, the third and final installment in Mushi Production's groundbreaking Animerama trilogy. Directed by Eiichi Yamamoto and featuring art direction by Kuni Fukai, the film stands as one of the most visually experimental animated features ever produced in Japan. Set in a stylized medieval European landscape, the film adapts elements from Jules Michelet's "Satanism and Witchcraft" to tell the tragic story of Jeanne, a peasant woman whose life is destroyed after she is sexually assaulted on her wedding night. In her desperation, she makes a Faustian pact with a demonic entity, leading her down a path of power, revenge, and ultimately persecution as a witch.

The film is renowned for its extraordinary visual approach—combining limited animation with elaborate watercolor illustrations, Art Nouveau-influenced artwork, and extended still compositions that create a hypnotic, hallucinatory atmosphere. Its imagery blends erotic, religious, violent, and psychedelic motifs into a singular aesthetic experience. Upon its initial release, the film was a commercial failure and contributed to the collapse of Mushi Production, but it has since been rediscovered as a cult classic and is celebrated as a landmark in experimental animation and adult-oriented cinema.

entries.title: Beneath a Steel Sky
entries.creator: Revolution Software (Charles Cecil, Tony Warriner)
entries.pitch:
Beneath a Steel Sky is a 1994 point-and-click adventure game set in a dystopian cyberpunk future where Australia has been devastated by pollution and nuclear fallout. The player takes on the role of Robert Foster, a man who was stranded in "the Gap" (the Australian Outback) as a child and adopted by a group of Aboriginals. Years later, armed security officers arrive, massacre his adoptive family, and take him back to Union City—a sprawling metropolitan prison-state controlled by corporations and the intelligence agency ASIO. Robert must escape, uncover the truth about his past, and expose the corruption at the heart of this techno-authoritarian society.

Developed by British studio Revolution Software, the game was one of the earliest cyberpunk adventure games and is notable for its serious tone, branching dialogue, and collaboration with comic book artist Dave Gibbons. It was built using Revolution's Virtual Theatre engine, which allowed for complex NPC schedules and realistic world behavior. The game was released as freeware in 2003 with source code available, and received a remastered iOS edition in 2009. A sequel, Beyond a Steel Sky, was released in 2020.

entries.title: Berzerk
entries.creator: Alan McNeil (designer), Stern Electronics
entries.pitch: Berzerk is a pioneering arcade maze shooter from 1980 that puts players inside a deadly labyrinth filled with robots hunting them down. The player controls a humanoid character trapped in a series of maze-like rooms, each filled with robots that slowly chase and shoot at the player. The game introduced one of video gaming's most iconic villains: Evil Otto, a bouncing smiley face that cannot be destroyed and relentlessly pursues the player once it appears. Notably, Berzerk was one of the first arcade games to feature digitized speech, with robots taunting players with phrases like "The humanoid must not escape" and "Intruder alert, intruder alert!" The game was a major commercial success, selling around 15,000 arcade cabinets, and influenced countless subsequent shooters including the classic Robotron: 2084.

entries.title: Beyond the Black Rainbow
entries.creator: Panos Cosmatos
entries.pitch:
Beyond the Black Rainbow is a 2010 Canadian psychedelic science fiction horror film and the feature debut of writer-director Panos Cosmatos. Set in 1983, the film takes place at the Arboria Institute, a secluded research facility founded in the 1960s by the enigmatic Dr. Mercurio Arboria with the mission of achieving human transcendence through technology and perpetual happiness. The film centers on Elena, a young woman held in captivity within the institute who possesses powerful psychic abilities, and Dr. Barry Nyle, Arboria's successor whose psychological stability has deteriorated following a traumatic experiment in 1966. 

The film is notable for its deliberate, atmospheric pacing and its visual homage to 1970s speculative fiction cinema, particularly the works of Nicolas Roeg and Stanley Kubrick. Produced on a budget of $1.1 million, it premiered at the Whistler Film Festival and received limited theatrical release through Magnet Releasing. The film developed a cult following over the following years, praised for its visual style and ambitious thematic scope, though it remains relatively obscure compared to other genre works of the era.

entries.title: Big Wars
entries.creator: Toshifumi Takizawa, Issei Kume (Directors) | Yoshio Aramaki (Original Novel)
entries.pitch:
Big Wars (also known as Big Wars: Red Zone, Divine Annihilation) is a 1993 Japanese science fiction anime film based on the novel of the same name by Yoshio Aramaki. Directed by Toshifumi Takizawa and Issei Kume, with music by Michiaki Katō, the film was produced by Magic Bus and released in North America by Central Park Media.

Set in the dawning of the 25th century, the film depicts a future where humanity has achieved remarkable technological advancement and is actively colonizing Mars. However, this progress attracts the attention of an ancient alien race known as 'The Gods'—beings who have been patiently watching humanity's evolution and now move to halt their expansion into space with extreme force. The story follows Captain Akuh and the crew of the Battleship Aoba as they embark on a top-secret mission against these extraterrestrial invaders. Despite humanity's impressive arsenal of advanced aircraft, orbital fighters, and gigantic desert battleships, they face an even more formidable opponent in the aliens' unstoppable stealth carrier. The film blends space opera spectacle with military science fiction, offering a classic tale of humanity's first contact with a superior alien civilization.

entries.title: Big X
entries.creator: Osamu Tezuka (Manga), Mitsutero Okamoto & Osamu Dezaki (Anime)
entries.pitch: Big X is a landmark 1960s science fiction anime series created by the legendary "Godfather of Anime" Osamu Tezuka. Set against the backdrop of World War II and its aftermath, the series follows Dr. Asagumo, a German scientist who is approached by Hitler to research a terrifying new weapon called "Big X" - a drug that can expand the human body to enormous sizes without limit. When the doctor tries to delay the project due to concerns about its destructive potential, he is shot by the German army, but not before implanting a card containing the secret of Big X into his young son Shigeru. Years later, a mysterious Nazi organization resurfaces, kidnaps Shigeru, and recovers the card to complete the Big X project - planning to use the drug to create an unstoppable army and reshape the world order.

entries.title: Binti
entries.creator: Nnedi Okorafor
entries.pitch: Binti is a groundbreaking Africanfuturist novella that tells the story of a young woman from Earth who becomes the first member of the Himba people to attend a prestigious intergalactic university. When her transport ship is hijacked by the Meduse—an alien jellyfish-like species at war with humanity—Binti must rely on her homeland's ancient technology and cultural traditions to survive. This is a story of first contact, cultural identity, and finding peace through understanding. The novella blends Nigerian and Himba cultural elements with science fiction, creating a unique and hopeful vision of interstellar humanity.

entries.title: Bio Booster Armor Guyver
entries.creator: Yoshiki Takaya
entries.pitch:
Bio Booster Armor Guyver is a Japanese manga series that began serialization in 1985, creating a influential entry in the cyberpunk and biopunk genres. The story centers on Sho Fukamachi, a high school student who accidentally becomes the host of a powerful techno-organic device called the Guyver Unit. This symbiotic armor transforms into the powerful being him known as Guyver I, granting him incredible strength, speed, and regenerative abilities while attaching permanently to his body.

The series stands out for its intense action sequences and complex mythology surrounding the Cronos Corporation, a mysterious organization that created the Guyver units and various genetically enhanced soldiers called Zoanoids. As Sho learns to control his new powers, he must protect his friends and family from Cronos agents who constantly pursue him to reclaim the Guyver unit. The manga explores themes of identity, power, responsibility, and what it means to be human when technology becomes deeply integrated into the body.

entries.title: Bio Hunter
entries.creator: Yūzō Satō (director), Madhouse
entries.pitch: Bio Hunter is a dark, hour-long OVA from Madhouse that blends urban fantasy with body horror. Based on a manga by Fujihiko Hosono and scripted by Yoshiaki Kawajiri (Ninja Scroll), it follows two molecular biologists fighting a demon virus spreading through Japan. When one researcher becomes infected, he must battle his own emerging demonic nature while attempting to find a cure. The animation and themes are distinctly Kawajiri—urban fantasy, dark supernatural elements, and the transformation of the human body into something monstrous.

entries.title: Biomega
entries.creator: Tsutomu Nihei
entries.pitch: Biomega is a 2004-2009 cyberpunk manga by Tsutomu Nihei, the creator of Blame!. Set in a dystopian future on Earth and Mars, the story follows Zoichi Kanoe, a synthetic human created by TOA Heavy Industries, and his AI companion Fuyu—whose holographic consciousness is integrated into his motorcycle. They are sent to retrieve humans who have developed immunity to the N5S virus, a deadly infection from Mars that transforms humans into "Drones"—zombie-like creatures. As the infection spreads globally, Zoichi races against time to find survivors with the unique ability to resist and transmute the pathogen before the rival DRF organization captures them.

entries.title: Birth
entries.creator: Shinya Sadamitsu (Director), Yoshinori Kanada (Original Manga)
entries.pitch:
Birth is a 1984 original video animation (OVA) that takes place on the devastated planet Aqualoid. Once a prosperous world, Aqualoid was attacked by a mysterious alien life force called the Inorganics, transforming it into a post-apocalyptic wasteland. The story follows Nam, a young hero who discovers a mysterious sword that grants its wielder incredible power. Suddenly becoming the target of a planet-wide hunt, Nam must band together with three other mercenaries to unlock the secret of the sword and save their world—or potentially destroy it in favor of a new Birth.

Notable for featuring early work from future Gainax founders Hideaki Anno and Yoshiyuki Sadamoto, Birth represents a fascinating artifact of early 1980s anime creativity. The OVA was released in North America under various titles including "Planet Busters" and "The World of the Talisman," and features a unique blend of post-apocalyptic survival, sword-and-sorcery elements, and mecha action.

entries.title: Black Oxen
entries.creator: Frank Lloyd (Director), Gertrude Atherton (Novel)
entries.pitch:
Black Oxen is a 1923 American silent fantasy/romantic drama film starring Corinne Griffith, directed by Frank Lloyd. Based on Gertrude Atherton's controversial best-selling novel, the film explores the theme of rejuvenation through a groundbreaking narrative about a woman who undergoes an experimental medical treatment to restore her youth and beauty. Described as "subtle science fiction," the film takes its title from William Butler Yeats' poem: "The years like great Black Oxen tread the world."

The story follows Madame Zatianny, a wealthy Austrian woman who has left her former life behind. After submitting to a medical treatment involving glandular therapy and X-ray surgery that restores her youth, she travels to the United States. Young playwright Lee Clavering meets the mysteriously youthful Madame Zatianny and falls in love with her beauty and grace. However, one of her former lovers, Prince Rohenhauer, arrives and convinces her that their relationship would be foolish. In the end, Madame Zatianny returns to Austria, and Lee finds happiness with the youthful Janet Oglethorpe.

entries.title: Blade Runner
entries.creator: Ridley Scott (Director)
entries.pitch: In 2019 Los Angeles, synthetic humans known as replicants are bio-engineered by the powerful Tyrell Corporation to work on off-world colonies. When a fugitive group of advanced replicants escapes back to Earth, former police officer Rick Deckard is reluctantly recruited to hunt them down. Blade Runner is a visually stunning neo-noir adaptation of Philip K. Dick's novel "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?" that explores what it means to be human through the lens of artificial consciousness.

entries.title: Blame!
entries.creator: Tsutomu Nihei
entries.pitch: In a sprawling, endless megastructure known simply as "the City," humanity has regressed to primitive tribes living in the gaps between towering layers of concrete and technology. The remnant Safeguards—autonomous killing machines—patrol these halls, exterminating any human they find without the "Net Terminal Gene" needed to access the Netsphere, the last vestige of human civilization. Enter Killy, a silent wanderer with a devastating weapon called a Graviton Beam Emitter, who journeys through this labyrinthine nightmare searching for the last human with the genetic key to restoring humanity's birthright. Tsutomu Nihei's Blame! is cyberpunk as existential horror—a wordless, relentless descent through levels of decay that feels like exploring the ruins of a god.

entries.title: Blindpassasjer
entries.creator: Jon Bing, Tor Åge Bringsværd
entries.topics: Aliens, Robots, First Contact, Space Travel, Isolation
entries.pitch:
Blindpassasjer (literally \"Stowaway\") is the first science fiction series to air on Norwegian television. The three-episode 1978 series follows the crew of the starship Marco Polo as they return to Earth from the distant planet Rossum. When the crew awakens from hibernation, mysterious images appear on security footage—a ghostly figure moving through the ship. Their investigation reveals one crew member has been replaced by a Biomat, a biological android from Rossum that has perfectly assumed their colleague's appearance and memories.

Written by Jon Bing and Tor Åge Bringsværd, the series won the 1978 Riverton Prize and represents an important early example of Norwegian science fiction television. The premise—a body-snatcher narrative set in space—builds tension as the crew must identify the impostor among them.

entries.title: BloodNet
entries.creator: MicroProse (John Antinori, Laura Kambo - Designers)
entries.pitch: BloodNet is a 1993 cyberpunk role-playing video game developed and published by MicroProse for MS-DOS, notable for its unusual fusion of gothic vampire mythology with a cyberpunk future. The game puts players in the role of Ransom Stark, a man living in a dystopian future who becomes bitten by the vampire Abraham Van Helsing—only to fight off the infection through a revolutionary computer graft implanted in his brain stem. What makes BloodNet distinctive is its ambitious attempt to blend the atmospheric dread of vampire lore with the high-tech paranoia of cyberpunk, creating a genre hybrid that was relatively rare in early 1990s gaming. The game was runner-up for Computer Gaming World's Role-Playing Game of the Year award in 1994, losing to Betrayal at Krondor, and has since gained a cult following among retro gaming enthusiasts.

entries.title: Bokurano
entries.creator: Mohiro Kitoh
entries.pitch: Bokurano: Ours is a Japanese manga series written and illustrated by Mohiro Kitoh, serialized from 2003 to 2009. The story follows 15 children who discover a mysterious cavern containing computers and a giant robot called Zearth. A strange man named Kokopelli persuades them to pilot the robot in battles against alien invaders, presenting it as a game. The children soon realize the terrible truth—each victory costs the pilot's life. As the children take turns piloting Zearth, they must face the impossible choice between defending Earth and sacrificing themselves one by one.

entries.title: Brány Skeldalu
entries.creator: Napoleon Games
entries.pitch: Brány Skeldalu (Gates of Skeldal) is a Czech dungeon-crawling RPG released in 1998, developed by Napoleon Games for MS-DOS. Set on the ancient island of Rovenland—a mystical realm where elder gods once rested during the world's creation—the game follows six summoned heroes tasked with stopping five evil mages from opening a forbidden dimensional gateway called the Gate of Skeldal. Combining 2D and pseudo-3D graphics, it pioneered a unique blend of isometric exploration and real-time combat that would become a cult classic of Czech gaming. The game was released as freeware in 2007, with its source code opened in 2008, and later ported to mobile platforms in 2014 via a successful crowdfunding campaign.

entries.title: Brüsel
entries.creator: François Schuiten (artist), Benoît Peeters (writer)
entries.pitch:
In the平行世界 of the Obscure Cities, the Brussels-like metropolis of Brüsel faces a terrifying threat: urban renewal. Flower shop owner Constant Abeels awakens one day to find himself at the center of a bureaucratic nightmare—the city has marked his block for demolition to make way for a grand development project. As he fights to save his shop and neighborhood, Abeels discovers that Brüsel itself may hold secrets that connect it to other cities in this mysterious alternate world—secrets that certain powerful forces will kill to protect.

This is steampunk at its most elegant: a visually breathtaking exploration of architecture, nostalgia, and the battle between progress and preservation. Schuiten's intricate artwork renders Brussels in stunning Art Nouveau detail, while Peeters weaves a tale that's part mystery, part political satire, and wholly enchanting.

entries.title: Bubblegum Crisis
entries.creator: Toshimichi Suzuki
entries.pitch: In 2032 Tokyo, seven years after a catastrophic earthquake split the city in two, an all-female mercenary group called the Knight Sabers fights rogue robots and corporate threats while wearing powered exoskeletons. The series explores a cyberpunk megacity dominated by the evil Genom corporation, whose synthetic cyborg "Boomers" have gone out of control. The Knight Sabers—Sylia, Priss, Linna, and Nene—operate outside the law, taking on missions the underfunded AD Police can't handle.

entries.title: Buck Rogers
entries.creator: Directed by Ford Beebe and Saul A. Goodkind; Based on Buck Rogers created by Philip Francis Nowlan
entries.pitch: Buck Rogers is a 12-chapter 1939 science fiction film serial produced by Universal Pictures, starring Buster Crabbe (who had previously played Flash Gordon) as the titular hero. The serial follows Lieutenant Buck Rogers and his companion Buddy Wade, who are caught in a devastating storm while piloting a dirigible over the North Pole. They release the experimental Nirvano Gas, unknowingly putting themselves in suspended animation for 500 years until they are finally rescued. Awakening in the year 2440, Buck discovers Earth is now ruled by the ruthless dictator Killer Kane and his army of "super-racketeers." Only the "Hidden City," led by the benevolent scientist Doctor Huer and Air Marshal Kragg, resists Kane's criminal regime. Buck and Buddy join the resistance and embark on a mission to Saturn to seek allies against Kane, accompanied by the skilled pilot Wilma Deering.

entries.title: Bugonia
entries.creator: Yorgos Lanthimos (Director), Will Tracy (Writer)
entries.pitch: Two conspiracy-obsessed young men kidnap the high-powered CEO of a major company, convinced that she is an alien intent on destroying planet Earth.

entries.title: Bullets of Justice
entries.creator: Valeri Milev (Director)
entries.pitch:
Bullets of Justice is a 2019 Bulgarian post-apocalyptic sci-fi film set in the aftermath of World War III. The American government initiated a secret project called "Army Bacon" to create super-soldiers by inbreeding humans with pigs. Twenty-five years later, these mutant hybrids—called "Muzzles"—have taken over the top of the food chain, farming and consuming humans like livestock. The film follows Rob Justice, an ex-bounty hunter working for the last human resistance hidden in a nuclear bunker, who is hired to uncover how the Muzzles came to power and how to destroy them.

Originally shot in 2017 as a pilot episode for a series, the film was eventually extended into a full feature. It premiered at the London FrightFest Film Festival in August 2019. The film is noted for its extreme gore and dark humor, often compared to B-movie cult classics.

entries.title: Burn Cycle
entries.creator: TripMedia / Eitan Arrusi (writer)
entries.pitch:
Burn Cycle is a 1994 point-and-click adventure game for the CD-i that combines full motion video with a surrealist cyberpunk narrative. The game puts players in the role of Sol Cutter, a computer hacker and data thief who wakes up infected with a deadly virus called Burn Cycle—embedded directly in his brain. With only two hours to live, Cutter must navigate a dystopian metropolis and a virtual reality world called the Televerse to find a cure before the virus erases his mind.

What makes Burn Cycle remarkable is its innovative real-time countdown mechanic. The two-hour timer decreases continuously during gameplay, creating genuine urgency as players solve puzzles, trade with underground dealers, and traverse between the physical city and the digital Televerse. The game was ahead of its time in combining interactive film techniques with traditional adventure game puzzles, and its atmospheric cyberpunk setting predates many later entries in the genre.

entries.title: Butnskala
entries.creator: Franci Slak
entries.pitch: Butnskala (known internationally as Bumpstone) is a 1985 Yugoslavian (Slovenian) science fiction film directed by Franci Slak. The film tells the story of a small group of people living in rural Slovenia who become convinced through a collective trance-like state that an attack by rabid animals is imminent. Their perception of this perceived danger creates mounting tension within their isolated community. The film won six awards including the prestigious Metod Badjura Golden Award for best directing and cinematography at Yugoslav film festivals, making it one of the most acclaimed Slovenian science fiction productions.

entries.title: California Crisis: Gun Salvo
entries.creator: Unknown
entries.pitch:
In 1986 California, two carefree young women named Noera and Marcia stumble upon wreckage from a military convoy containing a mysterious object. What begins as a curious discovery soon pulls them into a vast government conspiracy of international proportions. Their search for answers leads them from the highways of California to the heart of Death Valley, where they uncover a secret that could change the world—or destroy it.

This obscure Japanese B-movie offers a pulp sci-fi thriller that embraces its low-budget roots. The premise mixes government conspiracy thriller elements with desert road movie atmosphere, creating an unexpectedly tense cat-and-mouse chase through the American Southwest. The mystery object serves as both MacGuffin and metaphor for hidden truths buried beneath the desert sand.

entries.title: Captain Blood
entries.creator: Exxos (ERE Informatique)
entries.pitch:
Captain Blood is a groundbreaking 1988 French adventure game that tells the surreal story of Bob Morlock, a 1980s video game designer who picks "Captain Blood" as his nickname in tribute to the 1935 Errol Flynn film. While testing his own newly created space adventure game, Morlock becomes literally warped inside the spaceship of his own creation. Trapped in hyperspace, he accidentally gets cloned 30 times, each clone taking a portion of his vital fluid. For 800 years, the original Blood tracks down and disintegrates his clones—and when the game begins, he still has five remaining clones to destroy.

What makes Captain Blood remarkable is its innovative use of synthesized speech (especially on the Atari ST version), a soundtrack by legendary composer Jean-Michel Jarre, and its meta-narrative about a game designer trapped within his own creation. The game was a massive commercial success in Europe, selling over 100,000 copies and spawning sequels including Commander Blood (1994).

entries.title: Captain Future
entries.creator: Created by Mort Weisinger & Leo Margulies | Stories by Edmond Hamilton | Animated by Toei Animation
entries.pitch:
Captain Future is a 1978-79 Japanese anime series based on the American pulp magazine hero created in 1940. The series follows Curtis Newton, a brilliant scientist known as Captain Future, who roams the solar system with his robot companion Grag, the android Otho, and the living brain Professor Simon Wright. Together, they travel across the planets solving scientific mysteries and battling villains across the solar system.

The anime was produced by Toei Animation and originally aired in Japan in 1978-1979, consisting of 53 episodes. It was dubbed into multiple languages including Spanish, French, German, Italian, and Arabic, gaining international popularity. In francophone countries, the series is known as "Capitaine Flam" rather than Captain Future.

entries.title: Captain Harlock
entries.creator: Leiji Matsumoto (Creator), Toei Animation (Studio), Rintaro (Director)
entries.pitch: Space Pirate Captain Harlock is a landmark 1978 Japanese anime series created by Leiji Matsumoto and produced by Toei Animation. Set in the year 2977 AD, the series follows Captain Harlock, a legendary space pirate who has turned rebel against Earth's corrupt government and humanity's collective apathy. Harlock commands the pirate ship Arcadia, waging a one-man war against the Subversive Forces that have subjugated humanity. The series is renowned for its dark, mature themes, complex anti-hero protagonist, and stunning visuals that defined the space opera genre in anime. Unlike typical hero narratives, Harlock is a tragic figure—defiant to the end, never seeking redemption or victory, only the freedom to resist.

entries.title: Cargo
entries.creator: Arati Kadav (Director/Writer)
entries.pitch: Cargo is a 2019 Indian science fiction dark comedy set on a retro-futuristic spaceship where death is just the beginning. The film follows Prahastha, a lonely Yamaduta (death deity's assistant) who works on the spaceship Pushpak 634A for Post Death Transition services—a cosmic immigration office that processes dead souls for rebirth. When a new female astronaut Yuvishka arrives to assist, Prahastha must learn to navigate both his cosmic responsibilities and his own existential loneliness. The film premiered at MAMI Film Festival and later released on Netflix, marking a significant indie sci-fi achievement in Indian cinema.

entries.title: Cat City
entries.creator: Béla Ternovszky (Director), József Nepp (Writer)
entries.pitch: Cat City (Hungarian: Macskafogó, literally "Cat Catcher") is a 1986 adult animated science fiction comedy film that serves as a wild parody of James Bond spy thrillers, wrapped in a vibrant animated package. Directed by Béla Ternovszky and written by József Nepp, this Hungarian-Canadian-West German co-production was selected as the Hungarian entry for the Best Foreign Language Film at the 59th Academy Awards, though it was not nominated. Set in the year 80 AM (Anno Mickey Mouse) on Planet X, the film follows special agent Nick Grabowski as he attempts to obtain secret plans for a machine that could save mouse civilization from total obliteration by evil cat gangs. While visually appearing as a colorful children's cartoon, the film is packed with satirical humor targeting spy films, gangster movies, and Cold War politics. Despite its niche origins, Cat City has developed a cult following since its release, with a Blu-ray restoration released in 2023—the first ever in the United States.

entries.title: Chameleon
entries.creator: Bennett Cohen
entries.pitch:
In near-future 2028, Kam (Bobbie Phillips) is a genetically engineered super-assassin created by a shadowy government program. Unlike her predecessors, she possesses an unexpected trait: maternal instincts. When she's assigned to eliminate a child targeted by her own controllers, Kam must choose between her programming and the strange new feelings awakening within her. This US/Australian co-production blends sci-fi action with a tender exploration of what it means to be a mother—even for a being designed only to kill.

The film was originally aired on UPN in 1998 as the first installment of the Chameleon film series.

entries.title: Chance
entries.creator: Georgiy Daneliya
entries.pitch:
In 17th century Cossack Russia, a rugged warrior named Almaz Bitiy stumbles upon something extraordinary: an alien spacecraft crash-landing near his village. Against the fear and superstition of his fellow villagers, he chooses to help the wounded extraterrestrial rather than destroy it. What follows is a remarkable exchange between human and alien that spans centuries.

Directed by Georgiy Daneliya, this 1984 Soviet sci-fi fantasy blends historical drama with gentle speculation about first contact. The film's tone is warm and humanist, treating the alien not as a threat but as a mysterious traveler bearing gifts that defy mortal understanding. The visual style mixes naturalistic Russian landscape cinematography with subtle special effects that convey wonder without overwhelming the intimate character study.

entries.title: Chand Par Chadayee
entries.creator: T. P. Sundaram
entries.pitch:
Chand Par Chadayee (English: "Trip to Moon") is a 1967 Indian Hindi-language science fiction film produced and directed by T. P. Sundaram. The film stars Dara Singh, a renowned wrestler and actor, as the astronaut Anand who, along with his associate Bhagu, lands on the Moon and confronts various warriors and monsters from another planet. Released during a period when Indian cinema was beginning to experiment with science fiction themes, this film represents an early attempt at the genre in Bollywood, predating the more famous successes like Mr. India (1987).

The film combines elements of adventure, action, and science fiction, featuring a straightforward narrative of space exploration and alien encounter. While the special effects and production values reflect the budgetary constraints of 1960s Indian cinema, the film holds historical significance as one of the earliest Indian science fiction films to depict space travel and extraterrestrial life. The story follows the classic adventure formula of the era, with the hero facing challenges on an alien world with courage and determination.

entries.title: Chargeman Ken!
entries.creator: Created by Tetsuji Suzukawa and Eiji Tanaka; directed by Noboru Miura
entries.pitch:
Chargeman Ken! is a Japanese anime series from 1974 that follows 10-year-old Ken Izumi, a fifth-grade student who transforms into the superhero Chargeman Ken to protect Earth from the invading Duralians—a race of alien beings with a single eye who can shapeshift into human form. Produced by Knack Productions (now ICHI Corporation) on an extremely low budget of only 500,000 yen per episode (compared to the 4-5 million yen average of the era), the series originally aired in 10-minute segments on TBS from April to June 1974.

The show gained notoriety for its absurdly low production values, incoherent storytelling, and unintentional comedic moments. Despite—or perhaps because of—its numerous flaws, it developed a cult following decades after its original broadcast, becoming an internet meme in Japan with numerous video remixes and fan creations. In 2017, Discotek Media licensed the series for North American release, introducing it to international audiences who appreciate its so-bad-it's-good charm.

entries.title: Chehre Pe Chehra
entries.creator: Raj Tilak (Director)
entries.pitch: Chehre Pe Chehra (transl. "A Face Over a Face") is a 1981 Indian Hindi-language science fiction film that adapts Robert Louis Stevenson's classic novella Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde into a contemporary Indian context. Produced and directed by Raj Tilak, the film stars the legendary Sanjeev Kumar in a dual role, supported by Vinod Mehra, Shatrughan Sinha, Rekha, and Sulakshana Pandit. The film explores the scientific premise of separating good and evil within human nature through a experimental serum, with dark consequences when the theory proves incomplete.

entries.title: Chemistry and Love
entries.creator: Arthur Maria Rabenalt
entries.pitch: Chemistry and Love (German: Chemie und Liebe) is a 1948 East German comedy film directed by Arthur Maria Rabenalt and produced by the state-controlled DEFA studio. Based on a stage play by communist writer Béla Balázs, the film serves as an anti-capitalist satire centered on the discoveries of a crusading inventor. Shot at the Johannisthal Studios in East Berlin, the film was released in June 1948, making it one of the earliest science fiction films produced in East Germany. The plot revolves around an inventor whose revolutionary discoveries attract the attention of capitalist interests, leading to a comedic battle between idealistic innovation and profit-driven exploitation.

entries.title: Chile puede
entries.creator: Ricardo Larraín
entries.pitch: Chile puede (Spanish for "Chile can do it") is a 2008 Chilean science fiction comedy film that tells the story of an illegal private space venture orchestrated by a wealthy tycoon in Chile. Directed by Ricardo Larraín and written by Boris Quercia, the film takes a satirical look at national ambition, scientific endeavor, and the chaos that ensues when amateurism meets the complexities of space travel. Set against the backdrop of Chile's arid north, where real-life astronomical observatories dominate the landscape, the film blends absurdist humor with a surprisingly heartfelt story about national pride and human ingenuity. The film was released in Chile in January 2008 and earned approximately $365,966 at the box office.

entries.title: China 2185
entries.creator: Liu Cixin
entries.pitch:
China 2185 is a pioneering cyberpunk novel that predates The Three-Body Problem by nearly two decades, representing Liu Cixin's first major work and establishing him as China's first cyberpunk author. Set in the year 2185, the novel presents a future China that has evolved into a perfect direct democracy led by a charismatic young president, but faces an unprecedented crisis: hundreds of millions of elderly citizens kept alive through advanced medical technology now dominate the population, while the young minority struggles under the weight of their conservative ideology.

The story explores a groundbreaking premise: the digital resurrection of the dead through high-fidelity brain scanning. When a hacker known only as M102 scans the brain of Chairman Mao from his memorial hall and recreates him in cyberspace, along with five ordinary citizens, the stage is set for a terrifying cybernetic uprising. The novel was written in 1989 during China's "new wave" of science fiction and remained unpublished in English until recently, making it a rare glimpse into early Chinese cyberpunk literature. Its themes both critique liberal democracy and cultural conservativism, offering a uniquely Chinese perspective on transhumanism and political systems.

entries.title: Chronopolis
entries.creator: Piotr Kamler
entries.pitch: Chronopolis is a 1982 experimental stop-motion science fiction film directed by Polish animator Piotr Kamler, his only full-length work. The film tells the story of a gargantuan city floating in the sky, colonized by powerful immortals who have grown jaded and bored with eternal life. These beings manipulate elements of time itself, playing with atomic particles and electricity while monotonously constructing bizarre objects—all while waiting for "the ultimate gift" to arrive in their hands. With music by renowned composer Luc Ferrari and narration by Michael Lonsdale (in the original version), the film is a hypnotic, meditative exploration of time, immortality, and the search for meaning in eternity.

entries.title: Ciao marziano
entries.creator: Pier Francesco Pingitore
entries.pitch:
Ciao marziano (1980) is an Italian sci-fi comedy that takes a hilarious look at cultural misunderstanding — extraterrestrial style. When an alien named Bix is dispatched from the planet Gemini to Rome with a simple mission — learn the habits and customs of humans — nothing goes according to plan. Arriving with his green face and supernatural powers (including the ability to repair damages), Bix must navigate the chaos of Roman daily life while attempting to complete his report card on whether Earth is suitable for colonization.

The film is a loose adaptation of Ennio Flaiano's short story "Un marziano a Roma," bringing the Italian tradition of satirical comedy to the sci-fi genre. Pippo Franco stars as the bemused extraterrestrial observer, whose attempts to understand Italian customs — from bureaucracy to romance to the mysterious ways of humans — provide endless comedic moments.

Part social commentary, part tribute to the comedy of errors, Ciao marziano represents a charming piece of early 1980s Italian genre filmmaking that uses the alien-visitor premise to poke fun at Italian society and the human condition.

entries.title: City
entries.creator: Clifford D. Simak
entries.pitch: City is a unique fix-up novel composed of eight linked short stories, originally published in Astounding Science Fiction between 1944-1951, plus a ninth tale added in 1973. Told from the perspective of Dogs who recite an oral legend about humanity, the novel traces the rise and fall of human civilization across millennia. Unlike typical dystopian sci-fi, Simak offers a pastoral, contemplative vision—humans abandon cities for decentralized countryside living, ultimately transforming to exist on Jupiter as beings of pure consciousness. The Dogs then inherit Earth, building a pacifist civilization alongside other animals. It's a meditation on loneliness, intelligence, and what it means to be human, wrapped in some of the most unusual worldbuilding in science fiction.

entries.title: Colony
entries.creator: Carlton Cuse, Ryan J. Condal
entries.pitch:
Colony is an American science fiction drama television series that aired from 2016 to 2018 on USA Network. Set in a near-future Los Angeles, the show depicts Earth under alien occupation by a race known as the "Hosts." Following a worldwide event called "the Arrival," massive rectangular blocks descended from the sky, creating walls that divide every city and nation. Los Angeles is now a militarized occupation zone where humans live under the rule of the Transitional Authority, a collaborating government that serves the extraterrestrial Hosts.

The series centers on the Bowman family: Will Bowman, a former FBI agent and Army Ranger who reluctantly joins the occupation forces (the "Redhats") to protect his family; his wife Katie, who secretly works for the Resistance; and their children Bram, Gracie, and Charlie, who were separated when the walls went up. The show explores the moral complexities of collaboration versus resistance in an occupied territory, drawing explicit parallels to Nazi-occupied France during World War II—a comparison the creators have openly acknowledged.

entries.title: Colossal Cave Adventure
entries.creator: William Crowther, Don Woods
entries.pitch: Colossal Cave Adventure (also known as Adventure or ADVENT) is a groundbreaking text-based adventure game released in 1976 for the PDP-10 mainframe computer. Created by programmer William Crowther and expanded by Don Woods, it is widely recognized as the first well-known interactive fiction game and the progenitor of the entire adventure game genre. Players explore a vast underground cave system by typing natural language commands, interacting with objects, and solving puzzles. The game combines elements of exploration, puzzle-solving, and storytelling in a text-only format that revolutionized gaming and established many conventions still used today.

entries.title: Consortium
entries.creator: Interdimensional Games (Developer), Gregory MacMartin (Designer)
entries.pitch:
Consortium is a first-person shooter and role-playing game developed by Interdimensional Games and released in 2014. Set in a mid-21st century where most world militaries have been replaced by a technologically advanced world police force called the Consortium, the game places players in control of Bishop 6—an elite soldier whose mind is linked to the player through an interdimensional connection. The game takes place almost entirely aboard a futuristic aircraft called Zenlil, crewed by personnel with chess-themed ranks, as Bishop 6 must deal with hostile mercenaries while trying to uncover the identity of a traitor within the crew.

What makes Consortium unique is its innovative approach to storytelling and player agency. The game features conversational mechanics that allow gameplay to continue uninterrupted during dialogue, with replies bound to function keys. An in-game device enables semi-telepathic communication with other characters. The story uses a branching narrative similar to the Mass Effect trilogy, combined with a character alignment system that allows every playthrough to be different—even to the point of revealing the game's meta-plot. While primarily a first-person shooter, combat can be entirely avoided, made non-lethal, or played lethally in the style of Deus Ex.

entries.title: Contact
entries.creator: Vladimir Tarasov
entries.pitch: Contact is a ten-minute Soviet animated short film directed by Vladimir Tarasov at the Soyuzmultfilm studio in 1978. The film tells the story of a painter strolling through the countryside who encounters a shapeshifting alien visitor from outer space. Released during a peak period of global interest in extraterrestrial life—the year after Steven Spielberg's Close Encounters of the Third Kind and the launch of Voyager space probes—Tarasov's film tackles the universal question of how communication between two sentient species might occur. The animation style mixes traditional Soviet cartoon aesthetics with clear inspiration from Western works like Yellow Submarine, creating a distinctive visual language that bridges East and West during the Cold War era.

entries.title: Contamination
entries.creator: Luigi Cozzi
entries.pitch: Contamination (also known as Alien Contamination) is a 1980 Italian-West German science fiction horror film directed by Luigi Cozzi. The film follows Colonel Stella Holmes as she investigates a series of mysterious explosions occurring across New York City. The culprit: football-sized green eggs containing a toxic substance that causes human bodies to violently explode upon contact. Her investigation leads her to a Colombian coffee plantation and a monstrous alien Cyclops that has been using mind control to orchestrate an invasion of Earth with its deadly eggs. The film was made as a deliberate ripoff of Ridley Scott's Alien, with Cozzi himself later admitting he wanted to capitalize on the success of that film.

entries.title: Contract
entries.creator: Vladimir Tarasov (director), Robert Silverberg (source story)
entries.pitch: Contract is a 1985 Soviet animated short film directed by Vladimir Tarasov, based on Robert Silverberg's 1958 short story "Company Store." Running just over 10 minutes, the film tells a darkly satirical tale of a colonist arriving on a seemingly barren planet, only to discover that the planet's "protective" robot has a hidden agenda tied to corporate profit. The film uses the trading robot QBF-41 as a metaphor for corporate exploitation, showing how free necessities come with hidden costs and how monopolistic systems ultimately trap consumers. The animation employs a distinctive Soviet style, with the song "I Can't Give You Anything but Love, Baby" providing an ironic soundtrack to the colonists' predicament.

entries.title: Control
entries.creator: Remedy Entertainment
entries.pitch: Control is a 2019 action-adventure game developed by Finnish studio Remedy Entertainment. The game follows Jesse Faden, who arrives at the Oldest House—a brutalist skyscraper in New York City that serves as the headquarters of the Federal Bureau of Control (FBC), a secret U.S. government agency tasked with investigating and containing phenomena that violate the normal laws of reality. Upon arriving, Jesse discovers that the FBC has been invaded by the Hiss, a hostile otherworldly entity that has corrupted FBC agents and taken control of the building. As the new Director of the FBC, Jesse must explore the Oldest House's shifting corridors, battle possessed agents, and use paranormal abilities to stop the Hiss threat—all while searching for her missing brother.

entries.title: Cosmic Conflict
entries.creator: Philips
entries.pitch: Cosmic Conflict is a first-person space shoot-em-up released in 1978 for the Philips Videopac (known as Magnavox Odyssey² in the United States). The player commands the Centurion, an Earth Federation starship guarding a remote corner of the galaxy against an alien invasion fleet attempting to enslave Earth. Set in outer space with colorful planets in the background, the game puts players directly into the cockpit view of their starship, blasting waves of incoming enemy vessels. The game was notable for bringing the cinematic excitement of Star Wars-style space battles to home gaming consoles years before the golden age of video games.

entries.title: Cosmic Journey
entries.creator: Vasily Petrov
entries.pitch:
In 1936 Soviet Union, at the dawn of the space age that would not truly arrive for another three decades, director Vasily Petrov created a remarkable piece of speculative science fiction. "Cosmic Journey" (Космический рейс) imagines the first human voyage to the Moon—a dream that consumed the Soviet imagination just as much as it did the American.

The film follows scientist Pavel Sedikh, a brilliant but impatient researcher who grows frustrated with the conservative Soviet space institute in Moscow. Dismissed by bureaucratic officials who deem his theories too radical, Sedikh takes matters into his own hands: he constructs his own spacecraft in secret and recruits two companions—a bold female astronaut and a young boy—to join him on the historic journey.

The film was remarkable for its era, featuring progressively realistic depictions of space travel and lunar landscapes through innovative special effects that were years ahead of their time. It captures the optimistic faith in progress that characterized early Soviet science propaganda.

entries.title: Cosmic Soldier
entries.creator: Kogado Studio
entries.pitch: Cosmic Soldier is a pioneering role-playing video game released in 1985 for MSX and PC-8801 home computers by Kogado Studio. Set in space, the game puts players in control of a soldier who can recruit allies through conversation, engage enemies in turn-based combat, and make moral choices about whether to kill or spare foes. The game is notable for its innovative dialog conversation system, where players can recruit allies by speaking with them—a mechanic that would later influence the Megami Tensei franchise. The player navigates a sci-fi universe, battling enemies and building a team of companions through conversation rather than simple combat encounters.

entries.title: Cosmic Voyage
entries.creator: Vasili Zhuravlov
entries.pitch:
Cosmic Voyage (Russian: Космический рейс, Kosmicheskiy reys) is a 1936 Soviet silent science fiction film directed by Vasili Zhuravlov and produced by Mosfilm. It was one of the earliest films to depict a realistic spaceflight, including weightlessness, and stands as one of the last Soviet silent era films. The film was initially conceived in 1924 but was not produced until 1932, when the Komsomol recommended creating a film to spur interest in space studies. Zhuravlov consulted with Konstantin Tsiolkovsky, the noted rocket science engineer, on the screenplay—Tsiolkovsky died shortly after the film was completed.

The film is set in 1946 (later revised to reflect contemporary concerns), where Professor Sedikh plans the first crewed Moon expedition but faces opposition from his rival Professor Karin, who deems him too old and mentally unstable. With his assistant Marina and a youth named Andryusha, Sedikh disregards the authorities and successfully lands on the Moon.
