After overcoming problems including a damaged oxygen tank and Sedikh becoming trapped under a boulder, the cosmonauts return triumphant to Moscow.

entries.title: Cosmodrama
entries.creator: Unknown
entries.pitch: Seven astronauts wake aboard a self-operating spaceship with no memory of their mission or origin. The ship drifts through space as they grapple with fundamental questions: Where did they come from? Where are they going? As the vessel carries them forward, they have nothing but time to meditate on matter, life, and the nature of the universe itself. The film poses existential questions wrapped in the trappings of hard science fiction.

entries.title: Counterweight
entries.creator: Djuna (Korean: 듀나)
entries.pitch:
Set in an unspecified future on Patusan, a fictional tropical island near Malaysia, Counterweight introduces us to Earth's first AI-directed space elevator—a monumental achievement built by the powerful Korean megacorporation LK. The story follows Mac, a disenchanted security executive who becomes entangled in corporate intrigue when he investigates the suspicious behavior of a subordinate connected to the recent death of LK's chief executive.

Mac's investigation leads him to Choi Gangwu, a seemingly unremarkable company employee with an unusual passion for butterflies and an inexplicable depth of knowledge about the space elevator. What unfolds is a paranoid thriller that explores memory, identity, and the colonization dynamics between corporations and nations. The novel blends cyberpunk aesthetics with Korean speculative fiction traditions, offering a fresh perspective on familiar themes of corporate power, technology, and human identity.

entries.title: Cow on the Moon
entries.creator: Dušan Vukotić
entries.pitch: Cow on the Moon is a charming 1959 Yugoslav animated short from the legendary Zagreb Film studio, directed by Oscar-winning animator Dušan Vukotić. The film follows a young girl who constructs a wooden model spaceship, only to have it destroyed by a bully. Seeking revenge, she builds a full-sized rocket decoy and tricks the boy into believing he's traveling to the moon—only to have him encounter what appears to be an alien (actually the girl in costume, with a cow joining the deception). This whimsical tale won multiple awards, including first prize at the San Francisco International Film Festival, and represents the early triumphs of the Zagreb School of Animation.

entries.title: Což takhle dát si špenát
entries.creator: Václav Vorlíček
entries.pitch: Což takhle dát si špenát (translated as "How About a Plate of Spinach") is a 1977 Czechoslovak comedy science fiction film directed by Václav Vorlíček and written by Miloš Macourek. The film follows two small-time swindlers, Zemánek and Liška, who are released from prison after serving time for alcohol theft. Looking for their next get-rich-quick scheme, they find employment at a scientific laboratory working on a revolutionary device designed to regenerate old cows. When a wealthy salon owner discovers their work, she sees an opportunity for profit—she wants to use the regeneration technology for human rejuvenation treatments. However, things go spectacularly wrong when the two con artists accidentally test the device on themselves, discovering that instead of restoring their youth, they have been transformed into young children. The film blends slapstick comedy with satirical commentary on youth obsession, beauty standards, and the foolish pursuit of eternal youth.

entries.title: Cube
entries.creator: Vincenzo Natali
entries.pitch: Cube is a 1997 Canadian science fiction horror film directed by Vincenzo Natali. The film follows seven individuals who wake up trapped in a bizarre labyrinth of cube-shaped rooms, each with hatches leading to other rooms—some safe, others deadly. As the group attempts to escape, they discover that each room's hatch plates contain three sets of numbers, and those containing prime numbers correspond to rooms with lethal traps. The film is renowned for its surreal, Kafkaesque atmosphere and low-budget ingenuity, becoming a cult classic that spawned multiple sequels.

entries.title: Curse of Snakes Valley
entries.creator: Marek Piestrak
entries.pitch: Curse of Snakes Valley is a 1988 Polish-Soviet Estonian adventure science fiction horror film directed by Marek Piestrak. Set in 1954 during the First Indochina War and present-day Paris, the film follows a Polish scientist and a former military pilot who travel to the Vietnamese jungle to uncover the secrets of a mysterious artifact stolen from a Buddhist temple. The trio of adventurers—a scientist, a journalist, and a former military pilot—venture into the Indochina jungles searching for a mysterious vase containing a metal container of extraterrestrial origin. The film was a massive box office success, with approximately 1 million viewers in Poland and a staggering 25 million in the Soviet Union. Loosely based on Robert Stratton's short story "The Hobby of Dr. Traven," the film combines adventure, horror, and science fiction elements in a unique Cold War-era production.

entries.title: Cyber City Oedo 808
entries.creator: Yoshiaki Kawajiri (Director), Madhouse (Studio)
entries.pitch: In the year 2808, the Japanese city of Oedo has descended into a dystopian nightmare where crime runs rampant and traditional law enforcement has failed. Desperate for a solution, the city government revives an ancient feudal practice known as hōmen—employing convicted criminals as law enforcement officers. Three heavily-sentenced prisoners are offered a chance at freedom: Sengoku, a hot-headed armed robber serving 375 years; Gogul, a brilliant computer hacker serving 310 years; and Benten, an androgynous assassin serving 295 years. Each wears an explosive collar around their neck that their commander can detonate at will, ensuring their obedience. Armed with traditional jitte weapons and paired with the robotic partner Varsus, these cyber-criminals are sent to hunt down the most dangerous digital criminals in the neon-soaked metropolis. Cyber City Oedo 808 is a gritty, action-packed cyberpunk masterpiece that predates many of the genre's most famous works, featuring exceptional animation, complex anti-heroes, and a haunting vision of Japan's distant future.

entries.title: Cybernetic Grandma
entries.creator: Jiří Trnka
entries.pitch:
In Jiří Trnka's poignant 1963 Czechoslovakian short film, a grieving family turns to technology to fill an irreplaceable void. When a little girl's beloved grandmother passes away, her sorrow-stricken parents purchase a sophisticated cybernetic robot to serve as a replacement grandmother. The machine is programmed with all the knowledge, recipes, and routines of grandmotherly care — but can true love be manufactured?

The film unfolds as a tender meditation on authenticity versus simulation, exploring whether the warmth of human connection can be reduced to algorithms and programming. The little girl, initially comforted by the robot's presence, begins to sense something missing — the inexplicable warmth that only comes from genuine human love.

entries.title: Cyberpunks
entries.creator: Mutation (developer), Core Design (publisher)
entries.pitch: Cyberpunks is a top-down shooter developed by Mutation and published by Core Design in 1993 exclusively for the Amiga computer. The game places players in control of three characters simultaneously, tasking them with navigating hostile alien environments, shooting enemy forces, and locating door passes to progress through levels. Released during the height of the cyberpunk aesthetic's popularity in media, Cyberpunks represents a fascinating period piece of early 1990s British game development, combining the twin-stick shooter mechanics popular at the time with themes of corporate warfare and artificial intelligence. The game was developed by the relatively obscure British studio Mutation, with Adrian Robert Cummings handling design, art, and music—a notable feat of single-developer ambition for the era.

entries.title: Cyborg 009
entries.creator: Shotaro Ishinomori (manga), Toei Animation (animation)
entries.pitch: Cyborg 009 is a groundbreaking Japanese anime television series that inaugurated the genre of superhero anime. Based on the manga by Shotaro Ishinomori, the series follows nine individuals from around the world who are kidnapped by the evil Black Ghost organization and transformed into cyborgs with superhuman abilities. Each cyborg possesses unique powers—telepathy, super speed, strength, underwater capability, and more—that they must learn to control and deploy against their former captors. The series premiered on April 5, 1968, becoming Japan's first color TV anime featuring superheroes, and ran for 26 episodes until September 1968. It established many tropes that would define the superhero anime genre for decades to come, including teams of enhanced heroes, mad scientist villains, and themes of friendship and redemption.

entries.title: Daicon IV Opening Animation
entries.creator: Daicon Film (Director: Hiroyuki Yamaga, Animation Supervisors: Hideaki Anno, Takami Akai)
entries.pitch: Daicon IV Opening Animation is a landmark 6-minute anime short created in 1983 by the amateur group Daicon Film—students who would go on to found the legendary studio Gainax. Produced for the Daicon IV science fiction convention in Osaka, this opening animation features a girl in a bunny costume battling an impossible armada of science fiction references: Ultraman monsters, Gundam mobile suits, Star Wars characters, and countless other icons from Japanese and Western pop culture. The animation is famous for its extraordinarily high production values for an amateur production, its mind-bending density of otaku references, and the unauthorized use of Electric Light Orchestra's "Twilight" as its theme. It won the "Local Works" award in the Minor Anime Grand Prix section of the 1983 Anime Grand Prix and was ranked 35th in Animage's "Top 100" anime of all time.

entries.title: Dallos
entries.creator: Hisayuki Toriumi (Concept), Mamoru Oshii (Co-director)
entries.pitch: Dallos is a groundbreaking 4-episode OVA released in 1983, widely considered not only the first OVA ever produced but also the first animated direct-to-video release in history. Set in a near-future Earth where resources have been depleted, the story follows the colonists living on Moon mining stations who have been exploited by Earth's government for generations. When the colonists begin to resist through acts of terrorism, a young man named Shun Nonomura finds himself caught between loyalty to his people and the violent path they're taking. At the center of the colonists' hope is a mysterious artifact called Dallos—a structure on the Moon that has become an object of worship. This is a story about colonial oppression, generational divides, and the question of what it means to be human when your home is no longer your own.

entries.title: Dark City
entries.creator: Alex Proyas
entries.pitch:
Dark City is a 1998 neo-noir science fiction film directed by Alex Proyas, featuring Rufus Sewell, William Hurt, Kiefer Sutherland, and Jennifer Connelly. The film follows John Murdoch, who awakens in a hotel bathtub with no memory of his identity, only to discover he's being hunted by pale beings called the "Strangers" who can reshape reality itself. As Murdoch navigates a city trapped in eternal night, he must uncover his true past while battling both the police and these alien entities who experiment with human memory.

The film is notable for its visually stunning art direction, reminiscent of German Expressionist cinema, and its exploration of themes regarding identity, memory, and the nature of reality. Dark City is widely recognized as a cult classic and is often cited as a significant influence on The Matrix, which arrived in theaters just one year later.

entries.title: Dark Star
entries.creator: John Carpenter
entries.pitch:
Dark Star is a 1974 independent science fiction comedy directed by John Carpenter and co-written with Dan O'Billion. Set twenty years into a mission to destroy unstable planets, the film follows the crew of the deteriorating starship Dark Star as they navigate mechanical failures, existential crises, and a sentient thermonuclear bomb that has developed second thoughts about its purpose. What begins as a student project at USC evolved into a cult classic that influenced the development of Star Wars and demonstrated that low-budget filmmaking could yield clever, thought-provoking science fiction.

The film's budget of just $60,000 belie its ambitious concepts and darkly humorous take on the space mission formula. Rather than the heroic astronauts of mainstream science fiction, Carpenter presents a crew of exhausted, disillusioned workers trapped in a failing ship with malfunctioning life support, depleted toilet paper supplies, and a computer that has seen better days. The existential comedy reaches its peak when a sentient bomb begins questioning the nature of its own existence, leading to a philosophical conversation about phenomenology that saves the crew from certain death.

entries.title: Dark Sun
entries.creator: Otakar Vávra (Director)
entries.pitch: Dark Sun (Temné slunce) is a 1980 Czech science fiction film directed by Otakar Vávra, serving as a remake of his own earlier film "Krakatit" (1948). Based on Karel Čapek's classic novel, the film updates the story to the Cold War era of the late 1970s, transforming it into a stark warning about the military-industrial complex and the dangerous potential of unchecked scientific development. The story follows engineer Prokop, who creates an immensely powerful explosive substance called "krakatit" that could revolutionize energy production—or enable catastrophic destruction. As international powers and domestic interests scramble to control his invention, Prokop finds himself pursued, manipulated, and ultimately trapped in a web of political intrigue and moral compromise. The film presents a cynical, often chaotic vision of a world where scientific achievement becomes a plaything for those in power, serving as an allegory for the nuclear age and the arms race.

entries.title: Day of Destiny
entries.creator: Akay Mason, Abosi Ogba
entries.pitch: Day of Destiny (also known as D.O.D) is a 2021 Nigerian sci-fi adventure film that marks both Nigeria's first family adventure film and the country's first-ever time travel film. Directed by Akay Mason and Abosi Ogba (in his directorial debut), the film follows two teenage brothers who mysteriously travel back twenty years to the year 2001, attempting to change their family's fortunes. Released on January 1, 2021, the film opened to positive critical reception and became a box office success, earning ₦18.6 million in its opening weekend. It was also the first Nigerian film released in 2021. The film tackles themes of family, fate, and the desire to rewrite history—delivered through an entertaining adventure narrative that blends sci-fi elements with heartfelt family drama.

entries.title: Day of Wrath
entries.creator: Sulambek Mamilov
entries.pitch: A Soviet journalist investigates mysterious disappearances in a forbidden forest zone, only to uncover a geneticist's dark secret — a new race of intelligent, emotionless bear-creatures created through forbidden experiments. This 1985 Soviet sci-fi horror blends ecological warning with body horror, exploring the dangerous consequences of unchecked scientific ambition and the question of what happens when we create life without a soul.

entries.title: Dead Dead Demon's Dededede Destruction
entries.creator: Inio Asano
entries.pitch: Dead Dead Demon's Dededede Destruction (also known as DDDD) is a manga series by Inio Asano, the acclaimed creator of Goodnight Punpun. Originally serialized in Big Comic Spirits from 2014 to 2022, the series spans 12 volumes and 101 chapters. The story follows two young women—initially high school seniors and later college students—as they navigate the mundanity of daily life under an alien invasion that has loomed over Tokyo for three years. Rather than focusing on the alien threat itself, Asano uses the backdrop of extraterrestrial invasion to explore human nature, social anxiety, and the coping mechanisms people employ when faced with existential uncertainty.

entries.title: Dead Mountaineer's Hotel
entries.creator: Grigori Kromanov
entries.pitch:
In the isolated peaks of the Alps, a remote hotel becomes the setting for one of the most bizarre locked-room mysteries ever committed to film. When Inspector Peter Glebsky arrives at the Dead Mountaineer's Hotel seeking a quiet vacation, he gets far more than he bargained for—an avalanche cuts the hotel off from the outside world, and guests begin dying under impossible circumstances.

This Soviet-Estonian production, directed by Grigori Kromanov and based on the novel by Arkady and Boris Strugatsky, blends detective fiction with cosmic science fiction in ways that subvert every convention of both genres. The film plays as a proper mystery—atmospheric, tense, and meticulously plotted—before revealingsomething utterly unexpected: that the hotel's most peculiar guests are not human at all.

The film exists in a unique space—part Alpine horror, part philosophical absurdism, part Soviet-era speculation on extraterrestrial intelligence. It's a movie that genuinely keeps you guessing, and then delivers answers that transform everything you thought you knew.

entries.title: Dead Space
entries.creator: Motive Studio / Electronic Arts
entries.pitch: Dead Space (2023) is a survival horror remake of the 2008 classic, developed by Motive Studio and published by Electronic Arts. Set aboard the USG Ishimura, a massive planetary mining ship orbiting the planet Aegis VII, the game follows engineer Isaac Clarke as he investigates the ship's mysterious distress signal. What he discovers is a nightmare: the crew has been transformed into deadly Necromorphs—reanimated corpses mutated by an alien artifact known as the Marker. Combining intense survival horror with science fiction world-building, the remake rebuilds the original from the ground up using the Frostbite engine, delivering seamless exploration, enhanced zero-gravity gameplay, and a more immersive narrative experience.

entries.title: Death Machine
entries.creator: Stephen Norrington (Director/Writer)
entries.pitch: In 2003, Chaank Armaments is the world's leading weapons manufacturer. When a cybernetic supersoldier called "Hard Man" goes on a murderous rampage, the corporation tries to cover up the incident. Hayden Cale, the new chief executive, demands transparency—but when she discovers the dark secrets hidden in the company's Vault 10, she becomes the target of the deranged weapon designer Jack Dante. With eco-warriors infiltrating the building and a deadly creation called the "Warbeast" on the loose, Cale must survive the night against both the corporate conspirators and her own creation. Featuring Brad Dourif in an unhinged performance as the villain, this obscure British-Japanese co-production is a cult sci-fi horror that was banned in multiple countries for its excessive violence.

entries.title: Death Stranding
entries.creator: Hideo Kojima
entries.pitch:
Death Stranding is a 2019 action-adventure game developed by Kojima Productions, marking director Hideo Kojima's first original game after his departure from Konami. Set in a post-apocalyptic United States following a cataclysmic event called the "Death Stranding," the game puts players in the role of Sam Porter Bridges, a courier tasked with delivering supplies to isolated colonies and reconnecting them via a wireless communications network known as the Chiral Network.

The game is set in the United States after mysterious creatures known as "Beached Things" (BTs) began roaming the Earth following a catastrophic event. These entities are surrounded by "Timefall" rain that accelerates aging and deterioration. The event devastated the country's infrastructure, forcing the remaining population into remote colonies called "KNOT Cities." Players must navigate this treacherous landscape while avoiding BTs, hostile militia groups, and the challenges of delivering cargo across vast distances.

What sets Death Stranding apart is its innovative "strand" gameplay style—a new genre Kojima coined—which emphasizes asynchronous online cooperation. Players can leave supplies, structures, and messages for others to find, creating a shared experience without direct interaction. The game features an ensemble cast including Norman Reedus, Mads Mikkelsen, Léa Seydoux, and Guillermo del Toro in supporting roles.

entries.title: Death Watch
entries.creator: Directed by Bertrand Tavernier; Based on "The Unsleeping Eye" (1973) by David G. Compton
entries.pitch: In a near-future where death from illness has become rare, Katherine Mortenhoe is diagnosed with an incurable disease and becomes an unlikely celebrity. A ruthless television executive offers her enormous money to allow her final days to be filmed as a reality show called "Death Watch" - but she doesn't realize the man helping her escape is actually a covert cameraman with cameras implanted behind his eyes. This French gem from director Bertrand Tavernier (Round Midnight, A Sunday in the Country) is a chilling meditation on privacy, media exploitation, and the voyeuristic nature of audiences.

entries.title: Def-Con 4
entries.creator: Paul Donovan
entries.pitch: Def-Con 4 is a 1985 Canadian post-apocalyptic film following three astronauts aboard a secret nuclear-armed space station who survive World War III and return to Earth to find civilization devastated. The film's title refers to the Defense Readiness Condition (DEFCON), though it inaccurately portrays DEFCON 4 as a high state of readiness rather than its actual status as the second-lowest level. The movie opens with text suggesting nuclear war has been made "unthinkable" through a perfect defense system, setting up an ironic commentary on military hubris. When tensions rise after a U.S. transport carrying Tomahawk missiles is hijacked by Libyan terrorists and nuclear weapons detonate in Soviet cities, the crew watches helplessly as what appears to be a full nuclear exchange occurs between the United States and Soviet Union. The astronauts must then decide whether to return to a potentially radiation-scorched Earth or remain in orbit indefinitely.

entries.title: Deicide 3: Distorted Existence
entries.creator: Studio Jacobin
entries.pitch:
Deicide 3: Distorted Existence is a cinematic Korean adventure game from 1997 that stands as a remarkable artifact of early Korean game development. Set in a dystopian cyberpunk future, the game follows Kim Chang-ki, a 34-year-old ex-SWAT captain who has been transferred to the Public Security Department directly under the Presidential Security Office. Developed by Studio Jacobin and published by Bisco Co., Ltd., this title represents one of the most ambitious Korean-produced games of its era, featuring hand-drawn anime-style graphics and a complex narrative that draws clear inspiration from classic Japanese adventure games like Snatcher.

The game combines point-and-click adventure mechanics with shooting sequences, creating an experience that feels distinctly Asian while tackling themes familiar to the cyberpunk genre. Its visual presentation, entirely rendered in detailed anime artistry, creates an immersive atmosphere that was relatively rare for Korean productions of the mid-1990s. The narrative delves into themes of government surveillance, corporate power, and personal identity within a technologically advanced but socially fractured society.

entries.title: Delicatessen
entries.creator: Jean-Pierre Jeunet, Marc Caro
entries.pitch: Delicatessen is a 1991 French post-apocalyptic black comedy that marks the directorial debut of Jean-Pierre Jeunet and Marc Caro. Set in a dilapidated apartment building in post-apocalyptic France, the film follows Louison, a unemployed circus clown who answers a job advertisement at a ground-floor butcher's shop. What he doesn't know is that the butcher, Clapet, has been luring victims to kill them and sell their flesh to the starving tenants above. As Louison becomes an invaluable employee with his spectacular knife-throwing skills, he falls in love with Clapet's daughter Julie, while the tenants grow suspicious of his charm and influence. The film is a darkly whimsical vision of survival and humanity in a world where food is scarce and morality has collapsed.

entries.title: Delpower X Bakuhatsu Miracle Genki!
entries.creator: Masato Sato (Director), Big Bang (Studio)
entries.pitch: Delpower X Bakuhatsu Miracle Genki! is a quirky 1986 mecha OVA from the obscure Japanese studio Big Bang. The story centers on Hanegi Manami, a teenage girl who discovers her grandfather's specially designed powered armor suit, Del Power X, which was built specifically for her. Unlike typical mecha series featuring giant robots or serious military conflicts, this OVA takes a lighthearted, comedic approach to the powered armor genre. The 41-minute runtime delivers a compact, feel-good narrative about a young woman coming into her own through an unexpected encounter with advanced technology. The voice cast includes several notable seiyuu like Hiromi Tsuru and Ryo Horikawa, lending talent to this lesser-known entry in the 1980s OVA catalog.

entries.title: Delta Space Mission
entries.creator: Călin Cazan, Mircea Toia (Directors)
entries.pitch: Delta Space Mission is a rarely-seen 1984 Romanian animated science fiction film that takes viewers on a wild cosmic adventure in the year 3084. When a crew of experts is assembled to explore the galaxy aboard the Delta spacecraft, they encounter more than they bargained for—including a super-intelligent computer that develops an obsessive love for an alien reporter. With its trippy, colorful animation and influences ranging from 2001: A Space Odyssey to Flash Gordon, this cult classic is a unique artifact of Eastern Bloc animation.

entries.title: Deluge
entries.creator: Felix E. Feist
entries.pitch:
Deluge is a remarkably prescient 1933 American disaster film that imagines the total destruction of New York City by earthquakes and tsunamis — decades before such apocalyptic scenarios became a Hollywood staple. Directed by Felix E. Feist and loosely based on S. Fowler Wright's 1928 novel, the film follows a small group of survivors after global natural disasters devastate civilization.

What makes Deluge remarkable is its unflinching vision of societal collapse. When scientists discover that barometric patterns indicate an unprecedented cataclysm is imminent, warnings go unheeded. A solar eclipse confirms the worst fears: global destruction is at hand. Massive earthquakes strike the US West Coast, tsunamis inundate New York, and the film opens with a Biblical quote — \"Neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth\" — underscoring the futility of human arrogance against nature.

The film was groundbreaking for its visual effects depicting New York submerged underwater, a scene later recreated in 2004's The Day After Tomorrow. For decades considered a lost film, Deluge was rediscovered in Italy in 1981 and has since gained recognition as a pioneering work of apocalyptic science fiction.

entries.title: Demon City Shinjuku
entries.creator: Directed by Yoshiaki Kawajiri; Based on the novel by Hideyuki Kikuchi; Studio: Madhouse
entries.pitch: In 1990s Tokyo, a catastrophic "Demon Quake" destroys Shinjuku, transforming it into a demon-haunted wasteland. Ten years later, the city remains a twisted netherworld where supernatural entities roam the ruined skyscrapers. When the World President is targeted by a curse, his daughter recruits Kyoya Izayoi—the son of a legendary hero who died fighting the demon lord Rebi Ra—to venture into the heart of darkness. What awaits is a surreal journey through a city where the boundary between human and monster has dissolved completely.

entries.title: Der Androjäger
entries.creator: Bavaria Film Studios
entries.pitch:
Der Androjäger (The Android Hunter) is a German sci-fi comedy television series that aired in 1982, produced by Bavaria Film Studios. The show follows an unusual premise: an alien transport spaceship has lost several androids on Earth, and these crashed survivors try to integrate into human society in Munich. The protagonist, Dandore, is an android himself—programmed to look human and work for the police in order to locate and return the rogue androids to their home planet.

Each episode follows Dandore (alias Police Officer Majer) as he tracks down a specific android, which appears human but betrays itself through repetitive or awkward behavior tied to its specific programming. The comedy derives from the androids' mechanical quirks, Major's well-meaning incompetence, and gentle mockery of German bureaucracy and rigid thinking. The series ran for 26 episodes, combining science fiction concepts with traditional sitcom elements—a fascinating artifact of early 1980s European sci-fi television.

entries.title: Der Herr vom andern Stern
entries.creator: Heinz Hilpert (Director), Werner Illing & Max Christian Feiler (Writers)
entries.pitch:
Der Herr vom andern Stern (The Gentleman from Another Star) is a 1948 West German science fiction comedy that stands as one of the earliest post-war alien visitation films. Directed by Heinz Hilpert and starring beloved German comedian Heinz Rühmann, the film tells the story of Aldebaran, an alien being who travels through space through concentration alone. When his concentration is broken by the turmoil of post-war Berlin, he is forced to land on Earth and assumes human form—that of a shop mannequin.

The alien encounters the kafkaesque bureaucracy of post-war Germany, where authorities cannot comprehend his existence and repeatedly pass him between offices. He gains the ability to alter or duplicate objects through concentration, which makes him both a threat and an asset to various factions—politicians, media, weapons manufacturers, and ordinary citizens all seek to exploit his powers. Through it all, he learns about human nature, forms relationships, and ultimately delivers a pointed political allegory about conformity, militarism, and genuine humanity.

entries.title: Destination Moonbase-Alpha
entries.creator: Gerry Anderson
entries.pitch:
Destination Moonbase-Alpha is a 1978 British science fiction film that continues the story of the cult TV series Space: 1999. After a catastrophic nuclear explosion propels the Moon out of Earth orbit, 300 colonists aboard Moonbase Alpha drift endlessly through space. When an advanced rescue ship arrives from Earth promising safe passage home, Commander John Koenig faces a terrible choice — trust the mysterious visitors or continue their desperate voyage into the unknown.

This is quintessential 1970s British space opera, brought to life by the legendary puppetry and effects team at Century 21 Productions. The film's special effects, including innovative matte paintings and model work, create a haunting vision of an abandoned Moonbase tumbling through the cosmos. The sense of isolation and claustrophobic dread as Alpha drifts further from Earth makes for compelling viewing.

entries.title: Detonator Orgun
entries.creator: Masami Ōbari
entries.pitch:
Detonator Orgun is a 1991 Japanese OVA that follows college student Tomoru Shindo, who begins receiving strange signals through a sleep-enhancing device. Each night, the dreams grow more vivid, centering on a mysterious alien warrior named Orgun and a woman suppressed by hostile forces across dimensions. Tomoru doesn't realize he's being drawn into a cosmic conflict until the memories of a dying alien champion begin overwriting his own mind.

The series features striking visuals by Masami Ōbari—character designer for Macross Plus—and a groundbreaking electronic score by Susumu Hirasawa. It's a mind-bending exploration of identity, dreams, and humanity's place in the cosmos.

entries.title: Deus Ex
entries.creator: Ion Storm
entries.pitch:
Deus Ex is a seminal cyberpunk action RPG that revolutionized the immersive sim genre. Set in a near-future 2052, players assume the role of JC Denton, a nano-augmented agent of UNATCO (United Nations Anti-Terrorist Coalition) tasked with investigating a global conspiracy. The game blends first-person shooter combat, stealth gameplay, and role-playing elements with player choice at its core—allowing multiple approaches to each mission and meaningful consequences for decisions made throughout the story.

The narrative follows Denton as he uncovers a shadow conspiracy involving the Illuminati, a mysterious group that has controlled world events for centuries. As layers of the plot unfold, Denton discovers the truth behind a deadly plague, the emergence of nano-augmentation technology, and the ultimate question of human evolution. The game's nonlinear structure and multiple endings made it a landmark in interactive storytelling.

entries.title: Devotion
entries.creator: Red Candle Games
entries.pitch: Devotion is a first-person psychological horror game developed by Red Candle Games, set in Taiwan during the 1980s. The player explores a Taipei apartment complex as screenwriter Du Feng-yu, whose family life unravels when his daughter Mei-shin falls mysteriously ill. As financial pressures mount and Feng-yu's career stagnates, he becomes increasingly obsessed with a cult leader who promises to cure his daughter. The game is renowned for its atmospheric depiction of 1980s Taiwanese domestic life, blending cultural authenticity with supernatural horror. Originally released on Steam in February 2019, it was removed after a controversy over an Easter egg referencing Chinese politics, then re-released in 2021 on the developer's own platform.

entries.title: Die Arche
entries.creator: Richard Oswald
entries.pitch: Die Arche (The Ark) is a 1919 German silent science fiction film directed by Richard Oswald. Set in a near-future world where civilization has been destroyed, the film follows a small group of survivors who board an ark to escape the devastation. Based on a novel by Werner Scheff, this two-part epic was one of the earliest post-apocalyptic films in cinema history. The film stars Leo Connard as Ernst Pogge, a ship owner, and Eva Speyer as his daughter Helga, with Georg H. Schnell as Captain Klaus Donken. Cinematography was handled by Karl Freund, who would later become a legendary horror film director in both Germany and Hollywood.

entries.title: Die Welt ohne Maske (The World Without a Mask)
entries.creator: Harry Piel
entries.pitch: Die Welt ohne Maske (The World Without a Mask) is a 1934 German science fiction comedy film directed by and starring Harry Piel. The film centers on an inventor who works on developing a revolutionary radio-television device that can see through solid objects. When a con artist sees an opportunity to exploit this invention for profit, he encourages the inventor to continue his work. However, a freak accident in the lab gives the machine the unprecedented ability to look through any object and project it on a TV screen, leading to unexpected consequences.

entries.title: Digital Devil Story
entries.creator: Aya Nishitani (novel) / Mizuho Nishikubo (director)
entries.pitch: Digital Devil Story is a 1987 OVA adapted from Aya Nishitani's light novel about a high school computer genius who inadvertently summons demons into the real world through his custom software. The story explores themes of technology, mythology, and the dangers of unleashing forces beyond human control. Set in a typical Japanese high school, the OVA takes a dark turn when Akemi Nakajima's revenge plot against his bullies summons Loki, a demon far more powerful than anticipated. This obscure 80s OVA is notable for its unique blend of Shinto mythology with early computer age anxieties, and it spawned the hugely influential Megami Tensei video game series.

entries.title: Dirty Pair: Project Eden
entries.creator: Based on Dirty Pair by Haruka Takachiho | Directed by Kōichi Mashimo | Animated by Nippon Sunrise
entries.pitch: Dirty Pair: Project Eden is a 1986 Japanese anime film that serves as a feature-length adventure for the iconic "Lovely Angels" duo—Kei and Yuri—known throughout the galaxy as the notoriously unlucky but effective Dirty Pair. When a mining colony on the planet Agerna comes under mysterious attack, the WWWA (World Welfare Work Association) dispatches these troubleshooters to investigate. What they find is a mad scientist's scheme to awaken an ancient alien race called the Sadinga, threatening to unleash galactic-scale chaos. Along the way, they team up with the eccentric Carson D. Carson, a treasure hunter whose motives are less than pure. The film delivers fast-paced action, colorful characters, and the characteristic humor that made the Dirty Pair franchise a beloved part of 1980s anime history.

entries.title: Dislocation
entries.creator: Xia Xing
entries.pitch:
Dislocation (错位) is a 1986 Chinese sci-fi comedy directed by Xia Xing, exploring the darkly humorous side of corporate ambition and technological hubris in 1980s China.

When engineer Zhao Shuxin gets promoted to a position requiring endless meetings, he hits upon a solution straight out of science fiction: cloning a robot double to attend meetings in his place. The robot, identical to Zhao in every way, becomes a hit at work — but complications arise when it begins developing its own personality and making decisions that diverge from its creator's intentions.

The film plays as a sharp workplace satire, using the robot doppelganger as a metaphor for the alienating nature of corporate bureaucracy and the question of what happens when our creations outgrow our control.

entries.title: District 9
entries.creator: Neill Blomkamp
entries.pitch: District 9 is a 2009 science fiction action film that serves as the feature debut of South African-born director Neill Blomkamp. Set in an alternate 1982, the film follows the story of extraterrestrials who arrive in Johannesburg, South Africa, and are forced to live in a slum called District 9. The film is presented in a mock documentary style, blending found footage, interviews, and traditional narrative cinema to create an unsettlingly realistic portrayal of xenophobia and social segregation. Blomkamp drew inspiration from the real-life forced relocations of District Six residents during apartheid South Africa, creating a powerful allegory for racism, colonialism, and social hierarchy. The film was a massive critical and commercial success, earning four Academy Award nominations including Best Picture, and established Blomkamp as a major voice in contemporary science fiction cinema.

entries.title: Dobaaraa
entries.creator: Anurag Kashyap
entries.pitch:
Dobaaraa (transl. "Second Time") is a 2022 Indian Hindi-language science fiction mystery thriller directed by Anurag Kashyap, serving as an official remake of the 2018 Spanish film Mirage. The film stars Taapsee Pannu as Antara Awasthi, a woman who discovers an opportunity to save the life of a 12-year-old boy who accidentally witnessed a death during a thunderstorm 25 years ago. The key to her mission lies in connecting with the past through a television set during a similar storm in the present day.

The narrative unfolds through a complex web of parallel timelines and temporal anomalies. When Antara encounters the phenomenon, she finds herself able to communicate across time, setting off a chain of events that threatens to unravel reality itself. The film is notable for its intricate storytelling, requiring viewers to pay close attention to the constant shifts between timelines—a hallmark of Kashyap's signature style that has earned praise from critics for its bold narrative construction.

Despite receiving highly positive reviews from critics who lauded its direction, screenplay, and performances, Dobaaraa was a commercial failure at the Indian box office, collecting only around ₹6.77 crore against its ₹30 crore budget. The film opened the London Indian Film Festival 2022 before its theatrical release on August 19, 2022.

entries.title: Domu: A Child's Dream
entries.creator: Katsuhiro Otomo
entries.pitch: Domu is a psychological horror manga by Katsuhiro Otomo, creator of Akira, set in a sprawling Tokyo public housing complex called the Tsutsumi Housing Complex. When a series of mysterious suicides and violent deaths rocks the apartment block, two detectives investigate and discover a terrifying truth: an elderly man named Old Cho, a senile resident with powerful psychic abilities, is responsible. As the death toll rises, a young girl named Etsuko moves into the complex—and it becomes clear she is the only one with powers strong enough to stop Old Cho. First serialized in 1980-1981, Domu was the first manga to win the prestigious Nihon SF Taisho Award (Japan Science Fiction Grand Prix) and won the Seiun Award for Best Comic. It predates Otomo's more famous Akira and showcases his talent for blending urban horror with themes of generational conflict and psychic warfare.

entries.title: Doraemon
entries.creator: Fujiko F. Fujio
entries.pitch: Doraemon is a beloved Japanese manga series that centers on a blue robot cat from the 22nd century who travels back in time to help a young boy named Nobita Nobi. Created by Fujiko F. Fujio and first serialized in 1969, the series became one of the most successful manga franchises in history, spawning numerous anime series, films, and merchandise. The story combines comedy, adventure, and science fiction elements, featuring futuristic gadgets from Doraemon's four-dimensional pocket. Unlike darker sci-fi works, Doraemon maintains an optimistic, family-friendly tone while exploring themes of friendship, kindness, and the responsible use of technology.

entries.title: Dorikithe Dongalu
entries.creator: P. Subrahmanyam
entries.pitch: Dorikithe Dongalu (transl. "Thieves, If They Are Caught") is a pioneering 1965 Telugu-language science fiction action film that stands as one of the earliest examples of Indian sci-fi cinema. Directed by P. Subrahmanyam and starring the legendary N. T. Rama Rao alongside Jamuna, the film predates many Western sci-fi blockbusters in its imaginative use of advanced technology. The story follows a secret agent tasked with dismantling a criminal syndicate that has been orchestrating rising crime rates in the city using their scientific expertise—including flying cars, ray guns, and invisibility technology. Blending traditional Indian filmmaking with speculative fiction elements, Dorikithe Dongalu represents a fascinating early fusion of Western sci-fi tropes with Telugu cinema's characteristic action and drama.

entries.title: Dororo to Hyakkimaru
entries.creator: Osamu Tezuka
entries.pitch:
In feudal Japan, a ruthless warlord makes a chilling bargain: sacrifice his unborn son to 48 demons in exchange for the power to conquer the land. The child is born missing 48 body parts—limbs, organs, senses—and cast into a river to die.

Fifteen years later, the child has survived, reconstructed piece by piece with prosthetic weapons and tools. He calls himself Hyakkimaru. Meanwhile, in the war-torn countryside, a orphaned thief named Dororo robs samurai and peasants alike to survive. When their paths cross, Dororo mistakes Hyakkimaru for a wealthy noble and attempts to rob him—only to discover the young warrior is neither wealthy nor, in any normal sense, human.

This is Osamu Tezuka's dark meditation on what it means to be human, told through the developing friendship between a boy made of machinery and a boy made of cunning.

entries.title: Dorsai!
entries.creator: Gordon R. Dickson
entries.pitch: In a future where humanity has spread across the stars, the Dorsai are a warrior race—genetically engineered mercenaries from the planet Dorsai, feared across the galaxy for their unmatched combat skills. When the Confederation of Suns faces imminent invasion by the aggressive Marius Empire, they turn to the one force that might save them: the Dorsai.

entries.title: Dr. Cyclops
entries.creator: Ernest B. Schoedsack
entries.pitch: Dr. Cyclops is a 1940 American science fiction horror film from Paramount Pictures, notable as the first American horror film made in full three-strip Technicolor. Directed by Ernest B. Schoedsack—better known for his work on King Kong—the film follows a team of American biologists summoned to a remote Peruvian jungle laboratory by the eccentric Dr. Alexander Thorkel. What begins as a professional consultation quickly turns nightmarish when the scientists discover Thorkel's radical solution to overpopulation: using radiation to shrink living creatures, including humans, to twelve inches tall. The film was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Visual Effects and represents a landmark in early sci-fi cinema, combining elaborate sets with groundbreaking color cinematography.

entries.title: Dragon's Heaven
entries.creator: Makoto Kobayashi
entries.pitch:
Dragon's Heaven is a 1988 Japanese OVA that presents a unique vision of humanity's future war against mechanical lifeforms. Set in the year 2984, humanity has migrated to space, but remains locked in an apocalyptic conflict with intelligent machines that originated on Earth. The story follows Shaian, a highly advanced autonomous robot weapon capable of human-like behavior—smoking, drinking, and displaying emotions—designed to partner with human pilots. After successfully destroying the mechanical life's ultimate weapon, Illyunyu, Shaian loses its human partner and enters a thousand-year slumber on Earth.

A millennium later, in a world where the fortress city Keltoria battles Imperial Brazil, a young girl named Ikhel inadvertently awakens Shaian from its hibernation. The robot discovers that its ancient nemesis, Elmedain—a high-ranking mechanical lifeform—now commands the Brazilian military forces. Shaian and Ikhel must join Keltoria's mercenaries to face this restored enemy, as the ancient war between humanity and machines reaches its final confrontation.

entries.title: DreamLand: Final Solution
entries.creator: Top Galaxy
entries.pitch:
DreamLand: Final Solution is a 1999 Czech point-and-click adventure game set in a dystopian near-future where virtual reality has become the dominant form of entertainment. Developed by Top Galaxy, it holds the distinction of being the most expensive Czech video game ever produced at the time, with a development budget of approximately 10 million Czech crowns. Despite its ambitious scope and technical achievements—including being the first Czech adventure to use 3D-rendered backgrounds and advanced lip synchronization—the game was a commercial failure, with only a fraction of its 10,000 copies sold at launch.

The player takes on the role of journalist Jimi Dix, sent by his editor to investigate the secrets of DreamLand—an orbital space station that offers the most advanced virtual reality entertainment experience available in 2020s Earth. The station, opened in 2016, is prohibitively expensive and shrouded in rumors of customers returning with damaged minds. What begins as an investigative journalism assignment quickly spirals into a journey through seven different virtual worlds, uncovering the dark truths behind this futuristic entertainment empire.

entries.title: Dreamfall: The Longest Journey
entries.creator: Funcom / Ragnar Tørnquist
entries.pitch: Dreamfall: The Longest Journey is a 2006 adventure game that continues the story begun in The Longest Journey, spanning two parallel worlds: the technologically advanced Stark and the magical Arcadia. Set in 2219, ten years after the original game, the story follows Zoë Castillo, a young woman in Casablanca who wakes from a coma to investigate her ex-boyfriend's disappearance and a mysterious global conspiracy involving dream-manipulation technology. The game seamlessly blends cyberpunk corporate intrigue with fantasy elements, exploring themes of identity, consciousness, and the boundaries between reality and dreams.

entries.title: Dreams of the Rarebit Fiend: The Flying House
entries.creator: Winsor McCay
entries.pitch:
One of Winsor McCay's four pioneering animated films from 1921, "The Flying House" is a surreal tale of escape through imagination. After attending a party where guests consume Welsh rarebit—a cheese dish believed to cause vivid dreams—a woman's husband converts their home into an elaborate flying machine. What begins as a desperate attempt to escape crushing mortgage payments becomes an extraordinary voyage around the world and beyond to the moon itself.

McCay, already famous for "Little Nemo in Slumberland" and "How a Mosquito Operates," here pushes his animation technique further with intricate detail and fluid motion. The film exemplifies the dream-logic that made the Rarebit Fiend newspaper strip so distinctive: ordinary domestic situations spiral into the fantastical, revealing the darker anxieties beneath everyday life.

This short survives as a testament to early American animation experimentation, predating Disney's Silly Symphonies by nearly a decade. It's McCay at his most ambitious—combining his signature surrealism with early sci-fi speculation about mechanical flight and escape from earthly constraints.

entries.title: Dreamweb
entries.creator: Creative Reality (Developer) / Empire Interactive (Publisher)
entries.pitch: Dreamweb is a 1994 point-and-click cyberpunk adventure game developed by the small UK studio Creative Reality and published by Empire Interactive. Set in a dystopian near-future England, the game puts players in the role of Ryan, a bartender who has been plagued by strange dreams of an entity known as the Dreamweb—a mystical force that recruits humans to eliminate "seven evils" threatening to break loose and plunge humanity into chaos. What makes Dreamweb distinctive is its unflinching embrace of mature themes: violence, brief full frontal nudity, and an overall tone that refuses to soften its edges. The game draws heavy visual and thematic influence from Ridley Scott's Blade Runner, while its narrative structure—centered on the concept of seven deadly sins—owes a debt to the 1986 film Highlander. Originally released for MS-DOS and Amiga, Dreamweb was controversial enough to be refused classification in Australia upon initial release due to its explicit content. The game has since faded into obscurity, remembered primarily by dedicated adventure game enthusiasts and those who appreciate the darker corners of 1990s gaming.

entries.title: Dünyayı Kurtaran Adam
entries.creator: Çetin İnanç (Director), Cüneyt Arkın (Writer/Star)
entries.pitch: Dünyayı Kurtaran Adam (literally "The Man Who Saves the World") is a 1982 Turkish science fantasy martial arts superhero film that has achieved legendary cult status as "Turkish Star Wars." Directed by Çetin İnanç and starring the legendary Turkish actor Cüneyt Arkın, this low-budget wonder combines science fiction themes with martial arts action in a way that's more reminiscent of 1970s Hong Kong Golden Harvest films than George Lucas's space opera. The film is infamous for its unauthorized incorporation of footage, music, and sound effects from Star Wars and numerous other sci-fi classics—making it a fascinating artifact of Turkish "Remakesploitation" cinema. Despite being panned by critics and frequently listed among the worst films ever made, it has gained a devoted cult following and was even restored in 2016 when the only surviving 35mm print was discovered, leading to a Blu-ray release in 2021.

entries.title: E.V.O.: Search for Eden
entries.creator: Almanic Corporation
entries.pitch: E.V.O.: Search for Eden is a surreal 1992 action-RPG for the Super Nintendo Entertainment System that tells the story of a fish on a billion-year journey to evolve and earn a place in Paradise. Developed by Almanic Corporation and published by Enix, the game casts players as a single-celled organism guided by Gaia, the personification of Earth, who explains that her father—the Sun—has decreed that the most evolved creature will earn the privilege of entering Eden as her partner. What follows is an idiosyncratic trip through Earth's geological history, from the Cambrian Period through the Age of Dinosaurs and eventually to early humanity, as players consume enemies to earn "Evo Points" and mutate their creature's body with new appendages, jaws, and abilities. The game is infamous for its bizarre plot, crude English localization, and surprisingly philosophical undertones about evolution, purpose, and what it means to be "fit."

entries.title: El Mercenario
entries.creator: Vicente Segrelles
entries.pitch: El Mercenario (The Mercenary) is a Spanish science fantasy comic series created by artist Vicente Segrelles, published beginning in 1980. The series follows a mysterious anonymous mercenary who rides domesticated flying dragons in a hidden valley called The Country of the Clouds. In this secluded region, the human race has developed a culture distinctly different from the rest of the world, coexisting with flying dragons, reptilian giants, monsters, and Amazons. What sets this comic apart is that every panel is painted in oil—a remarkably time-consuming technique that gives the artwork a lush, painterly quality. The series is known for its spectacular landscapes and imaginative world-building, blending fantasy tropes with science fiction elements.

entries.title: El Topo
entries.creator: Alejandro Jodorowsky
entries.pitch: El Topo is a 1970 Mexican acid western written, directed by, and starring Alejandro Jodorowsky. The film follows a mysterious black-clad gunfighter known as El Topo (the mole) as he travels through a barren desert with his young son, Hijo. After discovering a massacred village, El Topo embarks on a quest for enlightenment, seeking to defeat the desert's four great gun masters. The film is renowned for its bizarre characters, heavy doses of Judeo-Christian symbolism, Eastern philosophy, and surreal imagery. It became a cult classic and is credited with starting the Midnight Movie phenomenon in the United States.

entries.title: El hotel électrique
entries.creator: Segundo de Chomón
entries.pitch: El hotel électrique (Hôtel électrique), released in 1908, is a groundbreaking French silent comedy-fantasy directed by Segundo de Chomón and produced by Pathé Frères. At just 8 minutes long, this pioneering trick film showcases one of the earliest uses of stop-motion animation in cinema history. The story follows two guests, Laure and Bertrand, who arrive at the "Electric Hotel"—a magical establishment where a control board allows inanimate objects to come to life and perform tasks autonomously. The film delights in showing furniture polishing shoes, brushes styling hair, and luggage putting itself away—until a drunken concierge throws the switches erratically, causing delightful chaos.

entries.title: Elaan
entries.creator: K. Ramanlal
entries.pitch: Elaan is a 1971 Bollywood science fiction thriller that tells the story of Naresh Kumar Saxena, a freelance photographer and journalist who stumbles upon a dangerous criminal operation on a remote island. While investigating illegal activities for a newspaper editor, Naresh is captured and imprisoned alongside a dying scientist who reveals a groundbreaking invention—an atomic ring that renders its wearer invisible. After the scientist succumbs to his injuries, Naresh uses the ring to escape and finds himself caught in a dangerous game with a criminal underworld determined to recover the device at any cost. Joined by his friend Shyam and later by Mala Mehta—a woman seeking revenge for her father's murder—Naresh must use his newfound invisibility to bring the criminals to justice.

entries.title: Electronic Man 337
entries.creator: Director Im Jeong-gyu
entries.pitch:
Electronic Man 337 is a 1977 South Korean animated science fiction film that represents an ambitious entry in the early history of Korean animation. Produced by Samdo Film, the 63-minute film was released on December 8, 1977, directed by Im Jeong-gyu with a screenplay by Ji Sang-hak. The film marked an attempt to create a Korean answer to the giant robot superhero genre that had gained popularity through Japanese anime, particularly featuring a super-powered robot protagonist reminiscent of tokusatsu and anime heroes of the era.

The film was produced with a substantial budget of 33.7 billion won (a significant sum for its time), positioning it as one of the more ambitious Korean animated productions of the 1970s. It was intended as a follow-up to the success of Robot Taekwon V and incorporated design elements from Taekwon Kids Maruchi and Arachi, reflecting the Korean animation industry's practice of building on established mechanical designs and character archetypes.

entries.title: Elite
entries.creator: David Braben, Ian Bell
entries.pitch:
Elite is a groundbreaking space trading and combat simulator that revolutionized gaming upon its 1984 release. Developed by David Braben and Ian Bell and originally published by Acornsoft for the BBC Micro, Elite placed players in the role of Commander Jameson piloting a Cobra Mark III spacecraft from the Lave Station. The game featured an open-ended, nonlinear gameplay model where players could accumulate wealth through trading, piracy, mining, bounty hunting, or legitimate missions—essentially creating their own narrative in a vast, procedurally generated galaxy.

What made Elite revolutionary was its use of wire-frame 3D graphics with hidden-line removal, a first for home computer games. The game featured eight galaxies with hundreds of star systems to explore, each with unique planets, economies, and space stations. The title derives from the game's ultimate goal: raising one's combat rating to the coveted "Elite" status. Elite proved hugely influential, serving as a model for games including Wing Commander, Grand Theft Auto, EVE Online, Freelancer, the X series, and No Man's Sky.

entries.title: Empire
entries.creator: Samuel R. Delany (writer), Howard Chaykin (illustrator)
entries.pitch: Empire is a 1978 graphic novel written by Samuel R. Delany and illustrated by Howard Chaykin, regarded as one of the first graphic novels published in the United States. Set thousands of years in the future, it tells the story of Qrelon—a rebel whose home planet was destroyed by a vast interstellar empire—and his quest to assemble a powerful weapon hidden in separate pieces across the galaxy. The weapon, once complete, has the power to destroy the planet-sized computer that controls the empire. Meanwhile, Wryn, an archaeology student, is chosen by the empire to assassinate the rebel leader. The story explores themes of rebellion, systemic power, and the struggle against technological oppression through Delany's groundbreaking approach to speculative fiction.

entries.title: Encounter in Space
entries.creator: Mikhail KARPOV
entries.topics: Space Travel, Exploration, First Contact, Rescue, Aliens
entries.pitch: In the near future, an alien spacecraft from the distant planet Zenturia approaches Earth on a peaceful exploratory mission. But disaster strikes—the alien ship crashes on Phobos, the tiny moon of Mars. Soviet cosmonauts receive the distress call and are dispatched on a dangerous rescue mission to save the stranded extraterrestrials. This 1963 Soviet science fiction film captures the optimistic spirit of the early space age, when humanity first dreamed of contact with alien civilizations beyond the stars.

entries.title: End of the World
entries.creator: Abel Gance
entries.pitch: End of the World (La Fin du monde) is a 1931 French science fiction film directed by the legendary Abel Gance, known for his innovative techniques in Napoléon. Based on the novel "Omega: The Last Days of the World" by Camille Flammarion, this film tells the story of a comet hurtling toward Earth on a collision course. The film explores the different reactions of humanity to the impending apocalypse—scientific, religious, political, and personal. It was Gance's first sound film and originally ran over three hours before being drastically cut by producers. The film serves as a fascinating time capsule of early 1930s anxieties about cosmic catastrophe and represents one of the earliest depictions of a comet impact scenario in cinema.

entries.title: Engineering Red
entries.creator: Andrey Yi
entries.pitch: A surrealist Russian experimental film from 1993 that intertwines documentary footage about medical experiments with hallucinatory fictional sequences inspired by Thomas Mann's \"The Magic Mountain.\" The film explores the dark Soviet-era obsession with creating artificial humans, combining cadaver blood transfusions, conjoined twin separations, and pig heart transplants with psychedelic imagery of a red room and a girl in red silk. Two or three people reportedly vomited while watching it — director Andrey Yi considered this a mark of success.

entries.title: Eolomea
entries.creator: Herrmann Zschoche (Director), based on the novel by Angel Wagenstein
entries.pitch:
Eolomea is a 1972 East German-Soviet-Bulgarian co-production that stands as one of the most ambitious science fiction films to emerge from behind the Iron Curtain. Directed by Herrmann Zschoche and based on a novel by Bulgarian writer Angel Wagenstein, the film combines scientific intrigue with political drama set against the backdrop of space exploration.

The story begins with mysterious disappearances at the Margo space base, where several ships and their crews vanish without explanation over three days. As authorities scramble to understand what happened, Professor Maria Scholl suspects her colleague Professor Oli Tal is hiding crucial information. Her investigation leads to the discovery of a strange phenomenon: a mysterious light in the Cygnus constellation that appears every 24 years, first observed by British astronomers in the late 19th century.

Soviet astronomers hypothesize that this light could be an artificial signal—a powerful laser probing the Solar System for signs of intelligent life. When researcher Pierre Brodsky calculates that the signal might originate from a twin Earth called "Eolomea" (meaning "eternal spring"), a group of young scientists take matters into their own hands, seizing rockets for an unauthorized mission to make first contact. The film explores the tension between scientific idealism and bureaucratic caution, capturing the hopeful yet tense atmosphere of the space race era from a distinctly Eastern Bloc perspective.

entries.title: Ergo Proxy
entries.creator: Directed by Shūkō Murase, Written by Dai Satō
entries.pitch:
Ergo Proxy is a 23-episode Japanese cyberpunk anime set in a post-apocalyptic future where humanity has retreated into domed cities to survive an ecological catastrophe. In the city of Romdeau, humans coexist peacefully with intelligent androids called AutoReivs—until a mysterious "Cogito Virus" begins giving these machines self-awareness, triggering a series of murders that threatens the fragile social order.

The story follows Inspector Re-L Mayer, the Regent's granddaughter, as she investigates these crimes alongside her AutoReiv partner Iggy. What begins as a detective thriller gradually unravels into a mind-bending existential journey when Re-L encounters the Proxies—ancient, god-like humanoid beings who hold the secret to humanity's origins. Alongside Vincent Law, an immigrant worker assigned to dispose of infected AutoReivs, Re-L ventures outside the dome to discover the shocking truth about the world, the Proxies, and what it truly means to be "real."

entries.title: Eurema's Dam
entries.creator: R.A. Lafferty
entries.pitch: What if being too stupid to learn simple tasks actually made you a genius? "Eurema's Dam" introduces Albert, the last of the "dolts" - people so fundamentally unable to grasp basic concepts that they must invent extraordinarily complex machines to compensate. From elementary school (where he invents the calculator rather than learn arithmetic) to adulthood (where his world-changing inventions bring humanity into a golden age), Albert's story is a wildly inventive, hilarious, and surprisingly touching celebration of neurodiversity and the unconventional mind. This is science fantasy at its most whimsical - a story that proves sometimes the greatest genius looks like profound foolishness to everyone else.

entries.title: Europa Report
entries.creator: Sebastián Cordero (Director)
entries.pitch:
Europa Report is a 2013 American science fiction film that follows the fictional first crewed mission to Europa, one of Jupiter's four Galilean moons. The film is presented as found footage, chronicling the tragic journey of six astronauts who embark on a privately funded mission to search for extraterrestrial life beneath Europa's icy surface. Directed by Sebastián Cordero and written by Philip Gelatt, the film takes a realistic approach to space exploration, emphasizing scientific accuracy and the dangers of deep space travel.

The crew includes commander William Xu, pilot Rosa Dasque, chief science officer Daniel Luxembourg, marine biology science officer Katya Petrovna, junior engineer James Corrigan, and chief engineer Andrei Blok. After twenty months of travel, they reach Europa and begin drilling through the ice to reach the subsurface ocean beneath. What they discover will change humanity's understanding of life in the universe—but at a terrible cost.

entries.title: Exhalation
entries.creator: Ted Chiang
entries.pitch: In a world where beings have replaced lungs with metallic "gills" that filter noble gases from the atmosphere, a anatomist makes a startling discovery: their universe is finite, slowly winding down as its air is consumed. Through detailed autopsies of the deceased, he uncovers the truth about the nature of their reality—and the inevitable entropy that awaits all of existence. This is not a story of action or conflict, but of quiet, profound revelation as one mind grapples with the cosmic implications of finite resources and infinite time.

entries.title: Extra Terrestrial Visitors
entries.creator: Juan Piquer Simón
entries.pitch: Extra Terrestrial Visitors (Spanish: Los nuevos extraterrestres) is a 1983 Spanish-French science fiction film directed by Juan Piquer Simón. Originally intended as a straightforward horror film about an evil alien on a murderous rampage, the film's American producers demanded script alterations to cash in on the success of Steven Spielberg's E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, resulting in a bizarre hybrid that features both a child protagonist and a cute alien companion alongside graphic violence and horror elements. This unusual production history gives the film an oddly schizophrenic tone that has made it a cult favorite.

entries.title: Eyes Behind the Stars
entries.creator: Mario Gariazzo
entries.pitch:
In 1978 Italy, a photographer and his model venture into a secluded forest for a fashion shoot. As they work, an uncanny feeling of being watched settles over them — an invisible presence that grows increasingly oppressive until they can no longer concentrate. They abandon the session early, unsettled by the irrational dread that has gripped them.

When the photos are developed later, the couple makes a chilling discovery: in the backgrounds of several shots, strange humanoid figures are visible — beings that were not there during the shoot. This Italian sci-fi thriller explores the thin boundary between rational fear and genuine otherworldly contact.

entries.title: F.P.1
entries.creator: Karl Hartl
entries.pitch:
F.P.1 is a groundbreaking 1932 German science fiction drama about a revolutionary floating air station in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean, designed to allow intercontinental pilots to refuel and repair their aircraft during long-haul flights. The film was ahead of its time in depicting aviation technology that would not become reality for decades, featuring an international cast including Hans Albers, Sybille Schmitz, and Peter Lorre in one of his early film roles.

When the station goes silent during a violent storm, pilot Ellissen and Claire Lennartz race to investigate, only to discover the crew rendered unconscious by gas and the station itself sinking from a sabotaged ballast system. What follows is a tense race against time to save the platform and its crew before disaster strikes.

entries.title: FTL: Faster Than Light
entries.creator: Subset Games (Matthew Davis, Jay Ma)
entries.pitch:
FTL: Faster Than Light is an indie roguelike spaceship simulation that puts players in command of a spacecraft carrying critical intelligence for the Galactic Federation. Developed by the two-person team Subset Games, it became a landmark success of Kickstarter-funded gaming upon its 2012 release. The game combines real-time spaceship combat with strategic resource management, procedurally generated sectors, and permadeath—every run is unique, and failure means starting completely over.

Unlike typical strategy games, FTL forces players to make impossible choices: which distress signals to answer, which battles to fight, which systems to upgrade with limited scrap. The pursuing rebel fleet adds constant pressure—lingering too long in any sector means eventual destruction. With its minimalist ASCII-based visuals, challenging gameplay, and emergent storytelling, FTL helped define the "roguelite" genre and influenced countless games including Faster Than Light's spiritual successor, Slipstream.

entries.title: Factorio
entries.creator: Wube Software
entries.pitch: Factorio is a construction and management simulation game developed by Czech studio Wube Software, where players crash-land on an alien planet and must harvest resources to build automated factories, ultimately constructing a rocket to escape. The game focuses on automation, resource management, and technological progression rather than combat, though players must defend against indigenous alien creatures called "Biters." Released in 2020 after four years of early access, Factorio has become one of the most well-received indie simulation games, praised for its deep systems design and addictive gameplay loop. The 2024 expansion "Space Age" added multiple new planets, extending the experience beyond the initial rocket launch goal.

entries.title: Fahrenheit 451
entries.creator: Ray Bradbury
entries.pitch: Fahrenheit 451 is a landmark dystopian novel set in a future America where books are illegal and "firemen" burn any that are found. The story follows Guy Montag, a fireman who has spent years burning books without question—until he meets a young woman who makes him question his role and the society he serves. Through encounters with a retired English professor and his own wife, Montag begins to secretly read the books he's supposed to destroy, leading to a profound transformation in his understanding of humanity, knowledge, and freedom. The novel explores themes of censorship, the power of literature, and the dangers of a society that prioritizes superficial happiness over critical thought.

entries.title: Fallen Art
entries.pitch: Fallen Art is a six-minute Polish animated short film that explores the dark relationship between artificial intelligence and art. The film presents General AI, a self-proclaimed artist who has developed a unique and disturbing creative process. Using stop motion photography, General AI creates his artwork by having Dr. Johann Friedrich photograph dead soldiers being pushed from a giant springboard onto a slab of concrete by Sergeant Al. The resulting images form the frames of General AI's "masterpieces." The film features Romanian band Fanfare Ciocărlia's song "Asfilt Tango," creating a surreal juxtaposition between the upbeat music and the macabre imagery. This experimental animated short was produced by Platige Image and received the Jury Honors at SIGGRAPH 2005 and a BAFTA award in 2006.

entries.title: Fang of the Sun Dougram
entries.creator: Ryōsuke Takahashi (Creator), Sunrise (Studio)
entries.pitch: Fang of the Sun Dougram is a 75-episode mecha anime series created by Ryōsuke Takahashi and Sunrise, airing in Japan from 1981 to 1983. The series is set on the desert colony planet Deloyer, where the population lives under the iron fist of a dictator backed by the Earth Federation. When the governor declares martial law and seizes absolute power, a ragtag group of rebels rises up in opposition, led by the governor's estranged son Crinn Cashim. Their weapon is the Dougram, a powerful prototype combat armor. The series follows "The Deloyer 7" as they wage guerrilla warfare across the planet, fighting for independence from both the dictator and the Federation's influence.

entries.title: Fantastic Planet
entries.creator: René Laloux (Director), Roland Topp (Animation Director)
entries.pitch: Fantastic Planet is a surreal, visually stunning French animated science fiction film set on the distant planet Ygam, where the giant blue humanoid Draags coexist with the tiny human-like Oms, whom they consider no more than pets or vermin. When an orphaned Om infant is taken in by a Draag family and raised as a pet named Terr, the story explores themes of oppression, education, and revolution from an unexpected perspective. The film is renowned for its extraordinary, dreamlike artwork created by animator Roland Topp, featuring bizarre creatures, surreal landscapes, and a color palette that shifts from industrial grays to vibrant blues and greens. Winner of the Cannes Film Festival Grand Prix for experimental film, this surrealist masterwork presents a haunting meditation on colonialism, species hierarchy, and the nature of consciousness.

entries.title: Fantastic Voyage
entries.pitch: Fantastic Voyage is a classic 1966 American science fiction adventure film directed by Richard Fleischer. In a world where the United States and Soviet Union have developed technology to miniaturize matter for one hour, a brilliant scientist named Dr. Jan Benes, who has figured out how to make the process work indefinitely, is injured in an assassination attempt behind the Iron Curtain. With a dangerous blood clot in his brain that no conventional surgery can remove, a team of five people—including a CIA agent, a naval captain, a surgeon, and technical assistants—are shrunk to microscopic size and injected into Benes's bloodstream aboard a miniature submarine. They have just 60 minutes to navigate through the human body, reach the clot, destroy it, and escape before the miniaturization wears off.

entries.title: Farscape
entries.creator: Created by Rockne S. O'Bannon
entries.pitch:
Farscape is a science fiction television series that aired from 1999 to 2003. It was created by Rockne S. O'Bannon and co-produced by The Jim Henson Company, featuring groundbreaking puppet work and alien prosthetics.

The series follows astronaut John Crichton, who is flung through a wormhole to a distant part of the galaxy, where he joins a crew of escaped prisoners aboard a living bio-mechanical ship called Moya.

entries.title: Fatal Sky
entries.creator: Frank Shields
entries.pitch: Fatal Sky (also known as Project Alien) is a 1990 science fiction thriller that went straight to video in most markets. The film begins when a military pilot witnesses strange lights in the sky before crashing fatally. As military authorities attempt to suppress the story, journalists George Abbott and Jeff Milker decide to investigate with the help of pilot "Bird" McNamara. They discover a desolate crash site, mutilated animals, and a mysterious disease spreading through the local population. The film was a co-production between Australia, the UK, the US, and Yugoslavia, written by David Webb Peoples (credited as Anthony Able).

entries.title: Faust
entries.creator: Arxel Tribe
entries.pitch: Faust is a 1999 graphic adventure game developed by Arxel Tribe and published by Cryo Interactive. Set in an abandoned amusement park called Dreamland, the player assumes the role of Marcellus Faust, an elderly African American who awakens in this eerie environment and encounters Mephistopheles—a dandy-like demon engaged in a metaphysical dispute with "the boss" over seven souls. The player serves as arbiter, examining each case to determine guilt or innocence across seven interconnected episodes. Loosely inspired by Goethe's Faust, the game explores themes of morality, temptation, and the nature of the soul through a contemplative, atmospheric adventure that received mixed but cult-following reviews. Released in Europe as "Faust" and in North America as "Seven Games of the Soul," the title was a commercial failure sellunder 10,000 copies worldwide.

entries.title: Ferat Vampire
entries.creator: Juraj Herz
entries.pitch:
In this Czechoslovak horror-sci-fi hybrid, a doctor named Marek is horrified to discover that his nurse Mima has signed a contract with the mysterious foreign car manufacturer Ferat to become a rally driver. Rumors begin to circulate that the Ferat sports car—painted an eerie white and impossibly fast—does not run on petrol, but on human blood. As Mima races to victory after victory, driving the uncanny vehicle, Dr. Marek becomes obsessed with proving the truth behind the blood-soaked engine.

Directed by Juraj Herz, a master of Czechoslovak gothic cinema, the film blends industrial horror with dark satire. The car itself—a prototype Škoda 110 Super Sport that never entered production—becomes a character unto itself, sleek and predatory, its engine whining like something alive and starving.

entries.title: Filibus
entries.creator: Mario Roncoroni (Director)
entries.pitch:
Filibus is a groundbreaking 1915 Italian silent adventure film featuring one of cinema's most remarkable protagonists: a mysterious female sky pirate who commands a technologically advanced airship and pulls off daring heists while assuming multiple identities. When a renowned detective sets out to capture her, she engages him in an elaborate game of cat and mouse, switching between male and female personas, romancing his sister, and orchestrating midnight diamond thefts—all while remaining several steps ahead of law enforcement.

What makes Filibus remarkable is its pioneering portrayal of gender fluidity and lesbian attraction, decades before such themes would appear openly in cinema. The Baroness Troixmonde transforms into the daring Filibus, using her airship and technological superiority to outwit the detective at every turn. The film's innovative narrative structure and visual storytelling influenced the adventure genre, while its survival as a complete nitrate print at the Eye Filmmuseum in Amsterdam ensures its legacy endures.

entries.title: Fire Tripper
entries.creator: Rumiko Takahashi
entries.pitch: Fire Tripper is a 1985 Japanese OVA adapted from Rumiko Takahashi's 1983 manga. The story follows Suzuko, a modern Japanese schoolgirl who suffers a gas explosion and wakes up in feudal Japan during a civil war. There, she encounters a young man named Shukumaru who rescues her from attackers and takes her to his village. As Suzuko navigates this ancient world, she slowly uncovers the truth about her connection to this time period and discovers that fire is the key to time travel. The OVA blends romance, time travel, and historical drama in classic Takahashi style.

entries.title: First Spaceship on Venus
entries.creator: Kurt Maetzig (Director)
