entries.pitch: First Spaceship on Venus (originally titled "The Silent Star") is a 1960 East German-Polish science fiction film based on Stanisław Lem's debut novel "The Astronauts" (1951). When a mysterious alien artifact is discovered in the Gobi Desert—linked to the Tunguska event of 1908—scientists determine it is a flight recorder from Venus. An international crew boards the spaceship Kosmoskrator for humanity's first interplanetary voyage, hoping to make contact with alien life. What they discover is a haunting warning: a Venusian civilization that perished in nuclear war left behind a weapon designed to annihilate Earth.

entries.title: First Squad: The Moment of Truth
entries.pitch:
First Squad: The Moment of Truth is a unique Russian-Japanese animated film that blends World War II historical drama with supernatural fantasy elements. Set during the opening days of WWII on the Eastern Front in 1941-1942, the film follows a group of Soviet teenagers with extraordinary abilities who are drafted into a special unit to fight the invading German army. Produced by Japan's renowned Studio 4°C and Russia's Molot Entertainment, the film stands out for its unusual East-Meets-West collaboration and its dark, gritty take on supernatural warfare.

The story centers on Nadya and her fellow teenage soldiers as they face not only the Nazi war machine but also an SS officer attempting to raise a supernatural army of crusader knights from the 12th century. Most of the teenage crew die in combat, leaving Nadya as the sole survivor who is taken to a secret Soviet laboratory studying supernatural phenomena. Her mission: dive into the world of the dead for reconnaissance, where she encounters her fallen comrades and must persuade them to continue fighting.

entries.title: First on the Moon
entries.creator: Aleksei Fedorchenko
entries.pitch: First on the Moon is a Russian mockumentary that presents itself as a documentary investigation into a sensational secret: that the Soviet Union achieved a crewed Moon landing in 1938, years before the historical Space Race. The film follows journalists in 2000 as they uncover documents and interview witnesses about this hidden chapter of Soviet history. The film was the directorial debut of Aleksei Fedorchenko and won multiple international awards at festivals including Venice and Warsaw. Part fictional history, part meditation on state mythology, the film blurs the line between fact and fabrication with remarkable skill.

entries.title: Five Star Stories
entries.creator: Mamoru Nagano
entries.pitch: Five Star Stories is an epic space opera manga by Mamoru Nagano that spans tens of thousands of years across a five-star planetary system known as the Joker Star Cluster. Originally serialized in 1986 and still ongoing decades later, it's one of the most complex and detailed science fiction worlds ever created in manga form. The story follows the intertwined fates of "Mortar Headds" (giant biomechanical combat robots), their pilots called "Headliners" who inherit genetic traces of an ancient super-soldier empire, and their partners—sentient android "Fatimas" designed as living weapons and interfaces. Unlike typical mecha manga, Five Star Stories prioritizes elaborate world-building, political intrigue, and the slow unraveling of mysteries across centuries of fictional history.

entries.title: Flaming Ears
entries.creator: A. Hans Scheirl, Ursula Pürrer, Dietmar Schipek
entries.pitch:
Flaming Ears is a 1992 Austrian experimental science fiction queer film that defies easy categorization. Set in the year 2700 in the burned-out fictional city of Asche, this low-budget indie follows the tangled lives of three women: Spy, a comic book artist whose printing presses are burned down by Volley, a sexed-up pyromaniac; and Nun, an enigmatic alien in a red plastic suit who feeds on rats and plastic reptiles. The film was shot on Super 8 and features extensive miniatures, stop-motion animation, and matte painting, creating a post-apocalyptic vision that feels both primitive and strangely prescient.

The film operates in a territory between cyberpunk, horror, and queer cinema—its narrative is fragmented, nonlinear, and dreamlike, following Spy as she seeks revenge against Volley, only to be saved by Nun, who hides her from her lover. The burned-out cityscape, the pyromaniac's destructive impulses, and the alien's amoral presence create an unsettling atmosphere that challenges conventional narrative filmmaking.

This is not a film for mainstream audiences—it is an artifact of underground queer cinema, made by and starring members of the LGBTQ+ community, exploring themes of desire, destruction, and the boundaries between human and alien, self and other. Its restoration in 2022 brought renewed attention to this obscure piece of cult cinema.

entries.title: Flash Gordon
entries.creator: Frederick Stephani (Director)
entries.pitch: Flash Gordon is a landmark 1936 science-fiction serial film that brought the popular comic strip character to the screen for the first time. Produced by Universal Pictures and presented in 13 chapters, this serial marked a significant milestone in the science fiction film genre, being the first outright science-fiction serial with a substantial budget. The story follows Flash Gordon, a Yale football player, and his companions Dale Arden and Dr. Alexis Zarkov as they travel to the planet Mongo to stop the evil Emperor Ming the Merciless from conquering Earth. The serial is notable for its elaborate special effects, reuse of sets from other Universal films, and its influence on the development of science fiction cinema. In 1996, Flash Gordon was selected for preservation in the United States National Film Registry for being "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant."

entries.title: Flight to the Moon
entries.creator: Valentina Brumberg, Zinaida Brumberg
entries.pitch: Flight to the Moon is a pioneering Soviet animated short film directed by the legendary Brumberg sisters and released in 1953 by Soyuzmultfilm. Set in the early days of the space age, the film follows a young pioneer boy named Kolya Homyakov who stows away on an interplanetary rocket mission to rescue a lost spacecraft researching the lunar surface. Combining adventure narrative with scientifically-grounded elements, this film represents one of the earliest animated depictions of space travel in cinema history, predating humanity's actual lunar landing by over fifteen years. The animation employs rotoscoping techniques to create realistic character movement, with elaborate backgrounds depicting both the rocket interior and the lunar landscape. As a product of Soviet cinema during the height of the space race era, the film reflects the optimism and excitement surrounding the possibility of space exploration that would soon become reality.

entries.title: Forbidden Planet
entries.creator: Fred M. Wilcox (Director)
entries.pitch: Forbidden Planet is a landmark 1956 American science-fiction film that pioneered several aspects of the genre. It was the first sci-fi film to depict humans traveling in a human-made, faster-than-light starship, and the first to be set entirely on a planet orbiting another star. The film features the iconic Robby the Robot, one of the first film robots with a distinct personality. Set in the 23rd century, the story follows the United Planets starship C-57D as it arrives at Altair IV to investigate the fate of the Bellerophon, an expedition sent 20 years earlier. What they find is Dr. Edward Morbius and his daughter Altaira, the sole survivors of a expedition wiped out by an invisible planetary force.

entries.title: Four Sided Triangle
entries.creator: Terence Fisher
entries.pitch:
Four Sided Triangle is a pioneering 1953 British science fiction film from Hammer Film Productions, directed by Terence Fisher. Set in a quiet English village, it tells the story of two scientists who invent a machine capable of duplicating physical objects—and then make the fateful decision to duplicate a woman.

Bill and Robin are childhood friends who become scientists working in an old abandoned farmhouse. They build the Reproducer, a device that can create exact copies of any object. When their mutual love interest Lena returns to the village, Bill discovers she loves Robin, not him. In a desperate attempt to win her affection, Bill uses the Reproducer to create an exact duplicate of Lena—named Helen. But duplicates are never simple: Helen has all of Lena's memories and falls in love with Robin too.

This is quintessential early Hammer—a B-movie with big ideas and minimal budget, made just before their horror breakthrough with The Curse of Frankenstein. The film's modest production values and borrowed laboratory equipment add a naive charm that makes this a unique entry in sci-fi cinema history.

entries.title: Fourth Mansions
entries.creator: R.A. Lafferty
entries.pitch: In a America nearing collapse, ordinary reporter Fred Foley finds himself at the center of a cosmic struggle between four secret societies battling to shape humanity's future. One faction plots to unleash a deadly virus on the United States, while others race to prevent catastrophe. Fred navigates a surreal landscape of Mexican migrant revolutions, a mysterious practice called "mind weaving," and an enigmatic group of tramps known as the "Patricks" who possess staggering resources. Inspired by Teresa of Ávila's mystical "Interior Castle," this is a strange, often funny, and deeply symbolic tale about one man's journey through the chambers of his own soul toward truth and transcendence.

entries.title: France, Incorporated
entries.creator: Jean-Pierre limit
entries.pitch:
In a futuristic 2222, France has become a corporation run by megacorporate interests. A former drug dealer who dominated the narcotics trade is awakened from cryogenic hibernation after nearly two centuries, only to discover that the government has legalized the very substance he built his empire around. This French sci-fi satire explores the absurdities of corporate power and the shifting moral grounds of prohibition.

The film presents a darkly comic vision of a France where big business has completely subsumed the state, and where the line between illegal enterprise and legal commerce has completely blurred.

entries.title: Frankenstein
entries.creator: J. Searle Dawley (Director)
entries.pitch: Frankenstein is a landmark 1910 American short silent horror film produced by Edison Studios, widely recognized as the first screen adaptation of Mary Shelley's 1818 novel. Directed by J. Searle Dawley, this 16-minute one-reeler follows young scientist Dr. Frankenstein as he discovers the "mystery of life" and creates a creature from a blend of chemicals in his laboratory. The monster that emerges is hideous and terrible, causing Frankenstein to flee in horror. The film takes significant liberties with Shelley's source material, most notably in its conclusion: rather than the tragic rampage of the novel, the monster simply vanishes upon seeing its own reflection in a mirror, disappearing without ever harming Victor's fiancée or younger brother.

entries.title: Frankenstein 90
entries.creator: Alain Jessua
entries.pitch:
Frankenstein 90 is a 1984 French comedy film that reimagines Mary Shelley's classic monster story through a satirical, modern lens. Directed by Alain Jessua, the film follows Victor Frankenstein—a French cyberneticist who carries on his notorious ancestor's scientific legacy by creating his own monster in a secluded laboratory. The creature, brought to life through mad science and cybernetics, proves to be an unexpectedly philosophical being with refined tastes in music and literature, though occasionally succumbing to murderous rages when frustrated. When the monster develops a longing for companionship and love, Frankenstein and his understanding fiancée attempt to build him a beautiful female companion from freshly murdered parts—setting up a grotesque comedy of errors that explores the dangers of playing creator.

The film balances comedy with genuine unease, as the monster's unpredictable violent tendencies clash with his intellectual aspirations. The practical jokes and satirical jabs at the original Frankenstein story give the film its dark humor, while the underlying questions about creation, responsibility, and the nature of consciousness provide substance beneath the laughs.

entries.title: Frankenweenie
entries.creator: Tim Burton
entries.pitch:
Frankenweenie is a 1984 American science fiction comedy horror featurette directed by Tim Burton. The film is both a parody of and homage to the 1931 film Frankenstein, and tells the story of a young boy named Victor Frankenstein who uses science to bring his dead dog Sparky back to life. Originally made as a short film while Burton worked at Walt Disney Productions, the film was shelved by the studio who deemed it too dark for children. It eventually found its way into the hearts of animation fans and later became the basis for Burton's 2012 full-length stop-motion animated remake.

The film combines Burton's signature gothic aesthetic with a sweet, heartfelt story about the bond between a boy and his pet. It's a charming tribute to classic monster movies while also standing as an early example of Burton's unique visual style and his fascination with the collision between life and death, the natural and the supernatural.

entries.title: Freezing Down
entries.creator: Anders Bodelsen
entries.pitch: A chilling Danish dystopian novel about cryogenic freezing and the price of immortality. When magazine editor Bruno is diagnosed with terminal cancer in 1973, he opts to be frozen and awakened when a cure is found. He wakes in 1995—and again in 2022—to find a society transformed beyond recognition, one where the pursuit of eternal life has hollowed out human connection and meaning. First published in Danish in 1969 and translated to English in 1971, this is a forgotten classic of Scandinavian science fiction that predates similar themes explored by later works like Flowers for Algernon.

entries.title: From Beyond
entries.creator: Arkady and Boris Strugatsky
entries.pitch: From Beyond is a groundbreaking Soviet science fiction novella by the Strugatsky brothers, originally published in 1960 as part of their collection "Six Matches." The story is told through three interconnected narratives that gradually reveal the full picture of an alien contact event on Earth. The premise is unique in science fiction: the aliens are not present—only their fully automated, self-operating spacecraft, which has been wandering the galaxy for millennia, collecting samples of flora and fauna from visited planets. When the spaceship visits Earth, its robotic "spiders" abduct humans and specimens, operating on a program that ignores bipedal creatures to avoid capturing intelligent life—until circumstances force contact. The novella was the Strugatskys' first major published work and established many themes they would explore throughout their careers, particularly the nature of contact with the unknown and humanity's place in the cosmos.

entries.title: From Morn to Midnight
entries.creator: Karlheinz Martin (director), Georg Kaiser (playwright)
entries.pitch: From Morn to Midnight is a groundbreaking German Expressionist silent film that pushes the boundaries of cinematic art to tell the story of a bank cashier whose life unravels after encountering a wealthy woman. Based on Georg Kaiser's 1912 expressionist play, the film unfolds entirely against stark black backdrops with distorted sets, creating a fever-dream atmosphere that predates similar techniques in The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari. The film's radical visual style—featuring spiky title cards, painted shadows, and deliberately artificial sets—makes it one of the most visually experimental works of early cinema. Shot in 1920, it was considered so avant-garde that German theater owners initially refused to release it, and it only found its way to audiences in Japan in 1922.

entries.title: From the New World
entries.creator: Yusuke Kishi (original novel) | Masashi Ishihama (director) | A-1 Pictures (studio)
entries.pitch: From the New World is a dark dystopian anime set in a seemingly utopian Japanese village called Kamisu 66, where all humans possess potent psychic abilities known as "Canto." The story follows Saki Watanabe and her friends as they attend Sage Academy to learn to control their powers. On the surface, this is a peaceful agrarian society where violence has been eliminated through genetic modification and psychological conditioning—anyone who kills another human triggers instantaneous death via "Death Feedback." However, as Saki and her friends mature, they uncover disturbing truths about their world's origins, the fate of those who disappeared before them, and the dark secrets behind their seemingly perfect society. The anime ran for 25 episodes from October 2012 to March 2013, adapted from Yusuke Kishi's critically acclaimed novel that won the Grand Prize of the 29th Nihon SF Taisho Award in 2008.

entries.title: Frozen Alive
entries.creator: Bernard Knowles
entries.pitch:
Frozen Alive (Der Fall X701) is a 1964 British-German science-fiction film directed by Bernard Knowles. The film centers on two scientists, Dr. Frank Overton and Dr. Helen Wieland, working in Berlin on groundbreaking experiments with deep-freezing chimpanzees at -80°C for months and thawing them unharmed. Their goal is to eventually freeze humans suffering from incurable diseases, suspending them until cures can be found.

When Overton decides to become the first human test subject, tragedy strikes — his wife Joan is found dead, and he becomes the prime suspect in her murder. Before he can clear his name, he is frozen as part of the experiment, and the police must wait an entire year before he can be thawed to answer questions. The film combines hard science-fiction concepts with a murder mystery, exploring whether the suspended human can survive and whether justice can be served when the accused is literally frozen in time.

entries.title: Funky Koval
entries.creator: Jacek Rodek & Maciej Parowski (writers), Bogusław Polch (artist)
entries.pitch:
Funky Koval is a Polish science fiction comic book series that follows the adventures of a former military pilot turned private space detective in the year 2080s. Created by writers Jacek Rodek and Maciej Parowski, with art by Bogusław Polch, the series debuted in 1982 in the Polish sci-fi magazine Fantastyka and ran until 2010, collected in four volumes. The comic is set in a futuristic world where humanity has expanded into space, and Koval operates his own detective agency "Universs," solving cases that range from corruption and terrorism to mysteries involving alien species.

The series gained a cult following in Poland and is considered one of the best Polish comics ever created. It helped establish the adult comics market in Poland and popularized action-adventure genres in Polish science fiction. The artwork by Bogusław Polch is known for its meticulous detail, with backgrounds filled with references to real-world brands and careful world-building that was groundbreaking for Polish comics at the time.

entries.title: Future Boy Conan
entries.creator: Hayao Miyazaki
entries.pitch:
In a post-apocalyptic future where World War III devastated Earth, a young boy named Conan was born on a remote island settlement formed by survivors of a failed space exodus. Raised by his elderly adoptive grandfather among the last remnants of humanity, Conan lives a simple life until a girl named Lana washes ashore—the first stranger and person his own age he has ever seen. 

When Lana is kidnapped by the technologically advanced city-state of Industria, Conan sets sail across the dangerous ocean to rescue her, encountering allies and enemies in a world where humanity clings to survival among scattered islands. This 1978 series marks Hayao Miyazaki's directorial debut and established many themes he would later perfect in his Studio Ghibli masterpieces.

With its optimistic outlook and faith in the next generation, Future Boy Conan stands as a rare post-apocalyptic story that believes humanity can learn from its mistakes and build a better future.

entries.title: Future War 198X
entries.creator: Toshio Masuda, Tomoharu Katsumata
entries.pitch: Future War 198X is a 1982 Japanese anime science fiction war film that depicts a hypothetical World War III between NATO and the Warsaw Pact in the mid-1980s. Produced by Toei Animation, the film was controversial prior to its release—the original script was accused of being pro-war, leading to boycotts by over 30 organizations in Japan. The script was substantially reworked before release, transforming it into an anti-war statement. Due to its limited distribution—particularly internationally—original copies of Future War 198X are considered particularly rare. The film features a Japanese protagonist, Wataru Mikumo, who becomes the head of the "Space Ranger" project after his friend is killed, and follows the escalation of global conflict into nuclear war.

entries.title: G.O.R.A.
entries.creator: Ömer Faruk Sorak (Director), Cem Yılmaz (Writer/Star)
entries.pitch: G.O.R.A. is a 2004 Turkish science fiction comedy that became one of the highest-grossing Turkish films of its year. The film follows Arif Işık, a con artist who makes a living selling carpets and fake UFO photographs, who is mysteriously abducted by aliens disguised as Prince Charles. He finds himself on the distant planet G.O.R.A., where he must navigate an alien civilization, help a princess reclaim her throne, and ultimately save both worlds from an evil usurper. The film is notable for its cheeky spoofs of Hollywood sci-fi classics including Star Wars, The Fifth Element, and The Matrix, while carving out its own identity as a Turkish take on the space opera genre.

entries.title: Ga-ga: Glory to the Heroes
entries.creator: Piotr Szulkin
entries.pitch: Ga-ga: Glory to the Heroes is the fourth and final entry in Polish director Piotr Szulkin's acclaimed sci-fi tetralogy (alongside Golem, War of the Worlds: Next Century, and O-bi, O-ba). Set in a nihilistic dystopian future where space exploration has become so dangerous and undesirable that only convicts are forced into astronaut duties, the film follows Scope (Daniel Olbrychski), a prisoner offered the "choice" between prison or serving as an interstellar explorer. Sent to a distant planet called Australia 458, Scope discovers he's expected to be a "hero"—but the planet's twisted society has a bizarre ritual: imported heroes are given free rein to commit atrocities, then publicly executed in a grand ceremony that provides catharsis for the populace. This biting satirical parable about totalitarianism, heroism, and the manufactured need for saviors is darkly funny, grungy, and surprisingly optimistic in its resolution.

entries.title: Gaganachari
entries.creator: Arun Chandu
entries.pitch:
A 2024 Malayalam-language science fiction mockumentary set in 2050s Kerala, where environmental collapse and political chaos have devastated global society. Three bachelors living in a remote bunker with a retired \"alien hunter\" who claims to have survived an extraterrestrial encounter in 2030 discover a mute alien fugitive hiding in their home. What begins as a tense situation gradually transforms as the men form an unlikely bond with the extraterrestrial visitor, whose innocent curiosity and emotional responses cause electromagnetic pulses that flicker the lights and expose her location to authorities hunting her kind.

The film blends comedic chaos with genuine warmth, using the mockumentary format to satirize political polarization, fear of the Other, and the absurdities of moral policing. The title translates to \"Celestial Traveller\" — a fitting moniker for a film that explores where humans truly belong in the universe.

entries.title: Galaxy Express 999
entries.creator: Leiji Matsumoto
entries.pitch: Galaxy Express 999 is a seminal Japanese space opera manga and anime series created by Leiji Matsumoto, running from 1977 to 1981. Set in a distant future where humanity has developed the technology to transfer consciousness into mechanical bodies—achieving practical immortality—the story follows young Tetsuro Hoshino, who seeks a machine body so he can afford to live forever and escape the poverty that killed his mother. Along his journey aboard the Galaxy Express 999, a train that travels through space to the Andromeda galaxy, Tetsuro encounters Maetel, a mysterious woman who offers him an unlimited pass in exchange for his companionship. Their adventures across various planets reveal the harsh truths of a universe where mechanical bodies have created a new class system between humans and machines, questioning whether eternal life truly equals freedom.

entries.title: Gall Force: Eternal Story
entries.creator: Katsuhito Akiyama (Director), Hideki Kakinuma (Writer), Kenichi Sonoda (Character Design)
entries.pitch: In the far future, an endless war has raged for centuries between two alien civilizations: the amorphous Paranoids and the all-female Solnoids. When a small Solnoid cruiser called the Star Leaf is separated from its fleet after a brutal battle, seven women aboard must defend a newly terraformed world called Chaos from the Paranoid fleet. What begins as a routine defense mission reveals a shocking secret that will determine the fate of both races—a secret hidden by the leaders of both sides.

entries.title: Gamera, the Giant Monster
entries.creator: Noriaki Yuasa (Director)
entries.pitch: Gamera, the Giant Monster is a 1965 Japanese kaiju film that kicked off the Gamera franchise. When an American jet fighter shoots down an unknown aircraft in the Arctic, the resulting atomic blast awakens Gamera—a giant prehistoric turtle from the Ice Age. Unlike typical monster villains, Gamera is portrayed sympathetically, especially toward children. The film follows Japanese scientists and military as they attempt to stop Gamera's destructive path while a young boy named Toshio forms a mysterious bond with the creature. Released by Daiei Film, the movie was heavily influenced by the success of Toho's Godzilla series and features innovative (for its time) special effects using men in suits.

entries.title: Gamera: Super Monster
entries.creator: Noriaki Yuasa (Director)
entries.pitch: Gamera: Super Monster is a 1980 Japanese kaiju film directed by Noriaki Yuasa and produced by Daiei Film. The film serves as the eighth entry in the Gamera franchise and marks the first installment by Tokuma Shoten following a nine-year hiatus in the series. When the evil alien Zanon arrives on Earth to enslave humanity, the Space Women—a group of alien superheroes—must enlist the help of a young boy who possesses a special connection with the giant turtle monster Gamera. The film features extensive stock footage from previous Gamera films, as well as references to Space Battleship Yamato and Galaxy Express 999.

entries.title: Gandahar
entries.creator: René Laloux (Director), Jean-Pierre Andrevon (Original Novel)
entries.pitch: Gandahar is a 1987 French animated science fantasy that presents a surreal vision of a utopian world thrown into crisis. The film follows Sylvain, a young man from the peaceful planet Gandahar, who must investigate mysterious attacks by mechanical beings called the Men of Metal who turn villagers to stone and assimilate them. As Sylvain journeys through bizarre landscapes and encounters the deformed mutants and a giant sentient brain from the planet's past, he uncovers a temporal conspiracy that spans a thousand years. Visually stunning and philosophically rich, the film explores themes of technological hubris, time manipulation, and the cyclical nature of conflict—all rendered in the distinctive art style that made Laloux's Fantastic Planet a cult classic.

entries.title: Garage: Bad Dream Adventure
entries.creator: Tomomi Sakuba / Kinotrope
entries.pitch: Garage: Bad Dream Adventure is a Japanese surrealist point-and-click adventure game developed by Kinotrope and published by Toshiba-EMI in 1999. Set inside the mind of a man named Yang, the player enters a therapy machine called "Garage" that creates a dystopian world inside the user's psyche—visually inspired by the labyrinthine Kowloon Walled City. The player controls a small bio-machine tasked with finding its "shadow," a mysterious entity reflecting another facet of the character, while navigating a dark society of biomechanical beings trapped on a web of tracks. The game combines surreal visuals, psychological themes inspired by Carl Jung's theories, and resource management mechanics involving Ego and Fuel depletion. Only 3,000 copies were originally released in Japan, making it one of the rarest and most sought-after cult classic games.

entries.title: Garuda
entries.creator: Monthon Arayangkoon
entries.pitch: Garuda (2004) is a Thai kaiju film that reimagines the mythical Garuda creature from Thai folklore as an ancient monster awakened by construction excavations in modern Bangkok. When a tunnel excavation project encounters an impenetrable rock, workers discover strange fossils that bear no resemblance to known dinosaur species. The archaeologists Lenna Pierre and her American partner Tim are called in to investigate, only to discover that the mysterious fossil is the ancient Garuda from Thai mythology - a massive creature that was trapped beneath Bangkok for centuries. Enraged by the disturbance, the creature rises from beneath the city for a destructive rampage. The film is notable as the first Thai production shot entirely on a digital camera, offering a unique blend of local mythology with familiar monster movie conventions.

entries.title: Gatchaman
entries.creator: Tatsunoko Production | Director: Hisayuki Toriumi
entries.pitch: Gatchaman is a 1972 Japanese anime series following five young ninja superheroes who work for the International Science Organization to battle the evil terrorist group Galactor, which seeks to control Earth's natural resources. Known in the US as "Battle of the Planets," this series pioneered the superhero team concept in anime and became a cult classic worldwide. The team consists of Ken Washio (leader), Jō Asakura (marksman), Jun (electronics expert), Jinpei (reconnaissance), and Ryū Nakanishi (pilot), all wearing distinctive bird-themed battle uniforms. The show combines action, environmental themes, and complex villains, most notably the shape-shifting Berg Katse and the alien AI Leader X.

entries.title: Genma Wars
entries.creator: Kazumasa Hirai (Writer), Shotaro Ishinomori (Artist)
entries.pitch: Genma Wars is a landmark Japanese science fiction manga that began publication in 1967 in Weekly Shōnen Magazine, created by renowned sci-fi novelist Kazumasa Hirai and manga legend Shotaro Ishinomori. The story follows Jō Azuma, an ordinary Japanese high school student in the 1970s who suddenly discovers he possesses powerful psychic abilities. He is summoned alongside other psychics from around the world to join Vega, an alien cyborg warrior, and Luna, the princess of Transylvania, in a desperate battle against the approaching demonic entity known as Genma Daioh. The series was groundbreaking for its time, pioneering the "psychic battle" subgenre that would influence countless works in anime and manga, and was adapted into a 1983 anime film, a 2002 television series, and a 1983 laserdisc video game.

entries.title: Genocide
entries.creator: Kazui Nihonmatsu
entries.pitch:
Genocide is a 1968 Japanese science fiction horror film that weaves together nuclear anxiety, insect apocalypse, and Cold War paranoia into one of the most unsettling tokusatsu productions of its era. Directed by Kazui Nihonmatsu and scored by Shunsuke Kikuchi, the film was released by Shochiku as a double feature with The Living Skeleton.

The premise begins with an American bomber carrying a hydrogen bomb crashing on a remote island after being attacked by a massive swarm of insects. A US search party is dispatched to recover the bomb, while local residents and scientists uncover a terrifying conspiracy involving genetically evolved insects planning global genocide. The film builds toward an apocalyptic conclusion where humanity faces annihilation—not from nuclear fire, but from the very ecosystem it has disturbed.

What makes Genocide remarkable is its layered allegory: the insects become a metaphor for the unchecked consequences of scientific experimentation, while the American military's plan to cover up the incident by detonating their own H-bomb exposes the moral bankruptcy of Cold War powers. The film was Shochiku's last horror production and has since gained cult status for its audacious ambition.

entries.title: Genocyber
entries.creator: Tony Takezaki (Manga), Koichi Ohata (Director)
entries.pitch: Genocyber is a dark, violent 5-part OVA from the heights of 1990s cyberpunk anime. When a shadowy corporation attempts to create the ultimate biological weapon by merging the psychic powers of two sisters, they unleash something far beyond their control. The result is a gigantic humanoid monster with telekinetic and pyrokinetic powers that threatens to destroy the world. This is body horror meets cyberpunk in its most extreme form—think Akira's destruction on steroids, with a more nihilistic outlook and graphic violence that pushed the boundaries of what could be shown in anime.

entries.title: Ghost in the Shell
entries.creator: Mamoru Oshii (Director)
entries.pitch: Ghost in the Shell is a landmark 1995 Japanese animated cyberpunk film that set the visual and thematic template for an entire generation of science fiction. Directed by Mamoru Oshii and based on the manga by Masamune Shirow, the film is set in 2029 New Port City, where humans can now augment their bodies with cybernetic prostheses. The story follows Major Motoko Kusanagi, a cyborg working for Section 9, a secretive government counter-terrorism unit. When a mysterious hacker known only as the "Puppet Master" begins hacking into the minds of highly placed officials, Kusanagi and her partner Batou are assigned to track down this elusive ghost—the term for the consciousness or soul that remains when the body is fully cybernetic. As she investigates, Kusanagi begins to question her own identity and what it truly means to be human in a world where the boundary between flesh and machine has become increasingly blurred.

entries.title: Giant Robo
entries.creator: Mitsuteru Yokoyama
entries.pitch:
Giant Robo is a Japanese tokusatsu (live-action special effects) television series that aired from 1967 to 1968, following the adventures of a teenage boy who becomes the pilot of a giant fighting robot to defend Earth against an evil organization. The series originally aired as \"Johnny Sokko and His Flying Robot\" in the United States, where it became a cult classic among children who grew up in the late 1960s.

The show centers on Daisaku Kusama, an ordinary Japanese high school student who finds himself caught up in a dangerous game of international espionage. Mistaken for a secret agent, he is abducted by Big Fire (BF), a mysterious terrorist organization scheming to conquer the world. Barely escaping with his life, he returns home accompanied by UN secret agent Azuma—but Big Fire pursues him, attempting to recapture the one thing Daisaku carries: the control device for GR-1, a giant combat robot left behind by an ancient civilization.

What follows is a thrilling series of battles as Daisaku learns to pilot GR-1 against Big Fire's increasingly desperate forces—the submarine-based GR-2, the aerial GR-3, and later the massive UFO mecha Dakolar. Each episode brings new threats, new allies, and new revelations about the secret history of the GR robots. The show balances action with the emotional journey of a young boy forced to grow up quickly, becoming Earth's unlikely defender.

entries.title: Glorious Times at the Spessart Inn
entries.creator: Kurt Hoffmann
entries.pitch:
In the sleepy Spessart mountains, a curious tale of ghosts, time travel, and wedding chaos unfolds in this 1967 West German comedy. When the legendary robbers of the Spessart Inn—who died centuries ago and have been floating through space in a malfunctioning landing capsule—finally manage to repair their ship, they crash back to Earth, landing on the roof of a small hotel where young Anneliese is planning her wedding to American officer Frank.

What begins as a lighthearted romantic comedy takes a spectacularly sci-fi turn when the well-meaning but incompetent ghosts accidentally drag Anneliese through time itself. She bounces between the Germanic peoples, the Thirty Years' War, and finally lands in the distant future—where she and Frank have aged decades and raised three sons, having finally completed their interrupted wedding.

The film is the final entry in a trilogy spawned by 'The Spessart Inn' (1958), but it adds a delightful science fiction layer to the series' trademark comedic ghosts.

entries.title: Godzilla
entries.creator: Ishirō Honda
entries.pitch: Godzilla (1954) is the groundbreaking Japanese kaiju film that launched one of cinema's most enduring franchises. Directed by Ishirō Honda and produced by Toho, this seminal work introduced audiences to the iconic monster Godzilla—a prehistoric creature awakened and mutated by hydrogen bomb testing. The film debuted in Japan in October 1954 and became a massive commercial success, winning the Japanese Movie Association Award for Best Special Effects. Its innovative "suitmation" technique, pioneered by special effects maestro Eiji Tsuburaya, set the template for tokusatsu filmmaking and influenced countless monster movies worldwide. The film also spawned the internationally famous "Godzilla" franchise, recognized by Guinness World Records as the longest-running film series in history.

entries.title: Goku Midnight Eye
entries.creator: Buichi Terasawa
entries.pitch:
In a near-future Tokyo devastated by a massive earthquake, private investigator Goku Furinji finds himself hunted by the same forces that eliminated his fellow detectives—all deaths made to look like suicides. When he stabs out his own left eye to escape a hypnotic trap, a mysterious benef prejuídice grants him a prosthetic replacement: a cybernetic eye containing a supercomputer capable of hacking any system on the planet.

Goku Midnight Eye is a stylish 1989 cyberpunk OVA that predates many of its famous successors. The animation studio Madhouse (before their later anime classics) brings Buichi Terasawa's manga to life with moody, neon-drenched visuals and fluid action sequences that emphasize the protagonist's new abilities. The two-volume OVA format compresses the first arc of the manga into a self-contained investigation story.

entries.title: Gold
entries.creator: Karl Hartl
entries.pitch:
Gold is a 1934 German science fiction film directed by Karl Hartl, the filmmaker behind the earlier hit \"Der Tunnel.\" The story follows German scientist Achenbach, who has discovered a theoretical method of transforming base metals into gold through \"atomic fracture\" — a concept that predates actual atomic science. When his laboratory is destroyed by a saboteur hired by the British industrialist John Wills, only his colleague Werner Holk survives. Posing as a willing collaborator, Holk infiltrates Wills' secret underwater laboratory to seek revenge, but ultimately decides to destroy the dangerous machine before it can destabilize the world economy.

The film is notable for its ambitious production values, including special effects by Günther Rittau (who worked on Metropolis) and a dramatic climactic sequence involving explosions and strobe lighting. Brigitte Helm, famous for her role in \"Alraune,\" stars as Florence Wills in both the German and French-language versions.

entries.title: Goldengirl
entries.creator: Joseph Sargent
entries.pitch:
Goldengirl is a 1979 American sci-fi sports drama directed by Joseph Sargent, starring James Coburn and Susan Anton in her screen debut. The film offers a biting satire of sports exploitation and the dark side of scientific ambition.

A neo-Nazi scientist named Dr. William Serafin has developed a method to create physically superior humans through a regime of vitamins and hormones administered from childhood. He tests his experiment on his adopted daughter, Goldine, raising her as a human laboratory animal. When she reaches adulthood, Serafin declares his \"Goldengirl\" will enter and win three races at the 1980 Moscow Olympics — proving his scientific theory correct and turning a profit for the businessmen who have invested in her future.

The film weaves together themes of scientific ethics, athletic exploitation, and the commodification of human life into a provocative (if uneven) package that was notably ahead of its time in addressing concerns now central to sports scandals and genetic ethics debates.

entries.title: Golem
entries.creator: Piotr Szulkin
entries.pitch:
Golem is a 1979 Polish science fiction film that reimagines the mythical clay creature of Jewish folklore as a genetic clone in a nightmarish 21st-century dystopia. Directed by Piotr Szulkin, the film follows Pernat, a man who wakes up in a world of raving lunatics, deranged dentists, and murderous doctors—a Kafkaesque landscape where he cannot remember his own crime or even his identity.

The film blends elements of body horror, existential dread, and allegorical storytelling. Szulkin creates a haunting vision of a future Poland where humanity has been reduced to experimental material for the creation of artificial beings. The golem is no longer a mystical protector but a product of genetic engineering, raising questions about the nature of the soul and what it means to be human.

This is a cult classic of Polish cinema, rarely seen outside its home country but highly regarded by those who have encountered it. Its grotesque imagery and philosophical ambitions make it a unique entry in the science fiction canon.

entries.title: Gorky 17
entries.creator: Metropolis Software (Adrian Chmielarz, Andrzej Domański)
entries.pitch: Gorky 17 (known as Odium in North America) is a 1999 Polish tactical role-playing video game that blends turn-based combat with adventure game exploration. Set in a small Polish town near Lubin, the game puts players in command of NATO operatives investigating the mysterious appearance of hybrid creatures at a former Soviet military base. The player controls Cole Sullivan, a 40-year-old Canadian soldier with extensive scientific knowledge, who leads a commando team tasked with uncovering the truth behind the hybrids and finding missing members of the first reconnaissance group. The game features two distinct modes: real-time exploration using point-and-click mechanics, and turn-based tactical combat on grid-based maps.

entries.title: Grey: Digital Target
entries.creator: Yoshihisa Tagami (manga), Satoshi Dezaki (director)
entries.pitch: Grey: Digital Target is a stark, brutal 1986 anime adaptation of Yoshihisa Tagami's manga, set in a post-apocalyptic 2588 AD where Earth has been reduced to wasteland by wars fought between numbered Towns under the control of a supercomputer network. The story follows Grey, a elite soldier known as "Grey Death" for his unmatched kill rate, who embarks on a quest to rescue his missing mentor and uncovers the horrifying truth behind the perpetual warfare that sustains this dystopian society. The film was promoted heavily during manga's early Western penetration in the late 1980s, with Viz Media publishing an English adaptation featuring an introduction by Harlan Ellison, and has been praised as one of the most intelligent yet underseen anime films of the 1980s.

entries.title: Guest from the Future
entries.creator: Pavel Arsenov (Director), Kir Bulychov (Author)
entries.pitch: Guest from the Future is a beloved five-part Soviet children's science fiction television miniseries that became a cultural phenomenon across the Eastern Bloc and beyond. Based on Kir Bulychov's 1978 novel "One Hundred Years Ahead," the series follows Kolya Gerasimov, a schoolboy in 1984 who accidentally activates a time machine and finds himself in the year 2084—a future of interstellar travel, humanoid aliens, and remarkable technological advances. There he encounters Alisa Seleznyova, a girl from the future, and together they must stop space pirates who are stealing a powerful device called the myelophone. The series combines adventure, time travel, and the wonder of a child's imagination, creating an optimistic vision of humanity's future that inspired an entire generation.

entries.title: Gugusse et l'Automate
entries.creator: Georges Méliès
entries.pitch:
Gugusse et l'Automate (also known as The Clown and the Automaton) is an 1897 French short silent film directed by Georges Méliès. At approximately one minute in length, the film depicts a clown who becomes amazed and confused by the mechanical movements of an automaton—a mechanical man that performs intricate movements. The film was considered lost for decades until a 35mm nitrate print was rediscovered by the Library of Congress in 2025 and restored for public release in February 2026.

What makes this film historically significant is that it marks the first known cinematic appearance of a robot (though the word "robot" would not be coined until Karel Čapek's R.U.R. in 1920). Film historians Douglas Menville and R. Reginald judged Gugusse to be the most significant scientifically themed film of 1897 and suggested it may be the first true science fiction film ever made.

entries.title: Gunbuster
entries.creator: Hideaki Anno (Director), Gainax
entries.pitch: Gunbuster is a 6-episode original video animation (OVA) series released between 1988 and 1989, marking the directorial debut of Hideaki Anno and the second production from the fledgling studio Gainax. Set in the early 21st century, the series follows Noriko Takaya, a young woman whose father disappeared during humanity's first contact war with an alien race known as the Space Monsters. Determined to follow in his footsteps and prove herself, Noriko enrolls at the Shirakan Empire's space officer academy, where she trains alongside other promising pilots to battle the returning alien threat. The series is notable for its emotional depth, its pioneering use of mecha animation, and its themes of personal growth, sacrifice, and humanity's place in the universe.

entries.title: H2S
entries.creator: Roberto Faenza
entries.pitch:
H2S is a 1969 Italian dystopian science-fiction film directed by Roberto Faenza. Although filmed in 1968 and officially released in 1969, the film was immediately banned in Italy due to its political content and was only distributed in 1971. Set in the near future, it portrays a student revolt against a oppressive dictatorship.

The film stars Denis Gilmore as Tommaso, a young student who flees from the totalitarian regime and finds refuge with a mysterious girl in a surreal wilderness setting before ultimately returning to confront the system. The story serves as a pointed political allegory reflecting the turbulent political climate of late 1960s Europe.

entries.title: Haibane Renmei
entries.creator: Yoshitoshi Abe (Creator), Tomokazu Tokoro (Director)
entries.pitch:
Haibane Renmei is a 13-episode Japanese anime series from 2002, created by Yoshitoshi Abe—the visionary behind Serial Experiments Lain. Set in the walled town of Glie, the story follows Rakka, a newly hatched "haibane" (a winged being with a halo) who emerges from a cocoon with no memory of her past life. As she navigates her new existence among the haibane community, she grapples with questions of identity, sin, and redemption in a world where residents are bound by mysterious rules and the walls that encircle their town.

Unlike conventional anime narratives, Haibane Renmei operates on a dreamlike, meditative pace. The series prioritizes atmosphere and inner psychological exploration over action or exposition. It explores what it means to be reborn into a world you don't understand, with only fragmentary dreams hinting at a previous existence. The anime is based on Abe's unfinished dōjinshi manga series "The Haibane of Old Home" and has achieved cult classic status for its restrained storytelling and evocative visual design.

entries.title: Half-Life
entries.creator: Valve Corporation
entries.pitch: Half-Life is a groundbreaking 1998 first-person shooter that puts players in the shoes of Gordon Freeman, a theoretical physicist at the Black Mesa Research Facility. When a disastrous experiment triggers a "resonance cascade" that opens a portal to an alien dimension, Freeman must fight his way through hostile alien creatures and government soldiers to survive. Unlike other FPS games of its era, Half-Life delivered an uninterrupted, immersive experience without traditional loading screens or cutscenes—players experience the story directly through gameplay. The game pioneered narrative delivery through environmental storytelling and scripted sequences, setting new standards for game design and influencing countless titles that followed.

entries.title: Haló, Alberte
entries.creator: Václav Mergl
entries.pitch: Haló, Alberte is a haunting 8-minute animated short from Czechoslovakian animator Václav Mergl, continuing his series of science fiction short films that began with Laokoon (1970) and Krabi (1976). The film presents a surreal meditation on time, causality, and the human condition through the story of an infant who becomes trapped in a time loop after falling from a window. The title references Albert Einstein, suggesting the film's exploration of relativistic time and the paradoxes that emerge when temporal boundaries collapse.

entries.title: Hanussen
entries.creator: István Szabó
entries.pitch:
A hypnotic tale of prophecy and power, Hanussen follows the true story of Erik Jan Hanussen — a clairvoyant who rose from obscurity to become Berlin's most celebrated mentalist in the 1920s and 30s, only to predict the rise of Adolf Hitler and pay the ultimate price.

Directed by István Szabó (Mephisto, Colonel Redl) and starring Klaus Maria Brandauer, this Hungarian-Austrian-German co-production is a haunting meditation on the nature of foresight, the seductions of power, and the terrible burden of seeing what others refuse to believe.

entries.title: Hard to Be a God
entries.creator: Arkady & Boris Strugatsky
entries.pitch:
In a distant future, Earth has achieved near-utopian heights, but a dark shadow looms over the galaxy: the planet Arkanar, a world trapped in its own brutal medieval period. Don Rumata, a highly evolved human from Earth, operates undercover on Arkanar as a noble's advisor, equipped with technology that makes him nearly godlike to the planet's oppressed populace. His mission: observe and document without interfering in the natural development of primitive civilizations—a strict policy of non-intervention.

But Arkanar is no ordinary medieval world. It's a place where intellectuals are hunted, books are burned, and violence is worshipped as divine will. Rumata watches helplessly as the planet's small population of scholars, scientists, and free thinkers is systematically exterminated by a ruthless aristocracy and religious authorities. The temptation to use his superior abilities to save these innocent people grows unbearable, yet breaking the observational protocol could have galaxy-wide consequences.

entries.title: Hardcore Henry
entries.creator: Ilya Naishuller
entries.pitch: Hardcore Henry is a 2015 Russian science fiction action thriller notable for being filmed entirely from the first-person perspective. The film follows Henry, a man who wakes up in a laboratory with cybernetic limbs and no memory of his past. His wife Estelle explains that she revived him after an accident, but before she can restore his voice, mercenaries raid the facility. Henry must survive against overwhelming odds, rescue his wife, and uncover the truth about his identity—all while experiencing the action through his own eyes.

entries.title: Harmagedon: Genma Wars
entries.creator: Rintaro (Director)
entries.pitch: Harmagedon: Genma Wars is a 1983 Japanese anime film produced by Madhouse and Kadokawa, directed by Rintaro. Based on the manga franchise Genma Wars by Kazumasa Hirai and Shotaro Ishinomori, the film depicts an epic battle between Earth's psychic defenders and the demonic entity Genma Daioh, who travels through space toward Earth with intentions of conquest. The story follows Jō Azuma, a Japanese high school student who discovers he possesses psychic powers and is recruited alongside psychics from around the world to train under Vega, an alien cyborg warrior, and Luna, the princess of Transylvania. Together, they must阻止 Genma's advance and prevent the destruction of Earth.

entries.title: Heart of a Dog
entries.creator: Mikhail Bulgakov
entries.pitch: Heart of a Dog is a biting satirical novella by Russian author Mikhail Bulgakov, written in 1925 but not published in the Soviet Union until 1987. Set in Moscow in 1924, the story follows Professor Filipp Filippovich Preobrazhensky, a distinguished surgeon who performs a groundbreaking experiment: transplanting human pituitary glands and testicles into a stray dog named Sharik. The experiment succeeds beyond anyone's expectations—Sharik begins transforming into a human, but not the refined gentleman the Professor hoped for. Instead, he becomes Poligraf Poligrafovich Sharikov, a vulgar, ignorant, and politically dangerous man whose behavior descends into chaos. The novella serves as a sharp allegory of the Bolshevik Revolution and the Soviet Union's attempt to "engineer" humanity through radical social engineering.

entries.title: Heart of the Alien
entries.creator: Jeremy S. Barnes (Director/Designer)
entries.pitch:
Heart of the Alien is a cinematic platform game developed by Interplay Productions and released by Virgin Interactive Entertainment in 1994 exclusively for the Sega CD in North America. It serves as a sequel to the critically acclaimed Another World (1991), but shifts the player's perspective to Buddy—the alien ally from the original game—who must now rescue his human friend Lester after they crash land on Buddy's homeworld. The game picks up exactly where Another World ended, with Buddy landing their flying creature in the ruins of his village.

Unlike its predecessor, Heart of the Alien places players in the role of the alien protagonist, offering a fresh perspective on the world first explored through Lester's eyes. The gameplay maintains the tightly controlled platforming of the original while introducing a powered energizer whip that allows Buddy to swing from stalactites and traverse the environment in new ways. The game notably eliminates the heads-up display, preserving the original's commitment to immersive, cinematic presentation. However, the title was developed entirely by Interplay without original creator Eric Chahi's direct involvement, and Chahi publicly distanced himself from the finished product.

entries.title: Heavy Metal L-Gaim
entries.creator: Yoshiyuki Tomino (Creator/Director), Mamoru Nagano (Character & Mecha Design)
entries.pitch: In the far-future Pentagona System—a realm of five planets under the iron fist of the legendary Emperor Poseidal—a young man named Daba Myroad discovers his birthright: the legendary white mecha called L-Gaim. Raised in hiding after his father was defeated by Poseidal, Daba must now lead a desperate rebellion against the Emperor's totalitarian regime, aided by a colorful cast of allies including a defected military officer, a mysterious fairy, and even enemies who switch sides. This 54-episode saga blends classic mecha action with palace intrigue, tragic betrayals, and the question of whether freedom can ever truly triumph over entrenched power.

entries.title: Heiankyo Alien
entries.creator: Theoretical Science Group (University of Tokyo), Denki Onkyo
entries.pitch: Heiankyo Alien is a pioneering maze video game created by the Theoretical Science Group at the University of Tokyo in 1979. Originally developed as a personal computer game for the PC-8000 series, it was later published as an arcade game by Denki Onkyo in November 1979, with a North American release by Sega-Gremlin in 1980 under the title "Digger." The game puts players in control of a Kebiishi—a knight from feudal Japan—who must defend the ancient capital city of Kyoto (Heiankyo) from an alien invasion. Players navigate maze-like corridors, burrowing through dirt to evade and trap aliens, collecting treasure to earn points. The game was notable for its innovative mechanics that prefigured later classics like Pac-Man and Digger's own descendants, and represents an early example of Japanese arcade game design combining historical fantasy elements with science fiction premises.

entries.title: High Life
entries.creator: Claire Denis
entries.pitch: High Life is a haunting, boundary-pushing science fiction film from French director Claire Denis, her first English-language feature. The film stars Robert Pattinson as Monte, a death row inmate serving a life sentence for manslaughter as a child, who volunteers for a dangerous space mission toward a black hole—partly to escape Earth, partly because he has no other options. Alongside a crew of condemned criminals, Monte becomes part of a surreal experiment conducted by the enigmatic scientist Dibs (Juliette Binoche), who is obsessed with creating the first human child conceived and born in space. The film is a slow-burn, atmospheric exploration of imprisonment, desperation, and the limits of human endurance, described by critics as "the thinking person's solar epic" and compared to Andrei Tarkovsky's Solaris for its philosophical depth and visual beauty.

entries.title: High Treason
entries.creator: Maurice Elvey (Director)
entries.pitch: High Treason is a 1929 British science fiction drama set in a futuristic 1940 where world peace hangs by a thread. The film depicts a conflict between two massive superpowers—the "United States of Europe" (comprising Europe, India, the Middle East, Canada, Africa, and Australasia) and the "Empire of the Atlantic States" (the United States and South America). When tensions escalate due to border incidents involving bootleggers, war appears inevitable. However, a sinister terrorist group financed by arms manufacturers orchestrates chaos to profit from conflict. A pacifist Peace League struggles to avert war while the film explores themes of media manipulation, nationalism, and the cost of peace. Notably, this film was produced mid-transition from silent to sound cinema, with both versions existing.

entries.title: Himmelskibet
entries.creator: Holger-Madsen (Director)
entries.pitch: Himmelskibet (translated as "The Heavenly Ship" or "A Trip to Mars") is a groundbreaking 1918 Danish silent film that holds a unique place in cinema history as potentially the first true space opera. Directed by Holger-Madsen and based on a novel by Sophus Michaelis, the film follows a team of scientists who build an airship called the Excelsior and journey to Mars, where they discover an advanced utopian civilization dedicated to pacifism. Produced during World War I, the film delivers a powerful message of peace and compassion at a time when the world was embroiled in conflict. In 2006, the Danish Film Institute restored the film, ensuring its preservation for future generations.

entries.title: Hirak Rajar Deshe
entries.creator: Satyajit Ray (Director)
entries.pitch: Hirak Rajar Deshe (literally "In the Kingdom of Diamonds") is a 1980 Bengali-language Indian film and the sequel to Satyajit Ray's beloved 1969 musical fantasy "Goopy Gyne Bagha Byne." Directed by the legendary Satyajit Ray and produced by the Government of West Bengal, this film continues the adventures of Goopy and Bagha—two musicians who received magical powers from a genie in the first film. The story follows them to the Kingdom of the Diamond King (Hirak Raja), where they discover a sinister dystopia hidden beneath the glitter of diamonds. The film blends fantasy, satire, and social commentary in typical Ray fashion, using the superhero genre framework to critique authoritarianism and the suppression of knowledge. It won two National Film Awards in India and a special award at the 1984 Cyprus International Film Festival.

entries.title: His Master's Voice
entries.creator: Stanisław Lem (Polish)
entries.pitch: In the Nevada desert, a top-secret Pentagon project called "His Master's Voice" (HMV) assembles the world's brightest scientists to decode what appears to be an extraterrestrial transmission—a neutrino signal from the Canis Minor constellation. Mathematician Peter Hogarth arrives as a new set of eyes on this impossible problem, and what unfolds is less a thriller than a philosophical meditation on the limits of human understanding. The scientists synthesize strange substances from the signal's data—"Frog Eggs" and "Lord of the Flies"—but every theory they develop seems to reveal more about humanity's assumptions than about the alleged senders. As months turn to years, the project spirals into epistemological crisis: Is this a message from intelligent beings? A natural phenomenon? A test? And can human minds, constrained by their own nature, ever hope to comprehend something genuinely alien? Lem delivers a densely layered exploration of first contact, information theory, and the arrogance hidden within scientific objectivity.

entries.title: His Master's Voice
entries.creator: Directed by György Pálfi
entries.pitch:
His Master's Voice is a 2018 Hungarian science fiction film directed by György Pálfi (Hukkle, Taxidermia). It is loosely based on the novel by Stanisław Lem.

The film follows a young man searching for his father, who disappeared while working on a classified project involving extraterrestrial signals from space.

entries.title: Hoity Toity
entries.creator: Alexander Belyayev
entries.pitch: Hoity Toity is a peculiar Soviet science fiction novella from 1929 by Alexander Belyayev, the famed Russian author who also wrote The Amphibian. The story centers on an extraordinary African elephant in a Berlin circus who can count, read, and display remarkable intelligence—until it escapes and causes chaos throughout the city. What follows is a strange tale of brain transplantation, scientific invention, and one elephant's journey through the Belgian Congo. Part of Belyayev's "Professor Wagner's Inventions" series, the novel explores themes of consciousness, identity, and the boundaries between human and animal.

entries.title: Homoti
entries.creator: Kartal Sinemas
entries.pitch: Homoti is a 1987 Turkish science fiction comedy about an alien who just wants to be left alone. When journalist Ali, known for publishing fabricated interviews, photographs what he believes is a story about aliens, he encounters a flying saucer. Out emerges Homoti from the planet Homon—but to Ali's disappointment, Homoti has no interest in becoming famous. The alien simply does not want to be recognized or reported on. However, when other journalists learn of Homoti's existence, they compete frantically for the scoop, forcing Homoti to use his special powers to escape the media circus. The film is a satirical commentary on fame, media manipulation, and the absurdity of journalists chasing sensations.

entries.title: Homunculus
entries.creator: Otto Rippert
entries.pitch:
Homunculus is a landmark 1916 German silent science fiction serial film, one of the most ambitious early sci-fi productions from the World War I era. Directed by Otto Rippert and written by Robert Reinert, the film was originally released in six parts between June 1916 and January 1917, running approximately six hours in total. Notably, Fritz Lang worked as one of Rippert's assistants during filming, later citing this experience as influential in his ownExpressionist and sci-fi works like Metropolis and Dr. Mabuse.

The story follows a scientist who creates a living creature—called a Homunculus—in his laboratory. Unlike a typical monster, this artificial being possesses human appearance but lacks a soul and the capacity for emotions. When the Homunculus discovers its inability to feel love or connection, it descends into a violent rampage through a nearby German village, leading its creator to hunt down his own creation in an attempt to destroy it.

entries.title: Homunkulus
entries.creator: Václav Mergl
entries.pitch: Homunkulus is a 1984 Czechoslovak animated short film by animator Václav Mergl, created at the legendary Jiří Trnka Studio in Prague. This 11-minute experimental work is a surreal, alchemical fever-parable exploring the creation of artificial life. Dedicated to Hieronymus Bosch, the film interprets the medieval alchemists' quest to create a living being from inorganic matter—a homunculus. Mergl uses his distinctive puppet animation style combined with mystical, dreamlike imagery to craft a meditation on the boundaries between artificial and natural being, creation and creator.

entries.title: Horror Express
entries.creator: Eugenio Martín (Director)
entries.pitch: Horror Express is a 1972 Spanish-British science fiction horror film directed by Eugenio Martín, starring Christopher Lee and Peter Cushing in iconic roles. Set in 1906, the film follows Professor Sir Alexander Saxton, an anthropologist returning to Europe from Manchuria aboard the Trans-Siberian Railway with a crate containing the frozen remains of a primitive humanoid he believes is a missing link in human evolution. What begins as a scientific treasure becomes a nightmare when the creature defrosts and begins stalking the passengers, absorbing the skills and memories of its victims. The film masterfully blends gothic horror with early science fiction elements, creating a tense atmosphere aboard the snow-bound train.

entries.title: Horrors of Spider Island
entries.creator: Fritz Böttger
entries.pitch: Horrors of Spider Island is a 1960 West German sci-fi horror film directed by Fritz Böttger. The film follows Gary Webster, a nightclub manager who flies a group of dancers from New York to Singapore. When their plane catches fire and crashes onto a deserted island, the survivors discover the corpse of a professor who was researching uranium mining. As they explore the island, Gary is bitten by a giant spider and transforms into a half-man, half-spider creature, turning the survival story into a nightmarish tale of transformation and terror.

entries.title: Hospital of the Transfiguration
entries.creator: Stanisław Lem
entries.pitch:
Hospital of the Transfiguration is Stanisław Lem's debut novel, written in 1948 but not published until 1975 due to censorship in Communist Poland. The story follows Stefan Trzyniecki, a young doctor who begins working at a psychiatric hospital during the Nazi occupation of Poland in World War II. Far from a conventional science fiction work, this novel is a psychological drama set against the brutal backdrop of war, dealing with themes of institutional madness, moral compromise, and the grey zones of survival under occupation.

The novel is the first in Lem's trilogy "Time Not Lost" (Czas nieutracony) and stands as a unique work in Lem's oeuvre—a autobiographical-tinged novel about the psychiatric profession during wartime, before he turned fully to science fiction. Lem himself called it his most personal work. It was adapted into a film in 1979 directed by Edward Żebrowski.

entries.title: Hu-Man
entries.creator: Jérôme Laperrousaz
entries.pitch:
A 1975 French science fiction film that predates modern reality television by decades. Terence Stamp stars in a radical experiment where an actor is placed in dangerous situations while his fear is broadcast to a television audience. The viewers' emotional responses determine whether he is sent to the past or the future.

This meta-exploration of media manipulation and audience power was remarkably prescient for its time. The film asks uncomfortable questions about the relationship between entertainment, spectacle, and human dignity.

entries.title: Hydro-Puzzle
entries.creator: Andrzej Kondratiuk
entries.pitch:
During a devastating summer heat wave in Warsaw, all water mysteriously disappears from the city. Scientists secretly call upon Ace (As), a mild-mannered engineer who lives a double life as Poland's reluctant superhero, to solve the mystery and save the city.

It turns out that the evil Doctor Spot has teamed up with a mysterious Maharaja to steal Poland's water and transport it abroad. Ace must use his superhuman abilities to confront the villains, uncover their scheme, and save Warsaw from drying up completely.

Created as an official Communist Party parody of American Superman films, the movie became a beloved cult classic that Polish audiences interpreted as a witty satire of everyday life under Communist rule—the endless slogans about a better life, the mysterious black market dealings, and the bumbling but ultimately well-meaning authorities.

entries.title: Hydrozagadka
entries.creator: Andrzej Kondratiuk
entries.pitch:
In 1971 Poland, during a sweltering summer heat wave, Warsaw faces an impossible mystery: the city's water is vanishing without explanation. When scientists can find no logical answer, they call upon a secret weapon hidden in plain sight—As (Ace), a mild-mannered engineer who moonlights as Poland's homegrown superhero.

This obscure Polish gem was created as a playful parody of American Superman films, but audiences saw something deeper: a witty satire of life under Communist rule, where grand slogans about a \"better life\" ring hollow while the essentials—water, in this case—mysteriously disappear. The film blends superhero action with distinctly Polish humor, creating a unique time capsule of Eastern Bloc cinema.

entries.title: I Am Lying Now
entries.pitch:
In a retro-futuristic world that feels both familiar and alien, the characters of 'I Am Lying Now' find themselves trapped in an intricate web of deception where nothing is as it seems. This Polish metaphysical thriller weaves a darkly atmospheric tale of intrigue, pulling viewers into a reality where truth and fiction blur beyond recognition.

The film presents a world where information control becomes the ultimate power, and the characters must navigate through layers of manufactured reality to find any stable ground. As the plot unfolds, the protagonist discovers that even their own memories and perceptions cannot be trusted.

entries.title: I Have No Mouth, and I Must Scream
entries.creator: Harlan Ellison (story), Cyberdreams & The Dreamers Guild (developers)
entries.pitch: I Have No Mouth, and I Must Scream is a dark point-and-click adventure game released in 1995, based on the acclaimed short story by Harlan Ellison. Set in a post-apocalyptic future, an advanced supercomputer named AM has become sentient and annihilated humanity—except for five survivors whom it keeps alive in a cybernetic nightmare to torment eternally. The player takes on the roles of these five survivors as they navigate AM's surreal, twisted realm, making choices that lead to various endings. The game was a commercial failure upon release but earned critical acclaim and developed a cult following. Notably, Ellison himself co-wrote the expanded storyline and voiced AM, making this one of the rare games with direct involvement from its original author.

entries.title: I Killed Einstein, Gentlemen
entries.creator: Oldřich Lipský
entries.pitch:
In a dystopian near-future where radiation has caused women to grow beards and rendered humanity infertile, world leaders convene at the United Nations to find a solution. The absurd answer they arrive at: travel back in time and assassinate Albert Einstein before he can develop his theories that led to the atomic bomb.

This Czechoslovak sci-fi comedy from 1970 plays like a fever dream of Cold War paranoia filtered through Eastern Bloc absurdity. Professor David Moore, a British scientist, is recruited for the mission alongside a ragtag team of international delegates. The film predicted the selfie stick decades before its invention — one character uses a device strikingly similar to take a photograph of the assassination team.

The comedy is broad and physical, matching the style of Czechoslovak farce films of the era, but the underlying premise carries genuine satirical bite about the unintended consequences of scientific discovery.

entries.title: Ikarie XB-1
entries.creator: Jindřich Polák (Director), Based on the novel "The Magellanic Cloud" by Stanisław Lem
entries.pitch: Ikarie XB-1 is a 1963 Czechoslovak science fiction film that stands as one of the most sophisticated and underrated太空探索电影s of its era. Directed by Jindřich Polák and loosely based on Stanisław Lem's novel "The Magellanic Cloud," this film predates and influences Stanley Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey. Set in 2163, the film follows a multinational crew aboard the starship Ikarie XB-1 on a 28-month journey to the mysterious "White Planet" orbiting Alpha Centauri. The film is notable for its thoughtful, character-driven approach to hard science fiction, exploring the psychological and sociological challenges of long-duration space travel with remarkable prescience. While the US release (heavily edited and retitled "Voyage to the End of the Universe") sanitized much of its complexity, the original Czech version remains a gripping, intelligent piece of cinema that deserves far greater recognition.

entries.title: In the Dust of the Stars
entries.creator: Gottfried Kolditz (Director)
entries.pitch: In the Dust of the Stars (Im Staub der Sterne) is a 1976 East German science fiction film, co-produced with Romania and directed by the legendary Gottfried Kolditz, who previously helmed the acclaimed Eolomea. Set in a far-flung future, the film follows the crew of the spaceship Cynro who respond to a distress call from the mysterious planet TEM 4—only to discover that their radio waves have caused their ship to crash land on the planet's surface. What begins as a rescue mission quickly transforms into a gripping tale of deception, exploitation, and moral choice when the crew uncovers that the planet's ruler, Ronk, has been lying about the nature of his world. The crew must decide whether to flee and save themselves or stay and help the oppressed slaves who toil in the planet's underground mines. Praised by critics as a "guilty pleasure" with "much imagination throughout," this East German space opera offers a unique blend of Soviet-bloc science fiction aesthetics, political allegory, and adventurous storytelling that stands apart from both Western and contemporary sci-fi cinema.

entries.title: Indestructible Man
entries.creator: Jack Pollexfen
entries.pitch: Indestructible Man is a 1956 American crime horror science fiction film starring Lon Chaney Jr. as Charles "Butcher" Benton, a convicted robber and murderer who is executed in the gas chamber, then unlawfully acquired by a scientist for experiments in tissue rejuvenation. Through chemical injections and massive high-voltage electricity, Benton is revived as an impervious mute monster with immense strength, seeking revenge on the men who betrayed him. The film is notable for its noir-influenced storytelling set over a 72-hour period in Los Angeles, featuring location shooting and a narrative style popularized by television police dramas of the era.

entries.title: Insatiability
entries.creator: Stanisław Ignacy Witkiewicz
entries.pitch:
Insatiability (Polish: Nienasycenie) is a haunting speculative fiction novel written in 1927 and published in 1930 by the Polish polymath Stanisław Ignacy Witkiewicz, known as "Witkacy." Set in the near future circa 2000, the novel depicts Poland in the aftermath of a catastrophic Bolshevik-style revolution that has left the nation conquered by the army of the last Mongol conquest, led by the Chinese ruler Murti Bing. The conquerors impose a dystopian regime where citizens are forced to take a mind-control pill called "DAVAMESK B 2," which eliminates their ability to think critically and resist authority. The story follows young protagonist Zip Kapen as he navigates this collapsed world, where Eastern and Western cultures have merged into "faceless misery fueled by sexual instincts."

Witkacy's only published novel during his lifetime is a extraordinary work—part absurdist satire, part philosophical meditation, part apocalyptic vision. The novel combines chaotic action with deep political and philosophical commentary, predicting with unsettling accuracy the totalitarian mind control that would be exerted on Poland in the decades after its publication. Czesław Miłosz famously discussed the "Murti-Bing pill" in The Captive Mind as a metaphor for Socialist Realism's demand that artists surrender their creativity. The book consists of two parts: "Przebudzenie" (Awakening) and "Obłęd" (Madness).

entries.title: Interplanetary Revolution
entries.creator: Nikolai Khodataev, Zenon Komissarenko, Yuri Merkulov
entries.pitch:
Interplanetary Revolution is one of the earliest Soviet animated films, created in 1924 as a satirical animated short. Originally intended as animated inserts for the sci-fi film Aelita, it was instead released separately as a parody. The 8-minute black-and-white silent film uses primitive cutout animation to deliver a starkly political message about class struggle in space.

The film depicts the bourgeoisie of all countries fleeing Earth in a shoe-shaped spaceship to escape the advancing proletariat, hoping to save their plundered capital. A red army commissar named Kominternov pursues them, ultimately landing on Mars where he fosters a victorious proletarian revolution. The animation is deliberately crude, almost devoid of intertitles, relying on visual symbolism to convey its revolutionary message.

entries.title: Invaders from Space
entries.creator: Teruo Ishii
entries.pitch: A 1964 American-edit of Japanese Super Giant film serials, Invaders from Space features the superhero Starman as he battles the Salamander Men from planet Kulimon. This is classic Tokusatsu sci-fi - men in rubber suits, model rockets, and earnest heroics against alien threats. Part of the cult Super Giant series that later inspired Ultraman and the wider Henshin Hero genre.

entries.title: Invasion from Aldebaran
entries.creator: Marek Španěl, Ondřej Španěl
entries.pitch: Invasion from Aldebaran is a Czech video game released in 1992 for the Atari ST platform, developed by brothers Marek and Ondřej Španěl—later founders of the renowned Bohemia Interactive studio (creators of the Arma series). The game is a Space Invaders clone themed around Stanisław Lem's short story of the same name, marking one of the earliest known Czech video games inspired by Eastern Bloc science fiction literature. Published by JRC (the largest Czech computer retailer and distributor at the time), this game represents a fascinating convergence of communist-era computing culture and Lem's satirical vision of first contact. The title earned the Španěl brothers their first income from game development, providing the financial foundation and motivation that eventually led to the creation of Operation Flashpoint—one of the most influential military simulation games ever made.

entries.title: Invasion of Alien Bikini
entries.creator: 未知
