entries.pitch: A low-budget South Korean sci-fi comedy that riffs on the superhero genre. Young-Gun is a masked vigilante who patrols the city streets every night — not because anyone asked him to, but because he can't stand by when he sees trouble. He risks his life for strangers, picks up litter along his route, and asks for nothing in return. One night, he hears a woman screaming. After battling mysterious attackers, he rescues her and brings her home — where things take an unexpected turn. The title promises aliens and bikinis, and the film delivers exactly the kind of earnest, weird superhero parody that thrives in Korean genre cinema.

entries.title: Invasion of the Body Snatchers
entries.creator: Don Siegel (Director)
entries.pitch:
Invasion of the Body Snatchers is a 1956 American science-fiction horror film directed by Don Siegel and based on Jack Finney's 1954 science-fiction stories "The Body Snatchers." The film was produced by Walter Wanger and stars Kevin McCarthy and Dana Wynter. Set in the fictional California town of Santa Mira, the film follows Dr. Miles Bennell, who discovers that extraterrestrial plant spores have fallen from space and are growing into pods that produce emotionless duplicates of sleeping townspeople. As the "pod people" slowly replace the human population, Dr. Bennell and his ex-girlfriend Becky Driscoll must fight to survive the quiet invasion before it's too late.

The film is notable for its film noir style, black-and-white cinematography, and its subtle approach to horror—rather than rely on monsters or violence, it taps into deeper fears of conformity, loss of identity, and the erasure of individuality. The film was an independent production distributed by Allied Artists Pictures and has become one of the most influential science-fiction horror films ever made.

entries.title: Invasión
entries.creator: Hugo Santiago (Director), Jorge Luis Borges & Adolfo Bioy Casares (Writers)
entries.pitch:
Invasión (Invasion) is a 1969 Argentine science fiction mystery film directed by Hugo Santiago and written by the legendary literary duo of Jorge Luis Borges and Adolfo Bioy Casares. Widely regarded as an important cult film, its style is considered intermediate between classic cinema and the French Nouvelle Vague. The film is set in the fictional city of Aquilea (representing Buenos Aires), where a group of defenders attempts to ward off an enigmatic alien invasion that remains abstract, undefined, and ultimately unstoppable.

The film achieved significant critical acclaim, ranking 38th in a survey of the 100 greatest Argentine films conducted by the Museo del Cine in 2000, and notably climbing to the 2nd position in a 2022 survey organized by specialized Argentine film magazines. Invasión premiered at the Cannes International Film Festival during the first Directors Fortnight and won an award at the Locarno International Film Festival in 1969. The film represents a unique collaboration between Santiago and the two most celebrated Argentine writers of the 20th century, bringing Borges' characteristic themes of labyrinths, impossible quests, and inevitable defeat to the screen.

entries.title: Invention for Destruction
entries.creator: Karel Zeman
entries.pitch: Set in a fantastical Victorian-era world that blends Jules Verne's imagination with stunning practical effects, this 1958 Czechoslovak film tells the story of an astronomer who discovers a pirate's secret weapon—a devastating explosive device capable of destroying entire islands. When the inventor is kidnapped by ruthless pirates, a daring rescue mission unfolds across seas and through the skies, involving balloon ships, submarine voyages, and an epic confrontation on a volcanic island. The film is a visual marvel, combining live actors with innovative stop-motion animation, matte paintings, and trick photography to create a world that looks like the original illustrations for Verne's novels come to life. Praised by Pauline Kael, André Bazin, and Alain Resnais, this is one of the most visually inventive science fantasy films ever made.

entries.title: Invisible Adversaries
entries.creator: Valie Export
entries.pitch:
Invisible Adversaries is a 1977 Austrian experimental feature film that serves as a feminist reimagining of the body-snatcher genre. Directed by Valie Export in her debut feature, the film follows Anna, a fashion photographer in contemporary Vienna, who begins to suspect that extraterrestrial beings are colonizing the minds of her fellow citizens, raising their aggression quotient and threatening to replace human consciousness entirely.

The film is a visually striking work that blends narrative experimentation with theory, combining elements of Cubism, Surrealism, Dada, and avant-garde cinema. Export uses mirrors, still photography, video, dance, and films-within-the-film to create what critics have called "one of the richest avant-garde features of the 1970s." The result is both a personal exploration of female identity and a chilling examination of how external forces—media, politics, technology—can colonize the inner self.

This is essential viewing for fans of experimental cinema and feminist theory, offering a female perspective on the alien-invasion narrative that predates similar works by decades. Its winning combination of sexual frankness and visual wit makes it a landmark of Austrian cinema and a crucial text in the history of women's filmmaking.

entries.title: Iria: Zeiram the Animation
entries.creator: Tetsurō Amino
entries.pitch:
A prequel to the cult live-action film Zeiram, this 6-episode OVA follows Iria, a rookie bounty hunter on the planet Myce, as she investigates her first encounter with the unstoppable alien called Zeiram. When her brother Gren is lost during a rescue mission aboard the spaceship Karma, Iria discovers that Zeiram was deliberately brought to Myce by a corporation seeking to weaponize the indestructible alien. With the help of her mentor Bob (whose mind has been uploaded to a computer after being critically wounded) and the cynical veteran hunter Fujikuro, Iria must uncover the conspiracy before she's eliminated.

The series combines classic bounty hunter action with genuine emotional stakes as Iria grapples with loss, identity, and the question of what it means to be human when consciousness can be digitized.

entries.title: Iron Sky
entries.creator: Timo Vuorensola
entries.pitch: Iron Sky is a 2012 Finnish-German-Australian science fiction comedy that takes one of history's most infamous factions—the Nazis—and sends them into outer space. When a group of German Nazis fled to the dark side of the Moon in 1945 after World War II, they built a secret fleet with plans to return and conquer Earth in 2018. The film follows the arrival of an American astronaut who discovers this lunar Nazi colony, setting up a satirical showdown between 1940s fascism and 2018 politics. Blending action sequences with sharp political commentary, Iron Sky is a cult comedy that uses the absurd premise to critique everything from American imperialism to media manipulation.

entries.title: Island City
entries.creator: Jonathan Glassner
entries.topics: Genetic Engineering, Virtual Reality, Mutation, Class Struggle, Surveillance
entries.pitch:
In 2035, humanity has discovered a fountain of youth drug that keeps people physically young. But there is a terrible side effect: most who take it mutate into barbaric proto-humanoids. The few immune survivors live behind the walls of a futuristic city, while mutants roam the wasteland outside. When a rescue squad loses one of their own to the mutants, they must organize a desperate search-and-rescue mission.

The film touches on fascinating themes: genetic compatibility determines who can marry whom, with citizens wearing color-coded crystals on their sternum based on genetic makeup. The morality of seeking eternal youth is explored through a character who refused the drug and has aged normally while his wife remains young. Virtual reality serves as both learning tool and escape into fantasy.

entries.title: Island of Lost Souls
entries.creator: Erle C. Kenton (Director)
entries.pitch: Island of Lost Souls is a 1932 American science fiction horror film that stands as one of the most disturbing early adaptations of H.G. Wells's novel The Island of Dr. Moreau. Directed by Erle C. Kenton and starring Charles Laughton as the sinister Dr. Moreau, the film follows shipwrecked sailor Edward Parker who finds himself stranded on a mysterious South Seas island inhabited by the eccentric scientist and his grotesque creations—human-animal hybrids who were surgically transformed against nature. The film is notable for its chilling atmosphere, Laughton's memorable performance, and its unflinching exploration of scientific hubris and the boundaries of humanity.

entries.title: Island of Rusty General
entries.creator: Valentin Khovenko
entries.pitch:
In late 21st century Moscow, schoolgirl Alisa Seleznyova lands the role of Little Red Riding Hood in a children's film. But her adventure goes far beyond the script when ancient military robots—discovered at an archaeological excavation and meant for remelting—escape and land on a deserted island. These aren't ordinary machines: they retain their combat programming and begin planning to enslave humanity. Alisa finds herself captured by the very robots she was meant to act alongside.

This 1988 Soviet children's film blends fairy tale aesthetics with Cold War anxieties about military technology run amok. The rusty, obsolete robots—nicknamed for their decaying hardware—represent fears of weapons systems that persist beyond their intended lifespan. Yet the film maintains an upbeat tone, trusting young viewers to handle themes of machine uprising without despair.

The production draws from Kir Bulychov's popular Alisa Seleznyova adventure series, which spawned multiple children's sci-fi films in the Soviet Union. Director Valentin Khovenko creates a visually inventive world where the line between film-within-a-film and reality blurs, giving young audiences a meta-narrative about stories and their power.

entries.title: Jabberwocky
entries.creator: Jan Švankmajer
entries.pitch: Jabberwocky is a 14-minute Czechoslovak animated short film directed by Jan Švankmajer, based loosely on Lewis Carroll's 1871 poem "Jabberwocky" and drawing inspiration from Czech surrealist Vítězslav Nezval's children's book "Anička skřítek a Slaměný Hubert." Created in 1971 during Czechoslovakia's normalization period, this film represents Švankmajer's distinctive fusion of stop-motion animation, live-action elements, and surrealist imagery. The film was produced by Krátký film Praha for Weston Woods Studios and stands as a seminal work in the Czech animator's early career, showcasing the techniques and thematic concerns that would define his later international acclaim.

entries.title: Jackpot 2
entries.creator: Matti Ijäs
entries.pitch: In a post-apocalyptic Helsinki reduced to ruins, three young people drift through the skeletal remains of the city on a Friday evening. The boys obsessively chase one thing: the legendary Flip-Flop pinball machine, the last working arcade in the blasted urban landscape. This Finnish oddity channels the existential ennui of youth culture through the neon glow of pinball bumpers, creating a haunting meditation on what people cling to when civilization collapses.

entries.title: Jaithra Yaathra
entries.creator: Sasikumar
entries.pitch: Jaithra Yaathra (Journey of the Phantom) is a 1987 Malayalam science fiction film that tells the story of Raghunathan, an ordinary man whose life changes when a lightning strike grants him the ability to become invisible at will. Originally a humble worker, Raghunathan discovers his new power after being struck by lightning during a freak accident at a scientific facility. Using his newfound ability to turn invisible, he takes on the criminals and corrupt officials who have oppressed his village, becoming a phantom-like protector. However, as his double life continues, he must grapple with the moral implications of his powers and the consequences of living between visibility and invisibility.

entries.title: Japon İşi
entries.creator: Kartal Tibet
entries.pitch:
In this 1987 Turkish sci-fi comedy, a hapless romantic named Veysel pines for the beautiful singer Başak, who spurns his advances. After rescuing a Japanese tourist from an accident, Veysel receives an unexpected gift: a robot double of Başak, sent from Japan in gratitude. The android is indistinguishable from the real singer—and far more affectionate.

The film plays as a gentle satire of sci-fi fantasies about the perfect partner: a lookalike without the original's attitude. It's a charming period piece that blends 1980s Turkish popular culture with robot technology that was then futuristic. The comedy relies on misunderstandings and the absurdity of passing off an android as one's spouse.

entries.title: Je t'aime, je t'aime
entries.creator: Alain Resnais (director), screenplay by Jacques Sternberg
entries.pitch: Je t'aime, je t'aime is a 1968 French science fiction film directed by Alain Resnais, one of the most acclaimed French New Wave filmmakers. The film centers on Claude Ridder, a man who has just left a Belgian hospital after attempting suicide. He is recruited for a mysterious time travel experiment conducted by researchers at the Crespel Research Center. The experiment, intended to send him back to relive just one minute from one year earlier, instead causes him to experience fragmented moments from his past relationship with his former lover Catrine in a disjointed, non-linear fashion. The film is notable for its psychological depth and its innovative exploration of memory, time, and guilt.

entries.title: Jet-Story
entries.creator: Miroslav Fídler, František Fuka, Tomáš Rylek
entries.pitch: Jet-Story is a 1988 action game developed by Cybexlab Software for the ZX Spectrum, published by Ultrasoft. The player controls a spacecraft navigating through a massive maze-like world containing 128 distinct areas. The objective is to locate and destroy 47 enemy bases scattered throughout this labyrinthine environment. The game is notable for its ambitious scope—a vast interconnected world filled with hostile forces in an era when ZX Spectrum titles typically featured more confined environments. Developed primarily by Miroslav Fídler with musical contributions from František Fuka, Jet-Story represents a distinctive Czechoslovakian contribution to the ZX Spectrum library.

entries.title: Journey to the Beginning of Time
entries.creator: Karel Zeman
entries.pitch: Journey to the Beginning of Time (Czech: Cesta do pravěku) is a 1955 Czechoslovak science fiction adventure film directed by the visionary Karel Zeman, renowned for his innovative special effects that seamlessly blended live-action with stop-motion animation. The film follows four teenage friends—Petr, Toník, Jenda, and Jirka—who discover a mysterious cave leading to a "river of time." As they row upstream, they travel progressively backward through geological eras, encountering the prehistoric creatures that once roamed Earth. The film is celebrated for its pioneering techniques, combining 2-D and 3-D models with live-action footage in ways that influenced future filmmakers, including Steven Spielberg, who cited it as an inspiration for Jurassic Park. It won awards at the Venice and Mannheim International Film Festivals and is considered the best Czech science fiction film of all time.

entries.title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
entries.creator: Henry Levin (Director), Charles Brackett (Producer), Jules Verne (Source)
entries.pitch:
Journey to the Center of the Earth is a 1959 American science fiction adventure film directed by Henry Levin and starring James Mason, Pat Boone, Arlene Dahl, and Diane Baker. Based on Jules Verne's classic 1864 novel, the film follows Professor Sir Oliver Lindenbrook, a geologist at the University of Edinburgh, who discovers a mysterious plumb bob with a cryptic inscription that leads him and his students on an epic journey to the center of the Earth via a volcanic passage in Iceland.

The film was a major commercial success and received critical acclaim, earning three Academy Award nominations. It is celebrated for its innovative special effects, Bernard Herrmann's sweeping score, and the breathtaking subterranean sequences featuring prehistoric creatures and the lost city of Atlantis.

entries.title: Just Imagine
entries.creator: David Butler
entries.pitch:
Just Imagine is a 1930 American pre-Code science fiction musical-comedy that portrays New York City in an imagined 1980. The film follows J-21 (John Garrick), who plans to marry LN-18 (Maureen O'Sullivan), but the marriage tribunal has refused his application. Meanwhile, scientists revive a man from 1930 who was struck by lightning while playing golf—now called "Single O" (El Brendel)—providing comedic commentary on the futuristic world of 1980, where numbers have replaced names, pills have replaced food, and aircraft have replaced automobiles.

When LN-18 is forced to marry the conceited MT-3, J-21 and his friend RT-42 join scientist Z-4 on a rocket plane to Mars. There they meet the Martian Queen Looloo and King Loko, encounter evil twins, and ultimately return to Earth, where J-21 earns the right to marry LN-18 as one of the first men to visit another planet.

entries.title: Justy
entries.creator: Tsuguo Okazaki (manga), Pierrot (anime)
entries.pitch: Justy (also known as Cosmo Police Justy) is a 1985 OVA adapted from Tsuguo Okazaki's manga series. Set in a distant future, it follows Justy Kaizard, the most powerful esper in the known universe working for the Galaxy Patrol System Cosmo Police. The story begins with Justy tracking down the criminal esper Magnamum Vega, whom he kills—setting in motion events that will define the rest of his life. Years later, the orphaned daughter of his target, Astaris, becomes his adoptive sister, and Justy must protect her from criminal espers who seek to use her immense psychic powers. The OVA was released as a double feature with the Area 88 film and has never received an official English release, making it a rare piece of anime history.

entries.title: Kaadu
entries.creator: William Berke
entries.pitch:
Kaadu (also released as "The Jungle") is a 1952 Indian-American science fiction adventure film that holds the distinction of being the first science fiction film ever produced in India. Directed by American filmmaker William Berke and produced by T.R. Sundaram's Modern Theatres Ltd, this cross-cultural collaboration represents a remarkable early instance of Indo-American cinematic cooperation. The film features Hollywood stars Rod Cameron, Cesar Romero, and Marie Windsor alongside Indian actors including M.N. Nambiar and Sulochana, blending Hollywood adventure conventions with Tamil cinema craftsmanship.

The story follows Princess Sati, who returns to India as regent to find her villages under siege from mysterious stampeding elephants. When her friend Rama Singh hires the famous hunter Steve Bentley to investigate, only one man returns from a team of ten—claiming the attacks are caused by mammoths, creatures thought extinct for millennia. The film combines adventure, mystery, and scientific curiosity as Bentley, Sati, and their party venture into the jungle to confront these prehistoric beasts. Though critics note the film is "low on monsters," its unusual premise and cross-cultural production make it a fascinating artifact of early global science fiction cinema.

entries.title: Kalai Arasi
entries.creator: A. Kasilingam
entries.pitch: Kalai Arasi is a 1963 Tamil-language science fiction film that holds the distinction of being the first Indian film to feature the concept of aliens visiting Earth. Directed by A. Kasilingam and starring the legendary M.G. Ramachandran, this pioneering film combines elements of space opera with traditional Indian storytelling. The plot follows Mohan, an honest farmer, who falls in love with Vani, the daughter of a wealthy landlord. Meanwhile, aliens from a technologically advanced but artistically backward planet arrive on Earth on a mission—they seek a talented performer to teach their people music and dance. After witnessing Vani's beautiful singing, the alien commander Thinna kidnaps her to take back to their planet. What follows is a tale of love, adventure, and cross-cultural artistic exchange as Mohan ventures into space to rescue his beloved.

entries.title: Karutha Rathrikal
entries.creator: P. Subramaniam (as Mahesh)
entries.pitch:
Karutha Rathrikal (The Darkest Nights) is a 1967 Malayalam-language science fiction thriller film directed by P. Subramaniam (credited as Mahesh). Considered the first science fiction film in the history of Malayalam cinema, it stands as a pioneering work that brought speculative fiction to South Indian film. The film is an adaptation of Robert Louis Stevenson's classic novella "The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde," transplanting the story of duality and transformation into a Malayalam cultural context.

The story follows Dr. Santhan, a medical practitioner who develops a revolutionary medicine capable of transforming a person into a monstrous creature. Driven by revenge against the bank directors responsible for his uncle's death, Santhan keeps his invention secret, using it to terrorize and eliminate those who wronged his family. As the body count rises and his double life becomes increasingly difficult to maintain, Santhan must confront the consequences of his scientific experimentation.

While the film did not achieve major commercial success, it represents a significant milestone in Indian cinema's exploration of science fiction themes. The film was released on June 9, 1967, and has since gained a modest cult following among fans of classic Indian cinema and early Malayalam science fiction.

entries.title: Kenny Begins
entries.creator: Carl Åstrand
entries.pitch:
Kenny Begins is a 2009 Swedish comedy science fiction film that serves as a prequel to the 1997 TV series Kenny Starfighter. The film follows Kenny Starfighter, an incompetent student at the Hero Academy of the galaxy, who crash-lands on Earth after botching a graduation attempt. There he teams up with Pontus, a bullied teenager who has stumbled upon a mysterious power crystal that has granted him superhuman abilities.

The film parodies superhero tropes while delivering genuine adventure. With a budget of $6.8 million, it holds the record for most special effects in a Swedish film. The comedy mixes slapstick with genuine heart, as Kenny must protect Pontus from Rutger Oversmart, the most intelligent being in the universe who seeks to steal the crystal's power.

entries.title: Key the Metal Idol
entries.creator: Hiroaki Satō (Writer/Director)
entries.pitch:
Key the Metal Idol is a Japanese OVA series released between 1994 and 1997, comprising 15 episodes across four parts. The story follows Tokiko "Key" Mima, a young woman who believes herself to be a robot created by her grandfather, Dr. Murao Mima. On his deathbed, Dr. Mima records a will telling Key she can become human if she gains 30,000 friends. Believing her "battery" is running low, Key leaves her rural hometown for Tokyo to become an idol singer, hoping to amass the required following.

What begins as a seemingly simple story about a robot girl wanting to become human gradually unfolds into a complex narrative involving corporate conspiracy, supernatural powers, spiritual themes, and existential questions about identity. The series was produced by Studio Pierrot and is notable for its unusual release structure—episodes of varying lengths culminating in two feature-length final episodes.

entries.title: Kikokugai: The Cyber Slayer
entries.creator: Nitroplus (Developer), Gen Urobuchi (Writer)
entries.pitch:
Kikokugai: The Cyber Slayer is a Japanese cyberpunk visual novel developed by Nitroplus, released in 2002. Written by Gen Urobuchi—later famous for works like Puella Magi Madoka Magica and Fate/Zero—this game represents an early exploration of Urobuchi's signature blend of dark themes, moral ambiguity, and visceral violence. Set in a dystopian future Shanghai, the story weaves together elements of Chinese wuxia martial arts tradition with cybernetic body horror and hardboiled crime drama.

The game is notable for being Nitroplus's third title and their first to receive an English translation. It was later remade in 2011 as "Kikokugai -Reichin Rinrinshan-" with enhanced graphics, full voice acting, and a non-adult version suitable for wider release. The title combines "kikokugai" (meaning "crying streets" or "ghost cry") with the subtitle "The Cyber Slayer," suggesting a narrative steeped in tragedy, violence, and urban decay.

What makes Kikokugai distinctive is its fusion of Eastern and Western genre traditions: the Chinese wuxia influence of wandering swordsmen and martial arts mastery collides with Japanese cyberpunk aesthetics and Western crime noir storytelling. The result is a grim, violent tale about loyalty, betrayal, and the dehumanization of humanity in a world where technology and organized crime have become inseparable.

entries.title: Killing in Istanbul
entries.creator: Yılmaz Atadeniz
entries.pitch:
Killing in Istanbul (Turkish: Kilink Istanbul'da) is a 1967 Turkish fantasy adventure superhero film, one of the earliest superhero movies produced in Turkey. Based on the Italian comic book character Killing (also known as Satanik), the film was directed by Yılmaz Atadeniz and features the masked vigilante Kilink battling criminals in Istanbul.

The film is notable as part of a wave of low-budget Turkish superhero films from the 1960s and 70s, which drew inspiration from European photo-comics and adventure serials. While crude by modern standards, these films represent an interesting chapter in Turkish genre cinema, where international comic book characters were adapted for local audiences seeking exciting action entertainment.

The film runs 71 minutes and was produced during a period when Turkish cinema was experimenting with various genres, including the emerging superhero action film. It features the typical hero-vs-villain storyline of the era, with the masked hero fighting to protect the innocent from criminal forces.

entries.title: Killing vs. the Flying Man
entries.creator: Dr. Türker İlioğlu
entries.pitch:
This is the second entry in the Turkish \"Kilink\" superhero film series, featuring one of Turkey's earliest attempts at creating a superhero movie. The film picks up where the first installment left off, with Superman (known as Kilink in Turkish) continuing his battle against the evil villain Kilink.

The plot involves Superman managing to locate Kilink's hideout on a remote island where his fiancé and her father are being held captive. Meanwhile, Kilink's scientists have developed a powerful destructive weapon capable of blasting away portions of mountains. The film continues the campy, low-budget superhero action that made these Turkish films cult classics, combining superhero themes with local storytelling.

These Kilink films represent an interesting piece of Turkish cinema history, being among the first superhero films produced in Turkey and showing the influence of American comic book culture on international film industries.

entries.title: Kin-dza-dza!
entries.creator: Georgiy Daneliya (Director), Revaz Gabriadze (Writer)
entries.pitch:
Imagine stumbling through a teleportation device on a Moscow street and ending up on a desert planet in a distant galaxy where civilization has collapsed into a rigid caste system based on genetic hierarchy. This is the premise of Kin-dza-dza!, a 1986 Soviet cult classic that blends dystopian sci-fi with absurdist comedy.

The story follows Uncle Vova, a gruff Moscow construction foreman, and a young Georgian student who accidentally travel to the planet Pluke in the Kin-dza-dza star system. There, they discover a post-apocalyptic society where the only spoken words are "ku" (meaning everything good) and "kyu" (the ultimate profanity), and where citizens are strictly divided into "Chatlanians" (privileged upper class) and "Patsaks" (lower class) - a distinction determined by a handheld device called a "visator."

The film is a biting satirical commentary on Soviet bureaucracy, class systems, and blind conformity, disguised as a psychedelic space adventure. Described by Little White Lies magazine as "Mad Max meets Monty Python by way of Tarkovsky," it's a singular piece of dystopian cinema that emerged from behind the Iron Curtain.

entries.title: King of the Rocket Men
entries.creator: Fred C. Brannon (Director), Franklin Adreon (Producer)
entries.pitch:
King of the Rocket Men is a classic 12-chapter Republic Pictures serial from 1949 that introduced one of science fiction's most iconic hero types: the Rocket Man. When evil genius Dr. Vulcan begins eliminating members of the Science Associates—an organization of America's greatest scientists—one survivor outfits journalist Jeff King with an atomic-powered rocket backpack, bullet-shaped flight helmet, and raygun. Transformed into Rocket Man, Jeff battles Dr. Vulcan's henchmen across twelve action-packed chapters, racing to stop the villain from using a devastating Sonic Decimator to destroy New York City.

The serial is notable for featuring the only character actually called "Rocket Man" in Republic's library—a title that would later be applied by fans to the wave of rocket-powered heroes that followed in subsequent serials like Radar Men from the Moon and Zombies of the Stratosphere. The flying sequences, achieved through stunt work on wires and springboards, became template for countless sci-fi serials to come.

entries.title: King of the Wild
entries.creator: B. Reeves Eason, Richard Thorpe
entries.pitch: King of the Wild is a 1931 American pre-Code Mascot movie serial starring Walter Miller, Nora Lane, and a young Boris Karloff in one of his earliest film roles. The story follows American adventurer Robert Grant, who is falsely accused of murdering an Indian Rajah and imprisoned. After escaping, he flees to Africa to find the real culprit and clear his name. In the African jungle, he encounters Sheik Mustapha (Karloff), who possesses evidence that could exonerate him, along with the location of a secret diamond mine. He also meets Muriel Armitage, who is searching for her missing brother Tom. Together, they face deadly dangers including man-eaters, treacherous villains, and the perilous jungle in pursuit of justice and treasure. The serial consists of 12 chapters running approximately 248 minutes total.

entries.title: Kingsajz
entries.creator: Juliusz Machulski
entries.pitch:
Kingsajz is a 1988 Polish cult comedy fantasy film that serves as a biting allegory of the communist regime. The story follows Olo Jedlina, a gnome (krasnoludek) who serves the underground kingdom of Szuflandia (Drawerland), a hidden realm beneath the Quaternary Research Institute. When Olo is permitted to visit "Kingsajz" — the world of full-sized humans — he discovers a green potion that allows him to achieve human proportions. He decides to stay, becoming a journalist and living a peaceful life in the human world, regularly drinking Polo-Cockta to maintain his size.

His friend Adaś Happs, the scientist who helped create the Kingsajz potion, rebels against the gnome government and escapes to Kingsajz. Working in a secret laboratory, he attempts to decode the potion formula so all gnomes can become human-sized. When authorities track him down, Olo must mount a rescue mission back into the underground kingdom — now at human size to confront the regime that sent agents to bring him back.

entries.title: Kite
entries.creator: Yasuomi Umetsu
entries.pitch: Kite is a 1998 adult OVA directed by Yasuomi Umetsu that follows Sawa, a young girl who becomes an assassin after her parents are murdered. Raised by her guardians Akai and Kanie (who were actually behind her parents' death), Sawa is trained as a professional killer, using special exploding bullets to eliminate targets for a corrupt system. When she meets fellow young assassin Oburi, she finds the will to escape her handlers and seek revenge. The film is notorious for its extreme violence, controversial content, and its themes of trauma, manipulation, and cycles of abuse.

entries.title: Koi... Mil Gaya
entries.creator: Rakesh Roshan (Director/Producer), Story by Rakesh Roshan
entries.pitch: Koi... Mil Gaya is a groundbreaking 2003 Indian Hindi-language science fiction film that tells the story of Rohit Mehra, a developmentally disabled young man who inadvertently makes contact with an extraterrestrial being through his late father's supercomputer. Raised by his mother after his father died in a car accident moments after receiving a signal from space, Rohit has the mental capacity of a child. When he stumbles upon his father's computer and sends signals into space, he receives a response—aliens land on Earth, and one accidentally gets left behind. What follows is a heartwarming tale of friendship between Rohit and the alien named Jadoo, who uses his psychokinetic powers to enhance Rohit's intelligence. The film seamlessly blends family drama, science fiction, and the theme of acceptance, becoming India's first major sci-fi film featuring aliens and launching the successful Krrish franchise.

entries.title: Kokey
entries.creator: Romy V. Suzara
entries.pitch: Kokey is a 1997 Filipino science fiction film produced by Star Cinema, one of the Philippines' most prominent film studios. The film tells the story of two siblings, Bong and Anna, who discover an extraterrestrial being whose spaceship has crashed on Earth. Rather than fearing the alien, the children befriend Kokey and hide him from their parents, eventually forming a deep bond with the gentle alien. Kokey uses his extraterrestrial powers to help the family's small business, attracting customers and bringing prosperity. However, Kokey becomes increasingly homesick, longing to return to his own planet and family. The film explores themes of friendship, compassion, and the pain of separation, set against the backdrop of a typical Filipino family struggling to make ends meet.

entries.title: Krabi
entries.creator: Václav Mergl
entries.pitch: Krabi (known internationally as "The Crabs") is a 1976 Czechoslovak animated short film that stands as a masterwork of Eastern European science fiction animation. Directed by Václav Mergl and based on a story by Soviet science fiction writer Anatoly Dneprov, this 12-minute wordless film uses striking cut-out animation to tell a chilling allegory about militarism and technological escalation. The film emerged from the renowned Krátký film Prague studio, known for producing innovative animated works during the communist era. Though obscure in the Western world, Krabi has gained a cult following among animation enthusiasts and is recognized for its unique visual style—featuring a deliberately simplified, almost childlike aesthetic that serves as a counterpoint to its deeply dark thematic content.

entries.title: Krakatit
entries.creator: Otakar Vávra (director), based on the novel by Karel Čapek
entries.pitch: Krakatit is a 1948 Czechoslovak science fiction mystery film directed by Otakar Vávra, based on Karel Čapek's 1922 novel of the same name. The story follows Prokop, a brilliant chemist who awakens in a hospital with severe burns to his hands, suffering from delirium. As his memories gradually return, he recalls inventing "krakatit"—a devastating explosive named after the volcano Krakatoa that can be detonated remotely using high-frequency radio signals. His former friend Jiří has sold the formula to Balttin Works, a foreign weapons manufacturer, and they coerce Prokop into recreating his invention. The film explores the terrifying power of scientific discovery weaponized for war and the moral responsibility of inventors.

entries.title: Kreed
entries.creator: Burut Creative Team
entries.pitch: Kreed is a Russian first-person shooter released in 2003, set in the distant future year of 2944. The player controls an unnamed space marine sent to stop a cult of religious fanatics from accessing a mysterious cross-dimensional anomaly known as "The Kreed." Developed by Burut Creative Team and published by Russobit-M, the game emphasizes world-building and exploration, presenting its narrative through in-game cutscenes and computer terminals that players can read. The story unfolds as humanity wages an interstellar war against an alien species called the Tiglaary, while the Kreed anomaly confuses scientists and religious followers alike—some believing it holds spiritual significance or serves as a gateway to higher beings.

entries.title: Krrish
entries.creator: Rakesh Roshan
entries.pitch: Krrish is a 2006 Indian superhero film that blends science fiction with Indian mythology and action. The story follows Krishna Mehra, a physically disabled boy who inherits superhuman abilities from his father Rohit Mehra, an eccentric scientist who made contact with an alien named Jadoo. When Krishna grows up, he becomes the superhero Krrish to fight the evil Dr. Siddhant Arya, who is creating a supercomputer that can predict the future. The film is notable for its cutting-edge visual effects for Indian cinema and for pioneering the superhero genre in Bollywood.

entries.title: L'Atlantide
entries.creator: G.W. Pabst
entries.pitch:
Two French officers, Saint-Avit and Morhange, become lost in the African desert and discover a hidden civilization in the sunken city of Atlantis. There, they encounter Antinea, the enigmatic queen who rules over the remnants of an ancient civilization. G.W. Pabst directs this German-French adaptation of Pierre Benoît's novel with striking visual compositions and a hypnotic atmosphere.

The film blends adventure narrative with psychoanalytic subtext, exploring themes of obsession, desire, and the destructive power of attraction. Antinea emerges as a mesmerizing figure—both alien queen and femme fatale—who ensnares her prisoners in a web of devotion and jealousy. The atmospheric desert cinematography and experimental camera angles create a dreamlike quality that elevates this beyond typical adventure fare.

entries.title: L'Inhumaine
entries.creator: Marcel L'Herbier
entries.pitch:
L'Inhumaine (meaning "the inhuman woman") is a 1924 French silent science fiction film that stands as a landmark of early avant-garde cinema. Directed by Marcel L'Herbier, the film was conceived as a "miscellany of modern art" - a collaborative spectacle featuring contributions from leading practitioners in decorative arts, architecture, fashion, and music. The film caused controversy upon release and was a financial disaster, but it has since been recognized as a "manifesto for Art Deco" and a fabulously inventive work of cinematic modernism.

The story follows Claire Lescot, a famous singer who lives on the outskirts of Paris and is renowned for her extraordinary beauty but also her complete emotional coldness. She cruelly taunts her many admirers, including a maharajah and a young Swedish scientist named Einar Norsen. When informed that Norsen has killed himself because of her indifference, she shows no feelings. At her next concert, she is booed by an outraged audience. However, when she visits Norsen's tomb and admits her feelings, she discovers his death was feigned. Norsen demonstrates his invention - a system for broadcasting television - allowing Claire to see global audiences. Jealousy leads the maharajah to have Claire bitten by a poisonous snake. In Norsen's laboratory, using his scientific inventions, he revives her from death.

entries.title: LFO
entries.creator: Antonio Tublén
entries.pitch:
In the basement of an ordinary Swedish apartment building, Robert Nord spends his nights experimenting with sound frequencies on his synthesizer. When a heated argument with his wife Clara leads to a breakthrough discovery—that certain sound waves can hypnotize the human mind—Robert begins testing his power on his new neighbors. What begins as harmless curiosity spirals into something far darker: a man who has lost his family and sanity, seeking to recreate the family he destroyed through mind control.

LFO (Low Frequency Oscillation) is a 2013 Swedish-Danish science fiction film that explores the dark psychology of obsession and power. The film premiered at Fantastic Fest and went on to win multiple festival awards, praised for its unsettling exploration of the "mad scientist" trope and its sharp commentary on manipulation.

entries.title: La Charcuterie mécanique
entries.creator: Louis Lumière
entries.pitch: La Charcuterie mécanique (The Mechanical Butcher) is an 1895 French silent short film directed by Louis Lumière and widely recognized as the first science fiction film ever made. At just 49 seconds long, this groundbreaking "humorous subject" depicts a live pig being placed into a mechanical device that transforms it into various pork products—sausages, hams, and other cuts—which emerge from the other end of the machine. The film was created by the Lumière Brothers, pioneers of cinematography who are best known for their documentary-style works. This film's inclusion in Phil Hardy's The Aurum Film Encyclopedia: Science Fiction establishes it as the genesis of the science fiction genre in cinema, predating by decades the elaborate futures and space operas that would later define the genre.

entries.title: La Foire aux immortels
entries.creator: Enki Bilal
entries.pitch: La Foire aux immortels (The Carnival of Immortals) is the first installment in Enki Bilal's acclaimed Nikopol Trilogy, published in 1980. Set in Paris in the year 2023, this groundbreaking French graphic novel follows Alcide Nikopol, a man who returns to Earth after spending 30 years frozen in space as punishment for dodging military service. What he finds is a drastically changed Paris—now ruled by the fascist dictator J. F. Choublanc, overrun with aliens, and descending into chaos. Adding to the surreal atmosphere, a giant flying pyramid housing Egyptian gods hovers over the city, having run out of fuel. The gods offer the dictator immortality in exchange for fuel, while Nikopol becomes the vessel for the renegade god Horus. Together, they embark on a quest to oppose the corrupt powers of the 21st century.

entries.title: La Jetée
entries.creator: Chris Marker
entries.pitch:
La Jetée is a groundbreaking 1962 French experimental short film constructed almost entirely from still photographs, telling the story of a post-nuclear war experiment in time travel. At just 28 minutes long, this black-and-white featurette has become one of the most influential science fiction films ever made, despite its minimal runtime and unusual construction method.

The film is set in post-apocalyptic Paris after World War III, where survivors live underground in the Palais de Chaillot galleries. Scientists are researching time travel to send subjects to different time periods to find help for their destroyed society. They select a prisoner—the protagonist—whose key to the past is an obsessive childhood memory of a woman he saw at Orly Airport observation platform ("the jetty") shortly before witnessing a man's death.

The protagonist successfully travels to the pre-war past, meets the woman from his memory, and develops a romantic relationship. The experimenters then send him to the far future, where technologically advanced beings give him a power unit to regenerate his society. But upon his return, he discovers a dark truth about his fate and the nature of time itself.

entries.title: Laal Paree
entries.creator: Hannif Chippa
entries.pitch: Laal Paree is a 1991 Bollywood fantasy romance that tells the unusual story of Shankar, a man who falls in love with a woman named Meenakshi, only to discover she is a mermaid living secretly among humans. Directed by Hannif Chippa and starring Aditya Pancholi, Jahnvi (in her debut as the mermaid), Javed Jaffrey, and Gulshan Grover, the film explores themes of love across species boundaries, the conflict between human curiosity and nature's mysteries, and the dangers of exposing hidden truths. The film was loosely inspired by the 1984 American hit Splash but adds distinctly Indian cinematic elements of song, romance, and dramatic tension. With music by the famous Nadeem-Shravan duo, Laal Paree represents an early Bollywood experiment in the mermaid fantasy subgenre—rare for Indian cinema of its era.

entries.title: Laika
entries.creator: Amelie S. Debattista
entries.pitch:
Laika is a 2017 Czech animated sci-fi fantasy that reimagines the true story of the Soviet space dog through a poignant tale of sacrifice and redemption. Set in an alternate history, the film follows Laika—a stray dog captured from the outskirts of a Russian city—who is forcibly trained and sent into space as humanity's first cosmonaut.

The film blends hand-drawn animation with surrealist imagery to create a haunting meditation on humanity's relationship with animals and our relentless drive to conquer the cosmos. Beautifully crafted in the Czech tradition of poetic animation, Laika explores themes of loyalty, sacrifice, and the cost of progress.

entries.title: Laokoon
entries.creator: Václav Mergl
entries.pitch: Laokoon is a 1970 Czech animated short film directed by Václav Mergl. The film is part of a series of Czech animated science fiction and horror shorts from the 1970s, which includes works like Krabi (1976) and The Cybernetic Grandma (1962). The title refers to the Greek mythological figure Laocoön, a Trojan priest who warned the Trojans about the Wooden Horse and was killed by sea serpents sent by the gods.

entries.title: Laser Squad
entries.creator: Julian Gollop / Target Games
entries.pitch: Laser Squad is a turn-based tactics video game originally released for the ZX Spectrum in 1988 and subsequently ported to Commodore 64, Amstrad CPC, Amiga, Atari ST, and MS-DOS. Developed by Julian Gollop and his team at Target Games (later Mythos Games), it expanded on the ideas from their earlier Rebelstar series and became a foundational work in the tactical turn-based genre. The game features seven scenarios where players command squads of soldiers on missions involving infiltration, assassination, rescue, and defense operations against droid forces controlled by megacorporations. What set Laser Squad apart was its innovative fog-of-war mechanics, line-of-sight combat systems, morale tracking, and resource management—all features that would directly influence the acclaimed X-COM series, which began as a planned sequel to this game.

entries.title: Late August at the Hotel Ozone
entries.creator: Jan Schmidt (Director), Pavel Juráček (Screenplay)
entries.pitch:
Late August at the Hotel Ozone is a haunting 1967 Czechoslovak post-apocalyptic film from director Jan Schmidt, based on a screenplay by Pavel Juráček. Set in the aftermath of a nuclear war that has devastated humanity, the film follows a small band of young women wandering through a desolate landscape in search of survivors—and most importantly, a man who might help them propagate the human race. Shot in stark black and white with minimal dialogue, the film is a cerebral, melancholic meditation on extinction, civilization's collapse, and the desperate measures survivors might take to prevent the end of humanity.

The film emerged from the Czechoslovak New Wave and has been praised as a "gorgeously shot and devastatingly well told" work that echoes the hopelessness of World War II narratives while预见了 later environmental and ecological anxieties. Its abstract, loosely structured approach targets art house audiences rather than mainstream science fiction viewers.

entries.title: Le Prix du Danger
entries.creator: Yves Boisset
entries.pitch: Le Prix du Danger (The Price of Danger) is a 1983 French-Yugoslav science fiction film based on Robert Sheckley's 1958 short story "The Prize of Peril." Set in the near future, the film presents a chilling vision of entertainment industry exploitation and media manipulation. A popular TV show hosted by the charismatic Frédéric Mallaire features contestants who must run for their lives while being hunted by volunteer killers, all for the chance to win a million dollars. The film explores how far society will go for ratings, and the moral compromises made in the name of entertainment.

entries.title: Le Vingtième siècle. La vie électrique
entries.creator: Albert Robida
entries.pitch: Le Vingtième siècle. La vie électrique (The Twentieth Century: Electric Life) is an 1891 French science fiction novel by Albert Robida that predicts life in 1955 France. Written in a lively, satirical tone with numerous illustrations by the author, the novel weaves the fictional scientist Philox Lorris's technological innovations into a vision of a future where electricity has transformed every aspect of society. Robida's speculative vision anticipates many technologies that would later become reality—including video calls, electric transportation, and biological weapons—while offering a trenchant critique of industrial progress, militarism, and the dehumanizing effects of unchecked technological advancement.

entries.title: Le avventure straordinarissime di Saturnino Farandola
entries.creator: Directed by Marcel Fabre; based on the novel by Albert Robida
entries.pitch: Le avventure straordinarissime di Saturnino Farandola (The Extraordinary Adventures of Saturnino Farandola) is an Italian silent film from 1913 that critics have cited as one of the first expressions of European science fiction cinema. Directed by Marcel Fabre and produced by Società Anonima Ambrosio of Turin, this pioneering film adapts Albert Robida's 1879 novel "Voyages très extraordinaires de Saturnin Farandoul." The film spans 57 minutes divided into four episodic adventures, featuring early special effects techniques inspired by Georges Méliès but applied in a more dynamic, action-oriented setting with aerial battles and innovative visual tricks. The film was shot using four main colors: ochre, green, blue, and brown—a remarkable technical achievement for the period.

entries.title: Legend of the Galactic Heroes
entries.creator: Yoshiki Tanaka (Novel), Katsumi Michihara (Manga)
entries.pitch: In the distant future, humanity has spread across the galaxy, dividing into two massive interstellar powers locked in an endless war: the authoritarian Galactic Empire and the democratic Free Planets Alliance. The epic follows two military geniuses—Reinhard von Lohengramm, an ambitious noble in the Empire driven to unseat the corrupt Goldenbaum dynasty, and Yang Wen-li, a historian-turned-admiral in the Alliance who fights to preserve democracy against impossible odds. This 110-episode OVA series (1988-1997) and its ten-novel source material are Japan's answer to "Dune" and "The Lord of the Rings"—a sprawling space opera that predates Star Wars' revival and offers a far more nuanced, cynical take on imperial ambition and democratic idealism. Winner of Japan's Seiun Award, it didn't receive an official English release until 2015, making it one of the most influential yet obscure sci-fi epics in the West.

entries.title: Lemon Angel
entries.creator: Tsutomu Ohashi
entries.pitch:
Lemon Angel is a 1988 Japanese anime series and the direct sequel to the influential adult anime series Cream Lemon. The series follows a new cast of characters navigating a blend of romantic drama and science fiction themes, continuing the exploration of relationships and emotional connections that made its predecessor notable in anime history. The anime ran for nine episodes and developed a cult following among fans of 1980s anime.

Unlike its predecessor's focus on more mature romantic themes, Lemon Angel incorporates science fiction elements into its narrative framework, featuring android characters and futuristic scenarios that add depth to the romantic storytelling.

entries.title: Lensman
entries.creator: Created by Koichi Mashimo | Based on novels by E.E. "Doc" Smith
entries.pitch:
Lensman (also known as Lensman: Secret of the Lens) is a 1984 Japanese animated feature film based on E.E. "Doc" Smith's seminal Lensman novel series. Directed by Koichi Mashimo and produced by Toru Ide and Shigehiko Koga at Ashi Productions, this film serves as an ambitious adaptation of one of science fiction's most influential space opera series. The film was later dubbed by Harmony Gold in 1988 and became a cult classic in the West, introducing many viewers to the source material that would influence everything from Star Trek to the Green Lantern Corps.

The film condenses Smith's massive narrative universe into a feature-length format, following the story of a young pilot named Kimball Kinnison (here rendered as "Bill" in some Western versions) who discovers his latent telepathic abilities and is recruited by the mysterious Arisians—an ancient, mentally-powered race who have been guiding the evolution of intelligent species across the galaxy. The Lens itself is introduced as a powerful psychic artifact that can only be worn by those who are pure of heart, granting its wearer extraordinary mental abilities including telepathy, telekinesis, and the power to communicate across light-years.

The animation, while dated by modern standards, was impressive for its time and features dynamic space battle sequences, imaginative alien designs, and a color palette that captures the grand scope of galactic civilization. The film's score blends electronic and orchestral elements typical of 1980s anime soundtracks, creating an epic atmosphere appropriate for the vast scope of the narrative.

entries.title: Les Cités obscures
entries.creator: François Schuiten (artist), Benoît Peeters (writer)
entries.pitch:
Les Cités obscures (The Obscure Cities) is a groundbreaking Franco-Belgian bande dessinée series that began publication in 1983. Created by Belgian artist François Schuiten and French writer Benoît Peeters, this visually stunning work follows no unifying narrative but instead presents a series of unrelated stories set in a parallel world reachable through mysterious "Obscure Passages" found in architecturally significant buildings. The series is commonly labeled as steampunk, featuring anachronistic technology and visual traditions inspired by Jules Verne's 19th-century Europe, though it defies easy categorization.

Each album tells a self-contained story exploring themes of architecture, identity, and the boundaries between worlds. The first volume, Les murailles de Samaris (The Walls of Samaris, 1983), introduces readers to the parallel world through the story of Franz Bauer, an investigator sent to examine the strange city of Samaris who gradually descends into paranoia. Subsequent volumes include La fièvre d'Urbicande (Fever in Urbicand, 1985), which won the prestigious Angoulême International Comics Festival Prize for Best Album, and La Tour (The Tower, 1987). The series has been translated into multiple languages and is recognized as a landmark work in the European comics tradition.

entries.title: Les Maîtres du temps
entries.creator: René Laloux
entries.pitch: Les Maîtres du temps (Time Masters) is a 1982 Franco-Hungarian animated science fiction film directed by the legendary René Laloux and designed by the renowned artist Mœbius. Based on Stefan Wul's 1958 novel "L'Orphelin de Perdide," this film continues Laloux's tradition of visually stunning science fiction animation following his earlier masterworks "Fantastic Planet" and "Light Years." The story follows a desperate space rescue mission to save a young boy stranded on the dangerous desert planet Perdide, where giant killer hornets have killed his mother. As the pilot Jaffar and his passengers—the deposed Prince Matton and his sister Belle—race against time, they encounter the mysterious Masters of Time, an alien race who can manipulate time itself. The film is notable for its breathtaking animation, complex narrative structure, and philosophical themes about time, memory, and sacrifice.

entries.title: Les Saignantes
entries.creator: Jean-Pierre Bekolo (Director)
entries.pitch:
Les Saignantes (The Bloodettes) is a 2005 Cameroonian-French science fiction erotic thriller directed by Jean-Pierre Bekolo. Set in the year 2025, the film follows Majolie and Chouchou, two sex workers navigating the dark underbelly of a futuristic Cameroon. When a high-ranking government minister dies during a sexual encounter with Majolie, the two women find themselves thrust into a nightmarish game of survival, desperately trying to dispose of the corpse while being hunted by the authorities. The film serves as a barbed political satire, blending elements of horror and science fiction with vampiric themes drawn from the ancient rituals of Mevoungou—a Cameroonian spiritual tradition.

The film marked a significant moment in African cinema, winning the Silver Stallion (second best African film) at Fespaco 2007 and earning Best Actress honors for Adèle Ado. Bekolo, known for his work under the patronage of African cinema legend Ousmane Sembène, crafted a bold vision that combines genre entertainment with sharp political commentary on corruption, power, and the marginalized position of women in Cameroonian society.

entries.title: Lexx
entries.creator: Created by Lex Gigeroff, Paul Donovan, and Michael Donovan
entries.pitch:
Lexx is a science fiction television series that originally aired from 1997 to 2002. It was a Canadian-German-British co-production that followed a group of mismatched fugitives aboard the organic spacecraft Lexx — "the most powerful weapon in the two universes."

The series began as four made-for-TV movies in 1997, then continued as a traditional TV series with 61 episodes across 4 seasons. It developed a cult following known for its dark humor, surrealism, and provocative content.

entries.title: Lightspeed Electroid Albegas
entries.creator: Toei Animation
entries.pitch: Lightspeed Electroid Albegas is a 1983-84 Japanese anime series following three high school robotics prodigies who must defend Earth from the Derinja, an alien civilization that has already subjugated most of the galaxy. When their award-winning competition robots are upgraded into combat machines by Professor Mizuki, the three students—Daisaku, Tetsuya, and Hotaru—combine their individual machines into Albegas, a powerful super robot with six different stackable formations. Each formation serves a different combat function, allowing Albegas to adapt to various enemy Mecha-Fighters. The series combines classic super robot action with educational themes about teamwork and innovation, packaged with the characteristic energy and enthusiasm of early 1980s Toei Animation.

entries.title: Lily C.A.T.
entries.creator: Hisayuki Toriumi (Director), Studio Pierrot
entries.pitch:
Lily C.A.T. is a 1987 cosmic horror anime OVA that pays heavy homage to Ridley Scott's Alien and John Carpenter's The Thing. Set in the 23rd century, the story follows the deep-space cruiser Saldes, hired by the Syncam Corporation to shuttle surveyors to investigate a relatively new planet for mining rights. The crew and passengers enter cryogenic hypersleep for the 20-year journey, aging only one month biologically.

When the ship awakens, the crew discovers that two of the surveyors are impostors—and far worse, an extraterrestrial bacterium has been released from collected space debris. This alien pathogen proves capable of mimicking human forms and evolves rapidly, killing crew members by dissolving their bodies while leaving clothes intact. As the infection spreads and the ship's computer is overrun, the survivors must confront not just the alien threat but also the truth about their own identities and the corporation that sent them.

entries.title: Liquid Sky
entries.creator: Slava Tsukerman
entries.pitch: Liquid Sky is a 1982 American independent science fiction film directed by Slava Tsukerman, depicting a darkly surreal alien invasion in the Manhattan new wave scene. When a small flying saucer lands on a penthouse apartment, its alien occupant discovers that humanorgasms produce a high-quality narcotic for their species. Anyone who has sex dies instantly, their bodies dissolving as the alien harvests the resulting endorphins. The film follows Margaret, a bisexual cocaine-addicted model whose lovers keep disappearing, as she becomes an unwitting host to the extraterrestrial. Shot on a shoestring budget of $500,000, the film went on to become the most successful independent film of 1983, grossing $1.7 million worldwide.

entries.title: Little Sun (小太阳 / Xiao Tai Yang)
entries.creator: Wang Minsheng
entries.pitch: Little Sun (1963) is China's first children's science fiction film, produced by the Beijing Science Education Film Studio. The film follows a group of science-loving children who, with the help of scientists, develop a satellite to launch a small artificial sun into the sky, hoping to end a harsh winter and boost food production. The story represents a utopian vision of technological progress and scientific advancement in early 1960s China.

entries.title: Logan's Run
entries.creator: Michael Anderson (Director)
entries.pitch: Logan's Run is a 1976 American science fiction action film set in a future society where citizens live in a sealed geodesic dome city, maintained by a computer that kills everyone at age 30 through a ritual called "Carrousel." The film follows Logan 5, a "Sandman" tasked with hunting down "Runners" who flee the city, until he's given a secret mission to find "Sanctuary" and destroy it. Featuring innovative visual effects and a distinctive dystopian vision, the film won a Special Academy Award for its visual effects and became a cult classic of 1970s science fiction cinema.

entries.title: Lokis
entries.creator: Directed by Janusz Majewski; Based on the novella by Prosper Mérimée
entries.pitch: Lokis is a 1970 Polish folk horror film directed by Janusz Majewski, based on an 1869 novella by Prosper Mérimée. Set in 19th century Lithuania, the film follows Pastor and folklorist Wittembach who travels to a remote countryside to catalog local folk customs. He arrives at the estate of Count Michał Szemiot, a young nobleman who initially cannot meet visitors due to an unspecified ailment. As Wittembach settles into the estate, he begins to notice the Count displaying increasingly strange, animal-like behavior. The local villagers whisper that Michał is a "Lokis"—the half-human offspring of a bear that attacked his mother before his birth. The film builds to a tragic conclusion that blurs the line between folklore and reality, leaving the question of Michał's true nature unresolved.

entries.title: Lone Sloane
entries.creator: Philippe Druillet
entries.pitch: Lone Sloane is a visually stunning French science fiction graphic novel that introduced readers to one of the most iconic characters in European comics. Created by Philippe Druillet, a pioneer of the French sci-fi comics movement, the story first appeared in 1966 in "Le Mystère des Abîmes" (The Mystery of the Abyss). Set 800 years after a catastrophic event called "The Great Fear," the narrative follows Lone Sloane, a space rogue who finds himself caught in an intergalactic struggle between space pirates, gigantic robots, dark gods, and other-dimensional entities after his spaceship is destroyed. The story is notable for its baroque, quasi-expressionist artwork that combines Lovecraftian space nightmares with Escher-inspired mathematically complex worlds, creating a visual language that influenced generations of comic artists worldwide.

entries.title: Long Distance Wireless Photography
entries.creator: Georges Méliès
entries.pitch:
In a glass-roofed workshop, an inventor demonstrates his extraordinary wireless photographic machine to a respectable lady and gentleman. The device projects small images onto a screen at life-size — and those projections briefly come to life. When the inventor photographs the lady client, her projected face makes grotesque faces, including a toothless grin and fierce scowl. The lady faints from shock.

The gentleman fares even worse: his projected portrait reveals him as a hairy, monkey-like creature. Enraged, he tries to destroy the machine, only to receive an electrical shock that makes his hair stand on end. Meanwhile, the lady's outer garments tear away when she stands too near another device, leaving her in her chemise. The clients flee in humiliation while the inventor and his servants laugh uproariously.

This 1908 French trick film from Georges Méliès — the magician who brought us A Trip to the Moon — is both a comedy of errors and a surprisingly sophisticated meditation on the nature of cinema itself.

entries.title: Loss of Sensation
entries.creator: Alexandr Andriyevsky
entries.pitch:
Loss of Sensation (original Russian title: "Gibel Sensatsii" meaning "The Downfall of a Sensation") is a 1935 Soviet science fiction film directed by Alexandr Andriyevsky. Based on the 1929 Ukrainian novel "Iron Riot" by Volodimir Vladko, this early sound film explores themes of technological innovation, worker solidarity, and the dangers of automated weapons. Set in an unnamed country, the film follows engineer Jim Ripple who invents universal robots designed to help workers, only to see his creation weaponized against the very people he sought to help.

The film is notable for its place in Soviet cinema history as an early sci-fi exploration of automation and labor, predating many Western robot films. Though the film uses the abbreviation "R.U.R" for its robots, it is not directly based on Karel Čapek's famous play but rather on Vladko's novel. The story presents a cautionary tale about technological progress serving authoritarian interests rather than worker emancipation.

entries.title: Lost World
entries.creator: Osamu Tezuka
entries.pitch: Lost World is a pioneering science fiction manga created by Osamu Tezuka in 1948, making it one of the earliest examples of Japanese science fiction comics. Part of what is known as Tezuka's early science fiction trilogy (alongside Metropolis and Nextworld), this work predates much of what would later define the genre in manga and anime. The story follows a team of scientists who discover that a mysterious planet named Mamango is approaching Earth—bearing an uncanny resemblance to ancient Earth and inhabited by dinosaurs. What begins as a routine scientific expedition becomes an adventure involving stowaway criminals, ancient creatures, and the mysteries of a planet that broke away from Earth millions of years ago.

entries.title: Luna
entries.creator: Pavel Klushantsev
entries.pitch:
Luna is a Soviet popular science and science fiction film that imagines humanity's first mission to the Moon. Produced in 1965, it represents a fascinating artifact of Cold War-era space optimism, made before the Apollo landings but after the first satellite launches.

The film is in two parts. The first is a documentary-style popular science segment featuring real Soviet scientists discussing current achievements and theories about the Moon - the origin of lunar maria, the temperature of the lunar surface, and the supposed properties of lunar soil. The second part is pure science fiction, showing a hypothetical first lunar mission establishing cities and laboratories on the Moon.

The film won the \"Golden Seal of Trieste\" at the IV International Science-Fiction Film Festival in Italy, 1966.

entries.title: M.D. Geist
entries.creator: Hayato Ikeda (Director), Riku Sanjō (Writer), Production Wave Studio
entries.pitch: M.D. Geist (aka Sōkihei M.D. Geist, "Armoured Demon Soldier M.D. Geist") is a gritty 1986 OVA set on the war-torn planet Jerra. The story follows Geist, a genetically-engineered supersoldier created using "Bioclone theory" - designed to be the ultimate killing machine. Due to his overwhelming ferocity in battle, he was placed in suspended animation and launched into orbit, only to crash back down years later. Now, with the world changed and both the Regular Army and the rebellious Negsrom Army engaged in a doomsday conflict, Geist must stop the "Death Force" - a weapon designed to annihilate all life on the planet. Known for its extreme violence, dark tone, and influence on later cyberpunk and post-apocalyptic anime, M.D. Geist is a cult classic of 80s OVA history.

entries.title: MDK2
entries.creator: BioWare
entries.pitch: MDK2 is a 2000 third-person shooter developed by BioWare (the renowned studio behind Baldur's Gate and Mass Effect) and published by Interplay Entertainment. A sequel to the 1997 game MDK, it tasks players with controlling three distinct characters—Kurt Hectic, Dr. Fluke Hawkins, and Max the genetically engineered robot dog—each with unique abilities and playstyles. The game begins moments after the original MDK's conclusion, as the heroes discover that Earth's alien invasion was not fully defeated. With his signature chain gun, sniper rifle, and infinite parachute, Kurt must once again don his superhero janitor persona to battle alien forces across various environments. The game stands out for its variety: Kurt's run-and-gun gameplay, Dr. Hawkins' puzzle-solving with his inventory combination system, and Max's heavy weapons approach offer three completely different experiences within one game.

entries.title: Mad Max
entries.creator: George Miller
entries.pitch: Mad Max is a landmark 1979 Australian dystopian action film that launched one of cinema's most iconic franchises. Set in a near-future Australia where society is collapsing due to resource depletion and civil unrest, the film follows Max Rockatansky, a weary Main Force Patrol officer who attempts to protect his family and community from the ramping savagery of a vicious biker gang known as the Toecutter's Marauders. Director George Miller, working with a shoestring budget of just $350,000, created a visceral vision of societal breakdown that proved wildly influential, becoming one of the most profitable independent films ever made and establishing the post-apocalyptic action genre that would dominate cinema for decades.

entries.title: Man Divided
entries.creator: Unknown
entries.pitch: In 2095, the world has been devastated by ecological collapse—oceans have risen and all natural freshwater has vanished. Scientist Fang Rung undergoes molecular fission, splitting himself into two consciousnesses: his present self and his past self, code-named Gordon Thomas, who is sent back to 2017. Gordon must find scientist Mona Lindkvist, whose groundbreaking research was lost before it could save the world. When Fang Rung loses contact with Gordon, the clock begins to tick.

entries.title: Man Facing Southeast
entries.creator: Eliseo Subiela (Director)
entries.pitch:
Man Facing Southeast (Hombre mirando al sudeste) is a 1986 Argentine science fiction drama that stands as one of Latin America's most thought-provoking entries into the genre. Written and directed by Eliseo Subiela, the film tells the story of Dr. Julio Denis, a psychiatrist at a Buenos Aires mental hospital who encounters a mysterious patient named Rantés—who claims to be an extraterrestrial being from another planet.

The film received wide acclaim upon its video release and was selected as Argentina's entry for Best Foreign Language Film at the 60th Academy Awards. Remarkably, it served as the uncredited inspiration for the 2001 American film K-PAX, which led to a plagiarism lawsuit. The film reached #10 in a survey of the 100 greatest films of Argentine cinema, with later surveys confirming its enduring critical reputation.

What makes Man Facing Southeast remarkable is its delicate balance between science fiction and psychological drama. The film never definitively answers whether Rantés is truly an alien or simply a delusional patient—leaving both the protagonist and the audience in a state of beautiful uncertainty. This ambiguity, combined with Subiela's poetic direction and Pedro Aznar's haunting score, creates an experience that lingers long after the credits roll.

entries.title: Man in Outer Space
entries.creator: Oldřich Lipský
entries.pitch:
A 1962 Czechoslovak science fiction comedy about an upholsterer who accidentally launches himself 600 years into the future. Josef, a simple craftsman working on the first Czech spacecraft, makes final adjustments to the rocket but accidentally triggers the launch. He flies to the planet Blue Star, where he meets an alien named Adam who accompanies him back to Earth — only to discover that 600 years have passed. Josef finds himself institutionalized in a psychiatric hospital, but with Adam's help (who is invisible to Earthlings), he escapes and attempts to return to his own time.

The film blends absurdist comedy with genuine satirical commentary on mid-20th century Czechoslovak society.

entries.title: Manhunt of Mystery Island
entries.creator: Spencer Gordon Bennet, Yakima Canutt, Wallace Grissell
entries.pitch:
Manhunt of Mystery Island is a 1945 Republic Pictures science fiction serial film that represents the dying gasp of the Golden Age of Movie Serials. Released in March 1945, it was the first of only two 15-chapter serials released that year—World War II had ended and the format's days were numbered. The serial follows private detective Lance Reardon and Claire Forrest as they journey to mysterious Pacific island Mystery Island to rescue Claire's father, Professor William Forrest, who has been kidnapped and forced to work on his revolutionary "radiatomic power transmitter" by the evil Captain Mephisto—a reincarnated pirate who uses a Transformation Machine to take on the appearance of his long-dead ancestor.

What makes Manhunt of Mystery Island notable is its surprisingly inventive plot for a Saturday afternoon chapterplay. The Transformation Machine, which rearranges blood corpuscles to physically transform its user into a molecular duplicate of Captain Mephisto, provides genuinely inventive pseudo-science that elevates the serial above typical Republic fare. Combined with excellent location work at Laguna Beach and the Lewis Mansion in Beverly Hills, the serial creates an atmosphere that critics have called surprisingly effective.

The serial features Roy Barcroft in what he considered his finest role—as both the suspicious mansion owner Higgins and the flamboyantly costumed Captain Mephisto. His performance dominates the serial, bringing a charismatic evil that makes the show memorable despite lead actor Richard Bailey's notably flat delivery. Meanwhile, Linda Stirling proves why she was one of the era's most celebrated serial heroines, rescuing the hero more than once and demonstrating genuine chemistry with her co-star.

entries.title: Manhunter: New York
entries.creator: Dave Murry, Barry Murry (Sierra On-Line)
entries.pitch: Set in 2004, Manhunter: New York drops players into a devastated New York City two years after an alien invasion by the mysterious Orb Alliance. These floating eyeball-like beings have conquered Earth, forcing surviving humans to wear brown monk robes, prohibiting speech under penalty of death, and implanting tracking chips in everyone. You play as a newly recruited Manhunter—a human collaborator tasked with using the Orbs' own surveillance technology to track down "criminals" and "insurgents." But as you investigate a series of murders, you discover a darker truth: the Orbs are using humans as a food source, harvesting bodies to feed their young. The game spans four days as you gradually realize your targets are actually members of an underground resistance, and ultimately choose to switch sides and fight back.

entries.title: Marooned!
entries.creator: Steve Hartford (Saguaro Software)
entries.pitch: Marooned! is a text-graphical adventure game released in 1985 for the TRS-80 Color Computer (CoCo), an 8-bit home computer manufactured by Radio Shack. Developed by Steve Hartford and published by Saguaro Software, the game places players in the role of an ordinary person who witnesses a UFO landing in their corn field. What begins as curiosity quickly transforms into a fight for survival as the player is abducted by extraterrestrials and left on a mysterious alien world. The player must explore the alien environment, collect items, solve puzzles, and find a way to escape back to Earth.

entries.title: Maska
entries.creator: Brothers Quay
entries.pitch:
A 23-minute animated short film based on Stanisław Lem's 1974 short story, directed by the acclaimed Brothers Quay. Set in a quasi-feudal world, the film follows a beautiful woman who is actually an insectoid robot — a \"hound machine\" — programmed both to love and to assassinate her target, a dissident wise man named Arrhodes.

The film explores the paradox of programmed love: can a machine designed to kill also learn to truly love? The Brothers Quay render the robot in both her forms — the beautiful girl and the mantis-like steel monster — while the surrounding human world appears rotten and decaying. The result is a haunting meditation on consciousness, identity, and what it means to be human.

entries.title: Master of the World
entries.creator: Harry Piel
entries.pitch: Master of the World is a pioneering German science fiction film from 1934, directed by Harry Piel. Set in a near-future industrial world, the film explores the ethical implications of robotic automation and the terrifying potential of AI-powered weapons. When visionary industrialist Dr. Erich Heller develops "machine men" (robots) to replace dangerous human labor in mines, his most trusted scientist, Professor Wolf, secretly pursues his own agenda: creating a "super robot" capable of achieving world domination. The film was ahead of its time in addressing themes of technological unemployment, the misuse of artificial intelligence, and the conflict between humanistic innovation and megalomaniacal ambition.

entries.title: Matango
entries.creator: Ishirō Honda
entries.pitch:
Matango is a 1963 Japanese horror film that stands apart from director Ishirō Honda's famous kaiju work. When a group of day-trippers aboard a yacht become stranded on a mysterious island after a storm, they discover an eerie landscape filled with unusually large mushrooms—and the rotting wreckage of a ship whose crew vanished under strange circumstances.

As food supplies dwindle, the castaways face a desperate choice: eat the mysterious mushrooms and risk unknown consequences, or starve. What begins as a survival story gradually transforms into a haunting meditation on humanity, identity, and the thin line between human and monster. With its dark tone and bleak atmosphere, Matango is unlike any other Toho film of the era—and was nearly banned in Japan upon release.

entries.title: Mavlin: Vesmírný únik
entries.creator: Mael Software Group
entries.pitch: Mavlin: Vesmírný únik (Mavlin: The Space Escape) is a Czech point-and-click sci-fi adventure game released in 1994 for MS-DOS. The player assumes the role of Mavlin Malner, an ordinary Earthling who is mistakenly kidnapped by an alien in a flying saucer and taken to the planet of the moguns—alien creatures resembling pink dragons of slightly humanoid shape. Upon discovering the kidnapping was a mistake (the alien was actually after someone named Gagif Kolkol), the mogun sees no reason to return Mavlin to Earth, leaving our protagonist stranded on an alien world.
