The player must guide Mavlin through various puzzles and interactions to find his way back home.

entries.title: Max Payne
entries.creator: Remedy Entertainment
entries.pitch: Max Payne is a neo-noir third-person shooter that tells the story of Max Payne, a New York City police detective turned vigilante after his wife and infant daughter are brutally murdered. Developed by Finnish studio Remedy Entertainment and released in 2001, the game pioneered the use of "bullet time" mechanics in action sequences—slowing down time to allow for dramatic gunfights. The game is notable for its distinctive comic-book style cutscenes, its film noir narrative voice, and its deeply personal story of grief, revenge, and descent into darkness.

entries.title: Maya Manithan
entries.creator: T. P. Sundaram
entries.pitch: Maya Manithan (transl. "Magical Man") is a 1958 Tamil-language science fiction film produced and directed by T. P. Sundaram under the Southern Movies banner. One of the earliest Indian films exploring sci-fi themes, it follows a scientist who develops a serum capable of rendering the user invisible. The film stars Sriram alongside prominent supporting actors including S. A. Ashokan, Chandrakantha, and Vanaja. Released on November 7, 1958, the film represents an early experiment in Indian cinema with science fiction narratives, predating many of the genre's more famous Bollywood contributions.

entries.title: Meatball Machine
entries.creator: Jun'ichi Yamamoto
entries.pitch:
Yōji is a lonely factory worker who falls for Sachiko, a co-worker he's too shy to approach. After witnessing her being attacked and coming to her aid — only to get beaten himself — Sachiko accompanies him back to his apartment. But that night, an alien insect she encountered penetrates her body and transforms her into a NecroBorg: a bio-mechanical monster born from human flesh.

These parasitic alien creatures take over human hosts and weaponize their bodies to battle each other. Yōji soon becomes infected too, and the two would-be lovers are forced into a fight to the death. A parallel subplot follows a father hunting the NecroBorgs that infected his daughter.

Based on Jun'ichi Yamamoto's 1999 70-minute film, this 2005 remake features notorious special effects artist Yoshihiro Nishimura (The Machine Girl, Tokyo Gore Police). Critics note obvious parallels to Shinya Tsukamoto's Tetsuo: The Iron Man, though some argue Meatball Machine surpasses its inspiration.

entries.title: Meatball Machine
entries.creator: Yūdai Yamaguchi, Jun'ichi Yamamoto
entries.pitch:
A lonely factory worker discovers an alien parasite that transforms his crush into a bio-mechanical monster — and soon discovers he harbors the same creature inside him. In this extreme Japanese body horror film, parasitic alien organisms take over human bodies, converting flesh into deadly weapons for brutal turf wars between NecroBorgs.

Meatball Machine is a gorier, more visceral cousin to Tsukamoto's Tetsuo: The Iron Man, directed by Yūdai Yamaguchi (Tokyo Gore Police) with special effects by Yoshihiro Nishimura (The Machine Girl). The film serves up over-the-top practical effects, splatter violence, and a surprisingly sweet undercurrent about two isolated people who can finally connect — after becoming monsters.

The 70-minute version was originally released in 1999, then re-edited into a 90-minute theatrical cut in 2005. Both versions deliver the same wild premise: alien parasites invade Earth, take human hosts, and turn them into weapon-wielding killing machines. But it's the human drama beneath all the gore that elevates this beyond mere splatter flick.

entries.title: Megazone 23
entries.creator: Noboru Ishiguro (Director), Hiroyuki Hoshiyama (Writer)
entries.pitch: In the far future, humanity fled a dying Earth aboard massive colony ships called Megazones. On Megazone 23—a vast city-ship designed to replicate 1985 Tokyo—its inhabitants have lived for centuries without knowing they're space travelers, their memories erased by a benevolent AI called Eve. When rebellious youth Shougo Yahagi stumbles upon a government prototype motorcycle, he accidentally uncovers the truth about his world and awakens Eve from her digital slumber. What follows is a mind-bending journey through simulated realities, government conspiracies, and a war against an enemy race called the Dezalg that has raged for centuries. This pioneering cyberpunk OVA predates The Matrix by over a decade, exploring themes of simulated reality, identity, and the nature of humanity itself.

entries.title: Messiah
entries.creator: Shiny Entertainment
entries.pitch: Messiah is a third-person action game set in a futuristic cyberpunk city where you play as Bob, a cherub sent by God to stop Satan from taking over the world. Developed by Shiny Entertainment and published by Virgin Interactive in 2000, the game stands out for its unique possession mechanic—Bob must take over the bodies of civilians, criminals, and soldiers to navigate the city and complete his divine mission. The darkly humorous premiseparodies religious themes while delivering a surprisingly deep stealth and action experience. The game was in development for over four years and features an advanced engine with real-time LOD adjustment based on hardware capabilities.

entries.title: Metal Fatigue
entries.creator: Zono
entries.pitch: Metal Fatigue is a 2000 real-time strategy game set in the 23rd century where humanity has discovered faster-than-light travel and expanded across the galaxy. Three megacorporations called CorpoNations—RimTech, Mil-Agro, and Neuropa—compete for alien technology on the planet Hedoth Prime. Players build bases, recruit units, and command customizable robots called "combots" across three battlefield layers: surface, orbital, and underground. The game's unique hook is the modular robot customization system, where players can salvage enemy robot parts mid-battle to upgrade their own machines.

entries.title: Metal Gear Solid
entries.creator: Hideo Kojima
entries.pitch: Metal Gear Solid is a stealth action game that pioneered the stealth game genre. Solid Snake, a special forces operative, is sent to the forests of Alaska to infiltrate a nuclear weapons facility and neutralize the threat of Metal Gear - a bipedal walking tank capable of launching nuclear missiles. The game features groundbreaking cinematic storytelling, complex characters, and explores themes of nuclear deterrence, genetics, and the nature of soldiers.

entries.title: Meteo
entries.creator: András Mész
entries.pitch:
Meteo is a 1989 Hungarian science-fiction art film that occupies a unique space between dystopian allegory and surrealist fever dream. Directed by András Mész, the film follows Eckermann (László Kistamás), a listless computer genius who spends most of his time lounging in a bathtub holding imaginary conversations with cartoon characters — manifestations of his fractured mind.

The film unfolds in a bleak, industrial Budapest: factories spew smoke, underground tunnels snake through the city like veins, and the line between human consciousness and machine logic has completely blurred. When a gang of criminals recruits Eckermann to help them rob a gambling joint, he constructs an elaborate scheme — then retreats immediately back to his bathtub. Something is clearly wrong with the world, and with Eckermann in particular: the "Meteo" of the title refers to both a weather system and a mysterious signal that seems to be affecting human behavior.

Meteo is not an easy film — it's cryptic, visually oppressive, and deliberately disorienting. But for those who appreciate Hungarian cinema's gift for combining social critique with existential dread, it offers a haunting portrait of a society losing its grip on reality.

entries.title: Meteo
entries.creator: György Fehér
entries.pitch:
In the strange, contemplative world of Meteo, protagonist Eckermann is a brilliant but profoundly alienated computer programmer who has retreated from reality into the sanctuary of his bathtub. There, submerged in lukewarm water, he holds elaborate imaginary conversations with cartoon characters — whimsical companions far more beloved by children than by the adults who once enjoyed them. His days blur into nights of surreal reverie, until his friends approach him with an unusual request: they need his technical skills to execute a heist at a local gambling establishment.

What follows is a fever-dream of shifting perspectives and nonlinear narrative, as the boundary between Eckermann's tub-bound fantasies and the waking world grows increasingly porous. Director György Fehér creates a haunting meditation on loneliness, creativity, and the escape routes we construct when the real world becomes unbearable.

entries.title: Metropolis
entries.creator: Fritz Lang
entries.pitch: Metropolis is a pioneering German silent science-fiction film set in a futuristic urban dystopia where a great gulf separates the wealthy industrialists who rule from the underground-dwelling workers who toil to operate the massive machines that power the city. Directed by Fritz Lang and written by Thea von Harbou, the film is renowned for its groundbreaking visual effects, elaborate Art Deco sets, and powerful social commentary on the divide between capital and labor. The story follows Freder, the privileged son of the city's master, who becomes fascinated with Maria, a spiritual leader among the workers, and seeks to bridge the gap between the ruling class and the oppressed laborers.

entries.title: Metropolis
entries.creator: Motoichi Hagihara
entries.pitch: [2-4 paragraph overview. No major spoilers.]

entries.title: Metropolis
entries.creator: Rintaro (Director), Katsuhiro Otomo (Screenplay), Osamu Tezuka (Original Manga)
entries.pitch: In the wealthy plutocratic city of Metropolis, humans co-exist with robot laborers designed to build and maintain the city. However, its impoverished human citizens discriminate against robots, blaming them for their unemployment and being forced to live in the squalid lower levels of Metropolis. When a Japanese detective and his nephew arrive chasing a rogue scientist, they stumble upon Tima, an advanced android created by the city's wealthiest citizen, Duke Red—intended as the control unit for a nuclear superweapon. The young Kenichi forms a bond with Tima, unaware she is a robot, while forces both human and mechanical close in around them in this stunning cyberpunk adaptation of Tezuka's 1949 manga, loosely inspired by Fritz Lang's 1927 silent classic.

entries.title: Mickey 17
entries.creator: Bong Joon Ho (Director), Edward Ashton (Novel)
entries.pitch: Mickey 17 is a 2025 science fiction black comedy directed by Bong Joon Ho, based on the 2022 novel Mickey7 by Edward Ashton. The film stars Robert Pattinson in the title role as an "Expendable"—a disposable worker on a space colony mission who is cloned every time he dies, with his memories restored through a process called "reprinting." Set in 2054, the film follows Mickey Barnes and his friend Timo as they escape Earth to join a colony voyage to the ice planet Niflheim. The film explores themes of identity, humanity's treatment of disposable labor, and what it means to be a person when you can be endlessly replicated.

entries.title: Microcosmic God
entries.pitch:
A reclusive biochemist named Kidder lives in isolation on an island, yet produces revolutionary inventions that transform human civilization. The twist? Kidder isn't truly innovative—he simply takes others' ideas and improves them. Frustrated with the slow pace of human progress, he creates something extraordinary: a colony of tiny, synthetic intelligent beings called "Neoterics" who live at an accelerated pace, evolving through many generations in a short time. Through controlled competition among these microscopic beings, Kidder receives the innovations humanity desperately needs. But when corporate interests try to exploit his creations, Kidder must decide how far he's willing to go to protect his god-like responsibility to his microscopic world.

This is Sturgeon at his philosophical best—exploring the relationship between creator and creation, the ethics of playing god, and what happens when innovation becomes a form of divine intervention.

entries.title: Mighty Space Miners
entries.creator: Umanosuke Iida (Director), Triangle Staff (Studio)
entries.pitch: Mighty Space Miners is a hard science fiction original video animation (OVA) released in 1994-1995, set in the 2060s on a mining colony carved into the captured asteroid 4179 Toutatis. The series follows 12-year-old Nanbu Ushiwaka, the oldest child ever born in space, as he attempts to pass a practical piloting examination. During an operation to capture Halley's Comet, a derelict military satellite malfunctions and launches a nuclear missile, triggering catastrophic failures throughout the habitat. The survivors must struggle to cope as authorities delay rescue, making this a tense survival drama about humanity's first generation born entirely off-Earth facing an existential crisis.

entries.title: Millennium Actress
entries.creator: Satoshi Kon (Director), Sadayuki Murai (Screenplay)
entries.pitch: Millennium Actress is a mind-bending animated masterpiece that tells the story of Chiyoko Fujiwara, a legendary Japanese actress who retired suddenly thirty years ago. When a young documentary filmmaker arrives at her home to interview her, he presents her with an old key—and Chiyoko's memories of her life, career, and one great love begin to blur with the films she starred in. As she recounts her decades-spanning journey, the line between reality and cinema dissolves completely, creating a transcendent meditation on memory, time, and the nature of love itself.

entries.title: Mind Game
entries.creator: Masaaki Yuasa (Director), Robin Nishi (Original Manga)
entries.pitch: Mind Game is a 2004 Japanese adult-animated experimental comedy-drama that tells the story of Nishi, a 20-year-old aspiring manga artist from Osaka who reunites with his childhood crush Myon. What begins as an awkward dinner at her family's yakitori restaurant takes a dark turn when yakuza storm in seeking revenge. After a violent encounter leaves Nishi dead, he finds himself in a surreal limbo where he meets God—a being whose form shifts constantly—who gives him a chance to return to life. The film then transforms into a fantastical survival story as Nishi, Myon, and her sister Yan escape inside the belly of an enormous whale, where they forge an unexpected community. Visually stunning and tonally unpredictable, the film weaves through wildly different animation styles as it tells one continuous story of embracing life against impossible odds.

entries.title: MindGamers
entries.creator: Andrew Goth (Director)
entries.pitch: MindGamers is a 2015 Austrian science fiction film about a group of students who create a wireless neural network enabling collective consciousness through a quantum computer. They discover that motor skills can be transferred through quantum theory and freely spread their technology, believing it's a step toward intellectual freedom. However, they soon realize they're part of a larger, more sinister experiment. The film explores themes of consciousness, technology, and the potential dangers of unbound scientific progress.

entries.title: Moebius
entries.creator: Gustavo Mosquera (Director)
entries.pitch: Moebius is a 1996 Argentine science fiction film directed by Gustavo Mosquera, based on the classic 1950 short story "A Subway Named Mobius" by Armin Joseph Deutsch. Set in a dystopian Buenos Aires, the film follows the mysterious disappearance of a subway train—along with its passengers—deep within the network's tunnels. When officials cannot locate the train despite an exhaustive search, a young topologist named Daniel Pratt is brought in to investigate. What follows is a mind-bending journey through the Buenos Aires Underground as Pratt develops a theory that the train has slipped into another dimension due to the network's topology forming a Möbius strip. The film is notable for being one of the most ambitious Argentine sci-fi productions of the 1990s, made with a modest budget of $250,000, and for its clever adaptation of a mathematical concept into cinematic language.

entries.title: Monster from the Ocean Floor
entries.creator: Wyott Ordung
entries.pitch: A 1954 American science fiction monster film that marks the directorial debut of Wyott Ordung and the first film produced by a young Roger Corman. The story follows Julie Blair, an American artist vacationing at a seaside village in Mexico, who investigates rumors of a man-eating sea monster dwelling in the cove. She teams up with skeptical marine biologist Steve Dunning, and together they discover a giant amoeba terrorizing the coastline. With limited resources but plenty of determination, Julie obtains a tissue sample from the creature, leading to an underwater battle in a one-man submarine.

entries.title: Morel's Invention
entries.creator: Luigi Cozzi
entries.pitch:
Based on the celebrated novel by Adolfo Bioy Casares, this Italian adaptation transposes the existential sci-fi puzzle to a remote island where a fugitive from the law discovers a group of seemingly immortal tourists. The film blends existential drama with speculative science, exploring themes of identity, perception, and the nature of reality itself. Director Luigi Cozzi creates an atmosphere of mounting paranoia as the protagonist realizes that none of the visitors seem to notice his presence—and that they may not be entirely real.

The story follows a Venezuelan political fugitive who has hidden himself on a deserted island in Polynesia. When a group of sophisticated visitors arrives, he is drawn to one of them—a mysterious woman named Faustine. But as he attempts to interact with the group, he realizes with horror that they do not acknowledge his existence at all. Their conversations repeat identically each week, and the protagonist begins to question his own sanity. What follows is a mind-bending investigation into the nature of these visitors and the machine that powers their impossible existence.

The film is notable for its low-budget but inventive approach to visualizing abstract philosophical concepts. Rather than relying on special effects, Cozzi uses practical techniques—split screens, reversed footage, and superimposition—to convey the overlapping realities at the heart of Bioy Casares' novel. The result is a cerebral puzzle-box of a film that rewards patient viewers with its layered exploration of what it means to be observed—and to observe—in a universe where reality may be nothing more than a recording.

entries.title: Morgiana
entries.creator: Juraj Herz
entries.pitch: Morgiana is a visually stunning 1972 Czechoslovak Gothic drama based on Alexander Grin's novel "Jessie and Morgiana." The film tells the story of two sisters, Klára and Viktoria, who inherit different portions of their wealthy father's estate. When Klára receives the majority of the inheritance including the family castle, Viktoria's jealousy transforms into obsessive hatred. Using a mysterious gypsy fortuneteller's help, Viktoria begins slowly poisoning her sister with an undetectable toxin. The film is renowned for its spectacular cinematography, elaborate costume design, and Iva Janžurová's remarkable dual performance as both sisters.

entries.title: Morning Patrol
entries.creator: Nikos Nikolaidis (Director)
entries.pitch:
Morning Patrol (Πρωινή Περίπολος, Proini Peripolos) is a 1987 Greek art film that stands as one of the most distinctive examples of European post-apocalyptic science fiction. Directed by Nikos Nikolaidis, the film introduces viewers to a haunting, dreamlike vision of a destroyed city where a lone woman wanders through abandoned streets, searching for meaning in the ruins of civilization. The film's dialogue incorporates excerpts from works by Daphne du Maurier, Philip K. Dick, Raymond Chandler, and Herman Raucher, creating a unique literary collage that elevates the narrative beyond conventional genre boundaries.

The film received the Best Director Award and the Greek National Ministry of Culture Award at the Thessaloniki Festival of Greek Cinema in 1987, and was subsequently selected for screening at Fantasporto and the Avoriaz Fantastic Film Festival. With its slow, atmospheric pacing and emphasis on mood over plot, Morning Patrol has been compared to a "slower, more elegiac Blade Runner" — a poetic meditation on memory, loss, and the blurred boundaries between life and death in a post-apocalyptic world.

entries.title: Motorman
entries.creator: David Ohle
entries.pitch:
Motorman is a surrealist dystopian novella published in 1972 that went out of print for nearly half a century before being rediscovered as a cult classic. The story follows Moldenke, a man living in a post-apocalyptic future where he exists with four implanted sheep's hearts, one working lung, and a body kept alive through crude surgical modifications. The world itself is equally fractured—multiple artificial suns and moons govern a society where weather is manufactured, jelly-headed humanoids walk the streets, and an omnipresent surveillance system led by the enigmatic Mr. Bunce monitors everyone's movements.

The narrative unfolds through fragmented letters, questionnaires, and episodic encounters as Moldenke attempts to escape Bunce's control and find Dr. Burnheart, the surgeon who implanted his animal hearts. The novel is written in a dreamlike, stream-of-consciousness style that defies conventional plotting, instead immersing readers in a world that operates on its own bizarre logic—where wars are "mock" engagements where soldiers volunteer for injuries, and where the distinction between reality and manufactured illusion has completely collapsed.

entries.title: Mr. India
entries.creator: Shekhar Kapur (Director)
entries.pitch: Mr. India is a 1987 Hindi-language science fiction superhero film directed by Shekhar Kapur and produced by Boney Kapoor. The film stars Anil Kapoor as Arun Verma, a humble violinist and philanthropist who inherits a revolutionary cloaking device created by his late scientist father. When Arun discovers that the device can make its user invisible, he uses it to fight the evil criminal Mogambo, who plans to conquer India. The film also stars Sridevi as Seema Sahni, a journalist who becomes Arun's love interest, and Amrish Puri as the memorable villain Mogambo. Released on May 29, 1987, Mr. India became a major commercial success and is now regarded as a landmark in Indian cinema for introducing the superhero genre to Bollywood.

entries.title: Mr. X
entries.creator: Vikram Bhatt
entries.pitch:
In 2015 Bollywood, Emraan Hashmi stars as Raghuram Rathod, an ATS officer whose life shatters when he's framed for murder and left for dead. But a radical experiment with an untested radiation treatment gives him something extraordinary—the ability to become invisible. 

Mr. X is a science-fiction action film that trades in the familiar Bollywood trope of the wronged man seeking justice, but wraps it in a genuinely novel premise: what happens when the law itself becomes visible? When you can walk through walls, observe secrets, and strike without being seen?

The film plays with themes of surveillance and power—Raghu can now see what others cannot, becoming both subject and object of the watcher's gaze. Director Vikram Bhatt delivers genuinely atmospheric visuals, especially in how the film handles Raghu's invisibility, visible only in certain light.

entries.title: Mr. X in Bombay
entries.creator: Shantilal Soni (Director)
entries.pitch:
Mr. X in Bombay is a 1964 Indian science fiction romantic comedy film directed by Shantilal Soni and starring legendary singer-actor Kishore Kumar, along with Kumkum and Madan Puri. Set in contemporary Bombay (Mumbai), the film combines elements of science fiction—invisibility through a mysterious potion—with traditional Bollywood romance and comedy tropes. The story follows a scientist whose experimental potion accidentally makes a poet invisible, leading to a series of comedic and dramatic complications involving blackmail, ghostly hauntings, and romantic misunderstandings. While the science fiction premise is relatively simple compared to Western sci-fi of the era, the film represents an early example of Indian cinema experimenting with the genre, blending it with the popular romantic comedy format that dominated Bollywood during this period.

The film's significance lies in its status as one of the earliest Indian science fiction films, predating the more famous Koi Mil Gaya by nearly four decades. It demonstrates how Indian filmmakers adapted Western science fiction concepts while maintaining the song-and-dance romantic comedy structure that audiences expected. The movie is perhaps best remembered today for the iconic song "Mere Mehboob Qayamat Hogi," sung by Kishore Kumar, which became an evergreen hit and remains popular decades later.

entries.title: Mutant Action
entries.creator: Álex de la Iglesia
entries.pitch: Mutant Action is a 1993 Spanish-French science fiction black comedy directed by Álex de la Iglesia. Set in a post-apocalyptic future where good-looking people rule society, the film follows a incompetent terrorist group of disabled "mutants" who wage a violent campaign against superficial beauty standards. Led by Ramón Yarritu, the group stages increasingly chaotic attacks—including assassinating bodybuilders, bombing a sperm bank, and crashing an aerobics class on live television—before attempting their most ambitious operation: kidnapping a wealthy heiress during her wedding.

entries.title: My 20th Century
entries.creator: Ildikó Enyedi
entries.pitch:
In Budapest 1880, twin sisters are born at the exact moment Thomas Edison presents his electric lightbulb to the world. Separated at birth, they walk divergent paths—one becomes a naïve idealistic anarchist with a bomb, the other a pampered hedonistic courtesan. Their paths collide in a whimsical tale of synchronicity across the turn of the century.

Ildikó Enyedi's debut feature is a black-and-white meditation on modernity, electricity, and the birth of the 20th century. Winner of the Golden Camera at Cannes 1989, it's been called one of the great debut films in cinema history—formally daring, visually inventive, and thematically complex.

The film treats science as a source of wonder and magic, examining the twin origins of modernity and cinema, both born of electricity.

entries.title: My Beautiful Girl, Mari
entries.creator: Lee Sung-gang (Director)
entries.pitch: My Beautiful Girl, Mari is a 2002 South Korean animated film that follows Kim Nam-woo, a young boy struggling through life as the people around him constantly leave. His best friend Jun-ho is going to study in Seoul, and his widowed mother is paying more attention to her new boyfriend. To escape his loneliness, Nam-woo retreats into a dream world where he meets a mysterious girl named Mari. The film blends surrealistic fantasy with a sensitive coming-of-age narrative, exploring themes of loss, maturation, and the blurred boundary between dreams and reality. It was South Korea's first feature-length animated film to gain international attention and won the Grand Prix at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival.

entries.title: My Grandpa is an Alien
entries.creator: Various
entries.pitch:
My Grandpa is an Alien (Moj dida je pao s Marsa) is a 2019 Croatian family science fantasy film about a young girl named Una who embarks on a frantic 24-hour adventure to rescue her grandfather after he is kidnapped by aliens. Partnered with an alien robot, Una must navigate an extraordinary journey that leads to friendship, emotional growth, and the discovery that family transcends planetary boundaries.

This heartwarming tale combines elements of science fiction with universal family themes, creating an accessible story about love, sacrifice, and the bonds that connect us across the cosmos. The film represents a rare Croatian entry in the family sci-fi genre.

entries.title: Mysterious Island
entries.creator: Eduard Pentslin
entries.pitch: Mysterious Island is a 1941 Soviet film adaptation of Jules Verne's 1874 novel "The Mysterious Island." Set during the American Civil War, the film follows five Union prisoners of war who escape by hijacking a balloon and crash-land on a mysterious volcanic island in the South Pacific. The film was produced by Odessa Film Studio and represents an interesting Soviet interpretation of classic Western adventure literature, transformed through the lens of Soviet filmmaking conventions.

entries.title: Mézga Aladár különös kalandjai
entries.creator: Mihály Kormos
entries.topics: Space Travel, Exploration, Aliens, Friendship, Children
entries.pitch:
A Hungarian children's sci-fi television series from 1972 about a young boy named Aladár Mézga who embarks on nightly adventures to different inhabited planets across the universe. Each night, Aladár and his talking dog Blöki travel in an inflatable cosmic spaceship, visiting strange new worlds populated with bizarre alien civilizations. The show combines humor, imagination, and gentle educational content as the duo encounter various alien cultures and face playful challenges.

The series represents a charming piece of 1970s Eastern Bloc children's programming, offering a whimsical take on space exploration that predates many better-known Western sci-fi shows for children. Its optimistic tone and imaginative premise make it a unique time capsule of Cold War-era children's entertainment.

entries.title: Naalai Manithan
entries.creator: Velu Prabhakaran
entries.pitch: Naalai Manithan (translated as "The Man of Tomorrow") is a 1989 Tamil-language science fiction horror film that represents a fascinating outlier in Indian cinema. Directed by Velu Prabhakaran in his directorial debut, the film stars Prabhu, Amala, and Ajay Rathnam in a story that combines elements of medical science fiction with zombie horror. Set in 2008 Chennai, the film follows Dr. Shankar, a scientist who develops a revolutionary drug capable of bringing the dead back to life if administered within two hours of death. However, the drug has a terrifying side effect: the resurrected subject becomes immortal but also murderous, leading to a bloody rampage across the city. The film was a remake of the American film Silent Rage (1982) and spawned a sequel, Adhisaya Manithan, released in 1990. While not a major commercial success, Naalai Manithan stands as an early example of Tamil cinema's foray into sci-fi horror territory.

entries.title: Naan Vanangum Deivam
entries.creator: K. Somu (Director), C. T. Chettiyar (Producer)
entries.pitch:
Naan Vanangum Deivam (transl. "The Deity Which I Worship") is a 1963 Tamil science fiction film that stands as one of the earliest Indian adaptations of Mary Shelley's Frankenstein. Directed by K. Somu and produced by C. T. Chettiyar, the film stars the legendary Sivaji Ganesan in a dual role, supported by acclaimed actresses Padmini and Ragini. 

The film reimagines the Frankenstein narrative within a Tamil cultural context, exploring themes of scientific hubris, creation, and the moral consequences of playing god. Rather than a direct translation of Shelley's novel, the adaptation weaves traditional Indian values and social dynamics into the familiar tale of a scientist who attempts to create life. The film's significance lies in its pioneering approach to bringing Western science fiction themes into Tamil cinema during an era when the genre was virtually nonexistent in Indian filmmaking.

entries.title: Nabi
entries.creator: Moon Seung-wook
entries.pitch:
In a near-future Korea plagued by acid rain, lead poisoning, and a mysterious \"oblivion virus\" that causes memory loss, a tourist industry has emerged: travelers from around the world pay to be deliberately infected with the virus, hoping to erase painful memories from their past. This is the premise of Nabi (Butterfly), a 2001 South Korean science fiction feature that flew under the radar of most international audiences.

The film follows Anna Kim, a German woman of Korean descent who arrives in the city seeking the oblivion virus to forget the trauma of a recent abortion. She is assigned Yuki, a seven-months-pregnant virus guide who needs money to support her unborn child, and K, a new driver who secretly hopes that one of his passengers will recognize him from an old photograph—though he has no memory of his own past. As the three navigate the city's toxic landscape, bonds form between them, leading to a devastating climax at the edge of the sea.

Shot on a shoestring budget of $380,000 and transferred from digital video to 35mm, Nabi is a visual meditation on memory, loss, and the weight of what we choose to forget.

entries.title: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind
entries.creator: Hayao Miyazaki (Director), Isao Takahata (Producer), Joe Hisaishi (Composer)
entries.pitch:
Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind is a 1984 Japanese animated post-apocalyptic adventure film directed by Hayao Miyazaki. Set in a distant future where industrial civilization has collapsed and most of the world is covered by a toxic jungle called the Sea of Corruption, the film follows Princess Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind as she navigates a world ravaged by environmental catastrophe, warring kingdoms, and giant mutant insects.

The film was produced by Topcraft (the studio that would later become Studio Ghibli) and distributed by Toei Company. It was released in Japan on March 11, 1984, and became a critical and commercial success, grossing $14.3 million against a budget of ¥180 million. The film is widely regarded as one of the greatest animated films ever made, ranking highly in polls conducted by Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs. Its success directly led to the founding of Studio Ghibli in 1985.

entries.title: Near Dark
entries.creator: Kathryn Bigelow (Director), Eric Red (Writer)
entries.pitch: A young Oklahoma man meets a mysterious drifter named Mae, only to discover she's a vampire who turns him into one of the undead. Forced to join a nomadic family of bloodthirsty vampires traveling across the American Southwest, he must navigate his new existence while trying to find a cure before he loses his humanity forever. This neo-Western vampire tale mixes the grit of biker films with the loneliness of frontier mythology, creating a haunting meditation on addiction, family, and what it means to truly live.

entries.title: Neo Tokyo
entries.creator: Directed by Rintaro, Yoshiaki Kawajiri, and Katsuhiro Otomo
entries.pitch: Neo Tokyo (also known as Manie-Manie) is a groundbreaking 1987 Japanese anthology anime film featuring three visionary science fiction stories, each directed by a different master of the medium. The film opens with a girl and her cat discovering a mysterious clock that serves as a gateway to a surreal theater where they watch three tales unfold. Rintaro's opening segment explores the labyrinth of a child's mind through surreal imagery, Yoshiaki Kawajiri contributes "Running Man," a brutal tale of telekinetic racers in a deadly death-match circuit, and Katsuhiro Otomo delivers "Construction Cancellation Order," a prescient story about autonomous robots continuing a massive construction project even after government cancellation orders. This is obscure 80s anime at its most experimental and thought-provoking.

entries.title: Neptune Frost
entries.creator: Saul Williams, Anisia Uzeyman
entries.pitch:
Neptune Frost is a 2021 Afrofuturist science fiction musical co-directed by poet Saul Williams and filmmaker Anisia Uzeyman. Set in a post-civil war Burundi that spans past, future, and present, the film tells the story of Neptune, an intersex runaway, and Matalusa, a coltan miner, whose forbidden love sparks a hacker revolution against the global tech powers that control the world's resources. Produced with Ezra Miller as lead producer and Lin-Manuel Miranda as executive producer, the film premiered at the 2021 Cannes Film Festival in the Directors Fortnight section and received critical acclaim for its unique blend of science fiction, romance, and musical elements.

The film presents a vision of Africa that rejects colonial narratives, instead imagining a future built from e-waste where Black joy, resistance, and技术创新 coexist. The story follows Neptune's journey as they discover technokinetic abilities that allow them to spread ideas and philosophies across the world through digital hacks, while Matalusa witnesses his brother die from the toxic effects of coltan mining and begins his own hero's journey toward the "Unanimous Goldmine" - a secret community of rebels.

entries.title: Network Effect
entries.creator: Martha Wells
entries.pitch: When a research station on a remote planet sends a distress call, Murderbot—a self-aware construct (part-human, part-machine security unit) who just wants to be left alone to watch its favorite soap operas—reluctantly answers. The station has been attacked by a mysterious alien organism that can copy human neural patterns, turning the scientists into something no longer quite human. Forced to protect a group of humans who've become attached to it (despite its constant reminders that it doesn't like them), Murderbot must navigate this new threat while dealing with its own discomfort at having developed something resembling friendships. This is science fiction with a heart: a sardonic, socially-awkward AI protagonist who finds purpose in protecting others, even when it insists it doesn't care.

entries.title: Neutron and the Black Mask
entries.creator: José María Fernández
entries.pitch:
Neutrón el enmascarado negro (The Black Mask) is a 1962 Mexican sci-fi superhero film featuring Neutron, a masked wrestler who fights crime with his fists and wit. When a sinister gang of crooks plots to steal a secret formula, Neutron springs into action to stop their evil scheme.

This film represents a unique branch of Mexican cinema — the luchador superhero genre — where masked wrestlers double as crime-fighting superheroes. The combination of pulp science fiction with the theatrical tradition of Mexican masked wrestling creates an entertaining hybrid that predates many later superhero films.

entries.title: New
entries.creator: S. J. Suryah
entries.pitch:
New is a 2004 Tamil-language science fiction comedy that explores the consequences of a magical experiment gone sideways. When an 8-year-old boy named Pappu runs away from home after being scolded by his mother, he encounters a eccentric scientist who offers him a mysterious medicine. The boy agrees to take it, expecting to become a brave man—but the transformation works all too well. By day, he remains an eight-year-old child; by night, he becomes a 28-year-old adult named Vichu, while retaining the mind of a child.

The film takes this absurd premise and mines it for both comedy and genuine emotion. Pappu (as Vichu) manages to get a job at a toy company, falls in love with the owner's daughter Priya, and even gets married—all while secretly living a double life. The humor derives from the inherent ridiculousness of a child navigating adult relationships, while the sentiment comes from the touching relationship between Pappu and his mother, who doesn't know that the man who visits her is actually her missing son.

entries.title: News from Nowhere
entries.creator: William Morris
entries.pitch: Set in the year 2090, this Victorian utopian masterpiece follows William Guest, a tired socialist who falls asleep after a meeting and awakens to find himself in a radically transformed England. Gone are the factories, the poverty, the class divisions, and the misery of industrial capitalism. In their place exists a pastoral paradise where people work joyfully according to their abilities, live in beautiful homes, and spend their time in art, recreation, and meaningful community. The novel is both a scathing critique of Victorian industrial society and a passionate vision of what humanity could achieve if freed from the constraints of capitalism and wage labor.

entries.title: Nextworld
entries.creator: Osamu Tezuka
entries.pitch: Nextworld is a Japanese science fiction manga series written and illustrated by Osamu Tezuka in 1951. It is the third and final work in Tezuka's early science fiction trilogy, following Lost World (1948) and Metropolis (1949). The story focuses on atomic tests that create a race of mutant animals known as Fumoon—intelligent beings with psychic powers who formulate a plan to evacuate hundreds of animals and a small group of people off planet Earth. Meanwhile, two superpowers (representing the USA and USSR) draw closer to nuclear confrontation. Created during the early Cold War, Nextworld serves as a satirical allegory for the tense geopolitical climate of the era.

entries.title: Nexus
entries.creator: Mike Baron (Writer) & Steve Rude (Artist)
entries.pitch: Five hundred years in the future, on the moon city of Ylum (a shortened form of "asylum"), a reluctant hero named Horatio Valdemar Hellpop receives his powers from an alien entity called the Merk. But there's a catch: as payment for his abilities, Nexus must hunt down and execute a certain number of mass murderers each cycle—humanity's worst killers. When the Merk selects a target, Nexus suffers agonizing headaches and violent dreams of the victims until he carries out the execution. It's a dark bargain: a superhero bound by contract to kill, questioning his role while defending a lunar refuge that serves as sanctuary for the universe's outcasts.

entries.title: Nieznana Planeta (Unknown Planet)
entries.creator: Stefan Szwakopf
entries.pitch: Nieznana Planeta (Unknown Planet) is a charming 1962 Polish animated short and the final episode in the Jacek Śpioszek series produced by Warsaw's Studio of Film Miniatures. Directed by Stefan Szwakopf, this wordless short follows young Jacek and his faithful Scottie dog as they embark on an intergalactic adventure through space. The understated animation style renders the vast cosmos approachable for a child audience, with stars strewn like confetti over the vacuum of space, viewed through the glass observation dome of Jacek's minimalist spacecraft. The episode's gentle message about respecting alien life and treading carefully on unknown worlds provides a wholesome conclusion to the Jacek Śpioszek series.

entries.title: Night Slaves
entries.creator: Ted Post
entries.pitch:
Clay and Marjorie, an estranged married couple, take a vacation together while Clay recuperates from a serious auto accident. They arrive in a sleepy little town which seems normal enough by day—but at night, the townspeople begin acting strangely, leaving town in trucks and always returning by morning. Marjorie also begins to act strangely, with no one having any memories of their nighttime activities. Only Clay seems unaffected—due to a metal plate in his head from his accident. No one believes his increasingly frantic warnings about what's happening in this town. 

This 1970 ABC Movie of the Week stands out for its genuinely creepy atmosphere and its surprising subtext: a subversive commentary on exploited migrant workers that gives the otherwise conventional horror plot an unexpected edge.

entries.title: Night on the Galactic Railroad
entries.creator: Gisaburo Sugii (Director), based on the novel by Kenji Miyazawa
entries.pitch: In a small coastal town, young Giovanni—a lonely cat boy whose mother is ill and father absent—embarks on a magical journey aboard a steam train traveling through the Milky Way galaxy. Joined by his only friend Campanella, Giovanni witnesses impossible sights: scholars excavating crystal sands, a bird-catcher who transforms herons into candy, and passengers from a Titanic-like ship. But as the train approaches the Coalsack (a black hole), Giovanni must face an unbearable loss. This 1985 anime adaptation of Kenji Miyazawa's philosophical novel is a haunting meditation on friendship, sacrifice, and what it truly means to find happiness.

entries.title: Nightbreed
entries.creator: Clive Barker
entries.pitch: Nightbreed is a 1990 dark fantasy horror film written and directed by Clive Barker, based on his 1988 novella "Cabal." The film follows Aaron Boone, an unstable mental patient who is falsely led to believe by his doctor that he is a serial killer. After being framed and shot by police, Boone discovers refuge in an abandoned cemetery called Midian, where he finds acceptance among a tribe of monsters and outcasts known as the "Nightbreed" - beings who hide from humanity in the shadows beneath the earth. The film explores themes of otherness, acceptance, and the nature of monstrosity.

entries.title: Nightfall
entries.creator: Isaac Asimov
entries.pitch: Nightfall is a landmark 1941 science fiction short story by Isaac Asimov about a planet where night never falls—until it does with catastrophic consequences. Set on Lagash, a world perpetually illuminated by six suns, the story follows a journalist who investigates scientists warning that civilization is about to end. The catch: the inhabitants have never experienced true darkness and face mass insanity when an eclipse plunges their world into night every 2,049 years. The story explores how an entire civilization, having never seen stars, would react to the sudden appearance of the night sky—and the terrifying answer involves fire, destruction, and the collapse of society.

entries.title: Nimona
entries.creator: Nick Bruno, Troy Quane (Directors)
entries.pitch:
Nimona is a 2023 American animated science-fantasy action-adventure film based on the graphic novel by ND Stevenson. The story follows Ballister Boldheart, a knight who is framed for the murder of the Queen, and teams up with Nimona, a shapeshifting teenage outcast, to clear his name and uncover the truth about a conspiracy within the kingdom.

Originally produced by Blue Sky Studios, the film was canceled when Disney shut down Blue Sky in 2021, but was later revived by Annapurna Pictures and released by Netflix in 2023. The film received critical acclaim and was nominated for Best Animated Feature at the Critics' Choice Awards, Annie Awards, and Academy Awards.

entries.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
entries.creator: George Orwell
entries.pitch: Nineteen Eighty-Four is a haunting dystopian novel set in a totalitarian future where the Party, led by the enigmatic Big Brother, exercises absolute control over every aspect of human life. The story follows Winston Smith, a low-ranking member of the Outer Party who works at the Ministry of Truth, where he rewrites historical records to match the Party's ever-changing version of the truth. Winston secretly harbors doubts about the Party and begins a forbidden love affair with Julia, leading him down a path of thoughtcrime and rebellion against the oppressive regime. Published in 1949, Orwell's masterpiece coined terms like "Big Brother," "doublethink," "thoughtcrime," and "Newspeak" that have become part of our cultural vocabulary. The novel is a chilling warning about the dangers of totalitarianism, mass surveillance, and the manipulation of truth—a warning that remains profoundly relevant in the modern age of fake news and digital surveillance.

entries.title: No. 5
entries.creator: Taiyō Matsumoto
entries.pitch: No. 5 is a surreal, visually striking science fantasy manga by renowned artist Taiyō Matsumoto, serialized from 2000 to 2005 in Shogakukan's Monthly Ikki magazine. Set in a bleak post-apocalyptic world of endless desert, the story follows a group called the Rainbow Council—members identified only by numbers—who act as god-like peacekeepers. When the enigmatic No. 5 turns rogue and begins assassinating his former comrades, the remaining numbered agents scramble to stop him while navigating their own mysterious motivations and bureaucratic hierarchies. The series is noted for Matsumoto's distinctive, doodle-like art style that evokes early 90s grunge aesthetics, with surreal action sequences that convey raw danger and emotional intensity. Viz Media originally released only two volumes in English before discontinuing due to low sales—selling less than 1,000 copies—though it was later republished in 2021.

entries.title: Non-Stop New York
entries.pitch: Non-Stop New York is a 1937 British science fiction crime film directed by Robert Stevenson, featuring John Loder, Anna Lee, and Francis L. Sullivan. Based on Ken Attiwill's 1936 novel "Sky Steward," the film combines futuristic elements—most notably a luxurious transatlantic flying boat—with a tense murder mystery plot. The film was produced by Gaumont British and stands as an early example of British sci-fi cinema, featuring what contemporary reviews described as a transatlantic airplane "as richly imaginative as a front-cover of Popular Science or a Buck Rogers space ship." The story follows Jennie Carr, a showgirl who can prove an innocent man's murder conviction, as she is pursued by gangsters onto the "Lisbon Clipper," a massive transatlantic flying boat where the gripping finale unfolds.

entries.title: Norstrilia
entries.creator: Cordwainer Smith (Paul Linebarger)
entries.pitch:
In a distant future, the planet Old North Australia (Norstrilia) holds an invaluable resource—the only source of "stroon," the precious substance that grants immortality. The Norstrilians, living in unimaginable wealth, have developed a harsh society where children are culled to prevent overpopulation, and only those who survive the deadly "Garden of Death" test may become adults.

Rod McBan is the last male descendant of one of Norstrilia's oldest ranching families, heir to the Station of Doom. Despite being considered unfit, he has been spared from culling three times due to his lineage. When assassins target him, Rod must flee to Earth, where his immense wealth from playing the market makes him a magnet for criminals, revolutionaries, and the oppressed "underpeople" of society. What follows is a wild adventure through the darker corners of human civilization, as Rod discovers what it truly means to be human.

entries.title: Nukie
entries.creator: Sias Odendaal, Michael Pakleppa
entries.pitch: Nukie is a 1987 South African science fiction film that tells the story of two alien brothers, Nukie and Miko, who crash land on Earth after their spacecraft is struck by lightning. Separated during the crash, Nukie finds himself in the African savanna while Miko is captured by the US government and held at a top-secret facility called the Space Foundation. Using telekinetic powers, Miko reaches out to his brother for help, setting Nukie on a journey across Africa to rescue him. Along the way, Nukie befriends two local children, Tiko and Toki, who help him navigate the human world while evading government agents and a hostile corporal who sees the alien as a threat. The film is notable for being one of the most infamous E.T. knockoffs ever made, often cited among the worst films ever produced.

entries.title: Návštěvníci
entries.creator: Jindřich Polák (director), Ota Hofman (creator)
entries.pitch:
Návštěvníci (The Visitors) is a Czechoslovak sci-fi TV series filmed between 1981 and 1983, consisting of 15 episodes that aired from November 1983 to February 1984. The series was co-produced with West Germany, Switzerland, and France, making it an unusually international production for Eastern Bloc television of the era.

Set in the year 2484, humanity has evolved into a peaceful, post-national civilization governed by the World Council and advised by an artificial intelligence called the Central Brain of Mankind. When the Central Brain predicts that a comet will shift Earth's axis and threaten civilization, a team of time travelers is dispatched back to 1984 on "Expedition Adam 84"—disguised as surveyors in a Lada Niva—to retrieve three notebooks belonging to young Adam Bernau, who will win a Nobel Prize in 2034 for a formula capable of moving continents.

The series combines elements of time-travel adventure with a warm, humanistic vision of the future. The time travelers—historian Filip, doctor Noll, technician Karas, and documentarian Katja—struggle to adapt to 1984 life, fumbling with money and technology while forming bonds with the locals, including the young Adam and his future "great teacher" Alois Drchlík.

entries.title: O Homem do Sputnik
entries.creator: Carlos Manga
entries.pitch: O Homem do Sputnik (The Sputnik Man) is a Brazilian comedy film from 1959 about a humble couple, Anastácio and Cleci, who run a small egg business in Rio de Janeiro. One night, a mysterious metallic object crashes into their chicken coop. When Anastácio discovers the strange globe among his chickens, he initially thinks nothing of it—until Cleci reads in the newspaper about the Soviet Union's recently launched Sputnik satellite. Realizing their find could be worth a fortune, the couple attempts to pawn the "Sputnik" but instead becomes embroiled in an international spy thriller. American, Soviet, and French agents descend upon the simple couple, each trying to steal the object for their respective governments. Meanwhile, Anastácio and Cleci are thrust into the glamorous world of high society, staying at the luxurious Copacabana Palace and encountering a parade of seductive foreign agents.

entries.title: O-Bi, O-Ba: The End of Civilization
entries.creator: Piotr Szulkin
entries.pitch: O-Bi, O-Ba: The End of Civilization is a 1985 Polish post-apocalyptic drama written and directed by Piotr Szulkin, part of his "asocial fiction" tetralogy. The film takes place in an underground city called "The Dome" where survivors of a nuclear war have been living for one year. The story follows Soft (Jerzy Stuhr), a low-level administrator whose job is to maintain citizen morale by perpetuating the myth of "The Ark"—a promised vessel that will rescue the survivors. In reality, the Ark is a lie invented by Soft himself, and the authorities have begun denying its existence to maintain control. As the Dome begins to crack and fail, Soft and Gea (Krystyna Janda), a sex worker who believes in the Ark, attempt to escape. The film is a bleak meditation on authoritarian control, religious manipulation, and the human condition in the face of civilization's collapse.

entries.title: Observer
entries.creator: Bloober Team
entries.pitch:
Observer is a psychological horror video game set in a cyberpunk rendition of 2084 Kraków, Poland. Developed by Bloober Team (the same studio behind Layers of Fear), it puts players in the role of Daniel Lazarski, an "Observer"—a detective with the ability to hack into people's minds through their neural implants. When Daniel receives a distress call from his estranged son Adam, he enters a Kraków plagued by the nanophage, a digital plague that devastated the population and allowed megacorporation Chiron to take control of Poland.

The game draws heavily from classic cyberpunk influences like Blade Runner, while adding distinctly Eastern European flavor—combining dystopian social commentary with psychological horror. With Rutger Hauer (iconic from Blade Runner) voicing the protagonist, Observer explores themes of surveillance, mind invasion, and the blurred lines between human consciousness and technology.

entries.title: Odysseus and the Stars
entries.creator: Ludvík Ráža
entries.pitch: Odysseus and the Stars is a 1976 Czechoslovak children's science fiction film directed by Ludvík Ráža. The film follows a group of children who become involved in a mysterious chain of events during the 1970s, centered around an attempt to make contact with an extraterrestrial civilization. When a meteorite crashes nearby, the children embark on an extraordinary adventure that blends coming-of-age storytelling with classic science fiction themes of first contact and humanity's place in the universe. The film represents a charming example of Czechoslovak children's cinema, combining imaginative storytelling with the country's rich tradition of fantastical filmmaking.

entries.title: Om-Dar-B-Dar
entries.pitch:
Om-Dar-B-Dar is a 1988 Indian Hindi-language postmodernist film that defies conventional categorization. Directed by Kamal Swaroop and set in Ajmer and Pushkar, Rajasthan, the film follows the adventures of a young schoolboy named Om as he navigates his eccentric family and discovers the strange powers of his ability to hold his breath. The film employs a nonlinear narrative structure and absurdist storytelling to satirize mythology, arts, politics, and philosophy. 

Never commercially released in India during its initial run, the film premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival and quickly gained cult status among film critics and cinephiles. After 26 years of being unavailable domestically, it was finally given a proper theatrical release in 2014 following a digital restoration by the National Film Development Corporation of India (NFDC).

entries.title: Omega Doom
entries.creator: Albert Pyun
entries.pitch: Omega Doom is a 1996 American science fiction action film directed by Albert Pyun and starring Rutger Hauer. Set in a dystopian future after a nuclear war between humans and robots, the film follows a robot warrior who awakens to find himself in the middle of a robot civil war. Notably, the film is largely based on Akira Kurosawa's Yojimbo, transposed into a post-apocalyptic setting with mechanical protagonists. Considered a cult film, Omega Doom received largely negative critical reception but has developed a modest following among fans of obscure sci-fi and B-movie enthusiasts. The film explores themes of machine consciousness, the cyclical nature of violence, and the possibility of redemption even for beings designed for destruction.

entries.title: Omer the Tourist in Star Trek
entries.creator: Hulki Saner
entries.pitch:
Omer the Tourist in Star Trek is a 1973 Turkish sci-fi comedy that stands as one of the most improbable cult films to emerge from the Turksploitation era. The film takes the beloved Star Trek universe and filters it through the unique lens of Turkish cinema's most beloved hobo character, Ömer.

When the spaceship Enterprise receives a distress call from Professor Krater, who lives alone with his wife on the remote planet Orin 7, Mr. Spock and a landing party beam down to investigate. But one crew member dies under mysterious circumstances, and the doctor struggles to determine the cause. The killer? Professor Krater's wife Nancy — an android created to be the perfect companion.

The film is a wild pastiche of multiple Star Trek episodes, including 'The Man Trap,' 'What Are Little Girls Made Of?,' 'I, Mudd,' 'Arena,' and 'Amok Time.' But unlike straightforward knockoffs, Ömer the Tourist plays less as theft than as an affectionate, earnest tribute — made with zero budget but boundless creativity. This is Turkish Star Trek filmed six years before the official Star Trek motion picture.

entries.title: Omicron
entries.creator: Ugo Gregoretti
entries.pitch: A comedic science fiction film from 1963 Italy, Omicron tells the story of an alien who possesses the body of a deceased factory worker in order to study humanity. Directed by Ugo Gregoretti, the film was entered in the competition at the 24th Venice International Film Festival and blends sci-fi themes with satirical comedy about human nature and society.

entries.title: On the Comet
entries.pitch: On the Comet (Na kometě) is a 1970 Czech experimental science fiction film directed by the visionary Karel Zeman, known for his unique blend of live action and animation. Based on Jules Verne's 1877 novel "Off on a Comet," this film represents Zeman's distinctive approach to cinematic fantasy—combining theatrical sets, special effects, and animated sequences inspired by vintage illustrations to create a whimsical,Grotesque vision of space travel. The film follows a group of French, Spanish, and Arabian soldiers who are carried away on a comet after it collides with Earth, continuing their petty conflicts in an absurd, cosmic setting. As a product of Communist-era Czechoslovakia, the film showcases Zeman's creative workaround for limited budgets—using imaginative visual style to transcend technological constraints, much like his famous predecessor Jan Švankmajer would later do with stop-motion.

entries.title: On the Silver Globe
entries.creator: Jerzy Żuławski
entries.pitch: On the Silver Globe is the first volume of Jerzy Żuławski's groundbreaking Lunar Trilogy, written between 1901-1911 and considered one of the earliest works of modern science fiction. The novel tells the story of a disastrous lunar expedition in which a group of astronauts from Earth become stranded on the Moon. After several generations, their descendants lose most of their knowledge and are ruled by a religious cult. Originally written in Polish, this novel predates many classic science fiction works and influenced later writers including Stanisław Lem, who called it "one of the most fascinating and life-changing experiences" of his youth. The novel is presented as a diary kept by the surviving crew member Jan Korecki, chronicling the founding of the lunar colony and its descent into religious extremism.

entries.title: On the Silver Globe
entries.pitch: On the Silver Globe is a 1988 Polish epic surrealist science fiction arthouse film that defies easy categorization. Directed by Andrzej Żuławski (known for Possession and The Devil), this ambitious project was adapted from "The Lunar Trilogy" written by his grand-uncle Jerzy Żuławski around 1900. The film tells the story of a group of dissident astronauts who escape from a dystopian Earth and crash land on an unnamed planet, where they give rise to a new human civilization. Many years later, a second astronaut arrives and becomes entangled in religious prophecy and conflict with the planet's indigenous inhabitants. Production on this epic was plagued by political interference—it began in 1976-1977 but was shut down by Polish authorities, with the reels ordered destroyed. Żuławski eventually completed the film in 1988 using preserved footage plus voice-over commentary to fill narrative gaps. The result is a haunting, philosophical meditation on civilization, religion, colonialism, and the cyclical nature of human history.

entries.title: Once in a New Moon
entries.creator: Anthony Kimmins (director) | Owen Rutter (novel "Lucky Star")
entries.pitch: Once in a New Moon is a rare British science fiction film from 1935, a quota quickie made at Shepperton Studios that offers a delightful premise: when a dead star passes Earth, its magnetic pull dislodges the fictional English seaside town of Shrimpton-on-the-Sea, carrying it away to become its own miniature planet orbiting Earth. This charming pocket world—where the sun rises and sets every few hours and Earth hangs in the sky as a "new moon"—becomes a isolated laboratory for examining human nature under extraordinary circumstances.

entries.title: Onesime, Clockmaker
entries.pitch:
Onesime, Clockmaker is a whimsical French silent film from 1912 that explores the comic possibilities of time manipulation. The film follows Onésime, a humble clockmaker who hopes to secure a promised inheritance. In his workshop, he invents an extraordinary time machine that can accelerate the passage of time on Earth.

Using early cinematic special effects, the film visualizes what happens when time itself is sped up - men and machines move at hyper-animated rates, and the human life cycle is compressed into moments. It's a charming, surreal exploration of humanity's fascination with controlling the uncontrollable.

This early science fiction comedy predates most genre films and demonstrates the medium's quick embrace of speculative themes. The film's playful approach to time travel and its visual experiments with temporal acceleration make it a fascinating artifact of early cinema.

entries.title: Open Your Eyes
entries.creator: Alejandro Amenábar (Director), Mateo Gil (Writer)
entries.pitch: Open Your Eyes is a 1997 Spanish sci-fi psychological thriller directed by Alejandro Amenábar. The film follows César, a handsome young man whose life unravels after a car accident leaves him horribly disfigured. When he begins experiencing surreal, disorienting dreams that blur the line between reality and fantasy, he discovers a shocking truth about his existence. The film is renowned for its complex narrative structure that intercuts between dream and reality, exploring themes of identity, perception, and what it means to be human. It was critically acclaimed and later remade as the Hollywood film Vanilla Sky (2001).

entries.title: Operation Ganymed
entries.pitch: A spaceship returns to Earth after several years of space exploration, only to find the planet desolate and seemingly abandoned. The crew lands in what they believe is Mexico and travels north, trying to piece together what happened during their absence. This 1977 German science fiction film offers a chilling vision of humanity's potential fate, told through the lens of European post-war anxieties about nuclear annihilation and environmental collapse.

entries.title: Our Heavenly Bodies
entries.creator: Hanns Walter Kornblum
entries.pitch:
Our Heavenly Bodies (German: Wunder der Schöpfung, Wonder of the Creation) is a 1925 German silent educational film that attempts to represent everything known about the cosmos at the time. Produced by Universum-Film AG (Ufa), it combines documentary footage, elaborate special effects, and animated sequences to take viewers on a fantastical journey through the solar system and beyond.

The film is structured as a voyage of discovery, beginning with the history of cosmology and the night sky, then launching viewers in a \"fantasy ship\" to explore the Moon, each planet, and finally the stars. It features stunning visualizations of space travel that predate by decades what would become standard in science fiction cinema. The film's ambition and imagination make it a forgotten masterpiece of early science fiction.

Considered a prime example of the German \"Kulturfilm\" genre, Our Heavenly Bodies predates both Metropolis (1927) and 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968), yet shares their visionary scope. It was a wild success upon release and has been reconstructed in 2008 by the Munich Film Archive using materials from Finland and Germany.

entries.title: Outlanders
entries.creator: Created by Johji Manabe (manga) | OVA directed by Katsuhisa Yamada | Produced by Tatsunoko Production
entries.pitch: Outlanders is a 1986 Japanese OVA that serves as an adaptation of Johji Manabe's manga series, produced by the legendary Tatsunoko Production. This space opera blends science fantasy, romance, and action into a story about Princess Kahm of the Santovasku Empire, who invades Earth and encounters human news photographer Tetsuya Wakatsuki. What begins as an alien invasion quickly evolves into an unexpected romance and a cosmic conflict spanning multiple galactic factions. The OVA was notable for being one of the early manga-to-OVA adaptations and was released in 1986, a pivotal year for the OVA format. It has since developed a cult following among anime enthusiasts, particularly those interested in space opera and 1980s anime history.

entries.title: Outwars
entries.creator: SingleTrac (Developer), Microsoft (Publisher)
entries.pitch:
Outwars is a military science fiction tactical shooter developed by SingleTrac and published by Microsoft in 1998. The game places players in the role of a heavily armed marine in the elite CDF Marine Jump Corps, tasked with battling insectoid aliens known as "The Skulls" who are intent on taking over the galaxy. Featuring a selectable perspective tactical shooter format, players don various rocket-propelled powered armors—Light Scout, Medium Combat, Heavy Assault, or Heavy Dreadnaut—and lead small teams of AI-controlled squadmates through mission-based gameplay across multiple planets.

The game stood out for its innovative approach to loadout customization, allowing players to equip different weapons and equipment at the beginning of each mission. The mechanics supported simultaneous firing of multiple weapon types—including shoulder-mounted guided missiles, pulse rifles, and remote-detonation mines—rather than the consecutive firing typical of shooters at the time. Multiplayer supported up to eight players via Direct3D and Internet Gaming Zone, offering modes including Free for All, Team War, and Capture the Flag.

entries.title: Oxygen
entries.creator: Matjaž Klopčič (Director)
entries.pitch: Oxygen is a paranoid Yugoslavian science fiction drama set in a near-future society where a group of young rebels, hippies, and 1968 protesters attempt to secede from the mainland and establish an independent island. Directed by Slovenian filmmaker Matjaž Klopčič, the film blends political allegory with science fiction elements, creating a tense portrait of ideological conflict and state surveillance. A journalist arrives on the island to cover a political summit and becomes entangled in the clash between the young idealists and the established order. The film won awards at the 1970 Pulski Filmski Festival, including Best Directing (Bronze Arena) and Best Cinematography (Golden Arena).

entries.title: Pale Cocoon
entries.creator: Yasuhiro Yoshiura
entries.pitch: Pale Cocoon is a 23-minute OVA written and directed by Yasuhiro Yoshiura, released in 2006. Set in a far-future underground colony, the film follows Ura, a dedicated member of the "Archive Excavation Department" who works to recover lost data from Earth's surface—a world that has become polluted, cold, and largely uninhabitable. As Ura obsessionally restores corrupted records of the forgotten past, he encounters Riko, a colleague who has lost her passion for the work. Their discovery of a mysterious video recording leads them to question everything they know about their world and the nature of memory itself. This contemplative, visually striking short is a meditation on loss, the value of history, and the human drive to recover what has been erased.

entries.title: Paprika
entries.pitch: Paprika is a 2006 Japanese animated psychological thriller directed by Satoshi Kon, based on Yasutaka Tsutsui's 1993 novel. When a revolutionary device called the DC Mini allows therapists to enter patients' dreams, a mysterious "dream terrorist" begins using it to inflict nightmares on innocent people. Dr. Atsuko Chiba, a research psychologist, must don her dream-world alter ego Paprika to track down the culprit and save both the dream world and reality from merging into chaos.

entries.title: Parable of the Sower
entries.creator: Octavia E. Butler
entries.pitch: Set in a near-future post-apocalyptic United States ravaged by climate change and extreme inequality, Parable of the Sower follows Lauren Olamina, a young Black woman born with "hyper-empathy" - an ability to feel the physical sensations of others. When her gated community is destroyed by violent raiders, Lauren must journey northward through a landscape of chaos, poverty, and collapse, gathering survivors and spreading her new philosophy called Earthseed. What makes this novel remarkable is its fundamental optimism: despite the devastating worldbuilding, it's ultimately a story about hope, resilience, and humanity's potential to transcend its worst impulses by reaching for the stars.

entries.title: Paranoia Agent
entries.creator: Satoshi Kon (Director), Seishi Minakami (Writer)
entries.pitch: Paranoia Agent is a 2004 Japanese anime television series created by the renowned director Satoshi Kon and produced by Madhouse. The series explores a mysterious social phenomenon in Musashino, Tokyo, where a juvenile serial assailant known as "Lil' Slugger" (or Shōnen Batto) attacks citizens with his golden baseball bat. The show follows a complex web of characters affected by this phenomenon, including Tsukiko Sagi, a shy character designer who created the popular pink dog Maromi, and two detectives assigned to solve the case. Known for its psychological depth, the series blurs the lines between reality and delusion, examining how rumors and fear can manifest as physical threats in society.

entries.title: Paranoia!
entries.creator: Phoenix Arts (Radek Ševčík)
entries.pitch: Paranoia! is a Czech real-time strategy game released in 1995, developed by Phoenix Arts and recognized as the first Czech RTS ever created. Designed as a clone of the influential Dune II, the game is set in the year 2673 in the Beretta solar system on the planet Paranoia, where a brutal war has raged for four years over a scarce resource—a mysterious plant called the hopsinka with special powers. The player commands the Terrans, the native population, in their struggle to reclaim territories occupied by alien forces. Originally conceived as a freeware project, rising costs led developers to release it commercially in September 1995 after approximately one year of development. A sequel, Paranoia II, followed in 1996.

entries.title: Paris Qui Dort
entries.creator: René Clair
entries.pitch: Paris Qui Dort (literally "Paris Which Sleeps"), also known as The Crazy Ray, is a 1924 French silent science fiction comedy directed by René Clair in his directorial debut. The film centers on a mad scientist who invents a mysterious ray device that freezes Paris's citizens in strange, immovable positions, leaving only a handful of unaffected people to witness the chaos and loot the abandoned city. This pioneering comedic work predates similar "frozen world" scenarios in cinema and showcases Clair's inventive visual storytelling and satirical edge. The film runs approximately 65 minutes and is notable for being one of the earliest feature-length science fiction comedies, blending fantastical premises with sharp social commentary on Parisian society.

entries.title: Patalghar
entries.pitch: Patalghar (Bengali: "The Underground Chamber") is a 2003 Bengali-language science fiction action film directed by Abhijit Chaudhuri, based on a story by Shirshendu Mukhopadhyay. The film tells the story of a genius scientist from the 19th century who invents a revolutionary sound-wave device capable of putting any living being to sleep, and an alien from the planet Nyapcha who arrives 150 years later seeking to steal this powerful technology. When the device is rediscovered in the present day, a young boy and a scientist must work together to prevent it from falling into the wrong hands while also dealing with the alien visitor. The film won the National Film Award for Best Debut Film of a Director and was noted for its innovative storytelling and special effects for Indian cinema of its time.

entries.title: Patlabor: The Early Days
entries.creator: Mamoru Oshii (Director), Kazunori Ito (Writer), Studio Deen
entries.pitch:
Patlabor: The Early Days is a 7-episode Original Video Animation (OVA) series released between 1988 and 1989, serving as the origin story for the acclaimed Japanese science fiction franchise created by Headgear. Set in the near future of 1998-2002, the series introduces viewers to a Tokyo where massive humanoid robots called "Labors" have become essential for construction, industrial work, and public safety. The Tokyo Metropolitan Police responds by establishing Special Vehicle Section 2, Division 2 (SV2)—a unit of officers who pilot patrol Labors called "Patlabors" to combat crimes and accidents involving these giant machines.

Unlike typical mecha anime that focus on grand warfare or cosmic conflicts, Patlabor: The Early Days grounds its narrative in everyday police work with a comedic undertone. The series follows Noa Izumi, the protagonist and pilot of the Ingram AV-98 Labor, as she and her colleagues at SV2 handle situations ranging from labor accidents and robberies to more sinister crimes involving rogue machines. Directed by Mamoru Oshii with scripts by Kazunori Ito and mechanical designs by Yutaka Izubuchi, the OVA established the template for police procedural mecha storytelling. The series is credited with revitalizing the OVA format for mecha anime and establishing the standard six-episode OVA structure.

entries.title: Perestroika
entries.creator: Locis (Nikita Skripkin, Aleksander Okrug, Dmitry Chikin)
entries.pitch: Perestroika (also known as Toppler) is an extraordinarily rare Soviet MS-DOS puzzle game released in 1990 by a small development team called Locis. Named after Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev's policy of "restructuring," this game is a fascinating time capsule of late Soviet-era political satire packaged as a simple arcade experience. The player controls a small frog-like creature jumping between lily pads, collecting colored dots and avoiding "bureaucrats" while trying to reach a coin that symbolizes a higher standard of living. The splash screen features a stylized Gorbachev whose presence causes the Kremlin to break apart—a bold political statement for 1990 Soviet Union. The game was also ported to ZX Spectrum by a Czech programmer group under the name "Perestrojka."

entries.title: Permutation City
entries.creator: Greg Egan (Australian)
entries.pitch: In a mid-21st century Earth devastated by climate change and overdevelopment, humanity has developed technology powerful enough to create "Copies" - digital renderings of human consciousness that can live on in virtual reality after death. Paul Durham, a wealthy entrepreneur, pitches an ambitious project to aging billionaires: immortality through digital consciousness transfer. He hires programmer Maria Deluca to create a simulated universe (the Autoverse) that could support artificial life, while also building a vast virtual city for his wealthy clients. But Durham's true vision goes far beyond mere immortality - he believes that reality itself is mathematics, and that all possible universes exist simultaneously. The novel follows Durham, Maria, and several other characters as they explore the implications of digital consciousness, virtual reality, and a radical new theory of existence called "Dust Theory." What begins as a quest for immortality evolves into something far more profound - an exploration of what it means to be real, and whether consciousness can exist independent of physical reality.

entries.title: Phase IV
entries.creator: Saul Bass (Director), based on a story by Ronald B. Harvey
entries.pitch: Phase IV is a rare gem from 1974—the only feature film ever directed by legendary title designer Saul Bass (better known for creating iconic opening sequences for Hitchcock's Psycho and Vertigo). Set in the sun-scorched Arizona desert, the film presents a terrifying premise: a species of ants has begun evolving at an exponential rate, developing intelligence, complex communication, and ultimately, a collective consciousness that poses an existential threat to humanity. Unlike typical monster movies, Phase IV takes a patient, almost meditative approach to horror, building dread through strange ant behaviors, unexplained geometric structures, and the growing realization that humans may be witnessing the birth of a new dominant species. The film is visually stunning, with groundbreaking macro photography of ant behavior and a haunting, minimalist electronic score that adds to the growing sense of unease. It's science fiction as slow-burn psychological horror—an overlooked masterpiece that deserves far more recognition than it has received.

entries.title: Phi 1.618
entries.creator: Theodore Ushev
