entries.pitch: Phi 1.618 is a 2022 Bulgarian-Canadian dystopian science fiction film directed by Theodore Ushev in his directorial debut. Set in a bleak future where humanity has achieved immortality through artificial creation, the film presents a world where men are genetically engineered as asexual, immortal beings—and where women have become biologically obsolete. As a mysterious poison spreads across Earth, these loveless immortals embark on a galactic colonization mission, carrying with them the barely-living body of a woman as a relic of the past. The film is based on Vladislav Todorov's novel "The Spinning Top" and explores themes of gender, reproduction, memory, and what it means to be human when humanity itself has been redesigned.

entries.title: Phoenix 2772
entries.creator: Osamu Tezuka (Director/Writer), Taku Sugiyama (Co-Director)
entries.pitch: In a dystopian future where Earth is dying from energy depletion and humanity is controlled through test-tube births and computer-assigned roles, young pilot Godo is chosen by the ambitious politician Rock to capture the mythical Phoenix—a legendary bird whose blood can grant immortality and heal the dying planet. Guided by his loyal robot caretaker Olga and accompanied by a mysterious prisoner, Godo journeys into space to find the Phoenix, all while navigating forbidden love, political betrayal, and his own doubts about violence and sacrifice. This 1980 animated film from the legendary Osamu Tezuka is a visually stunning meditation on love, reincarnation, and selflessness that blends epic science fiction with mythic storytelling.

entries.title: Pilot Pirx's Inquest
entries.creator: Marek Piestrak (Director)
entries.pitch: Pilot Pirx's Inquest is a Polish-Soviet science fiction film directed by Marek Piestrak, based on a story by Stanisław Lem. The film follows Pirx, an experienced pilot hired to evaluate "nonlinears"—experimental android crewmembers—for use on future space flights. Sent on a top-secret mission to launch two satellites into the rings of Saturn, Pirx must determine which member of his mixed human-robot crew is secretly a hostile machine. Upon returning to Earth, an inquest begins to determine if Pirx was responsible for an accident that occurred during the mission. The film explores themes of artificial intelligence, humanity versus machines, and the nature of consciousness through a tense psychological thriller narrative.

entries.title: Planet Earth
entries.creator: Gene Roddenberry (Creator), Marc Daniels (Director)
entries.pitch:
Planet Earth is a 1974 American made-for-television science fiction film created by Gene Roddenberry, best known as the creator of Star Trek. Produced by Warner Bros. Television and airing on ABC on April 23, 1974, this 74-minute pilot film was intended as the first episode of a proposed weekly television series. The project marked Roddenberry's second attempt to develop a post-apocalyptic series concept, following Genesis II (1973), and featured John Saxon in the lead role of Dylan Hunt.

Set in the year 2133, the film depicts a world devastated by nuclear war centuries earlier. The story follows PAX (Latin for "peace"), a science-based organization dedicated to restoring civilization, as they dispatch Team 21 to survey central California. When their team member is severely wounded, they must locate a missing surgeon in a dangerous matriarchal society where men are enslaved. The pilot explores themes of gender relations through a 1970s lens, depicting a post-apocalyptic future where different factions struggle for control and survival.

entries.title: Planet of the Apes
entries.creator: Franklin J. Schaffner (Director)
entries.pitch: Planet of the Apes is a landmark 1968 American science fiction film directed by Franklin J. Schaffner, based loosely on Pierre Boulle's 1963 novel. The film stars Charlton Heston as astronaut George Taylor, who crash-lands on a mysterious planet in the distant future only to discover that evolved apes have become the dominant species while humans exist as mute, primitive beings. The film is renowned for its groundbreaking prosthetic makeup, Jerry Goldsmith's avant-garde score, and one of cinema's most iconic twist endings. It was a critical and commercial success, earning an honorary Academy Award for John Chambers' makeup work and spawning one of the most successful science fiction franchises in film history.

entries.title: Planet of the Vampires
entries.creator: Mario Bava
entries.pitch: Planet of the Vampires (Italian: Terrore nello spazio, literally "Terror in Space") is a 1965 Italian-Spanish science fiction horror film directed by Mario Bava. The film follows the harrowing experiences of two spaceships that crash-land on an unexplored planet called Aura, where disembodied alien entities possess the bodies of deceased crew members. Notably, this obscure gem predates and influenced Ridley Scott's Alien (1979), sharing similar narrative DNA—cosmic horror, hostile alien worlds, and the paranoia of infiltration. Produced on a modest budget by Italian International Film and American International Pictures, the film was released in Italy in 1965 and later in English-speaking markets under various titles including "The Demon Planet." Despite its limited release, it has since gained recognition as a pioneering work in space horror.

entries.title: Planeta Bur
entries.creator: Pavel Klushantsev
entries.pitch: Planeta Bur (Planet of Storms) is a 1962 Soviet science fiction adventure film that imagines humanity's first landing on Venus. Directed by Pavel Klushantsev and based on Alexander Kazantsev's novel, the film follows Soviet cosmonauts aboard the ships Sirius, Vega, and Capella as they journey toward Venus for first human contact with the planet. When Capella is destroyed by a meteor, the remaining crews must decide whether to continue the mission or wait two months for reinforcements. The film is notable for its innovative special effects and was later adapted by Roger Corman into American versions Voyage to the Prehistoric Planet and Voyage to the Planet of Prehistoric Women.

entries.title: Planetfall
entries.creator: Steve Meretzky (Infocom)
entries.pitch: Planetfall is a classic interactive fiction game from Infocom, released in 1983 as the company's eighth title. Players take on the role of an Ensign Seventh Class aboard the starship S.P.S. Feinstein, serving in the Stellar Patrol. After a series of explosions devastate the ship, the player escapes in a pod and crash-lands on the distant planet Resida—a world that appears completely deserted except for one mysterious structure. There, the player encounters Floyd, a childlike and lovable robot who becomes an invaluable companion. Together, they must unravel the secrets of this dead civilization and discover what happened to its inhabitants before time runs out. Planetfall was Steve Meretzky's first published game and became one of Infocom's most beloved titles, praised for its emotional storytelling and memorable characters.

entries.title: Planets Against Us
entries.creator: Romano Ferrara (Director)
entries.pitch: Planets Against Us (original Italian: I pianeti contro di noi) is a 1962 Italian-French science fiction horror film directed by Romano Ferrara. The film tells the story of an alien invasion where cyborgs disguised as humans infiltrate Earth, appearing identical to a missing young man named Robert Landersen. When atomic rockets begin failing mysteriously worldwide, authorities discover that identical-looking beings are behind the attacks—cylindrical skeletons beneath human skin, controlled from a flying saucer. The film is notable for featuring planned invasion by cyborgs rather than the common trope of aliens inhabiting or duplicating humans.

entries.title: Planzet
entries.creator: Jun Kawazaki
entries.pitch:
In 2047, an unknown alien lifeform descends upon Earth, annihilating all major cities in a single catastrophic strike. Humanity, pushed to the brink of extinction, unites to build the Diffusor—a desperate weapon capable of repelling the invaders. The military codename the aliens FEBRIUS (later FOS), and against all odds, the Diffusor achieves a temporary peace.

Six years later, in 2053, the war continues. Hiroshi Akishima, a soldier in humanity's last desperate counterattack, embodies the resolve of a civilization fighting not just for survival, but for the chance to reclaim its world. Planzet is a compact, intense piece of Japanese anime science fiction—less than 30 minutes long—that delivers alien invasion spectacle with economic precision.

The film's obscurity (only 10 votes on TMDB as of this writing) makes it a genuine rarity, even among the vast catalog of Japanese sci-fi animation. For fans of obscure anime seeking underexplored material, Planzet offers a focused, self-contained story of humanity's struggle against an incomprehensible extraterrestrial threat.

entries.title: Poklad
entries.creator: František Fuka
entries.pitch: Poklad (meaning "Treasure") is a 1984 Czech text adventure game developed by František Fuka for the ZX Spectrum, making it one of the oldest surviving games created in Czechoslovakia. The player finds themselves in a magical country and must task themselves with finding five treasures scattered across a 4x5 room matrix spanning three levels. The game was published by Proxima Software as part of their "Fuxoft uvádí" series, representing an important milestone in Eastern European gaming history during the early era of personal computing.

entries.title: Policenauts
entries.creator: Konami / Hideo Kojima
entries.pitch: Policenauts is a graphic adventure game developed and published by Konami, written and directed by Hideo Kojima. Originally released for the PC-9821 in Japan in 1994, it later came to 3DO, PlayStation, and Sega Saturn. Set in the mid-21st century, it follows Jonathan Ingram, an astronaut who was presumed dead after an accident at a space colony sent him drifting into space for 25 years in cryosleep. Recovered and revived, Ingram returns to Earth only to find his ex-wife has remarried—and then is murdered. Now a private investigator in Los Angeles, he travels to the space colony "Beyond Coast" to investigate her murder, uncovering a dark conspiracy involving illegal organ trafficking. The game is notable for its cinematic production values, blending anime-style cel animation with a narrative that combines hard science fiction with buddy-cop and noir detective tropes. Kojima conceived the game during development of Snatcher (1988) and wanted to explore how living in space might affect human society—medically, socially, and politically.

entries.title: Polygon
entries.creator: Anatoly Petrov (director), Sever Gansovsky (story)
entries.pitch: Polygon (also known as Proving Ground) is a 1977 Soviet animated science fiction short film directed by Anatoly Petrov and produced by the legendary Soyuzmultfilm studio. Based on a story by Sever Gansovsky, this 10-minute animated short uses a distinctive animation technique called "photographica" - featuring two celluloid layers for each character with special color schemes and deliberately out-of-focus layering to create three-dimensional depth without CGI. The film presents a dark anti-war parable set in a not-too-distant future where a grieving professor invents a mind-reading automated tank capable of detecting human hostility - with devastating consequences. The film won First Prize at the Yerevan Film Festival (1978) and was officially selected for the Oberhausen Film Festival (1979).

entries.title: Possible Worlds
entries.creator: Robert Lepage
entries.pitch: Possible Worlds is a mind-bending 2000 Canadian film adapted from John Mighton's acclaimed stage play, directed by Robert Lepage. The film follows George Barber, a mathematician who experiences strange recurring dreams and keeps encountering the same woman named Joyce at a bar—except in each encounter, she seems to be a different person with different memories. Meanwhile, a neuroscientist is conducting mysterious experiments connected to a serial killer who has been stealing brains from victims. Through these interwoven narratives, the film explores the nature of consciousness, identity, and whether reality is merely one of many possible worlds.

entries.title: Pretty Women Walking Through the City
entries.creator: Želimir Žilnik (Director)
entries.pitch:
Pretty Women Walking Through the City (original title: Lijepe žene prolaze kroz grad) is a 1986 Yugoslav post-apocalyptic science fiction film directed by Želimir Žilnik, one of the most prominent figures of the Yugoslav Black Wave cinema movement. Set in Belgrade in the year 2041, the film presents a haunting vision of a future Yugoslavia that has collapsed into environmental decay and social fragmentation. The story follows a group of elderly men attempting to raise young girls in the traditional values of their ancestors, while the world around them has deteriorated into a desolate wasteland.

What makes this film remarkable is its prophetic nature—Žilnik made this film in 1986, just years before the actual breakup of Yugoslavia, and the film uncannily predicted the nationalist tensions and social disintegration that would tear the nation apart in the early 1990s. The film was produced as part of a wave of Yugoslav cinema exploring socio-political criticisms, and it stands as a chilling artifact that anticipated one of the most violent dissolutions of a modern state.

entries.title: Prey
entries.creator: Arkane Austin / Bethesda Softworks
entries.pitch:
Prey is a 2017 first-person shooter and immersive sim developed by Arkane Austin, set in an alternate timeline where mankind built orbital research stations following an accelerated Space Race. Players assume the role of Morgan Yu, a scientist aboard the Talos I space station, who wakes to find the facility overrun by the Typhon—an hostile alien species with both physical and psychic powers. What begins as a survival horror experience gradually unfolds into a larger mystery about Morgan's identity, the nature of the Typhon, and the choices humanity makes in pursuit of knowledge.

The game draws heavily from classic immersive sims like System Shock and Deus Ex, offering players multiple approaches to every situation. Morgan can acquire both human weapons and alien abilities (called Neuromods), allowing for creative problem-solving and traversal. The entire game takes place aboard Talos I, a single continuous space station that players explore in true Metroidvania fashion—returning to previously inaccessible areas with new abilities.

entries.title: Prince Bayaya
entries.creator: Jiří Trnka
entries.pitch: Prince Bayaya (Bajaja) is a 1950 Czechoslovak animated feature film directed by Jiří Trnka, one of the founding fathers of European animation. Often called "the Walt Disney of Eastern Europe," Trnka created this film using intricate puppet animation combined with hand-drawn elements, crafting a visually stunning fairy tale based on a story by Božena Němcová, the most famous Czech children's writer. The film follows a poor half-orphan named Bayaya who discovers his destiny when summoned by his deceased mother, trapped in purgatory as a white horse. Bayaya must journey to a kingdom where three princesses await sacrifice to dragons and prove himself worthy through acts of courage and compassion. The film won the prestigious Golden Leopard at the 1954 Locarno International Film Festival, establishing Czech animation as a major artistic force on the world stage.

entries.title: Prince Planet
entries.creator: Sato Ōkura (director), TCJ (studio)
entries.pitch: Prince Planet is one of the earliest Japanese anime television series, originally titled "Planet Boy Papi" (遊星少年パピイ, Yūsei Shōnen Papī). The series follows a member of the Universal Peace Corps from the planet Radion who is sent to Earth on a mission to determine if humanity qualifies for membership in the Galactic Union of Worlds. Adopting the identity of an Earth boy named Bobby, he joins forces with allies including a wrestler named Dan Dynamo and a magician named AjiBaba to fight alien and terrestrial forces of evil. Produced by TCJ (now Eiken), the 52-episode monochrome series was notable for being one of the first heavily merchandised anime shows in Japan, with the Papi logo appearing on various products including shoes and candy prizes.

entries.title: Prince of Space
entries.creator: Tatsuo Umemiya (star), Toei Company
entries.pitch:
Prince of Space is a 1959 Japanese tokusatsu superhero feature film that represents an early ancestor of the giant monster and special effects films Japan would become famous for worldwide. Produced by Toei Company, the film stars Tatsuo Umemiya as the titular Prince of Space, a masked superhero who defends Earth from alien invaders.

The story centers on the villainous Dictator Phantom of the planet Krangkor, who arrives on Earth seeking to steal Dr. Makin's revolutionary new rocket fuel formula. With his henchmen, Phantom threatens global domination unless the scientist hands over his discovery. Prince of Space must use his superhuman abilities, wand-like laser gun, and advanced spaceship to stop the alien dictator and protect humanity.

The film has achieved cult status in the West largely due to its appearance on Mystery Science Theater 3000, where its campy production values, distinctive villain costumes, and earnest storytelling have provided endless entertainment. The English dub compiled two Japanese theatrical features released a week apart in 1959.

entries.title: Princess Knight
entries.creator: Osamu Tezuka
entries.pitch:
Princess Knight (Ribon no Kishi) is a pioneering 1967 anime series by Osamu Tezuka that follows Sapphire, a young princess born with both a boy's heart and a girl's heart. To inherit the throne of Silverland where only males may rule, she must pretend to be a prince while secretly longing to be herself.

The series was inspired by the all-female Takarazuka Revue, where women perform both male and female roles. Tezuka transposed this theatrical tradition into manga and anime, creating one of the first works to explore gender identity through a female superhero lens. At night, Sapphire dons a Zorro-style mask to fight crime as the Phantom Knight.

This 52-episode series launched the World Masterpiece Theater and established countless trends in shōjo manga that followed. It balances adventure, romance, and fairy tale fantasy while quietly questioning the rigid gender expectations of 1960s Japan.

entries.title: Princess Mononoke
entries.pitch:
Princess Mononoke is a 1997 Japanese animated epic fantasy film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki of Studio Ghibli. Set in Muromachi-period Japan, the film follows Ashitaka, a young Emishi prince who journeys west to find a cure for a curse inflicted on his arm while defending his village from a demon. He becomes embroiled in a conflict between the forest gods and a nearby iron-mining town led by Lady Eboshi, as well as San, a human girl raised by wolves.

The film explores themes of environmentalism, industrialization, and the complex relationship between humanity and nature. It was the first Studio Ghibli film to gain significant international distribution and remains one of the most acclaimed animated films ever made.

entries.title: Probudím se včera
entries.creator: Miloslav Šmídmajer
entries.pitch:
In this Czech time-travel comedy, a forty-something loser gets a chance to rewrite his own history. When Petr Kovář discovers a laboratory offering one-way trips to the past, he leaps at the opportunity to return to June 1989 — not to prevent a catastrophe or save the world, but simply to win back Eliška, the girl who got away in high school.

There\'s just one catch: he arrives in the body of his eighteen-year-old self, complete with all the wisdom, cynicism, and regret of four decades. The result is a fish-out-of-water comedy that uses time travel as a lens to examine what we\'d really do with a second chance — and whether we\'d even recognize ourselves if we got it.

Part coming-of-age story, part nostalgic romp through the final days of communist Czechoslovakia, "Probudím se včera" balances humor with genuine heart. Petr\'s attempts to use foreknowledge to "win" Eliška lead to predictably unpredictable results.

entries.title: Promare
entries.creator: Hiroyuki Imaishi (Director), Trigger (Studio)
entries.pitch: Promare is a 2019 Japanese animated science fiction action film directed by Hiroyuki Imaishi and produced by Trigger. Set in a world ravaged by the "Great World Blaze" thirty years prior—where spontaneous human combustion killed half the population and left some survivors with pyrokinetic abilities known as the "Burnish"—the film follows Galo Thymos, a newly recruited member of Burning Rescue, a firefighting organization in the futuristic city of Promepolis. When Galo confronts the Mad Burnish, a group of radical pyrokinetic terrorists, he encounters Lio Fotia, their leader, and uncovers a vast conspiracy involving the city's governor Kray Foresight, who plans to use the Burnish's powers for human experimentation and to flee Earth as the planet faces destruction from within its core.

entries.title: Prophecies of Nostradamus
entries.creator: Toshio Masuda
entries.pitch:
In 1999, biologist Dr. Ryogen Nishiyama is called to analyze strange phenomena—mutant slugs, children with strange abilities after drinking contaminated water, and massive ice formations near Hawaii. As a prophet of Nostradamus's apocalyptic warnings, he races to uncover the truth before global collapse arrives.

This 1974 Japanese disaster film was Toho's second major entry in the genre following Japan Sinks. Based on Ben Goto's bestseller novel, it blends environmental anxiety with supernatural prophecy, delivering a stark warning about humanity's ecological destruction.

entries.title: Przekładaniec
entries.creator: Andrzej Wajda (director), Stanisław Lem (screenplay)
entries.pitch: Przekładaniec (literally "Layer Cake" or "Sandwich") is a 1968 Polish short science fiction comedy film directed by Andrzej Wajda, based on a screenplay by legendary Polish sci-fi author Stanisław Lem. This marks Wajda's first comedy, first television production, and only venture into science fiction—a remarkable collaboration between two of Poland's greatest artistic talents. The film explores the darkly humorous philosophical dilemmas surrounding organ transplantation and questions of personal identity: if you receive organs from another person, are you still yourself? What happens when half your body comes from someone else?

entries.title: Pulgasari
entries.pitch:
Pulgasari is a 1986 North Korean kaiju monster film, notable as one of the most ambitious productions ever attempt

ed by the reclusive Stalinist state. Directed by South Korean filmmaker Shin Sang-ok during his forced captivity in North Korea, the film represents a fascinating collision between Eastern Bloc cinema and Japanese tokusatsu tradition. The story unfolds in feudal Korea during the late Goryeo dynasty, where a blacksmith named Takse creates a small metal-eating monster to protect oppressed peasants from a tyrannical king. When Takse is starved to death by the royal authorities, his daughter Ami brings the creature to life with her blood, and Pulgasari grows into a massive beast that devours metal weapons and helps the rebellion overthrow the monarchy. However, the monster's insatiable hunger eventually threatens the very people it sought to save, leading to a tragic conclusion. The film was produced with an estimated budget of ¥200-300 million ($2-3 million), making it one of the most expensive North Korean films ever made, and involved collaboration with Japanese Toho Studios and Beijing Film Studio.

entries.title: Pumzi
entries.creator: Wanuri Kahiu
entries.pitch: Pumzi is a groundbreaking Kenyan science-fiction short film that represents a landmark in Africanfuturism. Directed by Wanuri Kahiu and funded through the Focus Features Africa First short film program, the 21-minute film premiered at the 2010 Sundance Film Festival as part of its New African Cinema program. The title "Pumzi" is Swahili for "Breath," and the film presents a haunting vision of post-apocalyptic East Africa set 35 years after World War III—referred to as The Water War. The film explores themes of environmentalism, technological control, and human resilience through the story of Asha, a curator at the Virtual Natural History Museum who receives a mysterious package containing soil that may indicate life still exists outside her controlled community.

entries.title: Puszka Pandory
entries.creator: Marcin Borkowski
entries.pitch: Puszka Pandory (Pandora's Box) is a pioneering Polish text adventure game created in 1986 by Marcin Borkowski for the ZX Spectrum computer. Set in a post-apocalyptic world, the player controls a protagonist sent to investigate an uninhabited island where a deadly missile system threatens to destroy what remains of humanity. The game features 1600 explorable locations across the island, making it one of the largest text adventure worlds of its era. Released during Poland's communist era under severe technical constraints—the ZX Spectrum had only 48 kilobytes of memory—Borkowski created the game as a technical challenge to push beyond the limitations of the platform. Remarkably, it was the first Polish video game to have its description appear in the Polish press, and Borkowski himself wrote the first extensive review under the pseudonym "Karol B. Mirowski."

entries.title: Quake 4
entries.creator: Raven Software
entries.pitch:
Quake 4 is a 2005 first-person shooter that continues the story from Quake II, pitting players against the Strogg—a cyborg alien race on their home planet Stroggos. Developed by Raven Software and published by Activision, the game uses the id Tech 4 engine and emphasizes both single-player campaign and multiplayer modes. The player takes on the role of Corporal Matthew Kane of the Rhino Squad, leading the invasion of Stroggos following the events of Quake II where the Makron was destroyed.

The game is notable for its intense military sci-fi action, graphic depiction of the "stroggification" process (where humans are captured and transformed into cyborg soldiers), and continuation of the dark, violent aesthetic established in the Quake series. While Quake 4 received moderate reviews, it remains a significant entry in the early 2000s military sci-fi shooter landscape.

entries.title: Quantum Break
entries.creator: Remedy Entertainment
entries.pitch:
Quantum Break is a 2016 action-adventure third-person shooter developed by Finnish studio Remedy Entertainment. The game centers on Jack Joyce, who gains time manipulation powers after a failed time-machine experiment, as he battles his former friend Paul Serene over preventing an apocalyptic "End of Time." What sets Quantum Break apart is its unique blend of traditional video game gameplay with integrated live-action television episodes, creating a transmedia experience where player choices affect the narrative.

The game was originally conceived as a sequel to Remedy's earlier title Alan Wake, but Microsoft redirected the project toward a new intellectual property focused on time travel. The result is a story-driven action experience that combines cinematic storytelling with interactive gameplay, featuring performances by actors like Aidan Gillen and Lance Reddick in both the game and the accompanying TV segments.

entries.title: Quatermass and the Pit
entries.creator: Nigel Kneale
entries.pitch:
Quatermass and the Pit is a groundbreaking British science fiction serial broadcast live by the BBC in six episodes from December 1958 to January 1959. The story begins when workmen excavating a site in Knightsbridge, London discover a strange skull and what initially appears to be an unexploded bomb. Professor Bernard Quatermass of the British Rocket Group becomes involved in the investigation when it becomes apparent that the object is an ancient alien spacecraft. What follows is a terrifying exploration of human evolution, psychic abilities, and the dark origins of human aggression.

The serial is celebrated as one of the most influential works of British television science fiction, praised for its sophisticated themes, allegorical depth, and groundbreaking special effects. It has been cited as a major influence on works ranging from Doctor Who to Stephen King's novels and John Carpenter's films.

entries.title: Quintet
entries.creator: Robert Altman
entries.pitch: In the frozen aftermath of a second ice age, seal hunter Essex wanders the blank tundra with his pregnant companion Vivia, searching for his brother. When tragedy strikes and Vivia is killed in an apartment bombing, Essex finds himself drawn into the dark heart of a dying world: the Hotel Electra, a gambling resort where the ultra-wealthy play "Quintet"—a deadly board game where virtual kills translate to real executions. As Essex assumes a dead man's identity and enters this tournament of survival, he discovers that the game is more than entertainment—it's a metaphor for humanity's final descent into nihilism. Director Robert Altman crafts a haunting, ambiguous meditation on civilization's end through non-linear storytelling and a oppressive, freezing atmosphere.

entries.title: R-Type
entries.creator: Irem
entries.pitch: R-Type is a 1987 side-scrolling shoot 'em up arcade game that tasks players with piloting the R-9 "Arrowhead" starship to defeat the Bydo, a mysterious alien race threatening humanity. Developed by Irem and known for its striking visuals inspired by H.R. Giger's alien designs and the film Aliens, R-Type became a landmark in the shoot 'em up genre. The game introduced innovative gameplay mechanics, including the "Force" system—a detachible orb that serves as both a protective shield and a powerful weapon. Players must navigate through eight challenging levels, memorizing enemy patterns and mastering the ship's various weapons to survive. The game's difficulty was notorious, but its satisfying combat and atmospheric design earned it critical acclaim and a devoted fanbase.

entries.title: R.U.R.
entries.creator: Karel Čapek
entries.pitch: R.U.R. (Rossumovi Univerzální Roboti) is a landmark 1920 science fiction play by Czech writer Karel Čapek that introduced the word "robot" to the English language and to science fiction as a genre. Set in the early 21st century on a remote island factory, the play depicts a world where artificially created beings called Robots—synthetic organic workers indistinguishable from humans—have become essential to global industry. The drama explores themes of industrialization, exploitation, and the ultimate consequences of treating sentient beings as mere property. R.U.R. was enormously influential, translated into thirty languages by 1923 and staging productions across Europe and North America, cementing Čapek's place as one of the foundational figures of science fiction.

entries.title: Radar Men from the Moon
entries.creator: Fred C. Brannon (Director)
entries.pitch: Radar Men from the Moon is a 1952 Republic Pictures serial that represents the height of 1950s science fiction serials. The story follows Commando Cody, a civilian researcher and inventor who discovers that Earth is under attack from the Moon. Using his atomic-powered rocket backpack and rocket ship, Cody travels to the Moon to confront Retik, the ruthless ruler who plans to conquer Earth and relocate his entire lunar population using spaceships armed with atomic weapons. This 12-chapter serial combines exciting action, early sci-fi themes, and the classic cliffhanger format that defined the genre during its golden age.

entries.title: Rafadan Tayfa: Göbeklitepe
entries.creator: İsmail Fidan
entries.pitch:
A group of children in Istanbul stumble upon a mysterious artifact connected to the groundbreaking archaeological discovery of Göbeklitepe, one of the world's oldest temples dating back to 9600 BCE. When young Akın receives a strange copper tray from his friend Veysi in Şanlıurfa, the Rafadan Tayfa is drawn into an adventure involving ancient secrets, treasure hunters, and a race against time to protect Turkey's invaluable cultural heritage. The film blends modern children's adventure storytelling with real archaeological discoveries, creating a unique educational entertainment experience.

The animated feature is a spin-off from the popular Turkish children's TV series Rafadan Tayfa, which portrays the mahalle (neighborhood) culture of 1980s and 1990s Turkey. This film takes the beloved characters on an exciting journey through actual Turkish history and archaeology.

entries.title: Raji: An Ancient Epic
entries.creator: Nodding Heads Games
entries.pitch:
Raji: An Ancient Epic is an action-adventure game developed by Nodding Heads Games, a small studio based in Pune, India. Released in 2020, it marks a significant milestone as one of the first major Indian video games to gain international recognition and distribution on mainstream platforms. The game draws heavily from Hindu mythology, incorporating elements from the Mahabharata and Ramayana, and presents players with a visually striking experience inspired by Pahari miniature paintings and the architecture of Rajasthan.

The story follows Raji, an orphaned circus performer whose younger brother Golu is abducted by demons during the festival of Raksha Bandhan. Chosen by the deities Goddess Durga and Lord Vishnu, Raji embarks on a quest to rescue her brother and stop the demon lord Mahabalasura from opening the gates of heaven to destroy the gods. The game was nominated for Best Debut Game at The Game Awards 2020—the first Indian game to achieve such recognition.

entries.title: Raumpatrouille Orion
entries.creator: Rolf Honold, Hans Gottschalk
entries.pitch:
Raumpatrouille – Die phantastischen Abenteuer des Raumschiffes Orion (Space Patrol Orion) is a groundbreaking 1966 West German science fiction television series, the first German sci-fi TV production ever made. Broadcast in seven episodes on ARD from September to December 1966, it achieved remarkable success with audience ratings as high as 56% and garnered numerous reruns over the decades. The series was co-produced with French ORTF Television and has achieved cult status in Germany.

The show follows Commander Cliff Allister McLane and the crew of the starship Orion as they patrol the galaxy in the year 3000-3003, defending Earth against an alien race called the Frogs. Set in a future where nation-states have been dissolved and humanity is united, the series features innovative special effects and a memorable electronic soundtrack by Peter Thomas. Despite its low budget, the production famously improvised set pieces using everyday objects—electric irons, clock pendulums, and designer furniture—as futuristic technology.

entries.title: Raumpatrouille – Die phantastischen Abenteuer des Raumschiffes Orion
entries.creator: Rolf Honold, Hans Gottschalk (writers) | Theo Mezger, Michael Braun (directors)
entries.pitch: Raumpatrouille – Die phantastischen Abenteuer des Raumschiffes Orion (Space Patrol Orion) is a pioneering West German science fiction television series that aired in 1966. It was the first German SF TV series and became a massive hit with audience ratings as high as 56%. The series follows Commander Cliff Allister McLane and the crew of the starship Orion as they patrol the galaxy in the year 3000, defending Earth against the mysterious alien conquerors known as the Frogs. Despite being demoted to mundane space patrol duties, McLane and his crew repeatedly save humanity from various threats, combining space adventure with political intrigue and social commentary. The series is notable for its innovative special effects and distinctive electronic soundtrack by Peter Thomas, which became iconic in German popular culture.

entries.title: Razzennest
entries.creator: Johannes Grenzfurthner
entries.pitch:
Razzennest is a 2022 Austrian supernatural horror film that defies conventional genre boundaries. Written and directed by Johannes Grenzfurthner, the film takes place in a Los Angeles sound studio where South African filmmaker Manus Oosthuizen and film critic Babette Cruickshank meet to record an audio commentary for Manus's new documentary about the Thirty Years' War. As they record, strange incidents begin occurring—their crew members are possessed by the ghosts of soldiers and peasants from 1645, and history begins to repeat itself in horrifying ways.

The film is noted for its unique meta structure—it's essentially a film about making a film, combining elements of satire, tragicomedy, drama, horror, and ghost story. It serves as the second installment in Grenzfurthner's trilogy, following Masking Threshold (2021) and preceding Solvent (2024). The film premiered at Fantastic Fest 2022 and received positive critical response, holding a 93% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

entries.title: Read or Die
entries.creator: Hideyuki Kurata
entries.pitch: Read or Die is a 3-episode OVA (2001-2002) based on Hideyuki Kurata's novels and manga, serving as a wild sci-fi spy thriller that follows Yomiko Readman, a bibliophilic agent of the British Library's Special Operations Division. Yomiko possesses an extraordinary supernatural ability to manipulate paper into any form—she can transform documents into weapons, create paper clones, and use paper as everything from shields to transportation. When historical figures have been cloned by a mysterious group called the I-Jin, Yomiko and her fellow agents must stop their plot to broadcast Beethoven's "Death Symphony" globally—a sound frequency designed to cause mass suicide. The OVA blends high-octane action with literary flair, featuring showdowns with clones of samurai Gennai Hiraga, explorer Otto Lilienthal, and other historical icons, all while exploring themes of knowledge, obsession, and the power of stories.

entries.title: Reah: Face the Unknown
entries.creator: Project Two Interactive / Black Friar (Detalion, LK Avalon)
entries.pitch: Reah: Face the Unknown is a 1998 Polish first-person puzzle adventure game that transports players to a distant planet where a human colony has been established to investigate a mysterious alien artifact. Developed by Project Two Interactive and Black Friar, published by Detalion and LK Avalon, the game was originally created in Polish before being translated into English and multiple other languages. It garnered attention for its ambitious scope, beautiful pre-rendered graphics, and non-linear gameplay that drew obvious comparisons to the Myst series. The game was notable for being one of the largest adventure games released at the time, with the DVD version requiring 10 gigabytes of storage—a massive undertaking for 1998. With over 150 scenarios and a supernatural-sounding musical landscape, Reah challenges players to solve intricate puzzles while uncovering the secrets of the alien artifact that could change humanity's understanding of the universe.

entries.title: Red Matter
entries.creator: Vertical Robot
entries.pitch: Red Matter is a 2018 sci-fi virtual reality puzzle game developed by the Spanish studio Vertical Robot. The player assumes the role of Agent Epsilon, an agent of the Atlantic Union who crash-lands on Rhea, one of Saturn's moons, to investigate a top-secret Volgravian military research facility. The game features meticulously detailed retro-futuristic environments and a Cold War-inspired setting between two fictional superpowers—the Atlantic Union and the People's Republic of Volgravia. As a VR title, Red Matter emphasizes immersion, allowing players to physically interact with objects, solve puzzles, and explore the atmospheric abandoned station using motion controllers. The game received critical acclaim for its visuals and world-building, though some critics noted that certain puzzles could be frustratingly opaque.

entries.title: Rendezvous with Rama
entries.creator: Telarium
entries.pitch: Rendezvous with Rama is a 1984 interactive fiction adventure game developed by Telarium (a subsidiary of Spinnaker Software) in cooperation with legendary science fiction author Arthur C. Clarke. Based on Clarke's acclaimed 1973 novel "Rendezvous with Rama," this game represents one of the earliest examples of a major science fiction intellectual property being adapted into a video game format. Players navigate a meticulously crafted text-based adventure exploring one of science fiction's most iconic alien artifacts—a massive, cylindrical spacecraft discovered entering the solar system in the early 22nd century. The game was released for platforms including Apple II, Commodore 64, MS-DOS, and MSX2, representing the cutting edge of interactive fiction technology of its era. German reviewers at the time recognized the complexity of the storyline and the various possibilities of interaction with non-player characters, praising the game's sophisticated narrative design.

entries.title: Reptilicus
entries.creator: Poul Bang (Danish version), Sidney W. Pink (English version)
entries.pitch: Reptilicus is a Danish-American science fiction monster film produced in 1961, notable as one of Denmark's first major contributions to the sci-fi horror genre. The film was directed by Poul Bang for the Danish version and by Sidney W. Pink for the English-language version, both shot simultaneously with nearly identical casts. The story follows the discovery of a massive prehistoric reptile tail in Lapland, which is transported to Copenhagen's aquarium where it mysteriously regenerates into a full-grown monster that terrorizes the Danish countryside and capital city. While the film is famously campy—with its monster appearing as a man in a reptilian suit—it has achieved cult status as an example of European monster cinema from the early 1960s. The film represents an interesting Cold War-era take on atomic age anxieties, exploring themes of scientific hubris and the dangers of awakening ancient forces.

entries.title: Restore Point
entries.creator: Robert Hloz (Director)
entries.pitch:
Restore Point (Bod obnovy) is a 2023 Czech cyberpunk science fiction thriller set in 2041 Central Europe, where society has granted citizens a constitutional right to be revived after unnatural death—provided they have routinely backed up their brain data every 48 hours. This innovative "restore point" technology is operated by the Institute of Restoration, offering resurrection to those who comply with the backup regime.

When the scientist who developed the recovery technology, David Kurlstat, and his wife are brutally murdered, detective Emma "Em" Trochinowska is assigned to the case. She is puzzled that Kurlstat, of all people, hasn't had a valid recovery point with which to be revived—leaving his murder seemingly permanent. As she investigates, she uncovers a group called "River of Life" who violently oppose the "unnatural" resurrection technology through terrorist attacks, believing death should remain final.

The film marks the directorial debut of Robert Hloz and has been described by critics as the "Czech Blade Runner" for its retro-futuristic cyberpunk aesthetic. It was co-produced by the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland, and Serbia, and premiered at the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival in 2023.

entries.title: Resurrection
entries.creator: Bi Gan (Director)
entries.pitch: Resurrection is a 2025 epic science fiction drama from Chinese filmmaker Bi Gan, whose previous work Kaili Blues and Long Day's Journey Into Night established him as a master of visual poetry and temporal manipulation. Set in a future where humanity has given up dreaming in exchange for longevity, the film follows a woman who tracks down a mysterious "Deliriant" - a dying monster who hides inside movies to continue dreaming. Through the lost techniques of cinema, she helps him replay four dreams spanning 100 years of his past life before he dies. The film is divided into six segments, each corresponding to one of the six senses in Buddhist thought: sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch, and mind. Winner of the Prix Spécial at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival.

entries.title: Rhea Gall Force
entries.creator: Katsuhito Akiyama (director), Artmic/AIC (studio)
entries.pitch:
Rhea Gall Force is a 1989 Japanese anime science fiction film that serves as a pivotal entry in the Gall Force metaseries. Set in an alternate timeline within the Gall Force universe, this film takes place after the events of "Gall Force: Eternal Story" and "Gall Force 3: Stardust War," but before the "Earth Chapter" arc. Unlike the earlier entries that focused on the centuries-long war between the Solnoids and Paranoids, Rhea Gall Force shifts the setting to near-future Earth, exploring a completely different scenario where humanity discovers alien technology on the Moon that leads to catastrophic consequences.

The film presents a haunting vision of a humanity on the brink of extinction, forced to abandon Earth and flee to Mars in the face of an enemy they created. This entry represents a bold creative departure for the series, moving from space opera to a more grounded post-apocalyptic narrative that explores themes of technological hubris, war, and survival.

entries.title: Ring
entries.creator: Arxel Tribe
entries.pitch:
Ring (subtitled "The Legend of the Nibelungen") is a 1998 point-and-click adventure game that reimagines Richard Wagner's four-opera cycle Der Ring des Nibelungen through a surrealist science fiction lens. Developed by Slovenian studio Arxel Tribe, the game presents the epic Norse mythology tale as a story set in the 40th century, where humanity has been enslaved by an alien race that destroyed Earth millennia ago. The player controls ISH, one of the last surviving humans, who is tasked by these aliens to experience the story of the Nibelungen in hopes that it will awaken humanity's lost creative spirit—or lead to their downfall through lust for power.

The game features music from Vienna Philharmonic performances conducted by Georg Solti and artwork by renowned French comic artist Philippe Druillet. Players navigate through four playable chapters (representing the four operas) in any order, with an asteroid serving as the central hub. Each chapter casts the player as a different character from the Ring cycle: Alberich, Loge, Siegmund, and Brünnhilde. The narrative explores themes of power, creativity, and redemption through this unique fusion of classical opera and science fiction.

entries.title: Rise of the Dragon
entries.creator: Dynamix / Sierra On-Line
entries.pitch: Rise of the Dragon is a 1990 graphic adventure game that marked Dynamix's venture into the cyberpunk genre. Set in a dystopian Los Angeles of 2053, players take on the role of William "Blade" Hunter, a former LAPD officer turned private detective. When the mayor's rebellious daughter Chandra is found dead and horribly mutated after experimenting with a new designer drug called MTZ, Blade is called upon to track down those responsible. The game combines detective work, strategy puzzles, and action sequences, featuring a time-management system where players must complete their investigation within three in-game days or lose. Originally released for DOS, it was later ported to Amiga, Mac OS, and Sega CD.

entries.title: Roadside Picnic
entries.creator: Arkady and Boris Strugatsky
entries.pitch: In the wake of an enigmatic alien visitation that left six mysterious "Zones" scattered across Earth, humanity struggles to comprehend what was left behind. Roadside Picnic follows Redrick Schuhart—a downtrodden worker who sneaks into the forbidden Zone to retrieve alien artifacts for profit—through a day in his life in the decaying industrial town of Harmont. The novel is less about the aliens themselves than about how humanity copes with the knowledge that we are not alone in the universe—and that the visitors cared nothing for us. Raw, gritty, and profoundly philosophical, this is Soviet SF at its most haunting: a story about the emptiness of modern life, the corrupting nature of hope, and the impossible question of whether humanity can ever truly understand what lies beyond our world.

entries.title: Robot Carnival
entries.creator: Multiple Directors (Katsuhiro Otomo, Koji Morimoto, Hidetoshi Ōmori, Yasuomi Umetsu, Takashi Nakamura, Hiroyuki Kitakubo, Hiroyuki Kitazume, Mao Lamdo)
entries.pitch: Robot Carnival is a groundbreaking 1987 Japanese anthology OVA featuring nine distinct short films by different animators, each exploring robots and humanity's relationship with machines. From the surreal to the comedic to the deeply melancholic, this collection showcases emerging talent who would later become legends in the anime industry—including Katsuhiro Otomo (director of Akira). The film ranges from a mad scientist accidentally killing himself while teaching his creation to dance, to a post-apocalyptic android's journey to rescue its human companion, to a surreal tale of a traveling carnival of robots destroying a desert village. With music by the legendary Joe Hisaishi, Robot Carnival is a time capsule of late-80s Japanese animation creativity—a must-see for anyone interested in the evolution of anime as an art form.

entries.title: Robotrix
entries.creator: Jamie Luk Kin-ming (Director)
entries.pitch:
Robotrix is a 1991 Hong Kong science fiction exploitation film that blends cyberpunk themes with erotic thriller elements. The film follows a psychotic scientist who transfers his mind into a cyborg after killing a female police officer, only for her mind to also be uploaded into a powerful cyborg. The two become entangled in a cat-and-mouse game as the cyborg police officer pursues her tormentor through the neon-lit streets of Hong Kong.

The film was produced by Golden Harvest and directed by Jamie Luk Kin-ming, featuring Amy Yip in one of her most prominent roles. While primarily an exploitation film known for its adult content, Robotrix has gained recognition as an early example of Hong Kong cyberpunk cinema, exploring themes of identity, consciousness, and the boundaries between human and machine.

entries.title: Rogue Moon
entries.creator: Algis Budrys
entries.pitch: In 1960, legendary science fiction writer Algis Budrys delivered this haunting meditation on humanity's relationship with death and identity. When a massive alien artifact is discovered on the Moon, the U.S. Navy recruits Dr. Edward Hawks to lead a top-secret project investigating the mysterious structure—which kills anyone who enters it. Hawks develops a revolutionary matter transmission system that allows explorers on Earth to share the experiences of their duplicates on the Moon, experiencing death second-hand as their clones navigate the alien labyrinth. The story follows Al Barker, a thrill-seeker who becomes the first to retain his sanity after dying in the artifact, as he pushes further into the structure with each iteration. Part hard science fiction puzzle, part existential meditation, Rogue Moon explores what it means to face death, create identity, and transcend the boundaries of human existence.

entries.title: Roly Poly
entries.creator: Andrzej Wajda
entries.pitch: Roly Poly (Polish: Przekładaniec) is a 1968 Polish short science fiction comedy film directed by Andrzej Wajda, based on a screenplay by Stanisław Lem. The 35-minute film, made for Polish television, explores the identity crisis that emerges when organ transplantation becomes widespread. The story follows rally driver Ryszard Fox, who suffers terrible accidents and receives numerous transplants from the deceased—eventually leaving him as a patchwork of different people's body parts. The film is notable for being one of the rare Lem adaptations that satisfied the author himself, who praised Wajda's direction and called it the only film adaptation of his works that completely pleased him.

entries.title: Roots Search
entries.pitch: Roots Search is a 1986 Japanese OVA that borrows heavily from Ridley Scott's Alien while adding its own surreal, psychological horror elements. The story follows a research crew stationed on a space station who discover a desolate ship drifting in hyperspace with only one survivor, Assistant Captain Buzz. When the crew decides to investigate the alien corpse found aboard, they unleash a psychic entity that haunts them with visions of their past sins, slowly picking them off one by one. The alien claims to be sent by God to punish mankind for its transgressions, leading to a claustrophobic cat-and-mouse game aboard the station.

entries.title: Roy del espacio
entries.creator: Héctor López Carmona, Rafael Ángel Gil, Ulises Pérez Aguirre (Directors)
entries.pitch:
Roy del espacio (English: Roy of Space) is a 1983 Mexican animated science fiction film and one of the first feature-length Mexican animated films ever made. Produced from 1979 to 1982, the film follows the titular character Roy, who together with Dr. Faz and psychologist Elena, travels to a distant planet and faces an evil emperor who wants to conquer the Earth. The story includes robot fights, space battles, and a bit of romance, following a classic adventure structure reminiscent of 1930s serials like Flash Gordon.

The film premiered on March 3, 1983 in Mexico City theaters but was quickly withdrawn due to poor public acceptance. Retrospective critics have classified it as an example of artistic ineptitude, and it was considered a lost film until November 2025 when restoration work was announced. Despite its reception, it represents an important milestone in Mexican animation history as one of the first feature-length animated sci-fi films from Mexico.

entries.title: Royal Space Force: The Wings of Honnêamise
entries.creator: Hiroyuki Yamaga (Director), Gainax
entries.pitch: In an alternate world bearing an uncanny resemblance to Earth, a disengaged young man named Shirotsugh Lhadatt has given up on his dreams of becoming a fighter pilot and instead drifts through his life in the Royal Space Force—a fledgling space program demoralized by repeated failures. Everything changes when he meets Riquinni, a devout young woman who preaches on the streets about humanity's fallen nature and the stolen fire of knowledge. Inspired by her quiet conviction, Shirotsugh volunteers for humanity's first orbital mission, becoming the pilot of a desperate last-ditch attempt to launch a person into space. Set against a backdrop of government corruption, war, and public indifference, this is a deeply human story about finding meaning beyond oneself.

entries.title: Running Against Time
entries.creator: Bruce Seth Green
entries.pitch:
A time-traveling professor races against the clock in this obscure 1990 sci-fi TV movie. David Rhodes, a college history professor, is haunted by his older brother Chris's death in Vietnam in 1966. When his girlfriend Laura interviews an eccentric physics professor about revolutionary time travel theories, David discovers a way to travel back to the 1960s. He embarks on a desperate mission: prevent his brother's death and stop the assassination of President John F. Kennedy.

But trapped in a time warp with no way back to his present, David finds himself unable to effect any change. The film explores the paradoxes of time travel and the weight of history itself.

entries.title: Running Delilah
entries.creator: Richard Franklin
entries.pitch:
Top agent Delilah dies in a risky mission against weapons dealer Kasharian. But death is not the end for her — she is revived using high-tech medicine and artificial body parts, transformed into an invincible superwoman. She returns to continue her fight against Kasharian, whose newest deal includes plutonium from Russia.

This 1994 made-for-television science fiction thriller was intended as the pilot episode for a TV series, starring Kim Cattrall and Billy Zane. Directed by Richard Franklin, it explores the intersection of human emotion and cybernetic enhancement.

Running Delilah offers a compelling take on the bionic woman archetype, blending Cold War intrigue with emerging cyberpunk themes. While the concept may echo RoboCop, itcarries its own identity through strong performances and a tense narrative.

entries.title: S.O.S. Coast Guard
entries.creator: Alan James, William Witney (Republic Pictures)
entries.pitch: S.O.S. Coast Guard is a 1937 Republic film serial that blends science fiction with action-adventure. The story follows Coast Guard Lieutenant Terry Kent as he battles the mad scientist Boroff, who has invented a deadly "disintegrator gas" made from the rare radioactive substance Arnatite. Boroff plans to sell this superweapon to the highest bidder in the fictional country of Morovania, but Terry opposes him—both professionally and personally, as Boroff killed Terry's brother during his escape attempt. Alongside two intrepid reporters, Terry pursues Boroff to his cave-based hideout in a race against time to prevent the weapon from falling into the wrong hands.

entries.title: S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Shadow of Chernobyl
entries.creator: GSC Game World
entries.pitch:
S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Shadow of Chernobyl is a first-person shooter developed by Ukrainian studio GSC Game World, set in an alternate reality where a second disaster of mysterious origin occurred at the Chernobyl exclusion zone in 2006. The game is heavily inspired by the 1971 novella Roadside Picnic and Andrei Tarkovsky's 1979 film Stalker, borrowing terminology and atmosphere from those works.

Players take on the role of the Marked One, an amnesiac survivor who must navigate the deadly "Zone" surrounding Chernobyl—now a hazardous wasteland filled with strange anomalies, mutated creatures, and warring factions of stalkers, scientists, and military personnel. The player must uncover the mysteries of the Zone while searching for the enigmatic figure known as Strelok.

entries.title: SOMA
entries.creator: Frictional Games
entries.pitch:
SOMA is a 2015 survival horror game developed by Frictional Games, set in an underwater research facility called PATHOS-II in the year 2104. The player assumes the role of Simon Jarrett, who awakens at the facility after apparently traveling through time from 2015—where he survived a car accident—only to discover that a comet has devastated Earth, leaving PATHOS-II as humanity's last known outpost. What begins as a conventional horror exploration gradually transforms into a philosophical meditation on consciousness, identity, and what it means to be human.

Unlike typical horror games that emphasize combat, SOMA strips away weapons entirely, forcing players into stealth and evasion. The atmosphere is suffused with dread—not from monsters alone, but from existential questions that accumulate as Simon explores the facility's dark corridors and discovers the truth about its former crew, the rogue AI called the WAU, and his own impossible existence. The game received widespread acclaim for its narrative depth, thematic ambition, and masterful atmosphere.

entries.title: Sabash Satyam
entries.creator: G. Viswanatham
entries.pitch: Sabash Satyam is a 1969 Indian Telugu-language science fiction film starring Krishna and Rajasree. The film follows Satyam, a young scientist working at his uncle Dayanand's cancer research facility, who falls in love with his cousin Chaya. However, Chaya's family has other plans for her and seeks to separate the couple. In a cruel twist, Chaya's relatives sabotage Satyam's laboratory, causing an accident that renders him completely invisible. Now invisible and unable to prove his identity, Satyam must find a way to become visible again and win back his love before it's too late.

entries.title: Sailboat
entries.creator: R.A. Lafferty
entries.pitch: Sailboat is a whimsical, deeply optimistic tale from the golden age of science fiction that reads like a fever dream of pure joy. The story follows Jonathan Teague, an ordinary man who one day finds an extraordinary sailboat washed up on the shore of Lake Michigan—a boat that can sail not just through water, but through time and space itself. What unfolds is a picaresque adventure across centuries and worlds, as Teague discovers that the universe is far stranger and more magnificent than he ever imagined. Unlike the dark, cautionary tales that dominate SF, Sailboat is suffused with wonder, humor, and a profound sense that magic is real and waiting to be found. It's the kind of story that makes you remember why you first fell in love with science fiction.

entries.title: Santa Claus
entries.creator: René Cardona
entries.pitch: Santa Claus (also known as Santa Claus vs. the Devil) is a 1959 Mexican fantasy film directed by René Cardona. The film has achieved cult status after being featured on Mystery Science Theater 3000 in 1993. In this unique holiday sci-fi, Santa Claus works in outer space at his Toyland castle and must battle a demon named Pitch, sent by Lucifer to ruin Christmas by exposing Santa to the public and turning children evil.

entries.title: Saturn Apartments
entries.creator: Hisae Iwaoka
entries.pitch:
In a distant future, humanity has evacuated Earth to live in a massive ring-shaped structure orbiting 35 kilometers above the planet's surface. Earth has become a protected nature preserve, and the ring city—Saturn Apartments—is stratified into three tiers based on social class: upper levels house the wealthy who can afford clear windows to view Earth and sunlight, middle levels contain everyday workers, and lower levels suffer from darkness and limited resources.

The story follows Mitsu, a young man who has just graduated from school and takes over his father's former job as a window cleaner—a dangerous occupation that involves floating outside the ring in a spacesuit to clean the transparent panels that allow upper-class residents to see the cosmos. Mitsu's father disappeared five years ago during a job, and the truth behind his death becomes a central mystery as Mitsu navigates his new career and learns about the lives of the ring's inhabitants through his work.

entries.title: Save the Green Planet!
entries.creator: Jang Joon-hwan
entries.pitch:
Save the Green Planet! is a 2003 South Korean science fiction black comedy that tells the story of Lee Byeong-gu, a paranoid conspiracy theorist who becomes obsessed with the belief that extraterrestrials from the Andromeda Galaxy are planning to invade Earth. When his mother falls into a coma after being poisoned in a pharmaceutical drug trial, Byeong-gu convinces himself that the company's executive is actually an alien commander who can communicate with the Andromedans during an upcoming lunar eclipse. He kidnaps the executive and holds him hostage in his basement, subjecting him to bizarre tests to prove his alien origins.

The film was a catastrophic box office failure, earning only $15,516 in South Korea, and received limited theatrical release. However, it has since achieved cult classic status both domestically and internationally. Critics praise its unique blend of genres—combining elements of black comedy, psychological thriller, and science fiction—along with its biting satire of corporate greed and government conspiracy theories. The film won multiple awards including Best New Director at the Blue Dragon Film Awards and the Grand Bell Awards, and has gained a devoted following among fans of offbeat Korean cinema.

entries.title: Sayonara Jupiter
entries.creator: Koji Hashimoto, Sakyo Komatsu
entries.pitch:
In the 22nd century, Earth faces an energy crisis as the planet's resources dwindle. A team of Japanese scientists is dispatched to the far edges of the solar system to research new fuel sources, leading them to Jupiter and its mysterious moons. There, they make an astonishing discovery: an ancient alien race that has been waiting for humanity to arrive—and a catastrophic black hole threatening to consume everything in its path.

Directed by Koji Hashimoto and based on Sakyo Komatsu's novel (which won the 1983 Seiun Award), Sayonara Jupiter was conceived as a Japanese response to Stanley Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey, aiming to compete with Hollywood's grand sci-fi tradition. The film blends hard science fiction with philosophical questions about humanity's place in the cosmos.

entries.title: Scanners
entries.creator: Written and directed by David Cronenberg
entries.pitch: In a near-future where corporations hunt for psychic humans called "scanners," a homeless man named Cameron Vale discovers he possesses devastating telepathic and telekinetic powers. Recruited by Dr. Paul Ruth to stop the rogue scanner Darryl Revok—who plans to wage war against the world using an army of newly-born psychic infants—Cameron must master his abilities and confront his own monstrous brother. The film features one of cinema's most iconic head-explosion scenes and explores themes of evolution, corporate control, and the price of power.

entries.title: Scanners Live in Vain
entries.creator: Cordwainer Smith (pen name of Paul Linebarger)
entries.pitch: In a far-future Earth where humanity has retreated underground to escape deadly radiation, a special class of telepaths called "scanners" serves as the sole link between isolated human settlements. These men and women possess the ability to "scan" - to send and receive thoughts across vast distances - but they live in rigid isolation, forbidden from normal human relationships to prevent their powerful minds from being corrupted or overwhelmed. The story follows one scanner's desperate journey as he attempts to make contact with a lost colony, revealing the profound loneliness and sacrifice required of those who serve as humanity's mental bridges.

entries.title: Scenes with Beans
entries.pitch:
In this hauntingly absurd Hungarian gem from 1976, an unseen cosmic observer watches from the stars as a civilization of sentient beans goes about its daily life — celebrating joys, enduring tragedies, and navigating the complexities of society. The all-seeing eye in the sky remains a passive witness until the beans finally become aware of being watched.

This surrealist masterpiece defies easy categorization. Part philosophical meditation on surveillance and the observer effect, part absurdist commentary on human (or bean-) nature, Babfilm presents a strange mirror to our own society's relationship with being observed. The film's dreamlike imagery and deadpan treatment of its ridiculous premise create an unsettling meditation on privacy, consciousness, and the thin membrane between watcher and watched.

entries.title: Schizm: Mysterious Journey
entries.creator: LK Avalon, Detalion / Terry Dowling, Tomasz Kołodziejczak
entries.pitch:
Schizm: Mysterious Journey is a first-person adventure game set on the alien planet Argilus, where two protagonists—Sam Mainey and Dr. Hannah Grant—must work together to survive and unravel the mysteries of a vanished civilization. The player switches between both characters, solving intricate puzzles across bizarre alien environments: floating islands tethered by organic balloons, ancient temple complexes, and the enigmatic Matia's Zone. The game stands out for its atmospheric world-building, cooperative dual-character gameplay, and the philosophical themes woven through its mystery.

Originally released in 2001 by Polish developers LK Avalon and Detalion, the game was a sequel to Reah: Face the Unknown and featured collaboration from acclaimed Australian science fiction writer Terry Dowling. Its Polish origins and international creative team make it a unique artifact of early 2000s European game development.

entries.title: Scorn
entries.creator: Ebb Software
entries.pitch:
Scorn is a biopunk survival horror adventure game that throws players into a grotesque, nightmare world filled with techno-organic structures composed of machines, flesh, and bone. Developed by Serbian studio Ebb Software and released in 2022, the game draws heavy inspiration from the visual artists H.R. Giger and Zdzisław Beksiński, creating one of the most unsettling and atmospherically dense experiences in modern gaming. The player controls a silent humanoid protagonist who awakens in a wasteland called The Field and must navigate through interconnected regions filled with horrifying creatures and living machinery.

Unlike traditional horror games that provide context through dialogue or exposition, Scorn drops players directly into its world with virtually no explanation. Every environment, every creature, every object feels alien and wrong—designed to evoke visceral discomfort and existential dread. The game emphasizes exploration, puzzle-solving, and combat within a non-linear structure that rewards patience and experimentation.

entries.title: Second Time Around
entries.creator: Jeffrey Lau
entries.pitch: Second Time Around is a 2002 Hong Kong sci-fi film directed by Jeffrey Lau, starring Ekin Cheng, Cecilia Cheung, and Ke Huy Quan. The film explores the concept of parallel universes through a time-travel narrative about luck, fate, and second chances. After surviving a bizarre assassination attempt by his pregnant fiancée—who fires six shots and misses every time—Ren Lee travels to Las Vegas seeking his fortune. When tragedy strikes and his best friend dies in a car accident, Ren himself is involved in another accident that sends him back in time, giving him the opportunity to change his fate and save his friend. The film blends elements of romantic comedy with science fiction, examining how small changes in the past can alter the future in unexpected ways.

entries.title: Seconds
entries.creator: John Frankenheimer (Director), Lewis John Carlino (Screenplay), David Ely (Novel)
entries.pitch: What if you could abandon your entire life and start fresh with a new face, new name, and new identity? That's the seductive offer made to Arthur Hamilton, a wealthy but emotionally dead banking executive in 1960s New York, by a mysterious organization called "The Company." Transformed into the younger artist "Tony Wilson," Arthur discovers that escaping your life is far easier than finding meaning in a new one. Rock Hudson delivers a haunting, career-redefining performance in this psychological sci-fi nightmare that explores identity, regret, and the hollow promise of reinvention.

entries.title: Sector 7
entries.creator: Kim Ji-hoon
entries.pitch:
A team of oil rig workers at Sector 7, an underwater oil field south of Jeju Island, search for undiscovered oil. When veteran driller Captain Lee Jeong-man arrives to oversee operations, he brings with him a secret agenda — to harvest a recently discovered deep-sea life-form whose bodily fluids burn for over 30 hours as an alternative fuel. But when the creature escapes and begins killing the crew, the survivors must fight to escape the rig before they're hunted down one by one.

The film delivers solid creature-feature thrills with impressive CG effects. The creature — resembling a monstrous deep-sea organism — attacks with terrifying speed, a spear-like tongue, and nearly impenetrable hide. The isolated oil rig setting creates claustrophobic tension as the workers are stranded with no power and no escape.

entries.title: Seoul Station
entries.creator: Yeon Sang-ho
entries.pitch:
Seoul Station is a 2016 South Korean adult animated post-apocalyptic zombie horror film and the prequel to the acclaimed Train to Busan. Directed by Yeon Sang-ho (the mastermind behind the Train to Busan franchise), this film explores the onset of a zombie outbreak that spreads through Seoul's busiest transit hub. The story centers on Hye-sun, a young woman who escaped a brothel and now struggles to survive with her boyfriend Ki-woong, and Suk-gyu, her father searching for her—all set against the chaotic first hours of the epidemic. The film earned the Best Animated Feature Film award at the 10th Asian Pacific Screen Awards in 2016.

The animation depicts the rapid collapse of social order as the infection spreads through crowds of commuters, drawing unflinching parallels to real-world crises like the 2015 MERS outbreak in South Korea. Yeon Sang-ho uses the animated medium to deliver graphic violence that would be difficult to achieve in live-action, creating visceral horror sequences set against the familiar backdrop of Seoul's subway system.

entries.title: Serial Experiments Lain
entries.creator: Yasuyuki Ueda (Creator), Chiaki J. Konaka (Writer), Ryūtarō Nakamura (Director)
entries.pitch: Serial Experiments Lain is a 13-episode anime that follows Lain Iwakura, a socially isolated teenage girl living in suburban Tokyo. Her quiet existence is disrupted when she receives a cryptic email from a classmate who recently committed suicide—claiming to have found "God" within the Wired, a virtual network that exists alongside the internet. As Lain delves deeper into this digital realm, she begins questioning the very nature of reality, identity, and the boundary between the physical and virtual worlds. The series is renowned for its surreal visuals, philosophical depth, and prescient exploration of our relationship with technology. It asks: What does it mean to exist? Where does the self end and the network begin?

entries.title: Sexmission
entries.creator: Juliusz Machulski (Director)
entries.pitch:
Sexmission (Seksmisja) is a 1984 Polish satirical science fiction comedy film directed by Juliusz Machulski. Set in the year 2044, the film follows two men, Max Paradys and Albert Starski, who volunteer for the first human hibernation experiment in 1991. Instead of waking up three years later as planned, they emerge into a post-nuclear world where males have become extinct and women now rule society through a totalitarian regime known as the League of Women.

The film is a cult classic in Poland, voted the best Polish film of the last 30 years in a 2005 poll of film magazine readers. It received the Złota Kaczka award for best Polish movie of 1984 and was fairly popular in Hungary when shown there. However, the film has been subject to feminist criticism due to its association of women's emancipation with communist dictatorship.

entries.title: Shadow of the Comet
entries.creator: Infogrames
entries.pitch: Shadow of the Comet is a 1993 point-and-click adventure game developed and published by French studio Infogrames, later repackaged as Call of Cthulhu: Shadow of the Comet. Set in 1910, the game follows British photographer John Parker as he travels to the isolated New England town of Illsmouth to photograph Halley's Comet. Parker discovers that in 1834, during the comet's previous appearance, Lord Boleskine observed the comet from Illsmouth and went insane under mysterious circumstances. With only three days until the comet arrives again, Parker must uncover the dark secrets of Illsmouth and survive the cosmic horror that awaits. The game is based on H.P. Lovecraft's Cthulhu Mythos, incorporating elements from "The Dunwich Horror" and "The Shadow Over Innsmouth."

entries.title: Shadwen
entries.creator: Frozenbyte
entries.pitch: Shadwen is a stealth action-adventure game developed and published by the Finnish studio Frozenbyte. Released in May 2016 for Windows, macOS, Linux, and PlayStation 4, the game follows Shadwen, an elite assassin living in the Dark Forest who is hired by the current king to kill the former ruler. When the king betrays her—and burns down her forest home to eliminate her—she seeks vengeance while protecting Lily, a young orphan girl whose father was taken to a quarry by the king's soldiers. The game features a "time-warp" mechanic allowing players to rewind time after decisions, creating strategic depth in its stealth gameplay. Critics gave mixed reviews, praising its innovative premise and tactical options but critiquing execution.

entries.title: She Came Out of the Blue Sky
entries.creator: Václav Pavel Borovička
entries.pitch: She Came Out of the Blue Sky is a 1978 Slovak-language children's science fiction television series fromCzechoslovakia that predates E.T. by four years and shares remarkable parallels with Spielberg's beloved classic. The story follows Maika, an extraterrestrial alien who lands on Earth near a small Slovak town and is discovered by a group of local children. Unlike typical portrayals of aliens, Maika is initially uncanny—her skin appears wax-like, she speaks in a staccato, robot-like voice, and she lacks understanding of basic human emotions and customs. Over the course of 13 episodes, the children help Maika experience human feelings for the first time, and she develops from a detached observer into something approaching a normal child. The series became extremely popular across Czechoslovakia and was exported to multiple countries under various titles.

entries.title: Shikari
entries.creator: Mohammed Hussain (Director)
entries.pitch: Shikari is a 1963 Indian Hindi-language science fiction adventure film loosely based on Hollywood films Dr. Cyclops and King Kong. When a struggling circus owner and his partner embark on an expedition to the jungles of the Malay Peninsula to capture a legendary giant ape known as Otango, they encounter something far more dangerous: a mad scientist living in the jungle who is conducting horrifying experiments to turn humans into gorillas. The film combines adventure, horror, and sci-fi elements in a uniquely Indian package, featuring popular music and the iconic villain performance by K.N. Singh as Dr. Cyclops.

entries.title: Shiva Ka Insaaf
entries.creator: Raj N. Sippy (Director)
entries.pitch: Shiva Ka Insaaf (transl. "Shiva's Justice") is a 1985 Indian Hindi-language superhero film that holds the distinction of being the first Hindi film ever shot in 3D. Directed by Raj N. Sippy and starring Jackie Shroff in his breakthrough role, the film combines superhero action with 3D visual spectacle to create a unique entry in Indian cinema history. The film follows Bhola, an orphan raised by three martial arts masters, who transforms into the masked superhero Shiva to fight the evil gangster Jagan who murdered his parents. With its innovative 3D effects and memorable R.D. Burman soundtrack, Shiva Ka Insaaf represents an important experimental moment in Indian popular cinema.

entries.title: Short Circuit
entries.creator: Faisal Hashmi
entries.pitch:
Short Circuit is a 2019 Gujarati science fiction film that holds the distinction of being the first sci-fi film ever made in the Gujarati language. Directed by Faisal Hashmi, the film combines the time loop concept with thriller elements to tell a story about love, fate, and breaking free from predetermined outcomes. The film received positive reviews for its direction, visual effects, and ambitious attempt at bringing a new genre to regional Indian cinema.

The film revolves around Samay, an IT professional who works repairing computers and lives with his mother, who constantly nags him to get married. Samay falls in love with Seema, a news anchor at Zee 24 Kalak. During an interview with a scientist named Dr. Parthsarthi, who is experimenting with creating a portable wormhole, things take a dark turn when the scientist threatens Seema. Tragedy strikes when Seema is shot by a masked man outside the building. That night, Samay witnesses a rare Aurora Borealis phenomenon—an event that never happens in India—alongside his friend Bhopa. When Samay goes to sleep, he wakes up to discover he is now living the same day over and over again.

entries.title: Shōjo Tsubaki
entries.creator: Suehiro Maruo
