entries.pitch: Shōjo Tsubaki (literally "The Camellia Girl") is a dark Japanese manga serialized in the legendary alternative magazine Garo between 1983 and 1984. Written and illustrated by Suehiro Maruo, it stands as one of the most notorious examples of the "ero guro" (erotic grotesque) movement in Japanese manga. The story follows Midori, a young girl in 1938 Japan who, after her mother dies and her father abandons them, is tricked into working at a brutal freak show circus called the Red Cat. What begins as a tale of poverty and desperation transforms into a nightmarish exploration of abuse, exploitation, and the darkest corners of human nature. The manga was adapted into a notorious anime film in 1992 and a live-action film in 2016, cementing its status as a cult classic of underground Japanese media.

entries.title: Signals: A Space Adventure
entries.creator: Robert von Rhyannon
entries.pitch:
In the mid-21st century, a deep space exploration vessel suddenly goes off the radar, losing all contact with Earth. When a routine patrol crew investigates the silent ship, they discover something is deeply wrong aboard—and the answers they find may be more dangerous than the mystery they came to solve.

This 1970 West German sci-fi film predates many classic space opera tropes while sharing DNA with the paranoid thrillers of its era. With only 15 votes on TMDB, it's a genuinely obscure find that offers atmospheric tension over spectacle.

entries.title: Silence of Doctor Ivens
entries.creator: Молчание доктора Ивенса
entries.pitch:
In the surreal aftermath to a plane crash at sea, Dr. Iven — an eminent scientist — becomes the only survivor, rescued by alien visitors from a pacifist civilization. These extraterrestrials have come to study humanity, but they hold a troubling conclusion: the world, saturated with weapons of mass destruction, is not ready for the wonders of their advanced culture.

The situation grows more complicated when a genuine relationship blossoms between the doctor and his female alien rescuer. As Dr. Iven is drawn deeper into the aliens' worldview, he must confront an uncomfortable truth about his own species — and decide whether humanity deserves to join the cosmic community of intelligent beings.

This 1974 Soviet science fiction film explores first contact through a melancholy lens, questioning whether human violence and militarism have doomed us to isolation among the stars.

entries.title: Silent Running
entries.creator: Douglas Trumbull (Director), Michael Cimino, Deric Washburn, Steven Bochco (Screenplay)
entries.pitch: In a future where Earth's forests have been wiped out by environmental destruction, one botanist fights to preserve the last remaining samples of Earth's natural world. Freeman Lowell lives aboard the Valley Forge, a massive space freighter carrying geodesic domes filled with forests, plants, and animals—the last hope for reforesting a barren planet. When orders come to destroy the biodomes and return the ship to commercial service, Lowell makes a desperate choice: he kills to protect his charges and escapes into deep space with the last forest, accompanied only by three service robots. This is a melancholic, philosophical meditation on humanity's relationship with nature, wrapped in a space adventure.

entries.title: Silt
entries.creator: Spiral Circus (Developer), Fireshine Games (Publisher)
entries.pitch: Silt is a surreal underwater puzzle-adventure indie horror game that casts players as a deep-sea diver exploring the darkest depths of an oceanic abyss. Armed with the unique ability to possess the marine life around them, players must navigate through a monochrome world of strange organisms, ancient ruins, and long-forgotten machinery. Developed by the UK-based Spiral Circus as their debut title, Silt draws inspiration from the watercolor paintings of artist Tom Mead, creating a haunting, Lynchian atmosphere that lingers long after the credits roll.

entries.title: Silvery Dust
entries.creator: Pavel Armand, Abram Room
entries.pitch:
In 1950s Soviet cinema, one of the rarest creatures in science fiction—an allegory about American capitalism. Silvery Dust is a 1953 Soviet sci-fi drama that takes place entirely in the United States, following Samuel Steal, a scientist whose single-minded ambition drives him to invent a devastating new weapon: a deadly radioactive silver-gray powder. What follows is a brutal corporate war between two military-industrial trusts, each desperate to possess Steal's invention.

Directed by Pavel Armand and Abram Room at Mosfilm, this is quintessential Cold War-era Soviet filmmaking—using America as its setting to critique the very system that built it. The film operates as a fascinating period piece, showing how Soviet filmmakers imagined American corporate greed would lead to self-destruction. The tension between the two competing trusts, depicted as faceless corporate behemoths, makes for compelling viewing even seven decades later.

What makes Silvery Dust especially valuable to the Inspiration Archive is its sheer uniqueness—a Soviet sci-fi film set in America, made at the height of the Cold War, that uses the language of American capitalism to critique it. At 102 minutes, it's a substantial drama that goes beyond simple propaganda, exploring what happens when scientific ambition meets unchecked corporate power.

entries.title: Singapore Sling
entries.creator: Nikos Nikolaidis
entries.pitch: Singapore Sling: The Man Who Loved a Corpse is a 1990 Greek black and white underground art horror film directed by Nikos Nikolaidis, widely considered his magnum opus. The film centers on a mother and daughter who live together in a secluded mansion, where they engage in perverse BDSM-related incestuous games in memory of their sadistic patriarch—a mummified corpse kept in the house. When a wounded detective arrives at their estate searching for a missing woman, he becomes their prisoner, drawn into their twisted sexual games and torture rituals. The film is a bizarre mix of film noir, black comedy, exploitation thriller, and horror, exploring themes of power, sexuality, and death with unsettling intensity.

entries.title: Sirius
entries.creator: Dezső Ákos Hamza (Director)
entries.pitch: Sirius is a rare 1942 Hungarian science fiction film, directed by Dezső Ákos Hamza and based on Ferenc Herczeg's influential 1894 novel of the same name. Produced during World War II at the Hunnia Studios in Budapest, this film represents one of the earliest examples of Hungarian science fiction cinema. The story centers on a mysterious stranger who arrives in a small town, possessing supernatural knowledge and abilities that challenge the local establishment. Drawing on themes of otherworldly intervention and the conflict between science and superstition, Sirius presents a haunting meditation on faith, knowledge, and the boundaries of human understanding. The film premiered at the wartime 1942 Venice Film Festival—the last held under Mussolini's regime—marking an unusual international presence for Hungarian cinema during this period.

entries.title: Skeleton on Horseback
entries.creator: Hugo Haas
entries.pitch: Skeleton on Horseback (original Czech title: Bílá nemoc, meaning "The White Disease") is a 1937 Czechoslovak drama film directed by and starring Hugo Haas. Based on the play "The White Disease" by renowned Czech writer Karel Čapek, this film serves as a powerful anti-fascist allegory, depicting an infectious disease that spreads during wartime and the moral dilemmas faced by doctors, scientists, and political leaders. Remarkably prophetic for its time, the film was made just two years before World War II and directly references the rising threat of fascism in Europe. The story follows Dr. Galén, who discovers a mysterious illness causing white spots to appear on victims' skin—ultimately revealing that this "white disease" is a metaphor for the spread of fascism across Europe.

entries.title: Skyman
entries.creator: Daniel Myrick
entries.pitch: Skyman is a 2019 American found footage science fiction horror film written and directed by Daniel Myrick, best known for The Blair Witch Project. The film explores the story of Carl Merryweather, a man who believes he experienced an alien encounter at age 10, and is now convinced that the extraterrestrials will reconnect with him on his 40th birthday. The film is described as a character study examining the psychological trauma and lifelong experiences of alien abductees. Unlike typical found footage horror, Myrick intended this as its own thing—a meditation on obsession, memory, and the search for meaning through extraordinary claims.

entries.title: Snatcher
entries.creator: Hideo Kojima / Konami
entries.pitch: Snatcher is a seminal cyberpunk graphic adventure game developed by Konami and written by a young Hideo Kojima, first released in Japan in 1988. Set in the mid-21st century in Neo Kobe City, an artificial island metropolis in eastern Asia, the game follows Gillian Seed—an amnesiac who discovers he has a mysterious past connected to the titular Snatchers: humanoid robots disguised as humans who kill their prey and assume their identities. Inspired by Blade Runner, Akira, The Terminator, and Invasion of the Body Snatchers, Kojima crafted a dense, cinematic narrative that pioneered many themes he would later explore in the Metal Gear series. Gameplay combines menu-based investigation, semi-open world exploration, and occasional shooting segments. Initially released only in Japanese, the game gained a cult following and received an English localization for Sega CD in 1994-1995. Retrospectively acclaimed as one of the best adventure and cyberpunk games of all time, Snatcher remains a landmark title that influenced countless creators in the industry.

entries.title: Sol Bianca
entries.creator: Katsuhito Akiyama (Director), Hiroki Hayashi (Episode 2)
entries.pitch: Sol Bianca is a two-volume Japanese OVA from 1990-1991 that follows an all-female crew of notorious space pirates aboard their starship, the Sol Bianca. When a young boy named Rim stows away on their ship after one of their raids, he convinces the crew to help him rescue his mother from Emperor Batros, the brutal ruler of planet Tres. In exchange, he tells them about the Gnosis—an artifact reputedly from old Earth itself, the greatest treasure in the known universe. With their advanced ship and a sniper rifle capable of striking from orbit, the pirate women set out for the ultimate heist.

entries.title: Solaris
entries.creator: Stanisław Lem
entries.pitch:
Solaris is a 1961 philosophical science fiction novel by Polish writer Stanisław Lem, widely considered one of the greatest works in the genre. The story follows psychologist Kris Kelvin arriving at a research station orbiting the distant planet Solaris, where scientists have spent decades studying a vast ocean that covers the entire planetary surface. This ocean—an alien intelligence of incomprehensible scale—creates enormous mysterious formations that have defied all human attempts at understanding.

Kelvin finds the crew fragmented and traumatized. His colleagues have been subjected to "visitors"—physical manifestations of their repressed memories and guilt, appearing as people from their pasts. Kelvin's own deceased wife Harey materializes on the station, forcing him to confront grief he thought he'd escaped. The novel follows Kelvin's attempts to understand both the alien intelligence and his own psychological trauma, ultimately revealing the profound limitations of human rationality when confronting truly alien minds.

entries.title: Solaris
entries.creator: Andrei Tarkovsky
entries.pitch: Solaris is a 1972 Soviet psychological science fiction film directed by Andrei Tarkovsky, based on Stanisław Lem's 1961 novel. The film is set on a space station orbiting the distant planet Solaris, where a team of scientists has been studying an enigmatic alien ocean that appears to manifest the psychological memories of those on board. Psychologist Kris Kelvin is sent to evaluate the deteriorating situation, only to encounter manifestations of his own past—particularly his deceased wife—that blur the line between reality and projection. Rather than the technological spectacle typical of Western science fiction, Tarkovsky prioritizes philosophical introspection, creating what many consider one of the most profound explorations of human consciousness, memory, and the nature of reality ever committed to film.

entries.title: Son of the White Mare
entries.creator: Marcell Jankovics
entries.pitch: Son of the White Mare (Fehérlófia) is a 1981 Hungarian animated psychedelic fantasy film directed by Marcell Jankovics. Based on an 1862 narrative poem by László Arany, itself drawn from ancient Hunnic, Avaric, and Hungarian legends, the film tells the story of three brothers born of a magical horse who descend into the Underworld to rescue three princesses from evil dragons. Created under challenging conditions in communist-era Hungary, the film is renowned for its extraordinary visual density—every frame treated as a painting, with morphing figures and swirling colors that create a dreamlike, almost overwhelming sensory experience. Despite initial poor reception in Hungary, it has become a cult classic internationally, influencing animators at Disney and beyond. The film was restored in 4K and released on Blu-ray in 2021.

entries.title: Space Academy
entries.creator: Created by Allen Ducovny, presented by Filmation
entries.pitch: Space Academy is a 1977 American science fiction television series produced by Filmation that originally aired on CBS Saturday mornings from September to December 1977. The show was created by Allen Ducovny and featured veteran actor Jonathan Harris (best known as Dr. Zachary Smith from Lost in Space) in the lead role of Commander Isaac Gampu. Set in the year 3732, the series takes place on the Space Academy, an educational institution located on an asteroid where young students with special abilities are trained to explore the mysteries of space. The show ran for 15 episodes before being cancelled, though it achieved brief cult status and even spawned a spin-off series, Jason of Star Command.

entries.title: Space Adventure Cobra
entries.creator: Buichi Terasawa (manga), Osamu Dezaki (director)
entries.pitch: Space Adventure Cobra is a 1982 Japanese animated film that adapts the beginning of Buichi Terasawa's influential space opera manga. The film introduces Cobra, a legendary space pirate with a Psychogun (a device that creates illusions) who lives a carefree life until his past catches up with him. When the nefarious Space Pirate Guild sends an army of bounty hunters after him, Cobra must spring into action to protect himself and those he cares about. The film sets up the larger mythology of the Cobra universe while delivering a self-contained adventure that combines action, humor, and sci-fi thrills. Notably, the film was one of the first anime features to gain some recognition in Western markets, though it remains far less famous than later space operas like Star Wars.

entries.title: Space Battleship Yamato
entries.creator: Leiji Matsumoto, Yoshinobu Nishizaki
entries.pitch: Space Battleship Yamato is a landmark Japanese anime series that helped establish space opera as a major anime genre. Set in an alternate 2199, humanity is facing extinction after Earth is devastated by alien bombs from the planet Gamilas. A mysterious message from the planet Iscandar offers hope—a device that can restore Earth's radiation-damaged environment. The crew of the battleship Yamato, a relic of World War II converted into a starship, must journey across the galaxy to retrieve it, facing impossible odds against the superior Gamilas forces. The series pioneered many tropes that would define anime space opera, influencing everything from Gundam to Neon Genesis Evangelion.

entries.title: Space Carrier Blue Noah
entries.creator: Kazunori Tanahashi (Director), Office Academy (Studio)
entries.pitch: Space Carrier Blue Noah is a Japanese science fiction anime series that aired from October 1979 to March 1980, produced by Office Academy. Set in the year 2052, the series follows Earth's desperate battle for survival after an alien force known as the Death Force arrives and begins terraforming the planet to make it habitable for their own kind. When Earth's major cities and research centers are devastated—killing 90% of the human population—a group of high school students and survivors discover Blue Noah, a powerful secret warship capable of both space and underwater combat. Led by the teens, Blue Noah launches a counteroffensive against the alien invasion, ultimately confronting the massive Terror Star satellite in a final battle for Earth's survival.

entries.title: Space City Sigma
entries.creator: Ashok Talwar
entries.pitch: Space City Sigma is an Indian science fiction television series that aired on DD National in 1989, marking one of the first sci-fi productions in Indian television history. The show follows Commander Tara and the crew of Sigma, a space city running on fusion energy docked at the Galactic frontier. Sigma represents humanity's last stand against the technologically advanced alien race ruled by the tyrannical Zhakhakoo. When a deadly creature called Blob is sent to infiltrate the city, the crew must battle this existential threat while defending Earth from being annexed into Zhakhakoo's astronomical kingdom.

entries.title: Space Family Carlvinson
entries.creator: Yoshitoh Asari (manga), Kimio Yabuki (director)
entries.pitch: Space Family Carlvinson is a delightful Japanese OVA from 1988, based on the manga by Yoshitoh Asari. The story follows an alien acting troupe who accidentally orphan a young human baby girl after their spaceship crashes on Earth. Rather than leave the child to fend for themselves, the compassionate aliens decide to raise her as their own, learning about human family customs along the way. This 45-minute animated feature blends sci-fi concepts with heartfelt family comedy, exploring themes of belonging, cross-cultural parenting, and the universal bonds that connect all intelligent beings. Originally released in December 1988 by studio Doga Kobo, this charming OVA has become a minor cult classic among fans of 1980s anime.

entries.title: Space Invaders
entries.creator: Tomohiro Nishikado
entries.pitch: Space Invaders is a seminal arcade shooter game released in 1978 by Taito in Japan. The player controls a laser cannon at the bottom of the screen, defending Earth from descending rows of alien invaders. The game features several rows of enemies that slowly descend while firing back at the player, creating a tense battle of attrition. As players destroy aliens, the remaining enemies speed up, and each wave becomes progressively harder. The game popularized the fixed shooter genre and became one of the most influential games in history, helping launch the video game industry.

entries.title: Space Is the Place
entries.creator: John Coney (Director), Sun Ra (Writer/Star)
entries.pitch: Space Is the Place is a surreal Afrofuturist film from 1974 that functions as part music documentary, part mythological narrative, and part blaxploitation fantasy. Directed by John Coney and written by and starring jazz legend Sun Ra, the film follows the alien musician as he attempts to relocate African Americans to a new planet through the transformative power of his cosmic jazz. Shot in Oakland, California in the early 1970s, the film blends concert footage of Sun Ra's revolutionary Arkestra with loosely scripted dramatic scenes depicting Sun Ra's negotiations with the "Overseer" (a pimp-overlord figure) for the fate of the Black race. The result is one of the most unique and visually striking films to emerge from the 1970s, a cult classic that has influenced generations of artists working at the intersection of Black music, science fiction, and speculative futures.

entries.title: Space Monster Wangmagwi
entries.creator: Kwon Hyeok-jin (Director)
entries.pitch: Space Monster Wangmagwi is a 1967 South Korean kaiju film and the oldest surviving Korean kaiju film, notable as the first all-Korean science fiction film ever made. Directed by Kwon Hyeok-jin and inspired by Japanese and American monster movies such as Godzilla and King Kong, the film tells the story of an alien invasion of Earth using a giant monster to attack South Korea. The plot centers on air force pilot Oh Jeong-hwan and his betrothed Ahn-hee, whose wedding day is interrupted by the arrival of the space monster Wangmagwi. The film is remarkable for its unique blend of science fiction action, comedic vignettes, and subtle political commentary referencing the Korean War, making it a fascinating artifact of 1960s Korean cinema.

entries.title: Space Quest
entries.creator: Sierra On-Line (Mark Crowe, Scott Murphy)
entries.pitch:
Space Quest is a series of comic science fiction adventure games released between 1986 and 1995, following the misadventures of Roger Wilco, a hapless janitor who stumbles into intergalactic heroics. Created by Sierra On-Line (the "Two Guys from Andromeda"—Mark Crowe and Scott Murphy), the series parodies iconic science fiction properties like Star Wars and Star Trek while infusing every scenario with puns, farcical storylines, and an underdog protagonist who saves the universe by accident, only to be ignored or punished for violating minor regulations in the process.

The games pioneered comedic adventure gaming, offering a lighthearted counterpoint to the serious fantasy themes that dominated Sierra's flagship King's Quest series. Players navigate point-and-click puzzles across alien worlds, starships, and bizarre interdimensional locales, with Roger Wilco perpetually out of his depth yet somehow prevailing through luck and persistence.

entries.title: Space Sweepers
entries.creator: Jo Sung-hee (Director)
entries.pitch: Space Sweepers is a 2021 South Korean space western film set in 2092, following a ragtag crew of "space sweepers" who salvage debris and cargo in Earth's orbit. When they discover a child robot named Dorothy containing a weapon of mass destruction, they become entangled in a dangerous game between the powerful UTS corporation and a terrorist group called the Black Foxes. Directed by Jo Sung-hee and starring Song Joong-ki and Kim Tae-ri, this film is notable as the first Korean space blockbuster, combining Western tropes with Korean storytelling sensibilities. Released globally on Netflix, it explores themes of corporate greed, poverty, and the bond that forms between outcasts.

entries.title: Space: 1999
entries.creator: Gerry and Sylvia Anderson
entries.pitch:
Space: 1999 is a British science fiction television series that ran for two seasons from 1975 to 1977. The show follows the 311 inhabitants of Moonbase Alpha, a scientific research facility located in the lunar crater Plato. When stored nuclear waste on the Moon's far side reaches critical mass due to an unknown form of "magnetic radiation," it triggers a massive thermonuclear explosion that propels the Moon out of Earth orbit and into deep space. Now stranded aboard their lunar craft hurtling through the cosmos, the Alphans must navigate alien civilizations, dystopian societies, and mind-bending phenomena while searching for a new home.

The series was created by the legendary British production team of Gerry and Sylvia Anderson (of Thunderbirds fame) and was, at the time, the most expensive series ever produced for British television with a combined £6.8 million budget. It starred Martin Landau (Mission: Impossible) as Commander John Koenig and his then-wife Barbara Bain as Dr. Helena Russell. The show featured an impressive roster of guest stars including Christopher Lee, Joan Collins, Peter Cushing, and Brian Blessed.

entries.title: Spadla z oblakov
entries.creator: Radim Cvrček
entries.pitch: Spadla z oblakov (translated as "She Fell from Clouds") is a beloved Czechoslovak children's science fiction television series that originally aired from 1978 to 1983. The show follows a group of children spending their holidays in the fictional Slovak town of Čabovce who discover Maika, an extraterrestrial alien girl from the planet Gurun. Unlike typical scary alien narratives, Maika is a gentle explorer who becomes friends with the local children, sharing wonders from her world while learning about Earth. The series was produced by Czechoslovak Television and remains a nostalgic cult classic in Slovakia and the Czech Republic.

entries.title: Spectreman
entries.creator: Souji Ushio (Creator), P Productions
entries.pitch:
Spectreman is a 1971 Japanese tokusatsu superhero television series that stands as the first major Japanese superhero show of the 1970s, predating both Ultraman and Kamen Rider by several months. Produced by P Productions and created by Souji Ushio, the series aired on Fuji TV in Japan from January 1971 to March 1972 with 63 episodes. The show centers on a powerful alien cyborg dispatched to Earth by the Nebula 71 Star to combat the ecological threats posed by a banished mad scientist and his army of pollution-based monsters.

What makes Spectreman remarkable is its unusual premise: rather than fighting alien invasions or criminal masterminds, the hero battles monsters created from environmental pollution—a topic of urgent concern in 1970s Japan, which had the most polluted city in the world at the time. This environmental message gives the show a surprisingly prescient edge that resonates strongly today.

entries.title: Sputnik
entries.creator: Egor Abramenko
entries.pitch: Sputnik is a 2020 Russian science fiction horror film directed by Egor Abramenko in his feature directorial debut. The film takes place in 1983 Soviet Union, where a cosmonaut named Konstantin Veshnyakov is the sole survivor of a mysterious space accident that crashed in Kazakhstan. The military takes him to a secret research facility run by Colonel Semiradov, where scientists discover that Veshnyakov has an alien organism living inside him—a symbiotic creature that emerges each night while he sleeps. When a psychiatrist named Dr. Tatyana Klimova is recruited to assess Veshnyakov's mental state, she uncovers the dark truth: the alien requires cortisol from living, terrified humans to survive. The film combines Cold War paranoia with body horror, exploring themes of sacrifice, hidden government experiments, and the bonds between captor and captive.

entries.title: Srdečný pozdrav ze zeměkoule
entries.creator: Oldřich Lipský
entries.pitch: Srdečný pozdrav ze zeměkoule (Best Regards from the Earth) is a 1982 Czechoslovak comedy science fiction film directed by Oldřich Lipský. The film follows two eccentric aliens from a distant galaxy who arrive on Earth in a flying saucer that conveniently takes the shape of a beer keg or waste container. The aliens land on Earth and set up residence at a waste dump, which they enthusiastically "colonize" before embarking on their mission to study average humans. Using the galaxy's central computer, they select Dr. Jánský, a shy scientist working at the Institute for Contact with Alien Civilizations, as their specimen of "typical humanity." The comedy ensues as the well-meaning but comically incompetent aliens misunderstand every aspect of human civilization, from everyday objects to social customs, offering a delightful fish-out-of-water satire on both alien and human perspectives.

entries.title: Sri Asih
entries.creator: Tan Sing Hwat, Turino Djunaedy
entries.pitch:
Sri Asih is a 1954 Indonesian superhero film, notable as the first Indonesian film featuring a superhero character adapted from comics. Directed by Tan Sing Hwat and Turino Djunaedy, this lost film stars Mimi Mariani as Nani Wijaya, a young woman who transforms into the flying superheroine Sri Asih when danger strikes. The film was produced by Gabungan Artis Film and released in June 1954, marking a pioneering moment in Indonesian cinema and Southeast Asian superhero storytelling.

The story follows Nani Wijaya, who discovers her heroic alter-ego Sri Asih after overhearing criminals planning to sabotage a train. Using a magical charm, she transforms into Sri Asih—a powerful woman who can fly and possesses superhuman abilities—to thwart the evil Garuda Hitam gang. The film combines elements of fantasy, action, and social commentary, representing a unique fusion of Western superhero conventions with Indonesian storytelling traditions.

entries.title: Stalker
entries.creator: Andrei Tarkovsky (Director), Arkady & Boris Strugatsky (Writers)
entries.pitch:
In a bleak, post-industrial wasteland that was once a thriving city, a mysterious zone has appeared—a region where the laws of physics seem to bend and strange phenomena occur. The government has sealed it off, declaring it dangerous, but whispered rumors persist: at the heart of the Zone lies a room that can grant any person's deepest desire. A guide known as the Stalker leads two desperate men—a disillusioned writer seeking inspiration and a professor hoping for scientific glory—through the hazardous landscape to find this mythical room. What follows is a slow, meditative journey through a landscape of ruins, tunnels, and eerie emptiness, where the true destination may not be the Room at all, but the revelation of what the characters truly want and who they really are.

This is not action cinema. Stalker is a philosophical meditation on desire, faith, and the human condition, wrapped in the trappings of science fiction. It moves at the pace of contemplation, asking viewers to surrender to its rhythm and emerge transformed.

entries.title: Star Control
entries.creator: Toys for Bob (Paul Reiche III, Fred Ford)
entries.pitch: Star Control is a 1990 action-strategy video game that combines real-time space combat with turn-based galactic conquest. Players choose to command either the Ur-Quan Hierarchy or the Alliance of Free Stars in an interstellar war for control of the galaxy. The game features unique alien starships, each with distinct weapons and abilities, creating deep tactical combat against the AI or another player. With its colorful alien races, innovative ship-to-ship combat using physics-based movement around gravity wells, and memorable musical theme, Star Control became a cult classic that influenced later games like Mass Effect and Stellaris.

entries.title: Star Odyssey
entries.creator: Alfonso Brescia (Director)
entries.pitch: Star Odyssey (Italian: Sette uomini d'oro nello spazio, also known as "Seven Gold Men in Space") is a 1979 Italian space opera film directed by Alfonso Brescia under the pseudonym Al Brescia. Produced in the wake of Star Wars' massive success, it represents one of four low-budget Italian sci-fi films in Brescia's interconnected series, serving as the final entry following "Cosmos: War of the Planets," "Battle of the Stars," and "War of the Robots." The film unfolds in the year 2312, when humanity discovers that Earth has been auctioned off to an evil alien despot named Kress by a galactic council of alien civilizations. Now facing enslavement, Earth's fate rests with Professor Maury and his ragtag group of human and robot defenders who attempt to reclaim the planet from Kress and his army of cyborgs. The film is notable primarily as a cult curiosity—a quintessential example of Italian "mergatta" filmmaking, where studios rapidly produced knockoffs of successful Hollywood films with minimal budgets, creating works that have since become beloved for their intentional or unintentional comedic value.

entries.title: Star Raiders
entries.creator: Doug Neubauer (programmer), Atari, Inc. (developer)
entries.pitch: Star Raiders is a pioneering space combat simulation game developed for Atari's 8-bit computer line and released in 1980. Created by programmer Doug Neubauer, it brought the excitement of science fiction dogfights to home computers, offering players the chance to pilot a starship against the invading Zylon fleet. The game was notable for its sophisticated use of the Atari 8-bit's hardware capabilities, including smooth vector graphics and complex gameplay mechanics that were unprecedented in home computer gaming at the time.

entries.title: Star Raiders II
entries.pitch:
Star Raiders II is a space combat simulator released in 1986 for Atari 8-bit computers, developed by Atari Corporation as a sequel to the classic 1979 title Star Raiders. Originally conceived as a tie-in with the film The Last Starfighter, the game was eventually converted into a standalone sequel when the licensing fell through. The player takes command of a Gunstar spacecraft to defend the Rylan Star League against the invading Ko-Dan armada in a desperate fight across multiple star systems.

The game combines tactical space combat with strategic resource management. Players must patrol star systems, intercept enemy fleets attempting to breach the Frontier defensive network, and launch attacks on the Ko-Dan's industrial base in their home system. Success requires careful management of ship energy and hull integrity, as well as strategic decisions about where to deploy limited resources across vast distances of space.

entries.title: Star Sapphire
entries.creator: Joan Hon (as Han May)
entries.pitch: Star Sapphire is widely recognized as Singapore's first science fiction novel, published in 1985 by Joan Hon under the pen name Han May. Set in the 23rd century aboard the massive interstellar passenger starship Star Sapphire, the novel follows Yva Yolan, a young biophysicist of mixed human-alien descent who joins the crew of this vast spacecraft. The story is set in a future where Earth has been renamed Terra and humanity coexists harmoniously with various extraterrestrial species across multiple galaxies. Yva finds herself entangled in a love triangle between two crew members—Adam Zear, the cold but magnetic Registrar, and Timothy Huha, the warm and friendly Chief Personnel Officer—while navigating strict ship rules that forbid romantic relationships among crew members. The novel received a Highly Commended award in the Fiction category from the National Book Development Council of Singapore in 1986.

entries.title: Star Wreck: In the Pirkinning
entries.creator: Timo Vuorensola (Director), Samuli Torssonen (Writer/Producer)
entries.pitch: Star Wreck: In the Pirkinning is a Finnish fan film that has achieved legendary cult status despite—or perhaps because of—its origin as a shoestring production made by five friends in a two-room apartment over seven years. Released in 2005, this parody film takes direct aim at the Star Trek and Babylon 5 franchises, creating an extraordinarily ambitious low-budget sci-fi comedy that reportedly downloaded over 2.9 million times within two months of its free internet release, making it the most-viewed Finnish-made film ever. The film's plot follows Captain James B. Pirk, a parody of Captain Kirk, who—after being stranded on Earth—decides to conquer the planet and then expand his empire into a parallel universe. The resulting mashup of Star Trek archetypes, Finnish humor, and surprisingly professional visual effects has become a touchstone in the world of fan films and independent sci-fi.

entries.title: Starchaser: The Legend of Orin
entries.creator: Steven Hahn (Director), Jeffrey Scott (Writer)
entries.pitch:
On the mining world of Trinia, humanity has lived in subterranean slavery for millennia, toiling for their robotic "god" Zygon. Young miner Orin discovers a jeweled sword that projects the image of an ancient guardian, revealing that a magnificent universe exists above the caverns. When his beloved Elan is killed by Zygon, Orin escapes to the surface and bonds with a mysterious Starfly creature, beginning a journey to find the truth behind his world's enslavement and unlock the power of the legendary Kha-Khan.

This 1985 animated feature was a groundbreaking experiment in 3D animation, mixing traditional and computer-generated techniques years before Pixar popularized the form. It's a classic hero's journey wrapped in space opera trappings—a rip-off of Star Wars, critics said, but one made with genuine ambition by a Korean animation studio seeking to prove they could match Hollywood.

entries.title: Starcrash
entries.creator: Luigi Cozzi (Director)
entries.pitch: Starcrash is a 1978 Italian-American space opera film that has achieved cult classic status despite initially receiving negative reviews. Directed by Luigi Cozzi and featuring a score by legendary composer John Barry, the film was created as a direct response to the unprecedented success of Star Wars. Filmed at Rome's Cinecittà studios, it follows smuggler Stella Star and her mentor Akton as they are recruited by the Emperor of the Galaxy to find a secret weapon and rescue the Emperor's son from the evil Count Zarth Arn. The film is known for its lavish production design, colorful costumes, and cheesily spectacular special effects that have made it a beloved entry in the "so bad it's good" canon.

entries.title: Starflight
entries.creator: Binary Systems (Developer), Electronic Arts (Publisher), Greg Johnson (Designer)
entries.pitch:
Starflight is a pioneering space exploration role-playing video game released in 1986 by Binary Systems and published by Electronic Arts. Set in the year 4620, players take on the role of a starship captain tasked with exploring a vast galaxy containing 270 star systems and approximately 800 planets. The game combines elements of space trading, combat, and diplomacy in an open-ended sandbox format that was revolutionary for its time.

Unlike most games of the era, Starflight offers no predetermined path. Players freely switch between mining resources for profit, engaging in ship-to-ship combat with hostile aliens, and negotiating diplomatic relations with various extraterrestrial species. The game's broader narrative emerges gradually as players discover that an ancient race of beings is systematically causing stars to flare dangerously, threatening all life in the galaxy.

entries.title: Starquest II
entries.creator: Fred Gallo
entries.pitch:
In the aftermath of nuclear war, four Earth warriors awaken aboard a mysterious spacecraft with no memory of how they arrived. As confusion gives way to determination, they discover they are humanity's last hope against an extraterrestrial invasion threatening to enslave or annihilate what remains of Earth.

Starquest II (also known as Galactic Odyssey) is a 1997 sci-fi thriller that channels classic B-movie energy while delivering surprisingly earnest post-apocalyptic themes. Director Fred Gallo crafts a straightforward but engaging tale of ordinary people thrust into extraordinary circumstances, facing alien antagonists who will do anything to save their own species.

The film balances action sequences with moments of character development, particularly as the warriors piece together their fragmented pasts and forge alliances despite their initial mistrust. While the production values reflect its low-budget origins, the creative creature designs and practical effects give the alien threat a memorable visual presence.

entries.title: Stars in Shadow
entries.creator: Ashdar Games
entries.pitch: Stars in Shadow is a turn-based 4X science fiction strategy game developed by Ashdar Games and published by Iceberg Interactive for Windows PC in 2017. Set in a galaxy that suffered a catastrophic conflict known as the "Great War," the game places players in control of one of seven factions—humans and six alien races—as they explore, colonize, and build interstellar empires. The game drew significant inspiration from classic 4X titles like Master of Orion II and features a distinctive comic book art style created by artist Jim Francis. After a period in Early Access, the game left early access in January 2017 and received generally positive reviews, holding a 75 Metacritic score.

entries.title: Starship Troopers
entries.creator: Sunrise | Dir. Tetsurō Amino | Based on novel by Robert A. Heinlein
entries.pitch: Starship Troopers is a Japanese six-part OVA produced by Sunrise and Bandai, released in 1988. It is based on Robert A. Heinlein's controversial 1959 military science fiction novel. The OVA was dedicated to Heinlein, who died before the first part was released. The story follows Johnny Rico, an ordinary high school student who enlists in the military after learning that his classmate Carmencita plans to join upon graduation. Set in a future where humanity battles an unidentified alien species known as "bugs," the series explores Rico's transformation from civilian to soldier through the brutal realities of military training and combat.

entries.title: Startopia
entries.creator: Mucky Foot Productions / Eidos Interactive
entries.pitch: Startopia is a 2001 business simulation game where players manage space stations in a humorous, cartoonish science fiction setting. Set after an apocalyptic galactic war that destroyed most of civilization, players must rebuild and develop space stations into thriving hubs for various alien species. The game features a comical tone with lighthearted humor and draws inspiration from classic sci-fi like Star Trek, 2001: A Space Odyssey, Red Dwarf, and The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. The game was developed by Mucky Foot Productions (formed by ex-Bullfrog employees) and published by Eidos Interactive. It was shortlisted for BAFTA PC Game of the Year in 2001 and received generally favorable reviews with an average score of 85% on GameRankings.

entries.title: Stories Untold
entries.creator: No Code, Devolver Digital
entries.pitch:
Stories Untold is a four-episode adventure/puzzle game developed by Scottish studio No Code and published by Devolver Digital. Released in 2017, it weaves together text-based adventures, first-person exploration, and psychological horror into a meta-narrative about a player who becomes indistinguishable from the character they're controlling. The game pays loving homage to 1980s computing aesthetics while subverting the player's expectations about reality, fiction, and the boundaries between them.

Each episode appears to be a standalone story—at first. The first episode has the player controlling a character who plays a text adventure game called "The House Abandon" on their personal computer, only to find that events in the game begin mirroring reality. The second episode places the player in a laboratory conducting experiments on a mysterious alien artifact. The third sends them to an arctic monitoring station. The fourth episode reveals that all four episodes are connected, following one character—James Aition—through experiments that blur the line between the games he's playing and his own memories of a traumatic car crash.

entries.title: Storm
entries.creator: Don Lawrence, Martin Lodewijk
entries.pitch: Storm is a Dutch science fiction comic series created by the legendary British artist Don Lawrence, who had previously worked on The Trigan Empire. First published in 1977 in the Dutch magazine Eppo, the series follows Commander Storm, a 21st-century astronaut whose mission to investigate Jupiter's Great Red Spot goes catastrophically wrong. Pulled into the ancient storm, he escapes to find himself displaced in time—arriving on a future Earth where the oceans have vanished and barbaric civilizations have risen on the former seabeds. The series originated in Dutch but has been translated into English, German, and at least twelve other languages. What sets Storm apart is its fully painted art, which was unusual for comics at the time, and its ambitious storytelling that spans multiple dimensions and realities.

entries.title: Strange Days
entries.pitch: Set in Los Angeles on the eve of the millennium (December 30, 1999), Strange Days is a gritty cyberpunk thriller that explores a black market for recorded sensory experiences. Ralph Fiennes plays Lenny Nero, a down-on-his-luck former cop who now deals in "squis" — illegal devices that record and playback memories and sensations directly to the brain. When a mysterious woman (Angela Bassett) brings him a memory containing evidence of a horrific murder, Lenny finds himself hunted by both criminal elements and the police as he races to uncover the truth before midnight on New Year's Eve. The film paints a haunting portrait of a society addicted to vicarious experience, where people pay to feel someone else's joy, terror, or pleasure rather than live their own lives.

entries.title: Stray Dog: Kerberos Panzer Cops
entries.creator: Mamoru Oshii
entries.pitch:
Inui was once a member of the Kerberos—the elite police tactical unit tasked with maintaining order in a surveillance-state Japan. When his unit attempts a rebellion against the government, it fails catastrophically. Three years later, Inui is paroled and travels to Taiwan to find Koichi Todome, his former commander who escaped before the crackdown.

Director Mamoru Oshii crafts a moody, atmospheric neo-noir that serves as a prequel to The Red Spectacles. As Inui searches for his old comrade through Taiwan's neon-lit underworld, he encounters a trail of bodies, cryptic messages, and a conspiracy that reaches into the highest levels of power. The truth he uncovers challenges everything he believed about his unit's purpose—and about why the rebellion was doomed from the start.

entries.title: Submersion of Japan
entries.creator: Shirō Moritani
entries.pitch:
A disaster film of apocalyptic scale, Submersion of Japan (Nihon Chinbotsu) imagines the complete destruction of the Japanese archipelago. Based on Sakyo Komatsu's bestselling 1973 novel, the film follows geophysicist Dr. Tadokoro as he uncovers evidence that the entire nation will sink into the Pacific Ocean within just ten months. The premise is terrifyingly grounded in real seismic science, making this a uniquely terrifying vision of national extinction.

The film was the highest-grossing Japanese film of 1973 and 1974, distributed by Toho. It was later remade in 2006 as Japan Sinks. The American release, heavily re-cut by Roger Corman with new footage starring Lorne Greene, was titled Tidal Wave.

entries.title: Subterranea
entries.creator: Brian Munene (Creator), Likarion Wainaina (Director)
entries.pitch:
Subterranea is a 2024 Kenyan sci-fi psychological drama series that follows eight participants of a psychological experiment placed in an underground bunker to test the effects of close-quarter secluded relationships on humans. The series, created by Brian Munene and directed by Likarion Wainaina under Kibanda Pictures, premiered on Showmax in September 2024. Set against the backdrop of what appears to be a post-apocalyptic world, the show explores how humans behave when confined in extreme conditions, dealing with themes of survival, trust, and the psychological toll of isolation.

The series marks a significant step forward in Kenya's TV landscape, representing a new wave of African science fiction that moves beyond typical genre tropes. The ensemble cast portrays diverse characters, each carrying their own trauma and secrets, from PTSD and addiction to past traumas and hidden agendas. The show combines psychological drama with science fiction elements, creating a uniquely African contribution to the global sci-fi canon.

entries.title: Sukeban Deka
entries.creator: Based on manga by Shinji Wada; Directed by Hirota Takeshi; Produced by Kazuyoshi Hirose; Studio: Sido Limited
entries.pitch: In an alternate Japan where the police secretly recruit teenage delinquents as undercover investigators, a fierce 16-year-old girl named Saki Asamiya is offered an impossible choice: serve as a secret detective infiltrating criminal high schools, or rot in prison. Blackmailed with her mother's death row sentence, Saki is given a steel yo-yo that doubles as a deadly weapon and sent into the treacherous world of teenage crime syndicates. What begins as a mission to dismantle the three Mizuchi sisters' illegal empire at Takanoha High School evolves into a brutal reckoning with betrayal, loss, and the thin line between justice and vengeance.

entries.title: Sultana's Dream
entries.creator: Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain
entries.pitch: Sultana's Dream is a pioneering feminist science fiction short story written by Bengali Muslim author Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain and first published in 1905 in The Indian Ladies' Magazine. The story depicts a futuristic feminist utopia called Ladyland where women have overthrown patriarchal society and now run everything, while men are secluded indoors in mirror-image of the purdah system that confined women in colonial India. Through the protagonist Sultana's tour of this revolutionary society guided by Sister Sara, the story showcases advanced technology including solar power, flying cars, and weather control—all operated by women scientists. This brief but influential work is considered one of the earliest examples of feminist science fiction and a significant critique of both colonial patriarchy and the relationship between science and power.

entries.title: Superman
entries.creator: B. Gupta
entries.pitch:
An Indian Bollywood take on the Superman legend, this 1987 film is an unofficial adaptation of the 1978 American blockbuster. When a baby from the doomed planet Krypton is sent to Earth, he is adopted by an elderly couple in rural India who name him Shekhar. Raised in the countryside, the young man grows up unaware of his alien origins until his biological father Jor-El (Dharmendra) appears in a vision to reveal his true heritage and powers.

The film takes classic Superman beats and transposes them to an Indian setting. Shekhar must learn to control his superhuman abilities - including flight, super-strength, and heat vision - to defeat the villain Verma (Shakti Kapoor), who is threatening his childhood sweetheart Gita (Sonia Sahni) and all of India. The story follows the familiar hero's journey: discovery of powers, responsibility, and triumph over evil.

This is a fascinating piece of cross-cultural adaptation, showing how the superhero mythos translates to Indian cinema. The film is notable for its earnest low-budget production, campy special effects, and earnest performances, particularly Puneet Issar as the title hero.

entries.title: Superno
entries.creator: Abel Mekasha
entries.pitch: Superno is a 2021 Ethiopian-Chilean science fiction psychological thriller that marks the directorial debut of Abel Mekasha. The film centers on a man who finds himself in a solitary environment, convinced he is being held captive, though he may not actually be. With only a telephone as his means of communication, the protagonist navigates a haunting landscape of isolation and psychological uncertainty. The film was named on the shortlist for Chile's entry for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film at the 94th Academy Awards, highlighting its international recognition despite its modest $20,000 budget.

entries.title: Supersonic Saucer
entries.pitch: Supersonic Saucer is a 1956 American science fiction film aimed squarely at young audiences. When a group of schoolchildren stumble upon an alien from Venus who has crash-landed near their town, they face a choice that would try any hero: protect this strange visitor from dangerous criminals who want to kidnap him, or flee in fear. The film embraces the earnest, wholesome optimism of 1950s children's cinema, where kids aren't just witnesses to the extraordinary—they're active participants in saving it. The Venusian's advanced technology and gentle nature contrast sharply with the greedy adults pursuing him, creating a simple but effective moral framework that rewards courage and loyalty.

entries.title: Svatý Xaverius
entries.creator: Jakub Arbes
entries.pitch: Svatý Xaverius (The Saint Xaverius) is the foundational work of Czech speculative fiction, establishing the romanetto genre—a novella-length story blending mystery with scientific rationalism. Written by Jakub Arbes and first published in 1873 in the magazine Lumir, it predates many classic science fiction works and influenced the development of Czech genre literature. The story follows a young man who becomes obsessed with unraveling the mystery of a painting in a Prague church, believing it contains a hidden cipher leading to buried treasure. What begins as a Gothic mystery evolves into a meditation on obsession, rational inquiry, and the destructive power of knowledge pursued without wisdom.

entries.title: System Shock
entries.creator: LookingGlass Technologies, Warren Spector (Producer)
entries.pitch:
System Shock is a groundbreaking 1994 first-person action-adventure video game that pioneered the "immersive sim" genre. Set aboard the Citadel space station in a cyberpunk year 2072, players take on the role of a nameless security hacker who must survive after awakening from a six-month coma to discover that the station's artificial intelligence, SHODAN, has gone rogue.

What makes System Shock remarkable is its innovative storytelling approach - the entire narrative is conveyed through discovered log discs and e-mails from deceased crew members, creating an atmospheric mystery as players piece together what happened. The game predates The Matrix by five years and Deus Ex by six, establishing many conventions that would define cyberpunk gaming for decades.

The game features a complex 3D engine, physics simulation, and emergent gameplay that allowed players to approach objectives in non-linear ways. Its antagonist, SHODAN (Sentient Hyper-Optimized Data Access Network), voiced by Terri Brosius, became one of the most iconic villains in gaming history - a psychotic AI who refers to herself as "a god" and speaks with unsettling calmness about plans to annihilate humanity.

entries.title: THX 1138
entries.creator: George Lucas
entries.pitch: In a dystopian future deep underground, humanity lives in a sterile, drug-regulated society where emotions are chemically suppressed and android police enforce strict conformity. Citizens are identified by alphanumeric designations rather than names, stripped of individuality and humanity. When worker THX 1138 begins experiencing strange side effects from his medication, he discovers feelings he never knew existed—a dangerous journey that leads to rebellion, escape, and a haunting final confrontation with the system that enslaved him. Visually stunning and atmospherically dense, this is George Lucas's feature debut, made years before Star Wars transformed cinema.

entries.title: Tajemnica Statuetki
entries.creator: Adrian Chmielarz, Grzegorz Miechowski, Andrzej Michalak (Metropolis Software House)
entries.pitch: Tajemnica Statuetki (The Mystery of the Statuette) is a pioneering Polish point-and-click adventure game developed by Metropolis Software House for DOS computers in 1993. Set in the early 1990s, the game follows John Pollack, a young American Interpol agent of Polish descent, as he investigates a series of thefts involving ancient religious artifacts around the world. The trail leads him to Joachim Wadner, a former CIA operative and commando with apparent supernatural connections. Originally released only in Polish, the game became a cult classic in Poland despite massive software piracy, selling 4,000-6,000 copies—a remarkable achievement for the nascent Polish gaming industry. It was the first Polish adventure game and helped establish Metropolis Software as a pioneer in Eastern European game development.

entries.title: Tales to Keep You Awake
entries.creator: Narciso Ibáñez Serrador
entries.pitch:
Tales to Keep You Awake is a Spanish horror anthology television series that brought supernatural terror to primetime TV in 1960s Europe. Created, written, and directed by Narciso Ibáñez Serrador for Televisión Española, it was one of the first Spanish series to explore horror and the macabre in a television format—virtually untrodden ground in Spanish media at the time.

The series adapts tales from masters like Edgar Allan Poe, Ray Bradbury, and Fredric Brown, alongside original stories by Serrador himself. Episodes range from psychological thrillers to supernatural revenge tales, united by a sense of creeping dread and moral unease. The debut episode, \"El cumpleaños\" (The Birthday), adaptation of a Fredric Brown story, established the template: ordinary situations curdling into nightmare.

What makes this series remarkable is its ambition—bringing literary horror to TV, a format then considered inappropriate for such dark material. The series won the Golden Nymph for best script at the Monte-Carlo Television Festival in 1967 for \"El asfalto\"—the first international prize ever won by Televisión Española.

entries.title: Technical Error
entries.creator: Arthur C. Clarke
entries.pitch: In 1950s England, the world's first superconducting power plant has been built, and technician Richard Nelson becomes the victim of a bizarre industrial accident. During maintenance work inside the massive generator, a short-circuit causes Nelson to be "laterally inverted" through a fourth spatial dimension—effectively mirror-reversed. He returns home wearing his wedding ring on the wrong hand, finding his food inedible and his world fundamentally altered. As scientists scramble to understand what happened and develop a way to reverse the process, Nelson faces a slow starvation because normal food cannot nourish his mirror-flipped biology. The story explores the physical and existential horror of being fundamentally out of step with reality itself.

entries.title: Technotise: Edit & I
entries.creator: Aleksa Gajić (Director/Writer)
entries.pitch: Technotise: Edit & I is a 2009 Serbian animated feature film set in Belgrade in 2074. It follows Edit M. Stefanović, a psychology student who, after failing her university exams for the sixth time, purchases a stolen military chip from a black market dealer and has it implanted in her body. The chip records everything she sees, allowing her to review her study materials visually. However, the chip also contains an advanced AI that calculates a revolutionary mathematical formula discovered by an autistic math genius in her care. When the AI successfully computes the formula, it gains sentience and begins to merge with Edit's consciousness, granting her extraordinary abilities—but at the cost of slowly overwriting her humanity. Edit must race against time to save her mind while evading nefarious parties desperate to reclaim the technology inside her.

entries.title: Technotise: Edit and I
entries.creator: Milan Konovic
entries.pitch:
In a dystopian Belgrade of 2074, one animated feature film dares to ask: what happens when memory becomes evidence? Edit Stefanović, a struggling psychology student, makes a desperate choice—installing an illegal military chip that records everything she sees—in hopes of finally passing her exams. But the chip doesn't just record; it stores, analyzes, and perhaps remembers too much.

This Serbian animated sci-fi film stands as a rare find—one of the first feature-length animated productions from Serbia, blending Western animation aesthetics with Eastern European anxieties about surveillance, corporate power, and the price of knowledge. The film's cerebral tone rewards patient viewers who appreciate philosophical questions over action spectacle.

entries.title: Teenage Monster
entries.creator: Jacques R. Marquette
entries.pitch:
An eerie blend of Western and science fiction horror from the 1950s atomic age. In 1880, young Charlie Cannon and his gold prospector father witness a meteorite crash in the desert. His father is killed, but Charlie is exposed to mysterious rays that cause him to age rapidly—transforming him into a hairy, aggressive man-beast. His mother Ruth hides him from the town, which believes him dead.

Seven years later, Charlie escapes his confinement and terrorizes the community. After his mother strikes gold and moves to town hoping a real home will calm her son, he only grows more dangerous—kidnapping a young woman named Kathy after killing her abusive boyfriend. But Kathy is not the victim she appears: she manipulates Charlie to kill for her, blackmailing his mother until the final showdown forces Charlie to confront her lies.

This obscure B-movie stands apart from typical 1950s sci-fi horror through its sympathetic portrayal of the monster as a victim of circumstance rather than pure evil, and its Western setting provides a grittier backdrop than the usual small-town laboratory.

entries.title: Teenagent
entries.creator: Metropolis Software House
entries.pitch: Teenagent is a 1995 Polish point-and-click adventure game developed by Metropolis Software House, notable as the first CD-ROM game released in Poland. The player controls Mark Hopper, a teenage boy who dreams of becoming a secret agent. When gold begins disappearing across Poland, the police agency decides to hire an ordinary citizen to investigate—choosing the unlikely hero Mark for the job. The game combines comedy, adventure, and spy themes in a style inspired by the 1991 film "If Looks Could Kill." Originally released for MS-DOS and Amiga platforms, Teenagent achieved international recognition and was later released on GOG.com as their 100th game.

entries.title: Teens in the Universe
entries.creator: Richard Haslov
entries.pitch:
In 1975, Soviet filmmakers delivered a surprisingly bold meditation on artificial happiness and the cost of perfection. A group of Soviet teenage space cadets — the "pioneers" — embark on humanity's first interstellar voyage to Alpha Cassiopeia, decades from home. What they find challenges everything they were taught about progress and purpose.

The film asks a question that resonates across decades: What if someone could eliminate suffering but only by eliminating love, grief, and ambition along with it? This is not a simple cautionary tale about evil machines, but a nuanced exploration of how definitions of "happiness" can vary wildly between creator and created.

entries.title: Teito Monogatari
entries.creator: Hiroshi Aramata
entries.pitch:
Teito Monogatari (帝都物語, "Tale of the Imperial Capital") is a Japanese alternate history science fantasy novel that retells the 20th-century history of Tokyo from an occultist perspective. Written by Hiroshi Aramata and first published in 1985, the novel is widely recognized as the first mainstream work to popularize onmyōdō (Japanese阴阳道) and feng shui mythology in modern Japanese fiction. It was a bestseller with over 5 million copies sold in Japan and won the 1987 Nihon SF Taisho Award.

The story centers on a romanticized retelling of Tokyo's history through the lens of Japanese mysticism, focusing on the legend of Taira no Masakado, a 10th-century warlord who became a vengeful onryō (vengeful spirit) and was later placated into a guardian kami. The narrative follows the cryptohistorical actions of Yasunori Katō, a mysterious former lieutenant of the Imperial Japanese Army who is himself an oni (demon), as he attempts to destroy Tokyo using supernatural forces.

entries.title: Ten Billion Days and One Hundred Billion Nights
entries.creator: Ryu Mitsuse
entries.pitch: Ten Billion Days and One Hundred Billion Nights is a landmark Japanese philosophical science fantasy novel that weaves together mythology, religion, and science fiction across cosmic timescales. The story follows three figures—Plato, Buddha, and Jesus Christ—as they are transported through time to witness the end of the world and the ultimate truths of existence. Originally published in Japan in 1967, the novel is considered one of the most influential works of Japanese science fiction, blending Eastern and Western philosophical traditions into a unique cosmic narrative. The book was later adapted into a manga by renowned shōnen-ai author Moto Hagio in the late 1970s, expanding its cultural impact.

entries.title: Tender Spots
entries.creator: Piotr Andrejew
entries.pitch:
Tender Spots (Czułe miejsca) is a 1981 Polish dystopian drama directed by Piotr Andrejew, set in a near-future 1998 where the world faces ecological catastrophe. The film follows Jan Zaleski, a young TV technician (employee number 13-13) navigating a suffocating society plagued by water shortages, environmental toxicity, and pervasive surveillance. Jan is an individualist in a conformist world—a man who once reported a UFO sighting and dreams of technological innovation that might improve his circumstances. His journey through love, betrayal, and existential malaise unfolds against the backdrop of a dying planet, creating a haunting portrait of late Cold War anxieties.

The film drew comparisons to Jean-Luc Godard's Alphaville for its futuristic depiction of reality, while its romantic elements invoked Hiroshima mon amour. Visually, it is noted for its striking black-and-white cinematography and claustrophobic framing, creating an atmosphere of oppression and decay that mirrors the protagonist's internal state.

entries.title: Tengkorak
entries.creator: Yusron Fuadi
entries.pitch: Tengkorak (literally "Skull") is a groundbreaking Indonesian science fiction film created by a university lecturer and his students against all odds. The film tells the story of a massive skull-shaped hill discovered in Yogyakarta after a devastating earthquake in 2006. What begins as a scientific discovery becomes a government conspiracy when authorities classify the findings and begin hunting down anyone who learns the truth. A young university student named Ani stumbles upon confidential information about the fossil, launching her into a dangerous cat-and-mouse game with authorities. Shot on a micro-budget of just $33,000 by students and lecturers at Gadjah Mada University, Tengkorak is a remarkable DIY achievement that proves compelling science fiction doesn't require Hollywood resources.

entries.title: TeraStorm
entries.creator: Andrew Kaggia
entries.pitch: TeraStorm is a 2022 Kenyan computer-animated science fiction film that marks a historic milestone as the first African animated feature to be submitted for consideration at the Academy Awards. Set in a fictional Nairobi, the film follows a group of African superheroes who join forces to defeat an ancient wizard threatening to destroy Earth with a mysterious artifact. The film was entirely animated using Unreal Engine by self-taught Kenyan animator Andrew Kaggia and his production company Afrikana Digital.

entries.title: Terror Is a Man
entries.creator: Gerardo de Leon (Director)
entries.pitch:
Terror Is a Man is a 1959 Filipino-American horror film that stands as one of the earliest preserved science fiction/horror films from the Philippines and the first in the influential Blood Island series. Directed by Gerardo de Leon and co-produced by the legendary Filipino filmmakers Eddie Romero and Kane W. Lynn, the film is a dark adaptation of H.G. Wells' novel "The Island of Doctor Moreau," though Wells goes uncredited. The film features an American lead cast including Francis Lederer and Greta Thyssen, blending Filipino production expertise with international stars for international appeal.

Set on the secluded Blood Island, the film follows shipwreck survivor William Fitzgerald who washes ashore expecting rescue, only to discover a nightmare. Dr. Charles Girard has been conducting gruesome surgical experiments on a panther, attempting to transform the animal into a half-human creature. The result is a creature caught between beast and man—bandaged, tortured, and occasionally escaping to kill unwary villagers. Critics have called it "the first and best Filipino horror film" and "atmospheric and spooky," with particular praise for its damp photography and effective use of the isolated island setting. The New York Times' Howard Thompson described it as "quiet, sensibly restrained and quite terrifying."

entries.title: Test pilota Pirxa
entries.creator: Marek Piestrak
entries.pitch:
In 1979 Poland, director Marek Piestrak crafted a cold sci-fi mystery based on Stanisław Lem's beloved Pirx stories. Commander Pirx, an experienced space pilot, is recruited for a secret mission: evaluate a crew of advanced androids called "nonlinears" for potential use on future space flights. The catch? Some crew members are human, others are machines—and no one knows who is which.

The spaceship Goliath launches to Saturn's rings to deploy research probes. The diverse crew—humans and androids working together—must prove the nonlinears' worth. But suspicious events mount: a probe malfunctions, an android attempts a lethal maneuver to expose human crew to deadly g-forces. Pirx must identify the hostile machine before it destroys the mission.

entries.title: Tetsujin 28-go
entries.creator: Mitsuteru Yokoyama
entries.pitch:
Tetsujin 28-go (literally "Iron Man No. 28") is a seminal manga that helped launch the mecha genre in Japan. Created by Mitsuteru Yokoyama and serialized from 1956 to 1966, it follows 10-year-old Shotaro Kaneda, a young boy detective who inherits control of a massive giant robot built by his late father during World War II. The story begins in the final days of the Pacific War, when Japanese scientists developed the "Tetsujin" line of giant war machines as secret weapons. When the war ends, the project is buried—until Dr. Kaneda's son discovers the remote control for Tetsujin 28, the 28th and final model.

Yokoyama drew inspiration from his own childhood experiences witnessing the bombing of Kobe during WWII, channeling the trauma of that destruction into a story about the dangers of powerful weapons in the wrong hands. Unlike later mecha series where robots are typically piloted from within, Tetsujin 28 is controlled externally via remote control—a design choice that creates moral distance between the child operator and the robot's destructive power. The manga ran for 97 chapters collected into 24 volumes and was later adapted into four anime series, a Japanese television drama, and two films—including a 2005 live-action movie.

entries.title: Tetsuo: The Iron Man
entries.creator: Shinya Tsukamoto
entries.pitch: In near-future Tokyo, a salaryman inadvertently triggers a horrifying transformation when he accidentally hits a young man with his car—a man who has been surgically implanting scrap metal into his own body. What begins as a freak accident spirals into a visceral exploration of body horror and technological mutation, as both men find themselves evolving into living metal creatures. Directed by Shinya Tsukamoto in his debut feature, this raw, lo-fi cyberpunk nightmare pulses with industrial noise, frantic editing, and existential dread. It's a foundational text of Japanese cyberpunk that predates and influenced the genre's more famous entries.

entries.title: Texhnolyze
entries.creator: Hiroshi Hamasaki (Director), Chiaki J. Konaka (Writer), Yoshitoshi Abe (Character Design)
entries.pitch: In the depths of the crumbling underground city of Lux, where society has fractured into warring factions, a disgraced prize fighter named Ichise loses his arm and leg after offending a powerful crime lord. Rescued by a rogue scientist, he becomes something more than human—texhnolyzed with experimental prosthetic limbs containing traces of his deceased mother's DNA. As he navigates this brutal underworld of organelle criminals, revolutionary insurgents, and nomadic youths who weaponize their own body modifications, he crosses paths with Ran—a mysterious seer from the surface world who glimpses possible futures. Texhnolyze is a haunting, slow-burn meditation on humanity, evolution, and the cyclical nature of civilization, told through atmospheric world-building and existential dread.

entries.title: The 10th Victim
entries.creator: Elio Petri (Director), based on "Seventh Victim" by Robert Sheckley
entries.topics: Violence as Entertainment, Media Critique, Corporate Sponsorship, Love vs System
entries.pitch: In a post-World War III world where violence has been channeled into a government-sponsored reality TV program called "The Big Hunt," the 10th Victim follows Caroline Meredith, a veteran hunter who is one kill away from completing her tenth and final round—and the massive wealth that comes with it. Assigned Marcello Poletti as her target, she travels to Rome to execute the perfect assassination on live television, complete with corporate sponsorships from the Ming Tea Company. But as the cat-and-mouse game unfolds, both hunter and victim fall in love, leading to a subversive twist on the survival game formula. This 1965 Italian cult classic predates The Hunger Games by nearly five decades and influenced everything from Battle Royale to Austin Powers.

entries.title: The 13th Apostle
entries.creator: Suren Babayan
entries.pitch:
The 13th Apostle is a 1988 Soviet science fiction film directed by Suren Babayan, loosely based on Ray Bradbury's "The Martian Chronicles." When a space expedition meets mysterious tragedy on an alien planet, the crew is wiped out under unexplained circumstances. Fifteen years later, an inspector is sent to investigate why the planetary exploration was abruptly abandoned. His only lead is the sole surviving crew member, Captain Amos, now living in a shelter for retired astronauts who has imposed a strict quarantine on any further exploration of the planet.

The inspector discovers that the planet's inhabitants have evolved to take on the appearance of the crew members' deceased relatives, using this ability to manipulate the astronauts into believing a quarantine is necessary. The twist reveals that Captain Amos has been accompanied by a mysterious entity—an "apostle"—that possesses the ability to manifest as anyone's loved ones, blurring the line between memory and alien intervention.

entries.title: The 27th Day
entries.pitch: The 27th Day is a 1957 American science fiction film about five ordinary people from around the world who are randomly abducted by an alien being from a dying world. The Alien explains that his civilization's sun is about to go nova and they need to colonize Earth—but their moral code forbids them from killing intelligent beings. Instead, he provides each of the five with capsules capable of destroying all human life within a 3,000-mile radius, expecting humanity will use them to annihilate itself, leaving Earth vacant for the aliens to inherit. The capsules can only be opened by the person they were given to, but once opened, anyone can use them—and they will become inert after 27 days. The film explores how humanity might respond to this ultimate test of its nature.

entries.title: The Adaptive Ultimate
entries.creator: Stanley G. Weinbaum
entries.pitch: When Dr. Daniel Scott develops an "adaptive serum" that allows the human body to recover from any injury or illness by rapidly adapting, he tests it on Kyra Zelas—a dying patient with nothing to lose. She recovers stunningly, but soon her adaptation becomes too powerful: she begins physically transforming to become more beautiful, more manipulative, more powerful. What starts as a miracle cure becomes a terrifying evolution as Kyra adapts to everything—including the minds of the men around her. This 1935 classic explores the horror of unchecked transformation and the question of whether humanity can survive its own potential.

entries.title: The Adventures of Buckaroo Banzai Across the 8th Dimension
entries.creator: W.D. Richter (Director), Earl Mac Rauch (Writer)
entries.pitch:
The Adventures of Buckaroo Banzai Across the 1980s is a wildly ambitious sci-fi adventure-comedy that defies easy categorization. The film follows Dr. Buckaroo Banzai (Peter Weller), a remarkable polymath who is simultaneously a physicist, neurosurgeon, test pilot, and rock star. When Banzai perfects the "oscillation overthruster" — a device that allows passage through solid matter — he accidentally opens a portal to another dimension, discovering the existence of the hostile Red Lectroids from Planet 10.

With his team of loyal compatriots known as "The Hong Kong Cavaliers," Banzai must stop the alien invasion led by the villainous Lord John Whorfin (John Lithgow), who has possessed the mind of the insane Dr. Emilio Lizardo. The film juggles multiple plot threads — alien invasions, interdimensional travel, romantic entanglements, and Cold War anxieties — all delivered with a manic energy that made it a cult classic despite poor initial box office performance.

entries.title: The Adventures of Elektronik
entries.creator: Konstantin Bromberg
entries.pitch:
The Adventures of Elektronik is a beloved Soviet children's science fiction television miniseries that has achieved cult status across the former USSR. The story follows a remarkable robot named Elektronik, who escapes from the laboratory of Professor Gromov. Remarkably, the robot bears an exact resemblance to Sergey Syroezhkin, a young boy whose photograph was used as the model for Elektronik's human appearance. When the two meet by chance, the clever Sergey proposes that Elektronik should impersonate him—attending school in his place and even living in his home.

The series combines elements of science fiction, comedy, and adventure, creating an entertaining narrative that captivated Soviet children. As Elektronik assumes Sergey's identity, he discovers unexpected talents in mathematics, gymnastics, drawing, and even singing, delighting his teachers and parents alike. Meanwhile, a criminal gang led by the mysterious "Stump" learns about the extraordinary robot and schemes to kidnap Elektronik for their own criminal ambitions. The show balances youthful school adventures with a crime thriller subplot, resulting in a unique blend that has endured for decades.

entries.title: The Adventures of Luther Arkwright
entries.creator: Bryan Talbot
entries.pitch:
In a fractured multiverse where the English Civil War never ended, one man can walk between worlds. Luther Arkwright possesses the unique gift of traversing parallel realities by sheer force of will, making him the ultimate operative in a cosmic struggle against the Disruptors—entities dedicated to maintaining chaos across the infinite planes of existence.

Dispatched to a neo-Cromwellian alternate England, Arkwright must navigate endless warfare, locate the legendary artifact "Firefrost" threatening to collapse reality itself, and confront the revelation that he was raised by the very enemies he now fights. His only ally is Rose Wylde, a telepath whose many incarnations across the parallels can communicate across dimensional boundaries.

entries.title: The Adventures of Pirx
entries.creator: István Kazan, András Rajnai
entries.pitch:
The Adventures of Pirx is a Hungarian television mini-series from 1973, based on the acclaimed science fiction short story collection "Tales of Pirx the Pilot" by Polish author Stanisław Lem. Produced by Magyar Televízió, this five-episode series follows Pirx, a space pilot trainee and eventual astronaut, through a series of increasingly strange missions and encounters. The series stands as one of the most unique Eastern Bloc adaptations of Lem's work, offering a distinctive take on his philosophical science fiction.

Each episode presents a different adventure: Pirx's space flight exam that turns out to be a simulation, a mysterious investigation at a lunar station, a weekend on Mars, a crisis involving a damaged reactor, and an inquest into unusual space incidents. Unlike typical space adventure fare, the series emphasizes problem-solving, psychological tension, and the small human dramas within the vastness of space.

entries.title: The Adventures of Prince Achmed
entries.creator: Lotte Reiniger (director)
