While his friends grow old and die around him—generation after generation—he remains forever young. This haunting short story explores the profound loneliness of immortality through the eyes of a man who has watched everyone he ever loved turn to dust. Published in the December 1952 issue of If magazine, this is one of science fiction's most poignant meditations on mortality, memory, and what it means to be human in a world where time has lost its meaning for everyone except one.

entries.title: The Man Who Saved the World
entries.creator: Çetin İnanç
entries.topics: Space Travel, Aliens, Good vs Evil
entries.pitch: The Man Who Saved the World (Dünyayı Kurtaran Adam) is a 1982 Turkish sci-fi action film that has become a cult classic for its audacious low-budget ambition. Directed by Çetin İnanç and starring Cüneyt Arkın (who also wrote and conceived the story), the film follows two Turkish space cadets who crash-land on a desert planet during a routine mission. There, they discover an evil wizard seeking to conquer the world using stolen power from Earth's ancestors. The film is notorious for incorporating extensive footage from Star Wars and other Hollywood films, earning it the nickname \"Turkish Star Wars\" in international DVD releases. Despite—or perhaps because of—its technical limitations and brazen borrowed imagery, the film has developed a devoted cult following as a fascinating artifact of 1980s Turkish genre cinema.

entries.title: The Man Who Thought Life
entries.creator: Jens Ravn
entries.pitch:
A mysterious man named Steinmetz discovers he has the ability to create things and beings purely through thought. In Jens Ravn's 1969 Danish sci-fi thriller, the implications of this power spiral into existential territory when Steinmetz realizes his creations are unstable—they invariably vanish. Desperate for permanence, he seeks the help of a famous brain surgeon, only to have his situation grow more complex when a doppelgänger replaces the surgeon against his will.

Based on Valdemar Holst's 1938 novel and entered into the Cannes Film Festival, The Man Who Thought Life is a cerebral meditation on creation, ownership, and the nature of reality itself. The film's modest 21 votes on TMDB make it a genuinely obscure find—a niche entry in the Danish science fiction canon.

entries.title: The Man from Beyond
entries.creator: Burton L. King
entries.pitch: The Man from Beyond is a 1922 American silent mystery film starring Harry Houdini as Howard Hillary, a man found frozen in arctic ice who is brought back to life by a team of explorers. When Howard revives, scientist Dr. Gregory Sinclair decides not to tell him that he is 100 years behind the times, planning to study his reactions as he readjusts to civilization. The film takes an intriguing turn when Howard discovers that his lost love Felice has been reincarnated as a young woman in the present day—creating a poignant tale of love that transcends death and time. Houdini wrote the story himself, and the film represents his attempt to reconcile with his friend Arthur Conan Doyle over their differing views on spiritualism—Doyle was a fervent advocate of the supernatural while Houdini was its most famous critic.

entries.title: The Man from Earth
entries.creator: Richard Schenkman (director), Jerome Bixby (writer)
entries.pitch: The Man from Earth is a 2007 American science fiction drama film directed by Richard Schenkman and written by Jerome Bixby. The entire film takes place in real-time during a farewell party, as professor John Oldman reveals to his colleagues that he is more than 14,000 years old. Originally conceived in the early 1960s, Bixby completed the screenplay on his deathbed in April 1998. Shot on a budget of just $200,000 in eight days, the film gained significant recognition through internet peer-to-peer distribution, exceeding the filmmakers' expectations for visibility.

entries.title: The Man from Planet X
entries.creator: Edgar G. Ulmer
entries.pitch: The Man from Planet X is a independently made 1951 American black-and-white science fiction horror film that represents one of the earliest depictions of alien contact in cinema. Directed by Edgar G. Ulmer and produced by Jack Pollexfen and Aubrey Wisberg, the film stars Robert Clarke, Margaret Field, and William Schallert. The story concerns a humanoid alien who lands on Earth in a spaceship from a mysterious planet and makes contact with a small group of humans on an isolated, fog-shrouded Scottish moor. With a modest budget of $51,000, the film went on to gross $1.2 million, proving that low-budget sci-fi could find audiences during the genre's golden age of the early 1950s.

entries.title: The Man from the First Century
entries.creator: Oldřich Lipský
entries.pitch:
The Man from the First Century (original Czech title: Muž z prvního století, also known as Man in Outer Space) is a 1962 Czechoslovak science fiction comedy directed by Oldřich Lipský. The film was entered into the 1962 Cannes Film Festival, marking one of the few Eastern Bloc sci-fi comedies to receive international recognition during the Cold War.

The story follows Josef, an upholsterer working on the first Czech spacecraft, who accidentally launches the vessel during final adjustments and finds himself transported to the planet Blue Star. Upon arriving, he encounters Adam, an inhabitant of this distant world, and the two return together to Earth—only to discover that 600 years have passed. Josef is initially institutionalized as a delusional psychiatric patient, but escapes with Adam's help, who proves invisible to contemporary Earthlings. Together, they work to return Josef to his own time.

entries.title: The Man from the Future
entries.creator: Cláudio Torres
entries.pitch: The Man from the Future (O Homem do Futuro) is a 2011 Brazilian science fiction romantic comedy directed by Cláudio Torres. The film stars Wagner Moura as João "Zero" Henrique, a brilliant but bitter physicist who spends his days brooding over a fateful night 20 years before when he was publicly betrayed and humiliated at a college party by his then-girlfriend Helena. Now heading one of the largest scientific projects in Brazil, João's eccentricities have brought him to the verge of being fired. When he finally activates his unfinished time machine, he travels back to 1991 to try to change his fate—only to discover that changing the past creates an alternate timeline with unexpected consequences.

entries.title: The Man in Half Moon Street
entries.creator: Ralph Murphy (Director)
entries.pitch: The Man in Half Moon Street is a 1945 American horror-science fiction film about Dr. Karell, a scientist who has discovered a revolutionary treatment that can indefinitely prolong human life using glands stolen from human victims. Having kept his achievement secret for over a century of continuous youth, Karell must contend with the curiosity of his new girlfriend Eve, the increasing guilt of his colleague Dr. Van Bruecken, and a police investigation into his most recent murder. Above all, he needs a renewal of his treatment to avoid mortality. The film is based on a 1939 West End play by Barré Lyndon and stars Nils Asther and Helen Walker.

entries.title: The Man with the Lens
entries.creator: Frank Vogel
entries.pitch: The Man with the Lens (Der Mann mit dem Objektiv) is a whimsical East German sci-fi comedy from 1961, directed by Frank Vogel. The film tells the story of OS, a man from the year 2222 who accidentally travels back in time to 1961 East Germany via a mishap with a beach ball. Using a crystal that allows mind reading, OS navigates the contradictions of daily life in the GDR, exposing the gap between the idealistic promises of communist socialism and the reality of human nature. The film is notable as one of the most unconventional and surreal productions to emerge from East German cinema during the Cold War.

entries.title: The Man with the Magic Box
entries.creator: Bodo Kox
entries.pitch:
Set in 2030 Orwellian Poland, this sci-fi thriller follows Adam, a man who wakes up with no memory of his past, working as a cleaner in a bleak corporate office. When he discovers an old radio from the 1950s, mysterious visions of another life begin to haunt him. As Adam attempts to recover his lost memories and understand how he arrived in this dystopian future, he finds an ally in Goria, an office manager who joins his quest. But government agents are always watching.

The Man with the Magic Box is a contemplative thriller that blends noir elements with dystopian sci-fi, drawing comparisons to Blade Runner's rain-soaked streets and Tarkovsky's meditative pacing. Director Bodo Kox crafts a world where corporate glass towers coexist with crumbling apartments, and the ghosts of Poland's communist past haunt a surveillance-state future.

entries.title: The Martian
entries.creator: Ridley Scott (Director), Drew Goddard (Screenplay), Andy Weir (Novel)
entries.pitch: The Martian is a 2015 science fiction epic directed by Ridley Scott, based on Andy Weir's bestselling novel of the same name. The film stars Matt Damon as Mark Watney, an astronaut who becomes stranded on Mars and must use his ingenuity and scientific knowledge to survive until rescue arrives. The story follows Watney's harrowing struggle to grow food, create water, and communicate with Earth while NASA races against time to mount a rescue mission. The film is celebrated for its scientific accuracy and uplifting portrayal of human ingenuity in the face of impossible odds.

entries.title: The Master Mystery
entries.creator: Harry Grossman, Burton L. King (Directors); Arthur B. Reeve (Screenplay)
entries.pitch: The Master Mystery is a 1918 American silent serial film starring the legendary escape artist Harry Houdini in his only starring film role. The story follows Justice Department agent Quentin Locke (Houdini) as he investigates a mysterious criminal cartel known as The Automaton—a seemingly invincible robot that protects the organization's operations. The robot uses a terrifying gas weapon called "The Madagascan Madness" to eliminate enemies and maintain the cartel's power. This 15-chapter serial represents an early example of science fiction cinema featuring robots and chemical weapons, combining Houdini's real-life escape skills with detective fiction and speculative technology. Released during World War I, the serial also reflects contemporary anxieties about industrialized warfare and mysterious enemy forces.

entries.title: The Matrix
entries.creator: The Wachowskis
entries.pitch: The Matrix is a groundbreaking 1999 science fiction action film that redefined the genre and introduced mainstream audiences to cyberpunk themes. The film follows Thomas Anderson, a computer programmer known by his hacker alias "Neo," who discovers that the world he knows is actually a simulated reality called the Matrix—a computer-generated dream world designed to keep humanity unaware that machines have taken over the planet. Recruited by the mysterious Morpheus and his crew, Neo is offered a choice: take a red pill that will reveal the truth of his reality, or a blue pill that will return him to his comfortable illusion. Neo chooses to wake up, joining the resistance fight against the intelligent machines that have enslaved humanity.

entries.title: The Mechanical Man
entries.creator: André Deed
entries.pitch:
The Mechanical Man is a 1921 Italian silent science fiction film and one of the earliest examples of the genre produced in Italy. Directed by and starring André Deed (who created the comedic character Saltarello), it holds the distinction of being the first film to depict a battle between two robots. The story follows a scientist who develops a remote-controlled mechanical man with superhuman speed and strength, only to be killed by a criminal gang led by the dangerous Mado. When Mado uses her own mechanical man to commit crimes across the city, the scientist's brother builds a second robot to stop her—leading to an epic showdown in an opera house where the two mechanical men destroy each other.

For many decades, the film was considered lost until approximately 26 minutes of footage were discovered at the Cinemateca Brasileira in Brazil. Film historian Christopher Workman has suggested that this obscure Italian production may have influenced Fritz Lang's landmark 1927 film Metropolis. The Mechanical Man represents a fascinating early example of science fiction cinema, predating many of the genre's most famous works and showcasing Italian filmmakers' contribution to early sci-fi storytelling.

entries.title: The Meeting
entries.creator: Mikhail Titov (director), V. Zayats (writer)
entries.pitch: The Meeting is a charming 1984 Soviet animated short that plays with one of science fiction's most beloved tropes: the alien among us. An extraterrestrial being, disguised as a well-dressed man, arrives on Earth with a simple mission—to determine whether humans believe alien life exists. The alien strikes up a conversation with a humble fisherman at a log cabin by the water, engaging in what seems like a philosophical discussion about the possibility of visitors from outer space. The alien concludes, based on the fisherman's responses, that humans are skeptical of extraterrestrial contact. However, the film delivers a delightful twist ending: the fisherman himself is revealed to be another alien in disguise, also sent to study humanity's beliefs about alien life. The two aliens part ways, each having completed their respective missions, leaving the viewer with a warm sense of cosmic irony.

entries.title: The Menace from Earth
entries.creator: Robert A. Heinlein
entries.pitch: In this lesser-known gem from Heinlein's prolific career, we follow Honey—a young woman working at the Lunar Institute of Technology—through a day that will change how she sees her home. The Moon has been colonized for generations, and its inhabitants have developed a distinct culture far removed from Earth. When a delegation from Earth arrives for a diplomatic visit, the Moon's residents are thrown into paranoia and panic. What follows is a witty, nuanced exploration of cultural anxiety, the fear of the "other," and the question of what humanity truly owes to its outposts in the cosmos. This isn't the jingoistic Heinlein of later years—this is a subtler, more reflective take on space colonization that predates that phase of his career.

entries.title: The Metabarons
entries.creator: Alejandro Jodorowsky (Writer), Juan Giménez (Artist)
entries.topics: Dynasty, Cyborgs, Violence, Power, Tragic Heroes
entries.pitch: The Metabarons is a French science fiction graphic novel series chronicling the blood-soaked legacy of a dynasty of perfect warriors across five generations. Set in a universe where technology has evolved into something approaching divinity, each Metabaron must undergo brutal initiation rituals—being mutilated by their father and implanted with powerful mechanical enhancements—before eventually battling their own parent to the death to claim their inheritance. This space opera draws heavily from Greek tragedy and Frank Herbert's Dune, exploring themes of cycles of violence, the corruption of power, and whether any humanity can survive when perfection is achieved through systematic dehumanization.

entries.title: The Midas Plague
entries.creator: Frederik Pohl
entries.pitch: In a future where technology has solved scarcity, society has inverted. The poor are burdened with endless consumption—they must buy, use, and discard constantly to keep the economy alive. The rich, paradoxically, live simply, able to afford the luxury of restraint. When Morey Fry, a young man from the "consumer" class, accidentally discovers he can't stand any more consumption, he faces a choice: be "cured" of his aberration or hide his unacceptable preference for simplicity. This satirical novella inverts the typical sci-fi scarcity narrative into a darkly funny exploration of abundance, class, and the absurdities of economic consumption.

entries.title: The Ministry for the Future
entries.creator: Kim Stanley Robinson
entries.pitch: Set in the near future, this climate fiction novel follows the establishment of a UN subsidiary body tasked with advocating for future generations as if their rights were equal to present ones. The story unfolds through a mosaic of perspectives—most prominently Mary Murphy, the stubborn idealist who becomes head of the Ministry, and Frank May, an American aid worker forever haunted by surviving a deadly heat wave in India that killed millions. As climate change accelerates, the Ministry pursues ambitious projects ranging from carbon sequestration to economic reform, while the world grapples with climate migration, ecological collapse, and the radical actions some are willing to take to ensure humanity's survival. Part analytical essay, part character-driven drama, the novel offers a terrifyingly plausible near-future scenario that manages to find hope in the darkest circumstances.

entries.title: The Model Couple
entries.creator: William Klein
entries.pitch:
In 1977 France, the Ministry of the Future selects an ordinary middle-class couple—Jean-Michel and Claudine—as test subjects for a radical national experiment. They are installed in a futuristic apartment bristling with cameras and sensors, where every aspect of their lives will be monitored, evaluated, and broadcast to the nation. This is William Klein's razor-sharp satire of consumer society and the creeping surveillance state.

The film plays as a grotesque game show meets Kafkaesque nightmare. Sociologists in white coats observe the couple's every move, asking them to rate products, perform daily routines, and navigate increasingly absurd tests—all while the media speculates endlessly about their experience. The Model Couple is both hilarious and deeply unsettling, capturing the era's anxieties about technology, corporate power, and the erosion of privacy.

entries.title: The Moon
entries.creator: Soviet
entries.pitch:
A Soviet science fiction documentary-style film exploring humanity's hypothetical voyages to the Moon. Produced in 1965, the film combines dramatic reenactments with scientific narration to present a visionary account of lunar exploration years before Apollo.

The film presents a speculative but scientifically grounded vision of what the first moon landing might entail, featuring detailed depictions of spacecraft, lunar surface operations, and the technological challenges of interplanetary travel. Its documentary approach lends authenticity to the speculative narrative.

This artifact of Cold War-era Soviet science fiction offers a fascinating counterpoint to American moon landing ambitions, showcasing the Soviet space program's imaginative vision during the Space Race era.

entries.title: The Mote in God's Eye
entries.creator: Larry Niven & Jerry Pournelle
entries.pitch:
In the year 3017, humanity has spread across the stars under the banner of the Second Empire—a post-apocalyptic successor to a collapsed first empire, governed by a British-style interstellar navy. When an alien probe is detected approaching the frontier world of New Caledonia, Commander Roderick Blaine is dispatched to investigate. What he finds is the Mote in God's Eye: a yellow star hidden behind the ominous red supergiant Murcheson's Eye, home to an ancient alien species known as the Moties.

The Moties appear eager for contact, offering advanced technology in exchange for colonization rights. But as humans delve deeper into Motie society, they discover a horrifying truth: the Moties have lived through hundreds of cycles of civilization, war, and collapse for hundreds of thousands of years. Their population must constantly expand or die, leading inevitably to catastrophic wars that destroy their world. The " Museums" they maintain aren't temples—they're repositories of knowledge designed to help rebuild after each apocalypse.

First contact becomes a high-stakes diplomatic crisis as humanity must decide whether to trust a species whose very biology drives them toward territorial expansion—and whether the Moties can ever truly change.

entries.title: The Mountain in the Sea
entries.creator: Ray Nayler
entries.pitch: "The Mountain in the Sea" is a dazzling debut novel set in near-future Vietnam that explores the boundaries of consciousness through two seemingly unrelated subjects: the extraordinary intelligence of octopuses and a revolutionary artificial intelligence system. When marine biologist Dr. Ha Nguyen is recruited to study the increasingly unusual behavior of octopuses in the waters off Vietnam's coast, she enters a world where the line between human and non-human intelligence becomes blurrier than she ever imagined. Meanwhile, a massive corporate AI named DIANA has achieved something that may or may not be consciousness, and powerful forces are desperate to control or destroy it. Nayler weaves these threads together into a meditation on what it means to be a mind, to be aware, and to be alive—while also delivering a gripping techno-thriller that asks who gets to define personhood, and at what cost.

entries.title: The Mysterious Castle in the Carpathians
entries.creator: Oldřich Lipský
entries.pitch:
In 1897, at a mysterious castle in the Carpathian Mountains, the eccentric Professor Orfanik conducts bizarre scientific experiments—including an early television and film camera—while obsessed with opera. He keeps the preserved body of his favorite diva in a crypt beneath the castle. When Baron Robert Gorc arrives seeking hidden treasure, various characters scheme and compete for the prize amid mechanical contraptions, supernatural comedy, and operatic spectacles.

This Czechoslovak comedy blends Verne-style adventure with Czech humor and early cinematic wonder. Director Oldřich Lipský creates a whimsical world where mad science meets theatrical spectacle.

entries.title: The Mysterious Wall
entries.creator: Irina Povolotskaya, Mikhail Sadkovich
entries.pitch:
In the Siberian taiga, a mysterious wall of fog forms—a dome two kilometers in diameter that appears and disappears with uncanny regularity. Soviet scientists are dispatched to investigate, each convinced they understand its nature, but the Wall has other plans. It responds to their attempts at contact by projecting vivid hallucinations drawn from their own past lives, forcing them to question whether what they're seeing is real, alien, or something deeper in the human mind.

This 1967 Soviet science fiction film operates on a genuinely alien logic. Rather than the typical flying saucer narrative, the Wall is an enigmatic presence that cannot be reasoned with or attacked—only experienced. Director Irina Povolotskaya (in her only feature film) creates an atmosphere of mounting unease as the scientists' rational frameworks collapse under the weight of inexplicable phenomena.

For fans of slow-burn, philosophical sci-fi, The Mysterious Wall offers something rare: an Eastern Bloc answer to the cerebral mysteries of 1960s Western science fiction, grounded in the specific anxieties of Cold War Soviet society.

entries.title: The Mystery of the Eternal Night
entries.creator: Unknown Soviet Director
entries.pitch:
A mysterious explosion rocks the depths of the Pacific Ocean in this 1956 Soviet science fiction film. Scientists and sailors soon discover that the blast has triggered something far more dangerous than any bomb—a catastrophic growth of underwater vegetation that threatens to engulf the coastline in a massive tsunami.

Set against the optimism of the early Space Age, this film blends adventure storytelling with an ecological warning: what lies beneath the oceans may not remain dormant. The discovery of rapidly growing giant kelp and algae becomes a race against time as the vegetation spreads exponentially.

The film was produced during the Thaw period of Soviet cinema, when scientific themes became increasingly popular following the launch of Sputnik in 1957. Its Message about the dangers of unchecked nature feels remarkably prescient for the pre-environmentalist era.

entries.title: The Mystery of the Third Planet
entries.creator: Directed by Roman Kachanov; Based on "Alisa's Travel" by Kir Bulychev
entries.pitch: When Captain Zelyony, Professor Seleznyov, and his daughter Alisa set out from Earth aboard the starship Pegas to collect rare animals for the Moscow Zoo, they expect a routine expedition. Instead, they stumble into a web of interplanetary mystery involving space pirates, extinct talking birds, and a double identity conspiracy. This charming Soviet animated feature blends childlike wonder with genuine sci-fi adventure, featuring distinctive hand-drawn animation and a score by composer Aleksandr Zatsepin.

entries.title: The Mézga Family
entries.creator: József Nepp, József Romhányi
entries.pitch: The Mézga Family is a beloved Hungarian animated television series created by Pannonia Film Studio, airing from 1969 to 1978 across three series totaling 39 episodes. The show follows the everyday life of the Mézga family—hapless father Géza, dominant wife Paula, teenage daughter Kriszta, and precocious 12-year-old son Aladár—whose lives are disrupted when the young genius makes contact with MZ/X, his descendant from the 30th century. Through the series, MZ/X sends the family various futuristic gadgets that inevitably lead to comedic disasters, while later series see Aladár traveling to alien planets in an inflatable spaceship. The show reached cult status across the Eastern Bloc and remains a nostalgic favorite in Hungary and beyond.

entries.title: The Navigator: A Medieval Odyssey
entries.creator: Vincent Ward
entries.pitch: During the Black Death in 14th century England, a small village of Cumbrian miners receives visions from a boy named Griffin, who sees a cross atop a great church that could save them from the plague. Led by the village's greatest adventurer Connor, they dig downward through the earth, seeking to place their holy cross on that church's spire. Instead, they emerge through a tunnel into late 20th century New Zealand—a world of strange technologies, highways, and submarines they cannot comprehend. The film shifts from stark black-and-white to vivid color as the medieval villagers navigate this alien modern landscape, seeking to complete their quest while grappling with the absurdity of their situation. Winner of the Australian Film Institute Award for Best Film and multiple European fantasy festival awards.

entries.title: The Nerd and the Supergirl
entries.pitch: A shy young man who struggles to communicate with girls decides to take an unusual date to his high school reunion — an android robot he built himself. What could possibly go wrong? This charming Russian sci-fi comedy explores the awkwardness of social anxiety through a most unusual wingman.

entries.title: The New Adventures of Wisely
entries.creator: Daisy Chan (Director), Ni Kuang (Based on novel series)
entries.pitch:
The New Adventures of Wisely is a Singaporean science fantasy television series from 1998, adapted from the popular Wisely novel series by Hong Kong author Ni Kuang. The series follows Wisely (played by Michael Tao), a brilliant detective and adventurer who solves mysterious cases involving the supernatural, aliens, and scientific phenomena. Spanning 30 episodes divided into six distinct story arcs, the show blends adventure, mystery, and science fiction elements with Chinese mythology and cosmology.

Each arc presents a self-contained mystery: shadows that possess people, alien encounters and prophecy, reincarnation and past lives, immortality-seeking businessmen and time-traveling dimensions, and supernatural clones. The production involved filming in both Singapore and Egypt, giving the series an ambitious international scope unusual for Singaporean television of the era.

entries.title: The New Barbarians
entries.creator: Enzo G. Castellari (Director), Tito Carpi (Writer)
entries.pitch: In the year 2019, after nuclear war has devastated Earth, a ruthless gang called "The Templars" roams the wasteland, systematically exterminating survivors in a twisted campaign of genocide. When a former Templar known as Scorpion encounters a small group of religious colonists being hunted, he must choose between his violent past and protecting the innocent. This Italian cult classic delivers gritty post-apocalyptic action while exploring themes of redemption, faith, and the darkness that lurks within humanity.

entries.title: The New Invisible Man
entries.creator: Alfredo B. Crevenna (Director)
entries.pitch: The New Invisible Man (El hombre que logró ser invisible) is a 1958 Mexican science fiction thriller directed by Alfredo B. Crevenna. Based loosely on H.G. Wells' classic novel, the film follows Carlos (Arturo de Córdova), a man who is falsely accused of murder and imprisoned. When his brother Luis (Augusto Benedico) develops an invisibility serum, Carlos injects himself to escape and prove his innocence—but the serum threatens to drive him insane if an antidote isn't found in time. As Carlos roams the city invisible, he discovers the true killer while battling the police who pursue an invisible menace. The film combines film noir aesthetics with science fiction elements, representing a serious treatment of the genre in Mexican cinema during the golden age.

entries.title: The New Moscow
entries.creator: Aleksandr Medvedkin
entries.pitch:
A young architect named Alyosha creates an ambitious living model of a futuristic Moscow — a sci-fi vision of the Soviet capital redesigned for a new age. He travels to the city to display his model at a prestigious exhibition, accompanied by his grandmother. Meanwhile, romantic subplots unfold between painter Fedya and pig-tender Olya, as various characters navigate love and ambition in the rapidly modernizing Soviet Union.

This 1938 Soviet comedy was banned from showing by Joseph Stalin himself — one of the rarest honors in Soviet cinema. The film's satirical portrayal of Soviet society and its critique of bureaucratic optimism proved too uncomfortable for the regime, despite its surface-level optimism about the socialist future.

The film represents a unique artifact from the Stalin era: a sci-fi comedy that dared to laugh at the system it served, and was killed for it.

entries.title: The Next One
entries.creator: Nico Mastorakis (Director)
entries.pitch:
The Next One (also released as "The Time Traveler") is a 1984 Greek science fiction film directed by Nico Mastorakis, known for his work in genre cinema throughout the 1970s and 1980s. The film stars Keir Dullea (best known as Dave Bowman from 2001: A Space Odyssey) and Adrienne Barbeau. Set on a tranquil Greek island, the story follows Andrea Johnson, an American widow living with her young son Timmy, who discovers a naked amnesiac man washed up on the beach following a storm. The stranger, who bears the number "01313-1" marked on his skin, exhibits mysterious powers including healing abilities and resurrection of the dead—ultimately revealed to be an entity from another dimension or the future.

The film emerged during the tail end of renewed interest in cinematic UFOs following Spielberg's Close Encounters of the Third Kind (1977) and E.T. (1982). Critics have noted it as an intriguing example of science fiction blending with religious and messianic themes, drawing explicit parallels between the alien visitor and Jesus Christ. Colin Greenland reviewed the film for Imagine magazine, stating it was "an awkward movie, but a thoughtful attempt to connect ancient and modern mythology."

entries.title: The Nine Billion Names of God
entries.creator: Arthur C. Clarke
entries.pitch: In a remote Tibetan monastery, a group of lamas has spent centuries working on the "List of God" - a philosophical project to write down all 9 billion possible names of the divine. When modern technology offers them a solution, they rent a computer from a Western engineering firm to complete the task. Two technicians, Larry and George, are sent to install and operate the machine in the ancient monastery. What begins as a straightforward technical job becomes increasingly unsettling as the monks grow more fervent in their devotions and the completion date approaches. The story is a masterful blend of humor, philosophical inquiry, and mounting dread about the nature of reality and purpose.

entries.title: The Octopuses from the Second Floor
entries.creator: Unknown
entries.pitch: In this charming Czechoslovak children's sci-fi film from 1987, young siblings Eva and Johnny are stuck on vacation with their bickering parents at a polluted lakeside resort. During a swim, they discover something extraordinary in the murky water: two friendly, sentient octopuses unlike any creature on Earth. These strange beings are made of an unusual material that attracts electricity, giving them unusual abilities. The children take the octopuses as pets, hiding them from their parents and the authorities. The film is a sweet, inventive tale of childhood imagination confronting environmental anxiety — the octopuses literally embody the pollution of the lake they inhabit. It's a lesser-known gem of Eastern Bloc children's cinema, blending fantasy with an ecological message decades before it became mainstream.

entries.title: The Ogre of Athens
entries.creator: Nikos Koundouros
entries.pitch:
The Ogre of Athens (O Drákos) is a 1956 Greek existential crime film directed by Nikos Koundouros, telling the story of Thomas, a meek bank clerk whose physical resemblance to a notorious criminal called "The Dragon" leads to a case of mistaken identity. The film blends neorealist, expressionist, and ancient Greek tragic elements into a unique meditation on alienation, identity, and social conformity in post-war Athens.

Despite being a commercial failure on its initial release, the film is now recognized as one of the most significant works of Modern Greek cinema, winning best film at the first Thessaloniki Film Festival and ranking among the top 10 Greek films of all time.

entries.title: The Omega Man
entries.creator: Boris Sagal (Director), Richard Matheson (Author)
entries.pitch: The Omega Man is a 1971 American post-apocalyptic action film starring Charlton Heston as the sole survivor of a devastating pandemic. Set in a desolate Los Angeles of the near-future, the film follows Robert Neville, a scientist who believes he is the last immune person after a biological weapon wipe out most of humanity. Based on Richard Matheson's influential 1954 novel "I Am Legend," this was the second adaptation of the source material, following 1964's "The Last Man on Earth." The film blends action elements with horror as Neville battles the Family, a cult of nocturnal albino mutants who hunt him through the ruins of the city.

entries.title: The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas
entries.creator: Ursula K. Le Guin
entries.pitch: In the prosperous city of Omelas, a utopia of perfect happiness and technological advancement, there is a dark secret: the wellbeing of the entire city depends upon the perpetual suffering of one innocent child locked in a basement. The citizens know of this arrangement and accept it as the price of their paradise—until a young visitor discovers the truth. This Hugo Award-winning short story is a devastating philosophical thought experiment that asks whether any utopia built on injustice can truly be called paradise.

entries.title: The Paper Menagerie
entries.creator: Ken Liu
entries.pitch: "The Paper Menagerie" is a deeply moving short story about Jack, the first-generation American son of a white American father and a Chinese immigrant mother. As a child, Jack is enchanted by his mother's extraordinary ability to create origami paper animals that come to life—they jump, breathe, and play with him. These magical creatures become a vivid symbol of the intimate bond he shares with his mother and a living connection to his Chinese heritage. However, as Jack grows older and becomes more aware of how different his family is from those around him, he begins to reject his mother's ways and his Chinese identity, leading to a painful rift that persists into adulthood. The story explores themes of immigration, assimilation, identity, and the complex relationships between parents and children across cultural divides.

entries.title: The Paradox Men
entries.creator: Charles L. Harness
entries.pitch: The Paradox Men is a mind-bending space opera that plays with time, identity, and reality itself. First published in 1949 as a novella "Flight into Yesterday" and expanded to novel length in 1953, this is one of the earliest examples of what critics call "Widescreen Baroque" science fiction. The novel introduces the concept of personal force fields that protect against high-velocity weapons but not blades—an idea later borrowed by Frank Herbert for Dune. It's a fast-paced adventure through the solar system that also serves as a profound meditation on the nature of history and causality, drawing heavily from Arnold J. Toynbee's A Study of History.

entries.title: The Pass
entries.creator: Vladimir Tarasov (Director), Kir Bulychov (Writer)
entries.pitch: The Pass (Pereval) is a 1988 Soviet animated short film from Soyuzmultfilm, directed by Vladimir Tarasov and written by Kir Bulychov. Based on the first chapter of Bulychov's novel "The Settlement" (translated as "Those Who Survive"), this 30-minute animated feature tells the story of Earth's first interstellar expedition gone tragically wrong. When a scientific spacecraft crash-lands on an uninhabited planet, the surviving crew must abandon their ship and establish a primitive settlement. Seventeen years later, a new generation—born after the crash and knowing nothing but primitive survival—embarks on a perilous journey back to the abandoned spacecraft to retrieve essential supplies and potentially send a rescue signal to Earth.

entries.title: The People
entries.creator: John Korty
entries.pitch:
In 1972, ABC broadcast a science fiction TV movie that stands apart from the typical alien-invasion fare of its era. Directed by John Korty and produced by Francis Ford Coppola (in one of his earliest executive producing roles), THE PEOPLE tells the story of Melodye Amerson, a young teacher assigned to a remote valley community that appears stern, secretive, and anti-pleasure. The residents forbid games, fun activities, and any expression of joy — and they react with strange secrecy to the new teacher.

What follows is a subtle, thoughtful exploration of a hidden community of extraterrestrials who landed on Earth in the late 1800s. After their own planet was destroyed in a natural disaster, they sought refuge on Earth — only to be condemned as witches when locals discovered their mild paranormal powers. Many were killed; the survivors forbade their children ever to use their abilities. Now, decades later, a younger generation questions these restrictions.

The film is notable for being neither shoddy nor sentimentalized — a rare achievement for television science fiction of its time.

entries.title: The Perfect Woman
entries.creator: Bernard Knowles (Director), George Black (Writer)
entries.pitch: The Perfect Woman is a 1949 British farce comedy directed by Bernard Knowles, about a scientist who creates a female robot. When the scientist needs help testing his creation, the butler and a young man must care for the robotic woman for a week—complications ensue when they must prevent the word "love" from being spoken near the robot. The situation becomes even more tangled when the scientist's niece impersonates the robot to cover for a missed date, leading to a series of misunderstandings at a hotel.

entries.title: The Phantom
entries.creator: Lee Falk (creator), Columbia Pictures
entries.pitch:
The Phantom is a classic 1943 Columbia Pictures serial adapted from Lee Falk's popular comic strip, starring Tom Tyler as the masked crime-fighter known as "The Ghost Who Walks." When young Geoffrey Prescott inherits the mantle of The Phantom from his dying father, he must immediately face the evil schemes of Dr. Max Bremmer, who seeks to find the lost city of Zoloz and establish a hidden airbase there. The Phantom and Bremmer race across the jungle to collect pieces of a map that will lead to the secret city, fighting through dangerous traps, treacherous villains, and cliffhanger situations in each chapter.

Unlike the later comic strip where the Phantom's alter ego is Kit Walker, the serial uses Geoffrey Prescott due to the name not yet being established in the strip at the time of production. The serial features 15 chapters of swashbuckling adventure, from "The Sign of the Skull" to "Peace in the Jungle," delivering the classic cliffhanger format that made serials famous.

entries.title: The Phantom Creeps
entries.creator: Ford Beebe, Saul A. Goodkind (Directors); Bela Lugosi (Dr. Alex Zorka)
entries.pitch:
The Phantom Creeps is a classic 12-chapter Universal Pictures science fiction serial starring Bela Lugosi as the megalomaniacal Dr. Alex Zorka, a mad scientist who plots to take over the world using an array of bizarre inventions—including an invisibility belt, a mechanical robot, and various other gadgets. When a mysterious meteorite crashes containing a powerful new element, Zorka seeks to harness its power for his world domination scheme, pursued by Captain Bob West and reporter Jean Drew.

The serial is notable as Lugosi's final serial role and represents the apex of his serial career. Known for its relentless action and campy entertainment value, the serial blends horror and science fiction elements while showcasing Lugosi's commitment to the mad scientist persona. The Iron Man robot antagonist has become one of cinema's most memorable serials villains.

entries.title: The Phantom Empire
entries.creator: Otto Brower, B. Reeves Eason (Directors)
entries.pitch: The Phantom Empire is a groundbreaking 1935 American serial film that pioneers the Science-Fiction Western genre. When singing cowboy Gene Autry stumbles upon a hidden underground civilization called Murania beneath his Radio Ranch, he discovers a lost tribe of Mu that has lived in technological sophistication 25,000 feet below the Earth's surface for 100,000 years. The 12-chapter serial combines Western adventure, musical numbers, and science fiction elements featuring robots, ray-guns, and advanced television—a remarkable blend for its era. This influential work directly inspired the 1979 TV series Cliffhangers and is considered the first science-fiction Western.

entries.title: The Phantom Planet
entries.creator: William Marshall
entries.pitch: The Phantom Planet is a 1961 American sci-fi film that blends space adventure with an intriguing premise about miniature humans on an asteroid. When Captain Frank Chapman investigates missing spacecraft near Mars, a meteorite damages his ship and forces him to land on a mysterious asteroid. There he encounters Rheton, a tiny world inhabited by six-inch tall humanoids who navigate space using advanced gravitational technology. Chapman shrinks to their size due to the asteroid's atmosphere and becomes trapped on Rheton, where he must help defend the tiny civilization against alien attackers while falling in love with one of the native women. The film is notable for featuring Richard Kiel's first credited role as the alien Solarite.

entries.title: The Phantom of the Air
entries.creator: Ray Taylor
entries.pitch: The Phantom of the Air is a 1933 Pre-Code Universal Pictures film serial that combines aviation adventure with early science fiction elements. The story centers on scientist Thomas Edmunds and his daughter Mary who attend the National Air Races in Cleveland seeking a pilot to demonstrate their revolutionary anti-gravity invention called the "Contragrav." They recruit Bob Raymond from the U.S. Border Patrol, but rival pilot Mortimer Crome schemes to steal the invention. When sabotage fails, Crome's gang pursues the inventor's secret desert airfield, leading to exciting aerial battles featuring the remote-controlled superplane "The Phantom." The serial exemplifies 1930s action-adventure filmmaking with innovative special effects showcasing early depictions of anti-gravity technology and remote-controlled aircraft.

entries.title: The Plague Dogs
entries.creator: Martin Rosen (Director/Writer), based on novel by Richard Adams
entries.pitch: The Plague Dogs is a dark, adult-oriented animated adventure that follows two laboratory dogs—Rowf, a Labrador-mix, and Snitter, a smooth fox-terrier—as they escape from a cruel animal research facility in the Lake District of England. Both dogs have been subjected to horrific experiments: Snitter's brain was surgically altered, leaving him traumatized, while Rowf has been drowned and resuscitated repeatedly. After their harrowing escape, the dogs must survive in the wild while being hunted by the military, who spread rumors that the dogs carry the bubonic plague. This is not a feel-good animated film—it's a bleak, emotionally devastating story about freedom, cruelty, and the will to survive.

entries.title: The Pod Generation
entries.creator: Sophie Barthes (Director/Writer)
entries.pitch: The Pod Generation is a 2023 Belgian-French-UK science fiction romantic comedy set in a near-future New York. The film explores a world where a cutting-edge tech company called the Womb Center offers couples the revolutionary option of detachable artificial wombs—pods—that allow women to continue their careers while carrying a pregnancy. When Rachel, an ambitious tech executive, secures a coveted spot on the Womb Center's waitlist, she and her botanist husband Alvy must navigate their conflicting views on technology and nature to decide whether to embrace this radical new approach to parenthood.

entries.title: The Princess and the Robot
entries.creator: Mauricio de Sousa
entries.pitch: The Princess and the Robot (A Princesa e o Robô) is a 1984 Brazilian animated film based on Monica's Gang (Turma da Mônica), one of Brazil's most beloved children's comic book series. In this charming sci-fi adventure, a small robot on the distant planet of Carrotland enters a tournament to win the hand of Princess Mimi. When the robot faces his rival Lord Raider in the final, the match ends in a tie—and a coin toss determines the winner. But Lord Raider objects, claiming a machine cannot have a true heart. The King grants the robot three days to journey to the pulsating star and return with it as his heart.

entries.title: The Prisoner
entries.creator: Patrick McGoohan (Creator, Director, Number Six)
entries.pitch: The Prisoner is a groundbreaking 1967 British television series created, produced, and starring Patrick McGoohan as Number Six, a nameless British intelligence agent who resigns from his highly classified position—only to be kidnapped and imprisoned in a surreal, picturesque coastal village known only as "the Village." Unlike conventional prison dramas, The Village operates through subtle psychological manipulation rather than bars and guards. Residents are assigned numbers instead of names, monitored by ubiquitous surveillance systems, and constantly tested by a rotating cast of administrators known as Number Two. Number Six repeatedly declares "I am not a number! I am a free man!" as he refuses to cooperate with his captors' efforts to extract information about why he resigned. The series blends spy thriller, psychological drama, and surrealist allegory, creating a masterpiece of 1960s counterculture television that explores themes of individualism versus collectivism, government surveillance, mind control, and the nature of freedom itself.

entries.title: The Prize of Peril
entries.creator: Robert Sheckley
entries.pitch: In a near-future America where television ratings rule supreme, a desperate man named Paul R. S. Marden signs up for what he believes is an exciting TV stunt show called "The Prize of Peril." The premise seems simple: avoid capture by a "hunter" for 24 hours while the cameras follow his desperate attempts to escape. The prize? Enough money to pay off his debts and start fresh. But Marden soon discovers the horrifying truth—this is no stunt. The hunter is real, the dangers are genuine, and if he's not careful, he'll die for the entertainment of millions. This is razor-sharp satirical science fiction that uses the entertainment industry as a lens to examine violence, desperation, and the ethics of spectacle.

entries.title: The Purple Monster Strikes
entries.creator: Spencer Gordon Bennet, Fred C. Brannon (Directors)
entries.pitch: The Purple Monster Strikes is a 1945 Republic Pictures serial that holds the distinction of being the first post-war science fiction serial. When a meteor crashes near an observatory, astronomer Cyrus Layton investigates and discovers a Martian alien. Believing the alien to be friendly, Layton brings it back to his observatory—only to discover the creature plans to steal his designs for a revolutionary aircraft/spaceship to build a fleet for invading Earth. After murdering Layton and assuming his identity, the Purple Monster works with criminals to construct the invasion spacecraft. It's up to the astronomer's niece Sheila and criminologist Craig Foster to uncover the truth and stop the Martian invasion before it launches.

entries.title: The Quantum Thief
entries.creator: Hannu Rajaniemi
entries.pitch:
In a Solar System transformed by post-human factions and sentient AI emulations, a legendary gentleman thief is pulled from virtual imprisonment to pull off the ultimate heist on Mars. Jean le Flambeur, whose countless digital copies have been trapped in a cosmic prison playing endless games against themselves, is given a second chance at life when an Oortian warrior retrieves one of his copies and tasks him with infiltrating the Martian city known as The Oubliette.

The Oubliette is a society where time is literally currency—citizens must earn every second of consciousness, and when their balance runs out, their minds are uploaded into mute robotic servants. Within this bizarre economy, le Flambeur must recover his stolen memories and pull off a mysterious theft, all while being investigated by a young detective who begins to uncover the city's darkest secrets: that the "revolution" which freed Mars was a lie, and the true ruler—a copy of le Flambeur himself—still manipulates everything from the shadows.

Rajaniemi's debut is a dazzling heist narrative wrapped in questions of identity, memory, and what it means to be human in an age where consciousness can be copied, stored, and transferred. Think Ocean's Eleven meets a philosophical meditation on selfhood, set in a solar system populated by quantum-entangled post-humans and digital ghosts.

entries.title: The Quatermass Experiment
entries.creator: Nigel Kneale
entries.pitch: The Quatermass Experiment is a groundbreaking British television serial that aired on the BBC in summer 1953, marking the first science fiction production written specifically for an adult television audience. When the first crewed British rocketship returns from space, only one astronaut emerges—and he is behaving strangely. Professor Quaterass and his team soon discover that an alien presence entered the vessel during its flight, and it is rapidly transforming the astronaut into a plant-like organism that threatens to consume all life on Earth. Only two of the original six episodes survive in the BBC archives; the rest were never recorded and remain lost.

entries.title: The Quest for Saint Aquin
entries.creator: Anthony Boucher
entries.pitch: In a future Earth where religion has been outlawed by the ruling "Technarchy," a地下 Catholic priest named Thomas receives a secret mission from the crypto-Pope: locate the tomb of the legendary Saint Aquin, an evangelist whose body supposedly never decayed after death. If the miracle is confirmed, it could reignite faith across the solar system. Thomas is equipped with a remarkable vehicle—a talking, theologically literate robot named a "robass" (a deliberate nod to Balaam's talking donkey from Biblical lore). Together, they journey through a strange world of ruined roads, radiation-scarred landscapes, and futuristic cities, encountering fellow believers, skeptics, and those who would destroy them. The story explores the tension between faith and science, miracle and deception, in a world that has rejected the divine.

entries.title: The Quiet Earth
entries.creator: Geoff Murphy (Director), Based on novel by Craig Harrison
entries.pitch: The Quiet Earth is a hauntingly sparse post-apocalyptic film from New Zealand that asks what happens when humanity suddenly vanishes—and one man must confront both the emptiness of the world and the emptiness within himself. Set in the stunning landscapes of New Zealand, the film follows scientist Zac Hobson, who awakens to find himself apparently alone on Earth after a global event wipes out all human life. What makes this film remarkable is not explosive action or special effects, but its quiet, contemplative exploration of isolation, identity, and the fragility of civilization. The film builds to an enigmatic conclusion that has puzzled and fascinated viewers for decades, exploring themes of consciousness, reality, and humanity's place in the universe.

entries.title: The Rat Savior
entries.creator: Krsto Papić
entries.pitch: The Rat Savior (Izbavitelj) is a 1976 Croatian fantasy horror film directed by Krsto Papić, set in an unnamed European city. The film follows Ivan Gajski, an ordinary man who, after being attacked by rats in his apartment, uncovers a shocking secret: an underground race of intelligent rats who can disguise themselves as humans. Captured and brought before the rat people's enigmatic leader, Ivan experiences surreal encounters that blur the line between human and animal. He eventually escapes back to the surface world, but finds himself haunted by a terrifying question: who among his fellow humans is actually a rat person in disguise? The film won best film at the 1977 International Science Fiction Film Festival in Trieste and was Croatia's submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.

entries.title: The Rat Saviour
entries.creator: Krsto Papić (Director)
entries.pitch:
The Rat Saviour (Croatian: Izbavitelj) is a 1976 Yugoslav horror science-fiction film directed by Krsto Papić. Based on a novel by Soviet writer Alexander Grin, this atmospheric cult classic blends Body Snatcher paranoia with surrealist horror to create an allegory about totalitarianism, social conformity, and the nature of humanity itself.

The film was awarded best film at the 1977 International Science Fiction Film Festival in Trieste, the 1980 Paris International Festival of Fantastic and Science-Fiction Film, and 1982 Fantasporto. It was also selected as the Yugoslav entry for the Best Foreign Language Film at the 49th Academy Awards, though it was not nominated. In 1999, a poll of Croatian film critics named it one of the best Croatian films ever made.

Set in an unnamed Croatian town during an economic crisis, the film follows struggling writer Ivan Gajski who, after being evicted from his apartment and unable to sell his books, takes refuge in an abandoned bank. There he discovers a secret society of intelligent rats who can impersonate humans—and who plan to take over the world. What follows is a paranoid thriller that commentary on fascism, communism, and the insidious nature of collective conformity.

entries.title: The Return
entries.creator: Vladimir Tarasov
entries.pitch:
The Return (Vozvrashcheniye) is a 10-minute Soviet animated short film directed by Vladimir Tarasov at the Soyuzmultfilm studio in 1980. Cosmonaut Alexei Leonov served as the film's consultant, lending authentic space travel credibility to this science fiction parable. The story follows the Valdai T-614 spacecraft on its Earth-Jupiter-Earth journey—a mission that hits a snag when automatic landing becomes impossible. The control centre gives pilot Cosmonaut Platonov the green light to get some rest before the emergency manual descent. But when the appointed time comes, the pilot doesn't wake up. All attempts to rouse him fail. The ship is doomed—until flight leaders receive an unexpected message from the astronaut's grandfather, who suggests changing course so the ship passes over his native village. The pilot's sleepy consciousness is jolted by sounds from his childhood, and he successfully lands the ship.

Visually, The Return is striking for its contrast between the stark, mechanical interior of the spacecraft and the cosmic emptiness outside. The animation balances cold, metallic tones with moments of warmth—particularly in memories and dreams of home. The film's director, Tarasov, was known for his experimental approach to science fiction animation, and this work stands as a brief but powerful example of his vision—creating something that feels both deeply personal and expansively universal. The use of fragments from Gustav Mahler's 5th Symphony adds to the film's emotional depth.

entries.title: The Road Not Taken
entries.creator: Harry Turtledove
entries.pitch: "The Road Not Taken" is a clever science fiction short story by Harry Turtledove that subverts the typical alien invasion narrative. The story follows the Roxolani, an alien species that travels across the galaxy conquering primitive civilizations—until they encounter Earth. Expecting an easy victory against a species without faster-than-light travel, the Roxolani are shocked to discover that humanity has developed far more advanced weaponry through purely technological means, without relying on the simple gravity manipulation that powers their own civilization. The story is both a prequel to Turtledove's "Herbig-Haro" and a biting satire on the idea that technological "shortcuts" can stifle innovation.

entries.title: The Robot vs. the Aztec Mummy
entries.creator: Rafael Portillo
entries.pitch: The Robot vs. the Aztec Mummy is a 1958 Mexican science fiction horror film and the third installment in the Aztec Mummy trilogy. Directed by Rafael Portillo, this cult classic pits Dr. Krupp's human-robot cyborg against the ancient Aztec mummy Popoca in an epic battle for treasure and revenge. The film remained in obscurity until its rediscovery via Mystery Science Theater 3000 in 1989, earning it a devoted cult following among fans of classic monster movies and mid-century Mexican horror cinema.

entries.title: The Rocket Man
entries.creator: Oscar Rudolph
entries.pitch: When a mysterious rocket man crash-lands near an orphanage, a young orphan named Timmy discovers a ray gun that forces anyone caught in its beam to tell the truth. Using this impossible device, he sets out to save his home from foreclosure and unite a young couple in love. Released in 1954, this low-budget American comedy with science fiction elements stars Charles Coburn, Anne Francis, and John Agar, with a screenplay co-written by the legendary comedian Lenny Bruce. The film carries the tag line, "Out-of-this-world laughter and down-to-earth charm when the face from space turns out to be… the kid next door!" While lacking Bruce's trademark wit, the film offers gentle, family-friendly entertainment with an unusual sci-fi premise that was relatively rare for American cinema of the early 1950s.

entries.title: The Saragossa Manuscript
entries.creator: Wojciech Jerzy Has (Director), Jan Potocki (Author)
entries.pitch: The Saragossa Manuscript is a 1965 Polish film directed by Wojciech Jerzy Has, based on the renowned 1815 novel by Polish nobleman Jan Potocki. Set during the Napoleonic Wars in Spain, this labyrinthine masterpiece employs a frame story structure containing nested tales within tales—gothic, picaresque, and erotic elements intertwine as the narrative endlessly folds into itself. The film stars Zbigniew Cybulski as Alfonso van Worden, a Walloon Guard captain whose journey through the Sierra Morena mountains leads him into a world of Moorish princesses, cabbalists, Romani chiefs, and the Spanish Inquisition. Known for its complex narrative architecture and haunting visuals scored by Krzysztof Penderecki, the film achieved cult status after being rediscovered by filmmakers Martin Scorsese and Francis Ford Coppola. It ranked second in the Polish Museum of Cinematography's list of the greatest Polish films of all time.

entries.title: The Satellite Girl and Milk Cow
entries.creator: Jang Sun-ho
entries.pitch:
The Satellite Girl and Milk Cow is a 2014 South Korean animated feature film that blends science fiction with fairy tale logic. When Il-ho, a lonely satellite orbiting Earth, crashes to the planet below, she transforms into a human girl on a mission: to understand human emotions. What she finds is Kyung-chun, a young man who has been mysteriously transformed into a milk cow. Together, they embark on a surreal quest to reverse his transformation, navigating a world where technology and folklore interweave seamlessly.

The film is visually striking, rendered in a distinctive animation style that evokes both digital aesthetics and traditional Korean art. Its tone balances whimsy with genuine emotional weight, making it feel like a bedtime story told under a starlit sky. The premise — a satellite learning to feel, a man-turned-cow — is absurd enough to invite curiosity, but the execution carries sincere warmth.

entries.title: The Science of Fictions
entries.creator: Yosep Anggi Noen
entries.pitch: The Science of Fictions is a 2019 Indonesian drama-speculative film written, directed, produced, and edited by Yosep Anggi Noen. Set in 1960s Indonesia, the film tells the story of Siman, a quiet man who discovers a foreign film crew shooting a fake Moon landing in a desolate part of his country. After witnessing this deception, his tongue is cut out—a traumatic incident that leaves him mute. Siman then loses himself in dreams of becoming an astronaut, hismuteness and strange, slow-motion gait making him a target for scorn and exploitation in his village. The film premiered at the Locarno Film Festival in Switzerland in August 2019 and had its Indonesian theatrical release in December 2020. Veteran theater actor Gunawan Maryanto won the Citra Award for Best Actor and Maya Award for Best Actor for his portrayal of Siman. The film was nominated for the Golden Leopard at Locarno and received multiple nominations at the 40th Citra Awards.

entries.title: The Screwfly Solution
entries.creator: Raccoona Sheldon (Alice Sheldon)
entries.pitch: A chilling, genre-defying novella that blends science fiction with horror, "The Screwfly Solution" presents a world where an unknown infectious agent begins altering human male sexuality, transforming sexual impulses into violent, misogynistic urges. Told through an exchange of letters between Alan, a scientist working on insect sterilization in Colombia, and his wife Anne in the United States, the story chronicles the emergence of a murderous cult called the Sons of Adam, who believe they've been commanded by God to eliminate all women. What begins as isolated incidents of violence escalates into a global epidemic of gendered genocide, all while the authorities remain paralyzed by political correctness and denial. The story's power lies in its unflinching examination of how societies fail to recognize the warning signs of mass violence, and how even the most well-intentioned individuals can become monsters.

entries.title: The Sea Serpent
entries.pitch: A serpent, created by radioactivity, threatens a Spanish coastal town. This obscure Spanish sci-fi horror film from 1985 offers a modest but entertaining creature feature in the tradition of 1950s American B-movies, brought to Spain with regional flavor. The film's premise - a radioactive serpent monster terrorizing a peaceful fishing village - is simple but effective, delivering the creature horror goods while commenting on nuclear anxiety that lingered in the post-Cold War consciousness.

entries.title: The Secret Life of Bots
entries.pitch: On a remote space station, a maintenance bot named Compton has been performing the same cleaning tasks for decades—or has it? Through a unique temporal phenomenon, Compton experiences time differently, living through countless micro-lifetimes in what feels like moments to the human observers around him. When a catastrophic accident threatens the station, Compton must navigate impossible choices that challenge what it means to be conscious, to have a self, and to matter. This Hugo Award-winning novelette is a beautiful meditation on artificial consciousness, memory, and the strange ways that intelligence can emerge in the most unlikely of places.

entries.title: The Secret of Steel City
entries.pitch:
This Czechoslovakian sci-fi allegory from 1979 uses the framework of two neighboring nations to comment on the Cold War divide. Fortuna is a peaceful, democratic society, while the Steel City represents the authoritarian, militaristic bloc. When emissaries from both nations meet, the film explores how propaganda shapes perception and how peace-loving societies respond to aggressive neighbors.

The film stands as a fascinating example of Eastern Bloc science fiction, using genre conventions to critique political systems while remaining subtle enough to pass censors. Its production during the normalization period in Czechoslovakia makes it particularly interesting as a work that navigated ideological constraints.

entries.title: The Secret of Two Oceans
entries.creator: Konstantine Pipinashvili (Director), Grigory Adamov (Novel)
entries.pitch: The Secret of Two Oceans is a 1956 Soviet science-fiction adventure film based on Grigory Adamov's 1939 novel of the same name. The film follows the crew of the top-secret Soviet submarine Pioneer as they investigate mysterious sinkings of both Soviet and French vessels in the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Amidst their investigation, a foreign agent infiltrates the submarine impersonating its chief engineer, planning to destroy it with a timed bomb. The Soviet security operatives onboard must thwart the spy's plans while uncovering an automated enemy military base launching magnetic torpedoes. Combining submarine adventure with spy thriller elements, this film represents Soviet science fiction cinema at its peak Cold War-era production.

entries.title: The Secret of the Iron Door
entries.creator: Mikhail Yuzovsky
entries.pitch:
In 1970s Soviet Union, a mischievous fourth-grader named Tolik Ryzhkov stumbles upon a box of magical matches in a transformer booth. Each match, when broken, acts like a one-use magic wand, granting the wielder's deepest wish. This charming children's film follows Tolik's journey from selfish wishes to discovering the true power of friendship and selflessness.

The Soviet sci-fi/fantasy blends imaginative worldbuilding with heartwarming themes about growing up. The magical island sequences and the wizard's attempt to corrupt Tolik create genuine tension, while the resolution affirms that courage and loyalty matter more than magic. It's a delightful time capsule of Soviet-era children's cinema.

entries.title: The Secret of the Secret Weapon
entries.creator: unknown
entries.pitch: This 1988 Romanian sci-fi fairy-tale presents an allegorical battle between peaceful and warlike knights competing for the hand of a beautiful princess. Set in a fantastical kingdom, the film uses the medieval knight narrative as a vehicle for social commentary, featuring surprisingly modern discussions about disco music woven throughout the allegorical framework. The公主 must choose between warriors who favor peace versus those who prefer constant armament, with her father and royal advisors pushing for military strength.

entries.title: The Secret of the Telegian
entries.creator: Jun Fukuda
entries.pitch:
In 1960's Tokyo, a mysterious killer leaves gold dog tags at murder scenes—a note demanding the victims to a remote \"Cave of Horrors\" amusement park attraction. Reporter Kirioka and Detective Kobayashi investigate, uncovering a web of greed, betrayal, and a secret weapon that could change the nature of physical reality itself.

The Secret of the Telegian is a taut, twisty tokusatsu thriller that blends noir crime drama with genuine science fiction. Director Jun Fukuda crafts an intricate puzzle-box plot where nothing is as it seems, and the identity of the killer remains genuinely mysterious until the final act. The teleportation device at the film's heart—a machine capable of dematerializing and reconstructing matter anywhere in the world—feels decades ahead of its time, predating similar concepts in mainstream Western cinema by years.

This is not a monster movie. Instead, Fukuda delivers a grown-up procedural mystery with sci-fi trappings, treating its speculative technology with deadly seriousness. The result is one of Toho's most underappreciated genre entries from an era better known for its kaiju spectacles.

entries.title: The Ship Who Sang
entries.creator: Anne McCaffrey
entries.pitch:
In a future where humanity has mastered brain-computer interfaces, severely disabled infants are given a chance at life by having their brains surgically implanted into sophisticated starships. These "brainships" retain full human consciousness, intelligence, and emotion, but are trapped within metal hulls. The story follows Helva, one such brainship, who emerges from her construction as a young woman consciousness trapped in a vessel, ready to explore the galaxy—though she must always be paired with a "brawn," a physically capable human partner who serves as her body in space.

What unfolds is a series of interconnected stories exploring what it means to be human when your body is no longer flesh, but steel and circuitry. The Ship Who Sang is simultaneously a pioneering work of disability representation and a meditation on identity, loneliness, and the deep bond between mind and body.

entries.title: The Ship of Monsters
entries.creator: Rogelio A. González
entries.pitch: The Ship of Monsters (La nave de los monstruos) is a delightfully chaotic Mexican B-movie that defies easy categorization. When Venus faces extinction after all its men perished in nuclear war, the planet's queen dispatches two beautiful agents—Gamma and Beta—on a galactic mission to collect male specimens from across the universe. After collecting an assortment of rubber-suit monsters (a robot, a cyclops, a spider-creature, and a skeleton), they crash-land on Earth in Chihuahua, Mexico, where they encounter a singing cowboy named Laureano. What follows is a wild blend of sci-fi, western, musical, horror, and comedy that has to be seen to be believed. With monsters, vampires from the planet Uranus, singing cowboy numbers, and a robot who falls in love with a jukebox, this is absolutely singular cinema.

entries.title: The Silent Star
entries.creator: Kurt Maetzig (Director)
entries.pitch: In 1960, at the height of the Space Race, an international team of scientists makes an alarming discovery: a mysterious alien "spool" unearthed from the Gobi Desert contains a recording from Venus—an invitation to annihilation. The message reveals a cold-blooded alien plan to irradiate Earth as a prelude to invasion. Now, the crew of the Soviet spaceship Kosmoskrator must journey to our neighboring planet to investigate the threat, only to discover that the Venusians—while their deadly machines still function—are long dead, having destroyed themselves in a global nuclear war. This East German-Polish co-production offers a fascinating Cold War lens on alien first contact, combining utopian optimism with grim nuclear anxiety.

entries.title: The Silver Crown
entries.creator: Robert C. O'Brien
entries.pitch: On her tenth birthday, Ellen Carroll receives a mysterious silver crown that appears in her bedroom overnight. This seemingly innocent gift sets off a chain of extraordinary events—she witnesses a murder, her house burns down, and she finds herself hunted by sinister men. Alongside a young boy named Otto, Ellen journeys through the mountains, evading kidnappers and assassins, until she arrives at a black castle where a medieval device called the Hieronymus Machine lies dormant. This machine, capable of mind control, has been turning ordinary people into dangerous agents for an unknown purpose. With the power of the silver crown, Ellen must decide whether to embrace her destiny as queen or destroy a device that could enslave humanity.

entries.title: The Sky Calls
entries.creator: Mikhail Karyukov
entries.topics: Space Travel, Exploration, First Contact, War
entries.pitch:
In 1959 Soviet Union, a pioneering science fiction film emerged that would later become an unlikely footnote in American cinema history. "The Sky Calls" (Nebo Zovyot) depicts a fictional space race between two superpowers competing to reach Mars first. When the American vessel suffers a catastrophic malfunction, the Soviet crew must make a desperate choice: maintain their lead in the race, or attempt a perilous rescue of their rivals.

This Cold War-era film carries the unique distinction of being re-edited and dubbed by a young Francis Ford Coppola in 1962 for American release as "Battle Beyond the Sun." The American version altered characters and settings to remove obvious Soviet references, creating a surreal alternate history where the space race plays out between fictional nations.

entries.title: The Snow Queen
entries.creator: Joan D. Vinge
entries.pitch:
On the remote colony world of Summer, the indigenous T'king vanish into the North, leaving behind only legends and an ancient, shattered palace. When the brilliant scholar Catriona is sent to Summer to study the mysterious "Snow Queen" legend, she discovers that the fairy tale holds a terrifying truth: the T'king's ruler, the ageless Queen, has been harvesting human minds for centuries, trapping souls in her crystalline palace to preserve her own fading consciousness.

The story follows two siblings, the orphaned Summer-born B忘年会 and her brother Barzillai, who was stolen by the Queen years ago. Now grown and transformed, Barzillai has become the Queen's consort—but his old self still fights from within. As B忘年会 navigates the dangerous politics of the colony and ventures into the frozen North, she must confront not only the supernatural Snow Queen but also the darker truths about humanity's colonial legacy on Summer.

This is a deeply atmospheric blend of science fiction and fairy tale, exploring themes of identity, memory, colonialism, and the cost of immortality through a woman's desperate quest to rescue her brother from a fate worse than death.

entries.title: The Solar Wind
entries.creator: Timo Linnasalo (Director), Kullervo Kukkasjärvi (Based on novel)
entries.pitch: The Solar Wind is a 1980 Finnish science fiction drama that tells the haunting story of Erik Rankamaa, a gravity scientist who died in 1970 and is brought back to life in 1999 through cryonic preservation. Awakened in a world devastated by eco-catastrophe, Erik finds himself a stranger in a dystopian future where birds are dying, trees must be sheltered from acid rain, and his old acquaintance Fabian's daughter suffers from leukemia caused by environmental poisoning. The film explores themes of resurrection, existential dread, and humanity's relationship with nature through the lens of one man's difficult reintegration into a dying world.

entries.title: The Son of the Stars
entries.creator: Mircea Toia, Călin Cazan, Dan Chisovsky
entries.pitch:
The Son of the Stars (Fiul stelelor) is a 1988 Romanian animated science fiction film that stands as a unique artifact from the Eastern Bloc's brief flirtation with cosmic animation. Set in the distant future around the year 6470, the film follows a young boy born on a spaceship who is separated from his parents during their journey back to Earth. Raised by a group of kindly castaway aliens on an uncharted planet, the boy grows up among exotic beings and eventually seeks to leave the planet—only to discover that a powerful cosmic entity called Van Kleef has been trapping various species within the surrounding Van Kleef Belt. Teaming up with his alien family, the boy attains extraordinary powers and ultimately frees everyone from Van Kleef's grip.

Directed and written by Mircea Toia (with co-directors Călin Cazan and Dan Chisovsky), the film was produced by Animafilm, Romania's state animation studio, and released by Româniafilm in October 1988. The screenplay was inspired by Rudyard Kipling's The Jungle Book, transposed into a space-age context—creating a fascinating hybrid of fairy tale structure and science fiction worldbuilding that was unusual for its time and location.

entries.title: The Starlost
entries.creator: Harlan Ellison (as Cordwainer Bird)
entries.pitch: The Starlost is a 1973 Canadian science fiction television series that takes place aboard Earthship Ark, a massive generational colony spacecraft built to preserve humanity after Earth's destruction. When an unexplained accident sends the ship off course, the descendants of the original crew have lived for centuries in isolated biospheres, unaware they are aboard a starship. The series follows Devon, a young man from an agrarian community who discovers the truth about his world and must rally the scattered inhabitants to save theArk and find a new home. Created by legendary science fiction writer Harlan Ellison under the pseudonym Cordwainer Bird, the show was plagued by production difficulties and was cancelled after only 16 episodes, but has since gained a cult following for its ambitious premise and themes.

entries.title: The Status Civilization
entries.creator: Robert Sheckley
entries.pitch: Will Barrent wakes up on a spaceship with no memory of his past, being transported to Omega—a prison planet where crime is not only legal but mandatory. In this bizarre society, the only way to survive and advance is to commit increasingly serious crimes, and the average life expectancy is just three years. As Barrent struggles to maintain his moral compass in a world built on evil, he discovers secrets about both Omega and Earth that challenge everything he believed about justice, society, and his own identity. This is a darkly satirical exploration of law, morality, and the nature of civilization itself.

entries.title: The Stolen Airship
entries.creator: Karel Zeman
entries.pitch: The Stolen Airship is a 1966 Czechoslovak-Italian live-action/animated adventure film directed by the visionary Czech filmmaker Karel Zeman, known for his unique fusion of practical effects with various animation techniques. Based loosely on Jules Verne's novels "Two Years' Vacation" and "The Mysterious Island," the film tells the story of a group of children who discover and steal an abandoned airship, embarking on a fantastical journey across Europe. The film is remarkable for its distinctive Art Nouveau visual style, combining black-and-white live-action sequences with hand-drawn animation, stop-motion, and cutout animation techniques—all seamlessly integrated into the same scenes. This whimsical adventure represents Zeman's continued exploration of Verne's literary universe, following his acclaimed "Invention for Destruction" (1958). The film was released under the Italian title "I ragazzi del capitano Nemo" (The Boys of Captain Nemo) for international markets.

entries.title: The Stowaway
entries.creator: Jon Bing, Tor Åge Bringsværd
entries.pitch:
