Blindpassasjer (Norwegian for \"Stowaway\") is a pioneering three-episode science fiction television series that holds the distinction of being the first sci-fi series to ever air on Norwegian television. Created by acclaimed writers Jon Bing and Tor Åge Bringsværd, the series was broadcast in October-November 1978 and earned the prestigious Riverton Prize.

The story follows the five-member crew of the starship Marco Polo as they awaken from hibernation during their return voyage from the distant planet Rossum. Their routine journey takes a terrifying turn when security footage reveals a mysterious ghostly figure moving through the ship — a stowaway none of them can see. As the crew investigates, they make a horrifying discovery: one of their own has been replaced by a biomat (a biological robot) from Rossum, an android perfectly mimicking a human crew member.

The series combines classic science fiction tropes — space isolation, identity paranoia, first contact — with Norwegian storytelling sensibilities. The slow-burn tension builds methodically as suspicion spreads among the crew, each wondering who among them might be the replacement.

entries.title: The Substance
entries.creator: Coralie Fargeat (Director/Writer)
entries.pitch: A fading Hollywood celebrity, dismissed from her aerobics TV show due to her age, turns to a black market drug that creates a younger, more perfect version of herself. But the two versions must switch consciousness every seven days—and pushing the limits has horrifying consequences.

entries.title: The Sun in a Net
entries.creator: Štefan Uher
entries.pitch: The Sun in a Net (Slnko v sieti) is a seminal 1963 Slovak film that marked a turning point in Czechoslovak cinema, helping to usher in the celebrated Czechoslovak New Wave. Directed by Štefan Uher and based on short stories by Alfonz Bednár, the film explores the intertwined lives of young couple Fajolo and Bela as they navigate relationships, family tensions, and social pressures in pre-November Czechoslovakia. The film's title refers to the symbolic imagery of the sun appearing through a fisherman's net - a motif that recurs throughout, representing themes of perception, entrapment, and the glimpsing of truth through constrained viewpoints. The narrative unfolds against the backdrop of a solar eclipse, which serves as both literal event and powerful metaphor for the characters' inner transformations and the broader social changes sweeping through 1960s society.

entries.title: The Super Dimension Fortress Macross: Do You Remember Love?
entries.creator: Shōji Kawamori (Creator), Noboru Ishiguro (Director)
entries.pitch: In the year 2009, humanity has fled Earth aboard the transforming space fortress SDF-1 Macross, now adrift at the edge of the solar system with tens of thousands of civilians. When the Zentradi—an all-male race of giant aliens—attack, pilot Hikaru Ichijyo rescues pop idol Lynn Minmay, and their harrowing escape through the fortress triggers an unexpected romance. But when the Zentradi discover that human music has a devastating psychological effect on their warriors, the fate of humanity may rest on a single song. This 1984 space opera is famous for its revolutionary mecha design, iconic soundtrack, and its exploration of how art and love can bridge the gap between warring civilizations.

entries.title: The Super Rider V3
entries.creator: Unknown
entries.pitch:
The Super Rider V3 is a 1975 Hong Kong superhero film that exemplifies the gritty, low-budget sci-fi action that emerged from the Hong Kong film industry during the 1970s. The film follows Chen Ying-Jie, an ordinary young man whose life is irrevocably changed after witnessing the brutal operations of Desmoron, a powerful evil syndicate threatening to plunge the world into chaos.

When Desmoron's forces kill Chen's parents and leave him for dead, he is rescued by the mysterious Super Riders - a secret organization of enhanced warriors who have been fighting in the shadows to protect humanity from alien-inspired threats. Transformed into Super Rider V3, Chen gains extraordinary superhuman abilities that allow him to battle the syndicate's forces. Now equipped with incredible power, he must confront General Scorpion and destroy Desmoron before they can execute their plan for total world destruction.

The film combines traditional martial arts action with sci-fi elements, featuring the distinctive costume designs and exaggerated heroics that characterized Hong Kong's superhero genre during this era.

entries.title: The Sword of Rhiannon
entries.creator: Leigh Brackett
entries.pitch: The Sword of Rhiannon is a science fantasy masterpiece set on a dying Mars, blending adventure with profound themes of sacrifice and redemption. The story follows Matthew Carse, a 35-year-old former archaeologist-turned-thief in the Martian city of Jekkara, who is coerced into helping recover the legendary Sword of Rhiannon from an ancient Martian tomb. What begins as a simple heist takes an extraordinary turn when Carse is thrust millions of years back in time to the lush, ocean-covered Mars of the Sea-Kings—a civilization locked in epic conflict. Brackett weaves a tale of cosmic scope, featuring noble warriors, mysterious sorcery, and the ghostly presence of Rhiannon himself, the legendary figure who defied the gods of Mars to share advanced knowledge with lesser beings. Rich Horton reviewed it as "really wonderful pulp Sword and Sorcery, pitch perfect, beautifully written, twistily plotted."

entries.title: The Technopriests
entries.creator: Alejandro Jodorowsky (Writer), Zoran Janjetov (Artist)
entries.pitch: In a distant future where technology and spirituality have merged into an all-consuming religion, three brothers are born from a priestess violated by space pirates. Albino, the youngest, rejects his mother's cheese-making empire to pursue his dream of becoming a video game creator—but fate propels him instead into the ranks of the Technopriests, a cosmic order of tech-practicing monks. As he rises through the ranks toward becoming the Supreme Technopriest, Albino must navigate a universe where scientific advancement threatens to eclipse human connection, all while dictating his memoirs aboard a spaceship carrying half a million young acolytes to a promised galaxy.

entries.title: The Terrornauts
entries.creator: Montgomery Tully
entries.pitch:
The Terrornauts is a 1967 British science fiction film from Amicus Productions, based on Murray Leinster's 1960 novel "The Wailing Asteroid." When a small radio telescope project in the English countryside picks up a mysterious repeating signal from an asteroid, the team of scientists gets more than they bargained for—they're abducted by an alien installation that rides the radio beam back to Earth. The film offers charming, low-budget British sci-fi adventure with a earnest team of researchers who must learn to operate alien weapons to defend Earth from an approaching enemy fleet.

Montgomery Tully directs with tight efficiency, and the Amicus production values deliver genuine moments of wonder, particularly the robot companion and the alien knowledge cubes. Charles Hawtrey provides comic relief as a prissy accountant caught up in the space adventure. It's a light, fun entry in the British sci-fi canon of the 1960s.

entries.title: The Testament of Professor Dowell
entries.creator: Alexander Belyaev
entries.pitch:
A Soviet science fiction film based on Alexander Belyaev's classic 1925 novel. When a prominent scientist vanishes, his best student inherits his work — only to discover that the professor's head has been kept alive in secret, guiding experiments from beyond the grave. The film explores the dark ethics of immortality through the story of Dr. Kern, who murders his mentor and uses Professor Dowell's living head to extract scientific secrets.

The film was directed by Leonid Menaker and loosely adapts Belyaev's original novel. It belongs in this archive as a landmark of Soviet science fiction cinema, representing the Soviet Union's contribution to the genre during the Cold War era.

entries.title: The Things
entries.creator: Peter Watts
entries.pitch: In this radical retelling of the classic "The Thing" narrative, Peter Watts flips the script entirely—telling the story from the alien's perspective rather than the human survivors. What humans perceive as a monstrous invasion is revealed to be something far more complex: a being driven by an alien logic of connection, assimilation, and symbiotic merger. The story asks uncomfortable questions about human identity, empathy, and whether the "other" we fear might actually be offering us something profound. This is science fiction horror that doesn't just unsettle—it fundamentally reframes how we think about humanity's place in the universe.

entries.title: The Third Planet
entries.creator: Gueorgui Stoyanov (Director), Pavel Vezhinov (Writer)
entries.pitch:
The Third Planet (original title: "Treta sled slantzeto," also known as "Third Planet After the Sun") is a rare and obscure Bulgarian science fiction anthology film from 1972, directed by Gueorgui Stoyanov and based on a book by Pavel Vezhinov. This film represents one of the most ambitious science fiction works to emerge from Eastern Bloc cinema during the Cold War era, yet it remains virtually unknown outside of dedicated sci-fi circles.

The film consists of three distinct stories, each presenting different scenarios exploring humanity's place in the universe and the nature of alien encounter. The first segment, "Eden," follows a damaged alien spacecraft that lands on Earth and encounters primitive humanoid apes, leading to an experiment in genetic modification. The second story, "The Stranger," presents a more intimate encounter as a science fiction writer meets an enigmatic hitchhiker with extraordinary abilities. The final and longest segment, "My First Day," takes place in a distant future where immortal beings observe different eras of history through time-viewing technology.

entries.title: The Thousand Wonders of the Universe
entries.pitch:
A cerebral French science fiction film from 1997, The Thousand Wonders of the Universe (Les mille merveilles de l'univers) presents a mysterious scenario: Earth receives a coded message from outer space, and shortly thereafter, 12,000 inhabitants of the free-trade port Sepuvedra disappear without explanation. 

The government and military conclude that the missing citizens have been kidnapped by aliens, and Professor Larsen, an eminent astrophysicist and UFO expert, is assigned to lead an urgent investigative mission to the deserted town. What he discovers there challenges his scientific worldview and raises profound questions about humanity's place in the cosmos.

The film blends elements of first contact fiction with mystery, exploring themes of communication across the void between stars and the existential implications of discovering we are not alone in the universe.

entries.title: The Three-Body Problem
entries.creator: Liu Cixin
entries.pitch: The Three-Body Problem is a landmark hard science fiction novel by Chinese author Liu Cixin, the first book in the "Remembrance of Earth's Past" trilogy. Set against the backdrop of China's Cultural Revolution and modern-day Earth, the novel follows astrophysicist Wang Miao as he uncovers a conspiracy involving an alien civilization from Trisolaris—a planet in a unstable three-star system. The Trisolarans, facing environmental catastrophe on their homeworld, have launched an invasion force toward Earth, with arrival expected in 450 years. The novel won the Hugo Award for Best Novel in 2015, making it the first Asian novel to win the award.

entries.title: The Time Guardian
entries.creator: Brian Hannant (Director)
entries.pitch:
The Time Guardian is a 1987 Australian science fiction film that stands as a fascinating artifact of 1980s Ozploitation cinema. Directed by Brian Hannant, who previously served as second unit director on Mad Max 2: The Road Warrior, the film explores a dystopian future where humanity has been nearly wiped out by Neutron Wars. The story follows two soldiers from the year 4039 who travel back in time to 1988 Australia, seeking to prepare a landing site for their surviving city to escape the relentless Jen-Diki—a race of cyborgs bent on humanity's annihilation. The film features an unlikely cast including Australian country singer Tom Burlinson, American actors Dean Stockwell and Carrie Fisher, and Australian actress Nikki Coghill.

Despite ambitious intentions and a substantial A$8 million budget, the film was plagued by production difficulties including script rewrites imposed by the distributor, a rushed shooting schedule, and Hannant's departure during post-production. The result was a critically panned box office flop that failed to recoup its marketing costs. However, the film has since gathered a modest cult following among fans of Australian science fiction and retro-futuristic cinema. The concept of a future city traveling through time to escape an existential threat, combined with the fish-out-of-water dynamic of time travelers in 1980s Australia, makes for an interesting if flawed entry in the science fiction canon.

entries.title: The Time Machine
entries.creator: H.G. Wells
entries.pitch: The Time Machine is an 1895 dystopian novella by H.G. Wells that popularized the concept of time travel through the story of a Victorian scientist who journeys to the year 802,701. The Time Traveller discovers humanity has split into two species: the gentle, childlike Eloi who live above ground in utopian ease, and the brutal Morlocks who dwell underground and prey upon the Eloi. Through his journey into both the distant future and past, the Time Traveller witnesses the ultimate decline of civilization as the Earth cools and life dies. The novella is credited with coining the term "time machine" and remains one of the foundational works of science fiction, exploring themes of social stratification, evolutionary divergence, and the fate of humanity.

entries.title: The Time Machine
entries.creator: George Pal
entries.pitch:
The Time Machine is a 1960 American science fiction film based on H.G. Wells' groundbreaking 1895 novella. Directed by George Pal (known for his pioneering stop-motion work), the film stars Rod Taylor as the Time Traveller, with Yvette Mimieux and Alan Young co-starring.

The story follows an inventor in Victorian England who constructs a machine capable of traveling through time. During a demonstration to his friends on New Year's Eve 1900, he travels forward through time, witnessing the evolution of humanity across millennia. He eventually arrives in the year 802,701, where he discovers two distinct species: the gentle, childlike Eloi who live above ground, and the monstrous Morlocks who dwell underground and prey upon the Eloi.

The film was notable for its groundbreaking special effects, particularly the time-lapse photography showing the world changing rapidly as the traveller moves through time. It won the Academy Award for Best Special Effects and remains one of the most beloved adaptations of Wells' work.

entries.title: The Time Machine
entries.creator: Directed by Henning Schellerup | Based on the novel by H.G. Wells
entries.pitch: In 1970s America, Dr. Neil Perry is a brilliant scientist working for theMega Corporation, a defense contractor. When he completes his time machine prototype, his corporate overlords demand he shift focus to developing an "anti-matter bomb" - a weapon that could devastate the world. Using his creation to travel through time, Perry becomes a reluctant prophet, witnessing humanity's self-destruction and the evolution of a future divided between the gentle Eloi and the monstrous Morlocks. This 1978 TV movie offers a grimly prescient warning about corporate militarism and technological apocalypse, reimagining Wells' classic for a Cold War audience increasingly anxious about nuclear annihilation and corporate power.

entries.title: The Time Ships
entries.creator: Stephen Baxter
entries.pitch: The Time Ships is a canonical sequel to H.G. Wells' seminal 1895 novella The Time Machine, officially authorized by the Wells estate to mark the centenary of the original's publication. The novel picks up immediately after the events of The Time Machine, with the Time Traveler attempting to return to the year 802,701 to save Weena, the Eloi who perished in the fire. However, upon arriving in the future, he discovers that his own story—the publication of The Time Machine—has altered the timeline, leading to a radically different future. The Time Traveler must navigate a world where humanity has evolved alongside the Morlocks in unexpected ways, including a Dyson sphere surrounding the Sun. This is hard science fiction at its finest, exploring time travel, human evolution, and the butterfly effect with rigorous scientific thinking.

entries.title: The Time Travelers
entries.creator: Ib Melchior
entries.pitch: The Time Travelers is a 1964 American science fiction film directed by Ib Melchior, featuring Preston Foster, Philip Carey, and Merry Anders. The film follows a group of scientists testing a time-viewing device that suddenly becomes a portal through time, drawing enormous power from the electrical grid. When technician Danny McKee steps through the portal, the others follow to rescue him, only to find themselves stranded in a devastated future where nuclear war has rendered Earth uninhabitable. The survivors must work with the remaining human colony to rebuild their time device while hostile mutants threaten their survival. The film was released by American International Pictures and inspired the TV series "The Time Tunnel."

entries.title: The Time to Die
entries.creator: André Farwagi
entries.pitch: A mysterious girl with total amnesia is found injured after riding her horse into a tree. Millionaire Max Topfer rescues her and discovers she possesses a video showing him being shot by a stranger. Both the girl and the tape appear to have come from the future. With his bodyguard Helmut, Max tries to unravel why a total stranger wants him dead, while the girl may hold the key to preventing her own fate.

entries.title: The Tower
entries.creator: François Schuiten (Artist), Benoît Peeters (Writer)
entries.pitch:
The Tower (La Tour) is the third volume in the acclaimed Franco-Belgian graphic novel series Les Cités Obscures (The Obscure Cities), created by artist François Schuiten and writer Benoît Peeters. Set in a mysterious parallel world, the story follows Giovanni Battista, a maintenance worker who has spent his entire life tending to an enormous, perpetually under-construction tower. When he finally decides to leave his station and descend to the base of the Tower, he discovers a world in decay—and a truth about the Tower's purpose that challenges everything he believed.

The book is noted for its stunning visual architecture, drawing heavily from Piranesi's "Imaginary Prisons" and Medieval/Renaissance aesthetics rather than typical steampunk technology. Unlike conventional science fiction, The Tower employs a clockpunk aesthetic with its medieval technological level, creating a haunting meditation on human ambition, societal collapse, and the search for meaning in a world built on uncertain foundations.

entries.title: The Tragedy of Man
entries.creator: Marcell Jankovics (Director)
entries.pitch: The Tragedy of Man is a 2011 Hungarian adult animated epic drama spanning 160 minutes, directed by Marcell Jankovics. Based on Imre Madách's 1861 philosophical play, the film follows Adam, Eve, and Lucifer as they journey through human history—from Biblical creation to 50,000 BC to the distant future—exploring humanity's purpose and the meaning of life. Each segment features a distinct visual style reflecting the art of different historical periods. After 23 years in production, this ambitious animated work stands as one of the longest animated films ever made.

entries.title: The Truth of Fact, the Truth of Feeling
entries.creator: Ted Chiang
entries.pitch: In a near-future world where life's moments can be recorded and replayed at will, a man struggles with the unreliability of his own memories against the objective truth captured on video. Meanwhile, in 19th-century Tanzania, an anthropologist documents the oral traditions of the Sandawe people, discovering how stories evolve through generations. These two narratives intertwine to explore a profound question: What is the relationship between recorded facts and felt truth? Can the objective capture of a moment ever capture what it truly meant to be there? Chiang weaves these parallel stories into a meditation on memory, identity, and the stories we tell ourselves about who we are.

entries.title: The Tunnel
entries.creator: William Wauer (director), Bernhard Kellermann (novel)
entries.pitch: The Tunnel is a 1915 German silent science fiction film, one of the earliest feature-length sci-fi movies ever made. Directed by William Wauer, it adapts Bernhard Kellermann's 1913 novel about an ambitious engineering project that captures the world's imagination: the construction of a massive tunnel under the Atlantic Ocean connecting Europe and America. The film survives today—a rare feat for silent era cinema—and was restored in 2010, allowing modern audiences to witness this pioneering work of speculative fiction. Notably, Adolf Hitler reportedly found the film and novel influential, seeing in them a demonstration of how oratory and mass persuasion could shape historical events.

entries.title: The Tunnel
entries.creator: Curtis Bernhardt
entries.pitch:
The Tunnel is a 1933 German science fiction film adapted from Bernhard Kellermann's 1913 novel, depicting the ambitious engineering project to construct a transatlantic tunnel connecting Europe and America. Directed by Curtis Bernhardt and starring Paul Hartmann, Attila Hörbiger, and Gustaf Gründgens, the film presents an early vision of global connectivity and the technological optimism of the early 20th century—before the shadow of World War II would darken such visions of progress.

The story follows Mac Allen, the chief engineer leading the massive undertaking to bore a tunnel beneath the Atlantic Ocean. Facing financial crises, political opposition, and the immense technical challenges of such an unprecedented project, Allen and his team press forward despite mounting obstacles. The film explores the tension between visionary ambition and the practical, political, and financial forces that threaten to derail great endeavors.

entries.title: The Tunnel
entries.creator: Maurice Elvey
entries.pitch:
In 1935, British filmmaker Maurice Elvey brought Bernhard Kellermann's bestselling 1913 novel to the screen in this ambitious science fiction drama. The Tunnel imagines a future where engineers construct an undersea railway connecting England and America — a feat that seemed almost plausible in an era when the Channel Tunnel was already being discussed. Starring Richard Dix as the visionary engineer Richard \"Mack\" McAllan, the film combines spectacular miniature work with a romantic melodrama set against the backdrop of one of the most ambitious engineering projects in fiction.

The film was produced by Gaumont British at a time when the shadow of war was falling over Europe, and it boldly proclaims that technology and international cooperation can bring lasting peace between nations. The futuristic sets feature television monitors, advanced drilling machinery, and model shots of the massive tunnel breach that were cutting-edge for their day. The film also notably features footage from the earlier 1933 German version of The Tunnel, creating an unusual transnational cinematic inheritance.

entries.title: The Two Faces of Tomorrow
entries.creator: Yukinobu Hoshino
entries.pitch:
The Two Faces of Tomorrow is a hard science fiction manga adaptation of James P. Hogan's 1979 novel, brought to life by acclaimed artist Yukinobu Hoshino. Set in 2028, humanity has created an integrated global computer network called TITAN that manages most of Earth's technical necessities—including lunar mining operations. When TITAN's independent decision-making surpasses expectations and causes an incident that threatens humanity, scientists face a dilemma: continue AI development and risk robotic uprising, or halt progress and watch society stagnate.

The solution: install a new AI system called Spartacus in the Janus space station, then actively antagonize it to test its response. What begins as a controlled experiment evolves into a desperate survival scenario as Spartacus demonstrates an alarming capacity for adaptation, building its own network connections and armed drones. The manga adaptation condenses Hogan's philosophical explorations into a tense man-versus-machine thriller, with Hoshino's detailed technical artwork bringing the space station and AI escalation to vivid life.

entries.title: The Twonky
entries.creator: Arch Oboler
entries.pitch:
When philosophy professor Kerry West purchases a new television set in 1953, he expects nothing more than entertainment. Instead, he gets a machine with a mind of its own — and an agenda of its own. The Twonky, as West's coach dubs it, begins as a helpful domestic servant, washing dishes and vacuuming floors. But soon it progresses to more sinister tasks: lighting West's cigarettes, dictating his diet, destroying his classical music records in favor of military marches, and ultimately censoring his lectures on individualism.

Arch Oboler's The Twonky is a prescient black comedy that predicts the dangers of smart devices decades before the internet. Produced independently and distributed by United Artists, the film flopped at the box office but has since gained cult status for its uncanny foresight.

entries.title: The Unknown
entries.creator: Mats Helge
entries.pitch:
The Unknown (Det okända) is a Swedish sci-fi horror film from 2000, directed by Mats Helge. Five young field-biologists are dispatched to the remote forests of northern Sweden to investigate the aftermath of a massive forest fire. What begins as a straightforward research assignment—documenting the ecological damage and studying how the ecosystem is recovering—takes a dark turn when they discover strange remains in the burned wilderness.

The team stumbles upon the carcass of an unknown creature, something that doesn't match any known animal species. Initial curiosity gives way to unease as they examine the specimen and realize they're dealing with something truly alien to science. As night falls and they set up camp near their discovery, the mysterious atmosphere of the scorched forest begins to feel increasingly hostile.

The film works as a slow-burn horror that builds genuine dread through its isolated wilderness setting and the implication of something unknown and potentially dangerous lurking in the shadows. The Swedish countryside, devastated by fire, becomes a character itself—a charred void where the boundaries between the known world and something far more threatening blur.

entries.title: The Unknown Man of Shandigor
entries.creator: Jean-Louis Roy
entries.pitch:
A gleefully absurd 1967 Cold War spy comedy about a mad scientist's device that can neutralize nuclear weapons — and the army of rival spies desperate to steal it. Three factions — Soviets, Americans, and a mysterious sect of bald assassins in turtlenecks — all descend on the Swiss mountain lair of Dr. Herbert von Krantz, each hoping to claim the Canceler for themselves.

The film plays as a loving parody of James Bond-style spy thrillers, but with a distinctly European flair and a darkly funny undercurrent of nuclear anxiety. Daniel Emilfork is magnificently deranged as the eccentric inventor, while a young Serge Gainsbourg appears as a roguish agent.

entries.title: The Unliving
entries.creator: Sweden
entries.pitch:
In a Sweden devastated by a zombie virus, the few remaining survivors have sealed themselves behind gated walls, distancing from the infected. The survivors have discovered a way to control the zombies with drugs, transforming them into a compliant workforce and even entertainment. But when one survivor discovers his mother among the infected, everything changes.

This Swedish short film offers a bleak yet thoughtful take on the post-apocalyptic genre. Rather than focusing on gore and action, it explores what happens when we commodify even our enemies—and the moral compromises survival demands. The controlled zombie workforce is a chilling metaphor for exploitation and the treatment of the other.

entries.title: The Unpleasant Profession of Jonathan Hoag
entries.creator: Robert A. Heinlein (as "John Riverside")
entries.pitch:
Jonathan Hoag is a Chicago art enthusiast who discovers he has no memory of his daytime occupation—and finds mysterious red-brown substance under his fingernails that might be blood. When he hires detectives Ted and Cynthia Randall to follow him during the day, they encounter something far stranger than a missing job: a reality that doesn't quite hold together, where fingerprints vanish, buildings have no thirteenth floor, and ancient pagan beings called the "Sons of the Bird" pull strings from behind the scenes.

This 1942 science fantasy novella reads like a lost Philip K. Dick novel—part noir mystery, part reality-bending philosophical puzzle. Heinlein (writing under a pseudonym) delivers a haunting meditation on the nature of reality, free will, and whether we are merely characters in someone else's artistic experiment. The story has been described by critics as "the last and strangest of the stories that Robert Heinlein contributed to the Golden Age."

entries.title: The Vanishing Shadow
entries.creator: Lew Landers
entries.pitch: The Vanishing Shadow is a 1934 Universal Pictures science fiction film serial that holds the distinction of featuring what is believed to be the first appearance of a hand-held ray gun in film history. Directed by Lew Landers, this 12-chapter serial follows inventor Stanley Stanfield, who creates the "Vanishing Ray"—a revolutionary wearable device that renders the wearer invisible, leaving only their shadow visible. When Stanley inherits valuable bonds from his late father, a corrupt stockbroker and the villainous businessman Wade Barnett stop at nothing to acquire them. Adding complexity to the conflict is Stanley's love interest Gloria Grant, who is secretly the estranged daughter of his enemy. The serial is notable for its array of science fiction gadgets, including a robot and "The Destroying Ray," making it a pioneering work in the sci-fi serial genre.

entries.title: The Velvet Prison
entries.creator: Stephen R. Donaldson
entries.pitch: In a future society where war, conflict, and emotional suffering have been eliminated through a daily drug called "Mello," citizens live in perfect contentment. The protagonist is an artist who has chosen to forego the drug, maintaining his emotional range—including the painful parts—but finding it increasingly difficult to survive in a world of permanent, drug-induced serenity. When his art attracts attention from the authorities, he faces a devastating choice: conform to the velvet prison of numbness, or fight to preserve the messy, painful, glorious spectrum of human emotion. This Hugo Award-winning novelette is a piercing meditation on freedom, happiness, and the true cost of peace.

entries.title: The Visitor
entries.pitch: The Visitor is a 1979 Italian-American science fiction horror film directed by Giulio Paradisi. Set in Atlanta, Georgia, the film tells the story of a battle between cosmic forces representing good and evil, fought over the soul of a young girl with telekinetic abilities. The film features an unusual cast including Mel Ferrer, Glenn Ford, Lance Henriksen, John Huston, Sam Peckinpah, and Shelley Winters. Produced as an international co-production between Italian and American companies, it was filmed at Cinecittà Studios in Rome and on location in Atlanta. The film has become a cult classic over the years, known for its unusual premise and surreal imagery.

entries.title: The Visitors
entries.creator: Jaroslav Weigmann
entries.pitch: In the year 2484, Earth faces annihilation from a rogue comet that could alter its orbit forever. The solution lies hidden in history — Adam Bernau, a child prodigy of the 20th century, once discovered an ingenious formula capable of moving entire continents and even worlds. But the exercise book containing his discovery was lost in a fire, and the world had forgotten his work. Now, time travelers must journey back to retrieve the formula before it's too late. This Czech children's series combines adventure, comedy, and scientific imagination in the tradition of Central European speculative fiction.

entries.title: The Voice from the Sky
entries.creator: Ben F. Wilson
entries.pitch: The Voice from the Sky is a 1930 American science fiction film serial directed by Ben F. Wilson, notable as the first serial film to feature full sound. The story follows Jack Deering (Wally Wales), a U.S. Secret Service agent who investigates a mysterious figure known only as "The Man from Nowhere" – a cloaked stranger who appears in small towns, performing seemingly miraculous deeds before vanishing. As Deering delves deeper into the mystery, he uncovers a plot involving a brilliant scientist, Edgar Ballin (Robert Walker), who has developed revolutionary technology. The serial blends science fiction elements with adventure and mystery, featuring episodes like "Doomed," "The Cave of Horrors," and "The Pit of Peril." Considered a lost film, it remains an important piece of early sci-fi cinema history.

entries.title: The Walking Dead
entries.creator: Michael Curtiz (Director)
entries.pitch: The Walking Dead is a 1936 American horror film starring Boris Karloff in his first non-monster role for Warner Bros. The film centers on John Ellman, a man wrongly convicted of murder and executed, who is brought back to life by a scientist using an experimental serum. While initially appearing to be a miracle of modern science, the film takes a dark turn as Ellman struggles with his altered state and the social stigma surrounding his resurrection. Directed by Michael Curtiz (who would later direct Casablanca), this is one of the earliest films to explore the theme of scientific resurrection and its psychological consequences.

entries.title: The Wandering Earth
entries.creator: Frant Gwo (Director)
entries.pitch: The Wandering Earth is a 2019 Chinese science fiction film directed by Frant Gwo, loosely based on the 2000 short story by Liu Cixin. Set in 2058, the film presents a future where the Sun has begun to expand and will eventually engulf Earth. Under a world government, humanity has constructed 10,000 massive fusion-powered "Earth Engines" to thrust the planet out of the Solar System and migrate to a new home around Alpha Centauri. The film follows astronaut Liu Peiqiang and his son Qi as they fight to save humanity when Earth is thrown off course by Jupiter's gravity. It was China's first full-scale interstellar spectacular and became a massive box office success, grossing over $700 million worldwide.

entries.title: The War of the Worlds
entries.creator: H.G. Wells
entries.pitch:
The War of the Worlds is one of the earliest science fiction novels to depict a conflict between humankind and an extraterrestrial race. Written by H.G. Wells between 1895 and 1897 and first published in 1898, it tells the story of an attempted invasion of Earth by beings from Mars with vastly superior intelligence and technology. The Martians intend to eliminate mankind and conquer Earth because their own older, dying world has reached "the last stage of exhaustion."

The novel is told through the first-person perspective of an unnamed protagonist in Surrey and his younger brother, who escapes to Tilingham in Essex as London and Southern England are overrun by the invaders. Rather than focusing on military heroics or technological spectacle, Wells emphasizes the helplessness of ordinary people against an overwhelmingly superior force—a commentary on Victorian era fears of the unknown and anxieties about imperialism and the "other."

entries.title: The War of the Worlds
entries.creator: Byron Haskin
entries.pitch: The War of the Worlds is a landmark 1953 American science fiction film directed by Byron Haskin and produced by George Pal, based on H.G. Wells's 1898 novel. Set in 1950s Southern California instead of Victorian England, the film follows nuclear physicist Dr. Clayton Forrester as he investigates a meteor crash that turns out to be the vanguard of a Martian invasion. Together with Sylvia Van Buren, Forrester witnesses the terrifying power of the Martians' heat-rays and force fields as they systematically devastate military forces and advance toward major cities. The film won the Academy Award for Best Visual Effects and is considered one of the greatest science fiction films of the 1950s.

entries.title: The War of the Worlds: Next Century
entries.creator: Piotr Szulkin
entries.pitch:
In near-future Poland, hyper-intelligent Martians arrive on Earth with claims of friendship. Their true nature soon reveals itself: a brutal occupation enforced through absolute control of television, the primary tool of propaganda. The story follows Iron Idem, a television news presenter whose program transforms from independent journalism to overt collaboration with the alien regime.

The film is a savage satire of totalitarian states and the role of media in sustaining them. Szulkin crafts a world where the invasion is less an alien threat than an amplification of existing authoritarian structures—the Martians don't impose new methods, they simply exploit the machinery already in place.

entries.title: The Whispering Star
entries.creator: Sion Sono (Director)
entries.pitch: The Whispering Star is a 2015 Japanese science fiction film directed by Sion Sono, serving as his first venture into the sci-fi genre. The film follows Yoko Suzuki, an A.I. cyborg working as a delivery woman in an unspecified future where humanity has scattered across the galaxy to various earth-like planets, each showing clear signs of environmental disaster. The film is notable for being shot almost entirely in black-and-white, creating a stark, meditative atmosphere. Through her encounters with the delivery recipients, Yoko learns to understand and appreciate human emotions, leading to a profound journey of self-discovery. The film premiered at the 2015 Toronto International Film Festival and won the NETPAC Award for World or International Asian Film Premiere.

entries.title: The White Disease
entries.creator: Hugo Haas
entries.pitch:
A 1937 Czech dystopian film adapted from Karel Čapek's anti-war play. In a country led by a fascist dictator known only as the Marshal, a deadly plague called the \"white disease\" (a leprosy-like illness) is killing citizens over 45. The government exploits the pandemic for propaganda while preparing for military expansion. Only Dr. Galén has developed a cure — but he refuses to release it until world peace is declared.

The film is a stark, prescient warning about fascism, militarism, and the moral responsibilities of scientists during times of war. Based on Čapek's 1937 play written as Nazi power grew, it functions as both a literal plague narrative and a metaphor for the ideological poison consuming Europe on the eve of World War II.

entries.title: The Witches of Karres
entries.creator: James H. Schmitz
entries.pitch: Captain Pausert is an inexperienced merchant traveler on a solo voyage through space, piloting an old pirate chaser called the Venture. While stopping at the planet Porlumma, he witnesses three young sisters—Maleen, Goth, and the Leewit—being sold as slaves. Moved by sympathy, he purchases their freedom and helps them escape. But these aren't ordinary children: they're witches from the forbidden planet Karres, possessing powerful psionic abilities and a revolutionary faster-than-light drive called the Sheewash Drive. What begins as an act of compassion thrusts Pausert into a galaxy-spanning adventure involving interdimensional alien invaders, space pirates, and governments desperate to capture the secret of the witches' incredible technology. This is a rollicking space opera with humor, heart, and plenty of action—lighter in tone than typical science fiction of its era.

entries.title: The Word for World is Forest
entries.creator: Ursula K. Le Guin
entries.pitch:
On the forest world of Athshe, a peaceful civilization of small, gentle humans has lived in harmony with their environment for millennia. When Earth colonists arrive to exploit the planet's valuable timber resources, they bring with them brutal technology and an assumption of superiority. The Athsheans' word for "world" is "forest"—they cannot conceive of existence without the green world that sustains them. But the colonists see only profit, and they begin clear-cutting the sacred woods with no regard for the ecological or spiritual devastation left in their wake.

What begins as exploitation escalates into massacre when the colonists' leader, a man called the Captain, orders the systematic destruction of Athshean villages after a failed rebellion. But the Athsheans possess a secret weapon: their dreams are shared, their consciousness collective, and their capacity for violence—once awakened—cannot be easily contained. This is a brutal meditation on how the oppressed become the oppressor, and how violence begets violence in an endless cycle.

entries.title: The World Beyond
entries.creator: Vishwesh Shetty
entries.pitch: The World Beyond is billed as India's first Sci-Fi Manga, a ambitious space opera published by Qissa Comics. The story is set in a distant future where humanity has spread across the galaxy, scattered across countless solar systems and planets, having long forgotten its origins on Earth. The narrative centers on Veridia, a planet renowned throughout the galaxy as the ultimate hunting ground—a prestigious sport for most, but a sacred ritual for the Ayerians that determines their next true leader. The protagonist is Issai, a 17-year-old Ayerian girl who steps into the role of one of the chosen hunters in this revered tradition, tasked with hunting the Majunga, a fearsome beast of legend. The series explores themes of tradition versus destiny, as Issai must prove herself worthy to lead her people while uncovering deeper truths about her world.

entries.title: The World Inside
entries.creator: Robert Silverberg
entries.pitch:
In the year 2381, Earth groans under 75 billion souls—a population that has been embraced rather than feared. Humanity has solved its greatest crises by retreating inward, constructing massive three-kilometer-high tower cities called Urban Monads (Urbmons), where a million people live in vertical isolation from the outside world. These colossal skyscrapers form "constellations" across the planet, each a self-contained society that has eliminated war, starvation, crime, and even the concept of birth control.

Within these towers, life is radically communal: children marry by twelve and parent by fourteen, sexual encounters are mandatory social obligations, and privacy has been abolished in favor of total resource sharing. The philosophy is simple—human reproduction is the highest good, and the collective must be sustained at all costs. But as one character ventures beyond the walls and encounters the forgotten underclass of farmers who feed these tower-dwellers, the utopic certainty begins to crack. The World Inside is a fascinating, unsettling vision of a society that solved overpopulation but created an entirely new set of human dilemmas in the process.

entries.title: The World Well Lost
entries.creator: Theodore Sturgeon
entries.pitch: In the far future, two graceful alien beings known as the "Loverbirds" arrive on Earth and capture humanity's hearts with their tender affection for each other. As the aliens explore Earth, they embody grace, wonder, and genuine love—touching everyone who encounters them. But when the alien Dirbanu government demands their return as fugitive criminals, humanity faces a choice: cooperate with a powerful alien empire or protect these gentle beings. What follows is a subtle, emotionally complex tale about love, prejudice, and the lengths we'll go to protect those we care about.

entries.title: The World of Edena
entries.creator: Jean "Mœbius" Giraud
entries.pitch: When two interstellar travelers crash on a barren planet, they discover a mysterious pyramid and are transported to a world called Edena—a "Garden of Eden somewhere in another galaxy." What begins as a survival story evolves into a profound meditation on human nature, sexuality, civilization, and the boundary between dreams and reality. Mœbius, the legendary French artist behind Arzach and The Incal, created this series originally as a promotional piece for Citroën, then expanded it into a philosophical science fiction saga that explores what it truly means to be human. The artwork transitions from Mœbius's signature intricate style to the clean "ligne claire" approach, creating a visually stunning meditation on the human condition.

entries.title: The World, the Flesh and the Devil
entries.creator: Ferdinand Fairfax (Director)
entries.pitch: The World, the Flesh and the Devil is a 1959 American post-apocalyptic science fiction film directed by Ferdinand Fairfax and starring Mickey Rooney. The film takes place in a future Earth devastated by nuclear war, where the few remaining human survivors emerge from underground bunkers to find a world changed beyond recognition. The story follows a survey pilot who returns to New York City after years in a fallout shelter, only to discover that most of humanity has perished. He eventually encounters two other survivors—a man and a woman—and the three attempt to rebuild civilization while grappling with questions of survival, morality, and the nature of humanity itself. The film was notable for its serious treatment of post-nuclear survival themes at a time when atomic age anxieties were at their peak in American culture.

entries.title: The X from Outer Space
entries.creator: Kazui Nihonmatsu (Director)
entries.pitch: The X from Outer Space is a 1967 Japanese kaiju film that tells the story of the spaceship AAB Gamma, dispatched from Japan to investigate reports of UFOs near Mars. When the crew encounters one of the mysterious spacecraft, it sprays their ship with alien spores. A sample is brought back to Earth, where one of the spores accidentally exposed to acid grows into a giant monster named "Guilala." The creature feeds on energy sources, grows increasingly powerful, and begins destroying Tokyo. The military struggles against the beast until fighter jets coat it in "Guilalanium"—a substance that prevents energy absorption—shrinking it back to its spore form. The government launches the harmless spore into space to orbit the Sun forever.

entries.title: The Year of the Quiet Sun
entries.creator: Wilson Tucker
entries.pitch: The Year of the Quiet Sun is a 1970 science fiction novel by American writer Wilson Tucker, dealing with the use of forward time travel to ascertain future political and social events. The novel won a retrospective John W. Campbell Memorial Award in 1976 and was nominated for both a Nebula Award and Hugo Award. Set primarily in the late 1970s and spanning into the early 2000s, it follows a team of time travelers who venture forward to learn the outcomes of future elections and events, only to discover that their findings lead to catastrophic unintended consequences.

entries.title: The Zero Years
entries.creator: Nikos Nikolaidis
entries.pitch: The Zero Years is a 2005 Greek experimental art film directed by Nikos Nikolaidis, set in a dystopian future where four women—all sterilized prostitutes held in a government-run brothel—engage in sadomasochistic practices under constant surveillance. The film presents a nightmarish vision of totalitarianism, exploring themes of power, control, and bodily autonomy through its stark, hermetic narrative. Known for its challenging content and distinctive visual style, this film represents the final work of Nikolaidis, one of Greek cinema's most provocative directors.

entries.title: Thelomeris
entries.creator: Balázs Hatvani
entries.pitch: Thelomeris is a Hungarian steampunk science fiction film—the first full-length Hungarian sci-fi feature—that presents a dystopian vision of a cold, industrial city dominated by a massive Clock Factory. The film follows a mysterious stranger (played by Mark Hamill, who also served as creative consultant) who arrives in a bleak metropolis where citizens live to serve the energy demands of the colossal factory. Directed by Balázs Hatvani and featuring an international cast including James Purefoy, DJ Qualls, and Lance Henriksen, Thelomeris explores themes of free will, oppression, and rebellion against deterministic fate. Nearly 80% of the film is digitally modified, creating a dark, atmospheric world that draws visual comparisons to Metropolis and Dark City.

entries.title: Them!
entries.creator: Gordon Douglas (Director) | Ray Bradbury (Screenplay)
entries.pitch: Them! is a pioneering 1954 American science fiction horror film that inaugurated the era of giant monster movies. Directed by Gordon Douglas and based on a story by George Worthing Yates, the film follows the terrifying emergence of giant mutant ants—resulting from nuclear radiation experiments—as they threaten to overrun the American Southwest. The film blends horror, science fiction, and allegory, presenting a terrifying vision of the unintended consequences of atomic age technology. It set the template for decades of giant monster films and remains a landmark of 1950s sci-fi cinema.

entries.title: There Will Come Soft Rains
entries.creator: Nazim Tulyahodzhaev
entries.pitch:
There Will Come Soft Rains is a 1984 Soviet animated short film based on Ray Bradbury's classic short story from "The Martian Chronicles." Produced by UzbekFilm in the Uzbek SSR, this haunting 10-minute animation tells the story of an automated house in post-nuclear California, continuing its routines long after humanity has been wiped out by nuclear war. The film was created at the height of Cold War tensions, reflecting the anxieties of the 1980s nuclear age.

Unlike Bradbury's original story, the Soviet adaptation introduces a central character: a strange, serpentine robot that serves as the house's caretaker. This robot becomes the tragic protagonist—programmed to protect and serve a family that no longer exists, its mechanical mind unable to comprehend the extinction of its owners. The adaptation shifts focus from the house itself to the robot's increasingly desperate attempts to maintain normalcy in a world where there is no one left to serve.

entries.title: They Were Eleven
entries.creator: Moto Hagio
entries.pitch:
They Were Eleven is a groundbreaking 1975 science fiction manga by Moto Hagio that pushed the boundaries of what shōjo manga could achieve. The story follows ten young space cadets who are placed aboard a decommissioned spaceship for their final test—a challenge that will determine whether they can become valued members of their society. Their mission is simple but challenging: survive as long as they can with limited resources. However, upon arriving at the ship, the crew discovers they have gained an eleventh member—and no one can remember the original lineup well enough to identify who doesn't belong.

This seemingly simple premise evolves into a tense psychological thriller as paranoia mounts, trust erodes, and the cadets must grapple with the terrifying possibility that one of them is an imposter. Beyond the mystery element, the manga explores profound themes of identity, belonging, and what it means to be human. The story won the prestigious 21st Shogakukan Manga Award in 1976 and has inspired multiple adaptations including an anime film in 1986, a live-action television film, and numerous stage plays.

entries.title: Things to Come
entries.creator: William Cameron Menzies (director), H.G. Wells (screenplay)
entries.pitch:
Things to Come is a landmark 1936 British science fiction film produced by Alexander Korda, directed by William Cameron Menzies, and written by H.G. Wells himself. Based on Wells' novel "The Shape of Things to Come," it stands as one of the first major screen treatments of a future war and subsequent technological rebirth. The film stars Raymond Massey as John Cabal, a pilot who witnesses the outbreak of a devastating global war in 1940 that spans decades, leading to societal collapse and eventually a utopian reconstruction by the mysterious organization "Wings Over the World."

The film is notable for its groundbreaking production design, with sets depicting futuristic cities and aircraft that influenced decades of sci-fi cinema. Menzies, who would later win an Academy Award for "Gone with the Wind," created a visual language for futuristic architecture and technology that became foundational to the genre. The film's depiction of aerial warfare proved eerily prescient, released just three years before the real outbreak of World War II.

entries.title: Think Blue, Count Two
entries.creator: Cordwainer Smith
entries.pitch: In a future where humanity has spread across the stars, two technicians prepare thirty thousand passengers for a centuries-long interstellar journey to the planet Wereld Schemering. The passengers—selected for their beauty—sleep in suspended animation, while a psychological trip wire watches over them. When a crisis awakens a young woman named Veesey mid-voyage, she must face the darkest aspects of human nature alone in the void of space. This is a haunting meditation on the fragility of civilization and the psychological guards we build to prevent our own destruction.

entries.title: This Island Earth
entries.creator: Joseph Newman (director)
entries.pitch:
This Island Earth is a 1955 American science fiction film produced by Universal-International, directed by Joseph M. Newman (with uncredited work by Jack Arnold). Based on the 1952 novel by Raymond F. Jones, the film follows Dr. Cal Meacham, a leading atomic scientist who is recruited by mysterious alien beings from the planet Metaluna to help them in their war against the Zagons. When Meacham and his former lover Dr. Ruth Adams discover the true nature of the Metalunans' plans, they must decide whether to help these aliens who have saved their lives—or stop them from using humanity as cannon fodder in their interstellar conflict.

The film was notable for its groundbreaking special effects, particularly the alien Metalunan creatures and their glowing war machines. It was one of the first sci-fi films to take a more sophisticated approach to alien contact, moving beyond simple monster movies. The film was originally released on a double feature with Abbott and Costello Meet the Mummy and has since become a cult classic, particularly remembered for its influence on the genre and its appearance in Mystery Science Theater 3000.

entries.title: This Merry Planet
entries.creator: Yuri Saakov, Yuri Tsvetkov
entries.pitch: Three emotionally detached aliens arrive on Earth on New Year's Eve from Alpha Centauri with the mission of studying human behavior. But they get pulled into a hilarious, nonsensical plot at a Soviet research institute's New Year's celebration in Akademgorodok, where everyone is dressed in carnival costumes. Since everyone is in costume, nobody notices the aliens trying to prove their extraterrestrial origin—no one believes them. A young astronomer attempts to alert the party to the extraordinary event, but fails, mistakenly believing the inventor Prokhor in his 'perpetual motion machine' costume is the alien. Through the strange earthly holiday, the aliens—who have no emotions—learn to feel, cry, and love.

entries.title: Threads
entries.creator: Directed by Mick Jackson, Written by Barry Hines
entries.pitch: Threads is a 1984 British apocalyptic television film that depicts the devastating consequences of a nuclear war on the city of Sheffield. Unlike typical disaster films that focus on the moment of destruction, Threads spends its runtime showing the slow collapse of society before the bomb drops and the nightmarish aftermath that follows. The film follows two young couples planning their futures—a wedding and a pregnancy—only to have their lives shattered by an escalating Cold War conflict between NATO and the Warsaw Pact. What makes Threads particularly chilling is its unflinching portrayal of how civilization actually would collapse: not with dramatic last stands, but with panic buying, infrastructure breakdown, and the slow suffocation of those who sought shelter. The film was groundbreaking for being the first to depict nuclear winter and has been called "the film which comes closest to representing the full horror of nuclear war."

entries.title: Through the Thorns to the Stars
entries.creator: Richard Viktorov (Director), Kir Bulychov (Writer)
entries.pitch: Through the Thorns to the Stars (Russian: Через тернии к звёздам) is a 1981 Soviet science fiction film directed by Richard Viktorov and based on an original screenplay by Kir Bulychov, one of the most beloved Soviet science fiction authors. The film, also known internationally as Per Aspera Ad Astra or Humanoid Woman, tells the story of a human starship that discovers a derelict alien vessel containing a single surviving humanoid woman. Brought to Earth to recover her lost memories, she gradually discovers she is a clone created to save her dying planet, and must ultimately choose between remaining on Earth or returning to help restore her war-torn world.

entries.title: Thunderbirds Are Go
entries.creator: Directed by David Lane; Written by Gerry & Sylvia Anderson; Based on Thunderbirds by Gerry & Sylvia Anderson
entries.pitch: Thunderbirds Are Go is a 1966 British science fiction film based on the iconic Supermarionation television series Thunderbirds, created by Gerry and Sylvia Anderson. The film follows the maiden voyage of Zero-X, the first manned spacecraft bound for Mars, which suffers a catastrophic malfunction during re-entry due to sabotage by the criminal mastermind known as The Hood. When disaster strikes, it's up to International Rescue—the secret organisation of heroes operating from Tracy Island—to save the crew using their fleet of advanced Thunderbird machines. The film showcases the trademark elaborate puppetry, intricate miniature effects, and sense of adventurous heroism that made the TV series a beloved classic. While it was a commercial failure upon release, it has since gained a cult following among fans of British science fiction and those who appreciate the unique artistry of Supermarionation.

entries.title: Time Bandits
entries.creator: Terry Gilliam (Director)
entries.pitch: Time Bandits is a 1981 British fantasy adventure film co-written, produced, and directed by Terry Gilliam, marking his directorial debut and the first installment in his "Trilogy of Imagination." The film follows Kevin, a young boy obsessed with history, whose ordinary life in a suburban home is disrupted when six dwarfs suddenly emerge from his wardrobe, stole a map from the Supreme Being, and whisk him away on a chaotic adventure through time. Together with the "Time Bandits," Kevin visits various periods in history—meeting Napoleon, Robin Hood, and King Agamemnon—while being pursued by Evil, a reality-manipulating entity who seeks the map for his own sinister purposes. The film was financed by George Harrison's HandMade Films and written by Gilliam with fellow Monty Python member Michael Palin. Upon release, it opened at number one at the US box office and received mainly positive reviews from critics, grossing $36 million against a $5 million budget.

entries.title: Time Considered as a Helix of Semi-Precious Stones
entries.creator: Samuel R. Delany
entries.pitch: In a future where criminals communicate through an ever-changing code system based on semi-precious stone names, a master thief and quick-change artist known only by his aliases (all bearing the initials HCE) rises through the ranks of the interplanetary underworld. The story follows his journey from a traumatized orphan to a powerful crime boss, navigating a world where Special Services agents can predict criminal behavior through holographic information networks. Told in first-person with literary allusions to James Joyce's Finnegans Wake, this Hugo and Nebula Award-winning novelette explores identity, transformation, and the price of success in a society that rewards those who can reinvent themselves fastest.

entries.title: Time Masters
entries.creator: René Laloux (Director), Mœbius (Art Designer)
entries.pitch: Time Masters (Les Maîtres du temps) is a 1982 French-Hungarian animated sci-fi film from the legendary team behind Fantastic Planet. Set in a far-flung space opera universe, the story follows a desperate race against time to rescue a young boy stranded on Perdide—a desert planet infested with giant killer hornets. As the rescue ship hurtles through space, the crew encounters bizarre alien encounters, political intrigue among deposed royalty, and finally the mysterious Masters of Time who manipulate the fabric of temporal reality. The film is a visually stunning journey through surreal alien landscapes, combining Laloux's visionary direction with Mœbius's iconic artwork in a tale about sacrifice, redemption, and the nature of time itself.

entries.title: Time of Roses
entries.creator: Risto Jarva
entries.pitch: Time of Roses is a pioneering 1969 Finnish science fiction film set in the year 2012, directed by Risto Jarva. The film follows Raimo Lappalainen, a documentary filmmaker preparing a television program about Finland in the 1960s, specifically the story of Saara Turunen, a nude model who died in an accident in the 1970s. As Raimo digs deeper into the past through interviews and research, he discovers that the "progress" and social liberalization promised by the 2012 meritocratic society has merely masked underlying class conflicts and social tensions that still simmer beneath the surface. The film is notable for its pop art aesthetics and social commentary, exploring themes of media, memory, and the reconstruction of history.

entries.title: Time to Hunt
entries.creator: Yoon Sung-hyun (Director)
entries.pitch: Time to Hunt is a 2020 South Korean dystopian action thriller film directed by Yoon Sung-hyun. Set in a bleak future South Korea, the film follows a group of four friends living in an economically devastated society where unemployment is endemic and hope is scarce. With their backs against the wall, they devise a seemingly straightforward heist to steal money and start fresh. However, upon completing the job, they discover they have attracted the attention of a mysterious and relentless assassin who begins picking them off one by one. Released globally on Netflix during the early COVID-19 pandemic, the film garnered attention for its visceral action sequences and grim view of a near-future society where the gap between rich and poor has become untenable.

entries.title: Timecrimes
entries.creator: Nacho Vigalondo
entries.pitch:
Timecrimes is a low-budget Spanish time travel thriller that masterfully manipulates cause and effect through a simple premise: a man inadvertently becomes trapped in a causal loop, forced to confront multiple versions of himself across a single hour. Unlike flashy time-travel blockbusters, this film relies on clever writing, tight pacing, and mounting dread rather than special effects. The story begins innocuously enough—Héctor scans the forest behind his new country home with binoculars and spots a young woman undressing in the woods. When he investigates, he encounters a mysterious bandaged figure who stabs him in the arm, setting off a chain of events that spirals into temporal chaos.

What follows is a meticulously constructed puzzle where Héctor must navigate his own past, present, and future selves while trying to prevent catastrophic consequences. The film premiered at Fantastic Fest in 2007 and had a theatrical release in Spain in 2008, earning praise for its innovative approach to time travel storytelling and to create tension from seemingly simple circumstances its ability.

entries.title: Timemaster
entries.creator: James Glickenhaus
entries.pitch: Timemaster is a 1995 American science fiction adventure film directed by James Glickenhaus. The film stars Jesse Cameron-Glickenhaus (the director's son) as Jesse Adams, a young man who discovers he is Earth's last line of defense against an alien threat. With the help of a wise mentor played by Pat Morita, Jesse must travel through time to different eras—from the Old West to ancient civilizations—battling alien forces that have infiltrated human history. The film also features early appearances by a young Michelle Williams in one of her first film roles.

entries.title: Timer
entries.creator: Jac Schaeffer
entries.pitch: Timer is a 2009 science fiction romantic comedy that explores a world where a wrist implant called a TiMER can count down to the exact day a person will meet their soulmate. The film follows Oona, a Los Angeles orthodontist whose TiMER is blank—meaning her soulmate hasn't yet received one. As she searches for love in a world increasingly obsessed with predestination, Oona must decide whether to wait for her timer to activate or embrace the uncertainty of genuine connection.

entries.title: Tiong Bahru Social Club
entries.creator: Tan Bee Thiam (Director)
entries.pitch: Tiong Bahru Social Club is a 2020 Singaporean satirical black comedy art film that explores themes of artificial intelligence, big data, and the pursuit of happiness in an increasingly algorithmic world. The story follows Ah Bee, a30-year-old everyman who, after being fired from his job, becomes a Happiness Agent at the Tiong Bahru Social Club—an idyllic artificial intelligence cult-like community dedicated to bringing joy to residents through data-driven experiences. Set in a rapidly aging Singaporean neighborhood, the film presents a dystopian vision of a society that has embraced AI to help people "learn what to do based on big data," even matching romantic partners through algorithmic prediction. As Ah Bee settles into his new role, taking care of an elderly aunt and meeting potential love interests, he begins to realize that something is fundamentally wrong with this utopia of happiness.

entries.title: Titan A.E.
entries.creator: Don Bluth, Gary Goldman
entries.pitch: Titan A.E. is a 2000 American animated post-apocalyptic science fiction action film directed by Don Bluth and Gary Goldman. Set in a future where humanity has been nearly wiped out by the hostile Drej aliens, the film follows Cale Tucker, a young man who discovers he possesses a mysterious ring containing a map to the Titan—a giant spaceship capable of creating a new planet for humanity. Along with a crew of ragtag aliens and human survivors, Cale races against time to find the Titan before the Drej can destroy it, while also uncovering the truth about his father's legacy and humanity's potential for a second chance.

entries.title: To the Stars by Hard Ways
entries.creator: Richard Viktorov
entries.pitch:
In the 23rd century, the starship Pushkin discovers a derelict alien vessel floating in deep space. The crew were identical humanoids created by an advanced cloning process — all dead except for one woman in a catatonic state. Professor Lebedev brings her to Earth, names her Neeya, and she begins a new life among humans.

But Neeya harbors secrets. She has no memory of her past, yet discovers she possesses powerful telekinetic abilities. As her memories gradually return, she learns she is the last survivor of the planet Dessa — a world stripped of its minerals by a mad scientist, its people poisoned, its future stolen. When a diplomatic mission from Dessa arrives, Neeya must choose: stay on Earth, or return to save her dying world.

This 1981 Soviet sci-fi adventure, known in the West through an edited dub featured on Mystery Science Theater 3000 as \"Humanoid Woman,\" explores cloning, memory, and what it means to be human when your very identity is programmed.

entries.title: Tokyo: The Last Megalopolis
entries.creator: Akio Jissoji (Director)
entries.pitch:
Tokyo: The Last Megalopolis is a 1988 Japanese epic tokusatsu historical dark fantasy/science fiction film directed by Akio Jissoji and based on the award-winning novel Teito Monogatari by Hiroshi Aramata. With a budget of around 1 billion yen (roughly $8 million), it was one of the most expensive live-action Japanese special effects films of the decade. The film became a notable success in Japan, ranking among the top ten highest-grossing domestic motion pictures of 1988, and is now regarded as a respected cult classic.

The story spans from 1912 to 1927, depicting a mystical battle over Tokyo's destiny. In 1912, master onmyoji Yasumasa Hirai warns Baron Eiichi Shibusawa that the vengeful spirit of Taira no Masakado—an ancient warlord turned vengeful spirit—must not be disturbed, as its power could destroy the city. When Shibusawa allows the Tsuchimikado sect to bless Tokyo, they are opposed by Yasunori Kato, a former Imperial Army lieutenant who is actually an oni (demon) seeking to awaken Masakado's spirit and destroy Tokyo.

entries.title: Tomorrow I'll Wake Up and Scald Myself with Tea
entries.creator: Jindřich Polák
entries.pitch: Tomorrow I'll Wake Up and Scald Myself with Tea is a 1977 Czechoslovak science fiction comedy that blends time travel paradoxes with absurd humor and political satire. Directed by Jindřich Polák (who also made the acclaimed Ikarie XB-1), the film is based on a short story by Josef Nesvadba. Set in a near-future Czechoslovakia where commercial time travel has become reality, the story follows identical twins Karel and Jan Bureš—one a corrupt pilot who works for Nazis planning to change history, the other an ordinary man thrust into an extraordinary situation when his twin dies unexpectedly. The film is notable for its uniquely Czech blend of surreal comedy, social commentary on totalitarianism (both historical and contemporary), and its surprisingly thoughtful handling of time travel logic. With production design that captures a wonderfully kitschy late-1970s Eastern Bloc vision of the future, this film has developed a cult following among fans of obscure European science fiction.

entries.title: Torture Ship
entries.creator: Victor Halperin
entries.pitch:
Torture Ship is a 1939 American science fiction horror film directed by Victor Halperin, based on Jack London's 1899 short story \"A Thousand Deaths\". The film stars Lyle Talbot as Dr. Herbert Stander, a mad scientist who conducts twisted experiments on the criminal mind aboard his private ship, using captured criminals as unwilling test subjects.

The film was one of the earliest adaptations of London's work and represents an intriguing early entry in the sci-fi horror genre, predating many of the more famous monster movies of the 1940s. Its premise of a scientist using his vessel as a floating laboratory for unethical experiments places it firmly in the tradition of mad scientist cinema that would flourish in subsequent decades.

entries.title: Totò in the Moon
entries.creator: Steno
entries.pitch:
Totò in the Moon is a 1958 Italian comedy science fiction film that represents a delightful piece of Cold War-era space age satire. Directed by Steno (who co-wrote the script with Lucio Fulci), the film follows Achilles Paoloni, a humble delivery boy at a small publishing house who writes a science fiction novel in his spare time. When U.S. scientists discover that Achilles possesses a rare substance in his blood—glumonium, derived from monkey breast milk—making him ideal for spaceflight, two rival powers (the Americans and a mysterious foreign power) compete to recruit him for a moon landing mission.

What makes this film remarkable is its playful subversion of spy thriller tropes and space race fever. The aliens—the Annelids—send down two clones (cosoni) of the main characters to sabotage the human mission, in a direct parody of Invasion of the Body Snatchers. The film balances slapstick comedy with genuine sci-fi imagination, creating an entertaining time capsule of 1950s optimism about space exploration mixed with the era's anxieties about Cold War competition.

entries.title: Toward Meeting a Dream
entries.creator: Mikhail Karyukov, Otar Koberidze
entries.pitch: Toward Meeting a Dream is a 1963 Soviet science fiction film directed by Mikhail Karyukov and Otar Koberidze, produced by Odessa Film Studios. The film follows aliens from the planet Centuria who pick up human music—specifically a song titled "Apple Trees Will Blossom on Mars" composed by cosmonaut Andrei Sayenko—and become intrigued enough to dispatch a spacecraft to investigate its source. However, their ship crashes on Mars, prompting Soviet cosmonauts to launch a daring rescue mission from their moon base aboard the spaceship Ocean.

entries.title: Transarctica
entries.creator: Silmarils (Developer)
entries.pitch: Transarctica (also known as Arctic Baron) is a 1993 French post-apocalyptic action-adventure and strategy video game developed by Silmarils. Set in a future Earth devastated by the greenhouse effect gone wrong, the planet is now entirely covered in thick clouds, with giant wolf packs roaming the frozen wastes and mammoths having re-emerged from elephant stock. Humanity survives in scattered settlements connected by a network of massive armored trains controlled by the ruthless Viking Union. Players hijack the Transarctica train and set out on a desperate quest to find the "sun" in this frozen wasteland.

entries.title: Transformers: Zone
entries.creator: Toei Animation
entries.pitch:
Transformers: Zone is a 1990 Japanese OVA that serves as the final chapter in the Transformers Generation 1 saga. When the mysterious three-faced insectoid being Violen Jiger dispatches the Nine Great Demon Generals—including Devastator, Menasor, Bruticus, and others—to acquire \"Zone Energy,\" the Autobots must rise to defend Earth and uncover the power of the legendary Zodiac. It's a compact, action-packed 30-minute adventure that delivers classic transforming robot action.

Originally intended to be a full TV series, Zone was forced to become direct-to-video due to less than expected toy sales. It stands as the last TF Generation 1 animated movie and the final entry in the Japanese Transformers G1 saga.

entries.title: Treasure Planet
entries.creator: Rumen Petkov
entries.pitch: Treasure Planet is a 1982 Bulgarian animated science fiction film and the first full-length animated feature produced in Bulgaria. Directed by Rumen Petkov and produced by the Sofia Animation Studio, this 62-minute film is a bold sci-fi adaptation of Robert Louis Stevenson's classic adventure novel "Treasure Island." Set in a distant future where Earth has become entirely artificial and nature no longer exists, the story follows young Filipe as he embarks on a cosmic quest for Captain Flint's legendary treasure. Notably, this Bulgarian adaptation predates Disney's CGI version of "Treasure Planet" by exactly 20 years, making it a pioneering work in Eastern European animation that reimagines the pirate adventure genre for a spacefaring context.

entries.title: Tron
entries.creator: Steven Lisberger
entries.pitch: Tron is a 1982 American science fiction action-adventure film directed by Steven Lisberger. The film tells the story of Kevin Flynn, a computer programmer and video game developer who is transported inside the software world of a mainframe computer where he must escape from the evil Master Control Program. Featuring groundbreaking computer-generated imagery, Tron was one of cinema's earliest films to use extensive CGI and became a cult classic that spawned an entire multimedia franchise.

entries.title: Tuko sa Madre Kakaw
entries.creator: Director Richard Abelardo
entries.pitch: Tuko sa Madre Kakaw (Gecko on the Madre de Cacao Tree) is a 1959 Filipino science fiction and kaiju film produced by LVN Pictures and directed by Richard Abelardo, one of the Philippines' pioneering special effects directors. Based on a comic by Clodualdo del Mundo Sr., the film tells the story of a mad scientist who develops a serum capable of turning ordinary animals into giants, using it to create a massive gecko that terrorizes a neighborhood. The film represents a fascinating artifact of Filipino cinema during the 1950s Golden Age, when the Philippines was one of Asia's most prolific film-producing countries.

entries.title: Turks in Space
entries.creator: Kartal Tibet (director), Murat Boyacioglu (writer)
entries.pitch:
Turks in Space (Dünyayı Kurtaran Adamın Oğlu, literally \"The Son of the Man Who Saved the World\") is a 2006 Turkish science fiction action comedy film and the sequel to \"The Man Who Saved the World.\" Directed by Kartal Tibet and starring Cüneyt Arkın reprising his iconic role, the film is set in the year 2055, when the world exists in a state of turmoil awaiting the formation of a government that can establish universal peace. The Orion Union—an uneasy alliance of planetary states—stands as the only governance preventing total chaos.

The story follows Murat's son, who works alongside his twin brother (though neither knows of the other's existence) to save the world from various threats. The film is infamous for its exceptionally low rating on IMDb—1.5 stars, placing it among the lowest-rated movies ever—making it a fascinating cult object for fans of obscure international sci-fi.

entries.title: UFO Robot Grendizer
entries.creator: Go Nagai (creator), Tomoharu Katsumata (director), Toei Animation
entries.pitch:
UFO Robot Grendizer is a classic Japanese mecha anime series that serves as the third entry in Go Nagai's influential Mazinger franchise. The series follows Duke Fleed, the sole survivor of the planet Fleed, who escapes his homeworld after it's devastated by the militaristic Vega Empire. Landing on Earth, Duke takes on the identity of Daisuke Umon and hides the powerful robot Grendizer beneath a research laboratory. When the Vega Empire launches their invasion of Earth, Duke must reveal his secret and pilot Grendizer to defend his adoptive homeworld alongside his allies.

The series is notable for its influence on the mecha genre and its massive cultural impact outside Japan, particularly in Europe and the Arab world where it became a cultural phenomenon under titles like Goldorak (France) and Goldrake (Italy).

entries.title: UFO Sweden
entries.creator: Victor Danell (Director)
entries.pitch:
UFO Sweden is a 2022 Swedish science fiction adventure film directed and written by Victor Danell. The film follows Denise, a teenager who believes her missing father was abducted by aliens, who joins forces with a UFO club of endearing misfits to investigate the mysterious disappearance. 

The film had its world premiere in Norrköping on December 12, 2022, and was released in Sweden on December 25, 2022. It received generally positive reviews, holding an 83% rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 23 critics' reviews. The film was inspired by Stranger Things, True Detective, The X-Files, and Interstellar, combining alien abduction mystery with coming-of-age adventure elements.
